UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO - CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L500] ECO-SUSTAINABLE TECHNOLOGIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL TOXICOLOGY
SECTION: STUDY PLANS INFORMATION
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1865

STUDY PLANS INFORMATION General information related to the current academic year Duration
3 years Ordinance
2020
status Open Credits
180 CFU Language Italian Type Bachelor's Degree Program Normative Reform 270/04
Degree class L-29 - Class of Bachelor's Degrees in Pharmaceutical Sciences and Technologies Joint Course No Limited Access (120 Places)
Location CHIETI (Sustainable enrollment: 120)
Department DEPARTMENT OF PHARMACY Website https://www.farmacia.unich.it/testa Teaching Method Conventional Admission Requirements Verification Methods for Access S  Course Instructors View list Admission Requirements Required Knowledge for Access Students must hold a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent under current regulations.
Basic knowledge is required to successfully follow the Bachelor's Degree program. Such knowledge includes satisfactory familiarity with basic mathematical calculation, mastery of fundamental laws of mechanical physics, and basic knowledge of cellular biology and general chemistry, logical reasoning skills, ability to express oneself orally and in writing without hesitation or errors, and a good general culture.
The methods for verifying such knowledge and skills will be determined in the course's didactic regulations. If the verification of the required knowledge for admission is not positive, the didactic regulations will also indicate the additional educational requirements that must be acquired in the first year of the program.
Admission Methods The Bachelor's Degree is limited access. Admission requires a five-year secondary school diploma.
By May 15th of each year, the Course Council proposes to the Department Council the maximum number of students to enroll in the first year, along with the enrollment and transfer deadlines to be included in the annual study plan.
For the 2024-25 academic year, the planned student enrollment is 120 units, of which 118 for Italian, EU, and non-EU citizens residing in Italy, and two for non-EU citizens residing abroad (Article 26, Law 189 of July 30, 2002). In case of exceeding 120 units, a merit ranking will be established based on the secondary school diploma grade, also considering the chronological order of enrollment (in case of equal grades, the chronological order of application submission applies).
Admission procedures will be adequately advertised on the University website (https://www.unich.it) and on the teaching structure noticeboards.
Enrollment and transfer deadlines are published in the Study Plan and the Admission Notice for the Bachelor's Degree in TESTA.
Additional Educational Requirements (OFA): criteria for determination and recovery methods After enrollment, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be defined through multiple-choice questions developed by instructors, containing 80 questions on Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Mathematics, and Logic.
The minimum diploma grade threshold for enrollment without OFA is 80/100. Students with a diploma grade below 80/100 will need to take the initial knowledge verification test. The recovery of OFA must be completed within the first year of the program and covers the courses in Mathematics, Physics, Biology, and Chemistry.
Verification Methods for Required Knowledge The initial knowledge verification test (mandatory per DM 270/04) is conducted to identify any educational gaps among new students and to organize necessary recovery activities (additional to the regular teaching activities of the Bachelor's Degree program), thus ensuring didactic support for students assigned OFA based on the gaps identified through the initial knowledge verification test.
Students transferring from other institutions, changing study programs, reactivating careers, or enrolling in a subsequent year with career abbreviation will be excluded from the initial knowledge verification. All information regarding the initial knowledge verification test (date, time, location, number of questions, test duration, registration methods, scoring criteria for correct, incorrect, or unanswered questions, etc.) will be published in the Admission Notice, on the University website (https://www.unich.it), and on the teaching structure noticeboards.
Specifically, the questions for OFA assignment relate to the following disciplines:
- Physics:
Direct and indirect measurements. Fundamental and derived quantities. Physical dimensions of quantities. Decimal metric system. International System of Units (SI). Units of measurement (names and relationships between fundamental and derived units). Multiples and submultiples. Kinematic quantities. Uniform linear motion. Uniformly accelerated linear motion. Uniform circular motion. Harmonic motion. Vectors and vector operations. Forces, moments of forces. Vector composition of forces. Definitions of mass and weight. Acceleration due to gravity. Density and specific weight. Law of universal gravitation. Work. Kinetic energy. Potential energy. Pressure and its units of measurement. Archimedes' principle. Heat propagation mechanisms. Laws of ideal gases. State changes. Basic concepts on acoustic and optical phenomena (reflection, refraction, dispersion). Electrostatics and electrodynamics. Electric field and potential. Electrical resistance and resistivity. Electrical work and power. Effects of electric currents.
- Mathematics:
Natural, integer, rational, and real numbers and their ordering and comparison. Algebraic operations and their properties. Proportions and percentages. Powers and their properties. Scientific notation. Radicals and their properties. Logarithms (base 10 and base e) and their properties. Algebraic expressions. Algebraic equations of first and second degree. Inequalities. Fundamental concepts on functions and their graphical representation. Measurement of lengths, surfaces, and volumes. Measurement of angles in degrees and radians. Sine, cosine, tangent of an angle and their notable values. Cartesian coordinate system in the plane. Equation of a line. Conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity. Distance from a point to a line. Equation of a circle, parabola, hyperbola, ellipse and their representation in the Cartesian plane.
- Chemistry:
States of matter aggregation. Heterogeneous and homogeneous systems. Compounds and elements. Ionic and molecular compounds. Atomic composition (electrons, neutrons, protons). Atomic number and mass number. Atomic weight and molecular weight. Chemical reactions and stoichiometry (balancing and elementary stoichiometric calculations). Concept of mole. Avogadro's number. Solutions. Solution concentration. Concepts of acid and base. Acidity, neutrality, basicity of aqueous solutions. pH. Carbohydrates. Lipids. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleic acids.
- Biology:
Organic molecules present in living organisms and their functions. Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Animal and plant cells. Cell membrane and its functions. Cellular structures and their functions. Cell division: mitosis and meiosis. Chromosomal complement. Animal and plant tissues. Photosynthesis. Glycolysis. Aerobic respiration. Fermentation. Sexual and asexual reproduction. Genes and DNA. Genetic code and its translation. Protein synthesis. Anatomy of main systems and their functions and interactions. General knowledge on viruses, bacteria, and fungi. Main organs and systems of plants and their functions.
Specifically, regarding the verification method for possessing such knowledge, the test, with a maximum time of 120 minutes, consists of 80 multiple-choice questions (4 answers) structured as follows:
-20 Chemistry questions
-20 Physics questions
-20 Mathematics questions
-20 Biology questions How Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) are determined The initial knowledge verification test will be conducted after enrollment. Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be assigned exclusively to students who answered correctly less than 50% of the questions in the disciplinary areas where recovery activities are provided (Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Biology). OFA must be completed within the first year through the recovery methods established by the Course Director and the instructors of the relevant disciplines.
Completing OFA by October 31st of the year following enrollment is mandatory to access the official exams of the corresponding courses as per the Study Plan.
Recovery Methods Based on the initial knowledge verification, if necessary, the Bachelor's Degree program will activate additional recovery courses beyond the official course lectures in each disciplinary area where students have educational gaps. In this regard, instructors of the disciplines subject to OFA will establish 1 or 2 weekly hours dedicated to recovery. Attendance at the recovery course is mandatory. Students attending recovery courses are not exempt from the mandatory attendance requirement for official courses. The educational gap is considered filled upon passing a written verification test.
In case OFA are not completed by October 31st of the year following enrollment, students cannot take exams for subsequent years unless they have passed at least 18 CFU related to the courses in the first year within the basic and characteristic types.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF STUDIES GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L500] ECO-SUSTAINABLE TECHNOLOGIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL TOXICOLOGY
SECTION: Program, texts, and objectives
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1865

Program, texts, and objectives Note regarding credits for other activities. The CFU window reserved for the final thesis, between 3 and 9 CFU, depends on the type of thesis the student intends to undertake (compilation or experimental). When the student chooses to follow a compilation thesis path, the thesis will be worth 3 CFU, and the student must complete a 150-hour training internship equivalent to 6 CFU. If the student is oriented towards an experimental thesis, it will be worth 9 CFU, with exemption from completing the training internship.
Communication skills (communication skills)
In terms of acquiring adequate knowledge and tools for communication, the graduate must acquire:
- a good scientific communication in Italian and English;
- computer skills, processing, presentation, and discussion of experimental data;
- ability to work in a group.
- ability to communicate with non-specialist interlocutors to implement prevention and education interventions for public health related to toxicological-environmental aspects.
Written and oral communication skills will be developed during seminars, exercises, and internship, which also include preparing reports and written documents and oral presentations of the same. The acquisition and assessment of the achievement of the aforementioned communication skills are also provided through the preparation of the final thesis and its discussion. English language (B1 level) is learned and verified through seminars and e-learning training activities and the corresponding assessment tests.
Both the acquisition of the four language skills (reading, writing, listening, and speaking) and mandatory attendance of lectures may be required, according to criteria to be specified during the course, in line with the requirements of the academic bodies.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF STUDIES GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L500] ECO-SUSTAINABLE TECHNOLOGIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL TOXICOLOGY
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1865

Autonomy of Judgment (making judgements)
In terms of acquiring conscious autonomy of judgment, graduates in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will be able to:
- evaluate and interpret experimental and process data;
- evaluate the process economics;
- implement a scientific approach to chemical-toxicological issues;
- acquire awareness of environmental risk assessment, of toxic compounds and/or their effects on environmental and food matrices;
- develop evaluations regarding chemical and industrial processes with particular reference to the monitoring of pollutants present in the environment and contaminants in food;
- capacity for reflection on social, scientific, or ethical issues connected to environmental themes.
Such capacities will be acquired in the basic, related, and professional characterizing training activities, both through attending lectures and exercises. The autonomy of judgment will be developed in particular through exercises, organized seminars, preparation of reports, especially in the areas connected to the assessment of toxicological-environmental risk, as well as during the internship and training activities and through the activity assigned by the supervisor for the preparation of the final exam.
The verification of the acquisition of autonomy of judgment occurs through the evaluation of laboratory reports, the evaluation of the degree of autonomy and capacity to work, also in groups, during the activity assigned for the preparation of the final exam, as well as of the internship.

Ongoing orientation and tutoring The ongoing orientation is conducted by the Dean of the Degree Programme, assisted by tutors Prof. Amelia Catladi, Giustino Orlando and Marcello Locatelli, and the academic secretariat of the Department of Pharmacy. Students can approach the identified teachers/tutors for clarifications regarding courses, internship, and traineeship. Additionally, tutors are appointed for international students, students with disabilities, working students, and student representatives.
For students engaged in documented work activities, a personalized study path is available to be agreed upon with individual teachers, including partial exemptions from attending lectures. If a student performs work activities in laboratories using techniques covered by the laboratory courses of the degree programme, a partial or total exemption from laboratory attendance may be granted upon prior agreement with the teacher.
The Degree Programme promotes accessibility in the facilities hosting the programme and in teaching materials for students with disabilities, ensuring the right to education for all enrolled students. Each year, teachers responsible for optional courses make themselves available to inform students about the content of the courses, enabling them to compile a personalized study plan. An annual meeting is organized primarily for second and third-year students to provide necessary information for activating the internship period, both in academic settings and external structures. Upon internship activation, each student is assigned an academic tutor who will follow them throughout the internship period.

Career Support The university has established a centralized Orientation and Placement service aimed at supporting the employment of its graduates.
Additionally, an advisory committee guided by the Internship Coordinator, Prof. Antonio Di Stefano, has been established within the degree program to facilitate students' internship pathways, enabling a satisfactory percentage to graduate during their studies. The committee's task is to systematically consult professional, technical-scientific organizations and companies in the sector, guide students towards training activities aligned with the degree program's objectives, and identify academic supervisors based on professional competencies to accompany students throughout their internship. Often, internships conducted at external institutions lead to actual employment contracts. Academic supervisors promote collaboration between the university and external institutions to establish a constructive and lasting trust relationship.

Student opinions A.A. 2020/21
The analysis reported relates to the 2020/21 Cohort that attended the first year of the CdL TESTA and the data regarding student opinions on teaching for the academic year 2020-21 are updated as of 31-07-2021 (Source PQA at link http://core.unich.it).
The number of questionnaires completed by attending students amounts to 107 out of 308 theoretical (34.74%) in the first year of observation with 7 courses covered for both semesters. In the academic year 2020/21, the general comment on the trend of judgments provided by attending students on the various courses of the program is globally positive, with good satisfaction regarding the teaching methodology, the qualification of teachers, and the schedules and availability of teachers for clarifications. All this is confirmed by an average score of 3.49, a value higher than the university average (3.35_data PQA_survey of student opinions 2019-2020_Table 3.a).
In particular, from the analysis of individual questions, it emerges high student satisfaction regarding teacher professionalism (punctuality in class: 3.78, availability during office hours: 3.84, consistency with the program: 3.70, clarity of teacher exposition: 3.59). The judgment reported by students in the 107 questionnaires indicates that they consider it appropriate to maintain the teaching load unchanged. The point requiring attention primarily concerns the preliminary knowledge possessed by the student for understanding what is provided in the program (2.74). Compared to the university average and the averages of health area programs (3.30_data PQA_survey of student opinions 2019-2020_Table 3.a), the score obtained by the CdL in TESTA (3.49) is higher.
Very interesting is the student evaluation of courses belonging to CUN areas of chemical and biological sciences: 3.54 and 3.48, respectively. No significant differences are evident.
A.A. 2021/22
The analysis reported relates to students who attended the first and second year of the CdL TESTA and the data regarding student opinions on teaching for the academic year 2021-22 are updated as of 31-10-2022 (Source PQA at link http://core.unich.it).
The number of questionnaires completed by attending students amounts to 390 in the first two years of observation with 15 courses covered for both semesters. In the academic year 2021/22, the general comment on the trend of judgments provided by attending students on the various courses of the program is globally positive, with good satisfaction regarding the teaching methodology, the qualification of teachers, and the schedules and availability of teachers for clarifications. All this is confirmed by an average score of 3.39, a value slightly lower than the academic year 2020/21 (3.49).
In particular, from the analysis of individual questions, it emerges high student satisfaction regarding teacher professionalism (punctuality in class: 3.61, availability during office hours: 3.62, consistency with the program: 3.50). The judgment reported by students in the 390 questionnaires indicates that they consider it appropriate to maintain the teaching load unchanged. The point requiring attention primarily concerns the preliminary knowledge possessed by the student for understanding what is provided in the program (2.99). However, this evaluation is higher than the academic year 2020/21 (2.79). Compared to the university average and the averages of health area programs (3.31_data PQA_survey of student opinions 2020-2021), the score obtained by the CdL in TESTA (3.39) is slightly higher.

Analysis 2022/23
The analysis reported relates to students who attended the TESTA Degree Course and the data regarding student opinions on teaching for the academic year 2022-23 are updated as of 31-07-2023 (Source PQA at link http://core.unich.it).
The number of questionnaires completed by attending students amounts to 678 with 38 training activities covered for both semesters. The percentage of questionnaires, which has significantly increased compared to the previous year (390 with 15 courses covered), is also due to the activation of the third year of the CdL.
In the academic year 2022/23, the general comment on the trend of judgments provided by attending students on the various courses of the program is globally positive, with good satisfaction regarding the teaching methodology, the qualification of teachers, and the schedules and availability of teachers for clarifications.
Regarding the academic year 2022/23 macro-indicators concerning teaching effectiveness (3.48) and organizational logistical aspects (3.50) of the CdS, they are in line with the health area values (3.43) and the university (3.48). Slightly lower is the overall satisfaction of the CdS (3.27) compared to health area (3.32) and university (3.35).
Students have evaluated very positively teacher punctuality (3.66), teacher availability (3.66), and clarity in examination procedures (3.46), all evaluations increased compared to previous years.
The judgment reported by students in the 678 questionnaires regarding the preliminary knowledge possessed by the same for understanding what is provided in the program has significantly increased in the academic year 2022/23, reaching 3.26 compared to 2.99 in the academic year 2021/22 and 2.79 in the academic year 2020/21. This increase is probably due to the actions taken by the CdS regarding the strengthening of entrance courses related to Additional Educational Requirements and to an orientation in entry primarily directed at scientific high schools.
The evaluation that is less high concerns the proportionality between study load and credits (3.16), in line with what was reported in the previous year (3.13). Regarding this point, meetings of the sector were held by the CdS President to harmonize course content and the proportionality of CFU per course. Compared to last year, the interest stimulated by the teacher in the disciplines is around the same value of 3.34.
The average evaluation of the Study Program (3.43) in the academic year 2022/23 is higher than the previous year (3.39) and in line with the average evaluation of Health Area Programs of the university (3.4).

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will be able to:
- interpret and predict the structure, physical properties, and chemical behavior of organic molecules, with particular reference to organic and inorganic pollutants;
- apply methodologies for the preparation and analytical characterization of samples collected from the environment (soil, water, air), interpret spectroscopic data, and prepare analytical reports;
- implement tools for verifying the environmental impact of chemical and pharmaceutical industrial processes and plan possible corrective actions;
- indicate new approaches for the industrial synthesis of chemical products through low-impact environmental processes (Green Chemistry);
- recognize and take corrective actions on factors influencing microbial development on matrices of different nature;
- apply experimental procedures for determining the composition or chemical-physical properties of food products;
- apply the most suitable preventive measures regarding occupational injuries and diseases and develop skills in managing exposure to chemical agents;
- evaluate the toxicity of drugs and other substances in relation to their presence in the environment;
- recognize mechanisms and characteristics of radioactive decays, perform radioactivity measurements;
- apply the most suitable preventive measures regarding occupational injuries and diseases.
- set up circular economy models and identify the main information necessary to carry out environmental sustainability assessments, and evaluate the related economic impacts through the appropriate tools;
- apply the EMA guidelines on Environmental Risk Assessment (EMEA/CHMP/SWP/4447/00 corr 2) within a pharmaceutical plant and in relation to production processes;
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology acquires the described competencies through: frontal lectures, exercises, laboratory activities, independent study, seminars, field practical activities, free courses, participation in external seminars, conferences, and congresses.
The acquisition of competencies is verified through: written exams, oral exams, laboratory practical tests, classroom discussions, reports to be submitted to the teacher.
Learning skills
Regarding the acquisition of adequate competencies related to learning skills, of fundamental importance will be:
- the ability to autonomously and guidedly update one's knowledge regarding technical-scientific and methodological innovations, particularly for professional disciplines;
- understanding scientific articles in English and bibliographic consultations;
- the ability to consult databases and other online information, through which to design and support arguments and solve problems in one's field of study.
- the ability to stay updated on national and community regulations of specific professional sectors such as the sector of chemical safety and environmental protection, the sector of food protection, or the regulatory section concerning drug production.
Learning skills are acquired throughout the study path, with particular regard to the teachings and individual study within the legal-regulatory context, related to the consultation of disciplinary databases.
The ability to learn is also evaluated through continuous verification forms during training activities, as students will be required to present autonomously researched data organized into reports to be submitted to the teacher, and through tutoring activities in project execution, and through the evaluation of the ability to self-learn developed during the final project activity. The development of adequate learning skills will be necessary to undertake subsequent studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge and understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will be able to acquire:
- knowledge of basic disciplines such as mathematics, physics, general chemistry, and organic chemistry, with their relevant methodologies and applications in environmental, biological, and chemical fields;
- basic knowledge of anatomy, biology, and pathology with particular reference to environmentally originated pathologies;
- theoretical and practical aspects of analytical chemistry and drug analysis, with reference to spectroscopic techniques and sample preparation for the determination of inorganic and organic analytes;
- knowledge of the general principles governing the production of all forms of pharmaceuticals, both sterile and non-sterile, focusing on the dynamics of containing potential environmental contamination;
- basic knowledge for understanding the most important chemical transformations occurring in air, water, and soil;
- in-depth understanding of the function of drugs in physiological and pathological processes and their role as environmental or food contaminants;
- basic knowledge of microbiology, with particular reference to the impact of microorganisms in the biotechnology, food, and industrial sectors;
- knowledge of the use of GMOs in the pharmaceutical industry for the production of recombinant proteins and drugs;
- basic knowledge of radioactivity and the laws of radioactive decay and the basis for understanding the interaction between radiation and matter and therefore how they can be detected;
- knowledge of nutrient classes, knowledge of the chemistry of fermented products, food preservation, and undesirable and toxic substances.
- knowledge of technologies for the recovery and valorization of industrial waste and principles of environmental monitoring, with particular reference to circular economy and the economic sustainability of recycling plants;
- basic knowledge of the Italian State Organization, regulations, and involved subjects in health and safety protection in workplaces, as well as regulatory bodies for national and international drugs, pharmacovigilance regulations, and environmental impact regulations for drugs (Environmental Risk Assessment, ERA).
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology acquires the described knowledge through: frontal lectures, exercises, laboratory activities, independent study, seminars, field practical activities, free courses, participation in external seminars, conferences, and congresses.
The acquisition of knowledge is verified through: written exams, oral exams, laboratory practical tests, classroom discussions, reports to be submitted to the teacher.

Brief course description The three-year Degree Course in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology (TESTA) was activated in the academic year 2020/21 at the Department of Pharmacy of the University of Chieti-Pescara 'G. d'Annunzio'.
TESTA graduates are fundamental for promoting scientific and cultural training aimed at protecting the environment. The distinctive characteristic of this course compared to others directed at the environment is the attention dedicated to the pharmaceutical, chemical, and food sectors. Thanks to the training path, graduates will acquire the necessary competencies to evaluate environmental risks related to the production and disposal of waste in the pharmaceutical, chemical, and food sectors, enabling them to successfully operate within these industries.
EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES:
The TESTA Degree Course aims to prepare professionals capable of applying the technical and scientific knowledge acquired in a wide range of sectors, including environmental chemical analysis, environmental toxicology, production and control of chemical and pharmaceutical processes, circular economy, recycling, and valorization of industrial waste.
COURSE STRUCTURE:
The TESTA Degree Course is structured over three years: the first year is centered around a core of fundamental subjects to provide a basic preparation, and the second and third years are based on more specific and professionalizing disciplines. During the three years of the course, students participate in lectures, exercises, laboratories, elective courses, seminars, conferences, congresses, and field practical experiences.
ACQUIRED COMPETENCIES:
The graduate will be able to perform functions in technical or professional roles in environmental protection, including:
  Preparation of protocols for chemical, microbiological, and eco-toxicological analyses on environment and atmosphere (waters, foods, waste, soil, and air);
  Preparation of protocols for monitoring waters, air, soil, and foods to detect potential contaminants;
  Execution of chemical controls according to the most modern certified quality systems, toxicological, and microbiological systems for the protection of food and industrial environment (water, air, soil);
  Ability to apply standardized sampling methodologies and certified instrumental analytical methodologies for the detection, recognition, and quantification of toxins and contaminants in different matrices included in the work context functions;
  Planning of preventive and educational interventions for public health in relation to toxicological aspects derived from chemical and biological pollution.
PROFESSIONAL PROFILE:
The TESTA graduate will be able to apply the acquired competencies in the fields of chemical-toxicological analyses, chemical-pharmaceutical sector, production and control of chemical processes, and environmental sustainability with particular reference to circular economy.
EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES:
The TESTA Three-year Degree Course prepares for the profession of:
Chemical Technicians Technicians in the field of chemical/toxicological analyses Technicians for the operation and control of chemical plants Environmental Control Technicians Waste collection and environmental remediation technicians Biochemical laboratory technicians Food products technicians Registration in the Register of Chemists Section B.
External effectiveness As of 1.09.2023, no student has obtained the degree, therefore data on graduates entering the workforce are not available.
Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path One of the fundamental determinants of the TESTA Course is the relationship with the environment, with particular reference to preserving the territory and the organisms that inhabit it, maintaining biodiversity, and the health status of the human population. At the same time, one of the main goals is to identify technological solutions capable of combining industrial production with ecological sustainability, with particular reference to circular economy. All this is reflected in the professional and cultural profiles that the course intends to form, namely professional technicians capable of implementing the technical-scientific knowledge acquired in numerous application fields related to environmental toxicology, production and control of chemical and pharmaceutical processes, ecology, and management of industrial waste and territory control.
Territorial control from a toxicological perspective thus becomes one of the main objectives of the graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology, as through the acquired competencies they can conduct research and analyses on the territory and potential contaminants, implementing control and evaluation of potential pollutants in waters, soil, and air. In addition to potential contaminants, the identification of existing environmental criticalities can help in seeking new strategies to define the changes to apply and the eventual environmental recovery. Such recovery and restoration of environmental conditions is of fundamental importance, as the environment must be considered a factor that can directly influence health.
The concept of environmental recovery, eco-sustainability, and territory control is certainly linked to the production and control of chemical and pharmaceutical processes, among the main responsible for the release of environmental contaminants that still possess biological activity, as well as active pharmaceutical ingredients or their metabolites/derivatives. The professionals that the course intends to form will have the opportunity to collaborate and assist specialists in controlling and managing the operation and safety of chemical flow processes and plant equipment, as well as pharmaceutical and food production. The emphasis will be placed not only on the control of chemical processes, but especially on the themes of circular economy, eco-sustainability, and the valorization of by-products from chemical and pharmaceutical industries. Indeed, the main objective will also be to provide in-depth knowledge of the methodologies applied for recycling waste in order to design, develop, and evaluate systems for controlling and detecting information on various types of environmental pollution. Such competencies can be put into practice within chemical and pharmaceutical companies, in laboratories of public and private structures, in Universities, in Research Institutes, and in the National Health Service.
The greater attention to the pharmaceutical sector characterizes and distinguishes the TESTA Course from other degree courses belonging to class L-29, as the proposed training path will enable the graduate to evaluate the environmental risk related to the production and release into the environment of pharmaceutical production waste, active ingredients, or final formulations, operating within chemical-pharmaceutical industries in relation to EMA guidelines on Environmental Risk Assessment (EMEA/CHMP/SWP/4447/00 corr 2). The objective is of particular importance to limit the environmental impact consequent to the market release and use of human medicines. The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will therefore be able to contribute concretely to the necessary requirements to prepare the documentation to be submitted to Regulatory Authorities (in the context of a new drug market authorization request or for modifications to existing drugs), to demonstrate having carried out the environmental impact assessment and adopted the preventive measures provided.
The TESTA Degree Course is structured over three years: two semesters intended to provide a basic preparation and four semesters of a more specifically professionalizing nature, during which lectures, exercises, laboratories, seminars, field practical activities, free courses, participation in external seminars, conferences, and congresses are scheduled. The didactic structure of the degree course includes a group of basic disciplines, followed by disciplines of a professional nature. The course aims to provide the graduate with adequate scientific-technical training to enable direct entry into the workforce. Each discipline will be evaluated by teachers through ongoing and final assessments, through the administration of written tests or oral assessments, or a combination of both. The examination methods will be detailed by each teacher in class, as well as illustrated in the corresponding Teaching Sheet.
At the end of the path, the possibility of completing a professional internship of at least 150 hours for the recognition of 6 CFU is provided, to be carried out in laboratories of Companies or Convened Entities. Alternatively, the student may choose a research thesis path to be carried out within the Department or at External Companies and Entities. The internship activity will be carried out not before the third year, according to the modalities indicated in the study regulations. The Course, together with the training internships at companies, public structures, and laboratories, also provides for study stays abroad within the framework of international agreements. Knowledge of a foreign language, preferably scientific English, is also required.

Consultation with representative organizations - at national and international level - of goods and services production, professions (Course establishment)
On April 15, 2019, the Establishing Committee for the TESTA Course, appointed by the Department of Pharmacy Council in 2018, met to evaluate the strategic plan for expanding the training offer with a shared training path of clear interest to companies operating in the regional and national territory. During the same meeting, the name 'Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology' was chosen for the Course to account for current industrial production needs for a 'circular' economy fully protecting the environment. During the discussion, the concrete availability of Fater SpA to contribute to the delivery of some professionalizing subjects to be included in the study program was highlighted. It was also proposed to introduce highly qualified professional company teachers, and periods of training abroad and internships on the national and international territory were outlined.
Consultations were carried out with the main stakeholders: Teachers, Directors of chemical and pharmaceutical companies, as well as the Order of Chemists and Physicists of Lazio, Umbria, Abruzzo, and Molise, through meetings of the Establishing Committee formed by teachers and an industrial sector representative, and through the administration of questionnaires to industrial realities of the territory to evaluate training requests and needs to form graduates capable of performing specific functions in technical or professional roles in environmental protection.
Among the consulted organizations, the Order of Chemists and Physicists of Lazio, Umbria, Abruzzo, and Molise, through the interregional delegate, on November 25, 2019, evaluated the activation of the Course with a very positive opinion, proposing to consider, among the educational objectives, also topics related to the management of plants not only pharmaceutical but also for example in the field of purification and energy recovery in the environmental sector, as well as considering deeper insights on the classification of substances according to REACH and CLP regulations and the management of safety data sheets (MSDS), without neglecting regulatory references in the field of environmental authorizations for plant operation. The Order suggested that the indications expressed during the consultation be integrated into elective courses (3 CFU each) within the laboratory waste management and forensic chemistry and toxicology, which was promptly received by the Establishing Committee.
The judgment expressed by Fater SpA during the Establishing Committee meetings, by the Analytic Hierarchy Bio Refinery Process (AHP) Development Leader, was widely favorable towards the current degree project, emphasizing that the current structure is suitable for adequate preparation of the required professional figures, especially specialized in the analysis and use of bioproducts extracted or recovered for direct industrial applications, essential for implementing eco-sustainable approaches in an economy based on recycling and valorization of industrial waste to be redirected to the production of medicated medical devices. The Establishing Committee accepted the reflections of the Fater SpA representative, proposing the establishment of a related course entitled 'Recycling and Valorization of Waste and Circular Economy'.
Among the industrial realities, the judgment of Domp Farmaceutici SpA was possible, which expressed its opinion through the completion of a questionnaire on July 24, 2019 by the Biotech Director of the L'Aquila plant. In particular, the opinion was positive regarding the course name and the proposed employment opportunities, considering that the professional figures the course aims to form respond to the needs of the company represented. The learning outcomes the course aims to achieve in all reference areas were considered positive, as well as being responsive to the competencies required for the formation of the professional figures provided by the course.
The company BSP Pharmaceuticals with headquarters in Latina was involved through the completion of questionnaires on July 23 and 29, 2019 by the following professionals: Environmental, Health & Safety Director (EHS) & Qualified Person, Corporate Quality Operations Director, and Plant Director. The professionals consulted expressed a favorable opinion regarding the course name, while for the proposed employment opportunities, emphasis was placed on greater attention to professional toxicology and deeper insights regarding WHO guidelines on environmental risk assessment in the pharmaceutical sector. The learning outcomes the course aims to achieve in all reference areas were considered positive, and among the proposed suggestions, the need for greater focus on systems for preventing environmental contamination and the ability to prepare protocols and environmental risk assessment (ERA) reports was highlighted. It was recommended to pay particular attention to the evaluation of products released into the environment in relation to climate change and ecosystem changes, to the implementation of knowledge and consequences related to human exposure to environmental pollutants, as well as to deepen knowledge of computational toxicology. Finally, it was proposed to develop some courses in English to facilitate opportunities abroad and to prepare company presentations within the Course.
The Establishing Committee, taking into account the indications of the company directors, took charge of introducing within the disciplines of chemical, biological, and medical sectors, training aspects that reflect the suggestions emerging in various sections of the questionnaire.
The questionnaires drafted by the responsible of the consulted industrial realities can be viewed at the address Consultation with representative organizations - at national and international level - of goods and services production, professions (Subsequent consultations)

2021: CONSULTATION WITH ITALIAN UNIVERSITIES FOR ADMISSION TO MASTER'S DEGREE LM-9 In March 2021, consultations were initiated, both by email and by phone, with the following Universities to allow TESTA graduates to continue their studies for the Master's degree LM-9.

From the consultations, a shared appreciation for the new TESTA Degree Course was evident, and a proactive willingness to accept our graduates. Access to these Master's degrees will be subject to a requirement assessment by the TESTA graduate, such as a minimum number of CFU acquired in basic and characteristic disciplines during the Bachelor's Degree. Additionally, since some Universities offer the Master's degree entirely in English, the TESTA graduate is required to have English language knowledge equivalent to level B2.
2021: NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL PHARMACEUTICAL COMPANIES The consultation between the TESTA Course Director, Prof. Ivana Cacciatore, the Third Mission Coordinator of the Department of Pharmacy, Prof. Antonio Di Stefano, and Dr. Mirko Gabriele, Production Director of THERMO FISHER SCIENTIFIC (multinational pharmaceutical company, Ferentino, RM), took place via teleconference on March 22, 2021.
From the consultation, a shared appreciation for the proposed training path for students of this Course was evident, and a confirmation of the necessity of the TESTA graduate figure in the current reality, considering the growing importance of environmental impact in all production sectors (traditional and biotechnological drugs, cosmetics, pesticides, biocides, food, etc.). Among the strengths of the Course, the cross-disciplinary and multidisciplinary competencies, not only theoretical but also practical and real related to real situations in the field of environmental toxicology, a sector often neglected in other university courses, were highlighted.

Entry, path, and exit data The statistical data relating to the first and second cohort of students enrolled in the TESTA Course are for the academic years 2020-21 and 2021-22 and are updated to August 29, 2022 (Source S.I.Ca.S. at link http://gestapp.unich.it).
COHORT 2020-21
The students enrolled in the TESTA Course for the academic year 2020-21 were 43, of which 32 were pure enrollments and 3 were incoming transfers (Tab. 1_S.I.Ca.S.). For the academic year 2020-21, 51 new careers were registered, but 7 students enrolled before January 31, 2021, withdrew, and one student transferred to another course (Tab. 2, 2-bis_S.I.Ca.S.).
The students enrolled in the 2020-21 cohort are predominantly female (60.5%) compared to male (39.5%). 58.1% of the enrolled students are 19 years or younger, 16.3% are between 20-22 years old, 7% between 23-24 years, and 18.6% over 25 years (Tab. 3_S.I.Ca.S.).
34.9% of the enrolled students come from the same municipality, 34.9% from another municipality in the province, 21% from another province in the region, and 9.2% from outside the region (Tab. 4_S.I.Ca.S.). The S.I.Ca.S. data in Table 4-Ter show that 39 students are from the Abruzzo region (90.8%), 2 from Molise (4.6%), 1 from Campania (2.3%), and 1 from Sicily (2.3%).
The high school diploma obtained at the licei is held by 46.51% of the enrolled students (of which 30.2% hold the scientific high school diploma and 9.3% the classical high school diploma), at technical institutes by 30.3%, at magistral schools by 13.95%, and at other schools by 7% (Tab. 5 and Tab. 5 Bis_S.I.Ca.S.).
The high school diploma grade of 100 with honors is reported by 2.3% of the enrolled students, 100 by 9.3% of the enrolled students, between 80 and 99 by 35% of the enrolled students, and up to 80 by 49% of the enrolled students (Tab. 6_S.I.Ca.S.).
PASSING TO THE SECOND YEAR COHORT 2020-21.
For productivity evaluation, type A, B, and C subjects are considered. The course productivity in the first year of study shows, in terms of CFU acquired by December 31, 2022, that the average CFU per student is 30 out of 60 CFU total offered in the first year (Tab. 7_S.I.Ca.S.). In particular, 13.95% of students did not acquire any CFU, 6.98% acquired CFU < 5, 13.95% acquired CFU between 6 and 20, 51.16% acquired CFU between 21 and 40, and 13.95% acquired CFU > 40 (Tab. 7-quater_S.I.Ca.S.).
The detail of the average grade % shows that 9.30% of students have an average grade between 28 and 30, 23.26% between 24 and 27, and 32.56% between 18 and 23 (Tab. 8 Bis_S.I.Ca.S.).
The subjects of the first semester of the first year, General Chemistry and Physics with Mathematics, were passed by 58.14% and 53.49% of students, respectively (Tab. 8 Ter_S.I.Ca.S.). Scientific English and Elements of Informatics, being type E and F subjects, respectively, are only considered in the calculation of CFU acquired by students.
The average grade reported by students in the General Chemistry exam is 23.4, while in the Physics with Mathematics exam it is 23.6 (Tab. 8 Quater_S.I.Ca.S.).
Chemical Analysis and Organic Chemistry and Human Anatomy and Applied Biology, subjects of the second semester of the first year, were taken by 11.63% and 23.26% of students, respectively (Tab. 8 Ter_S.I.Ca.S.). Lower percentages are attributable to the fact that students had only June and July 2022 exam sessions available to take these exams.
The average grade reported in the Chemical Analysis and Organic Chemistry exam is 26.20, while in the Human Anatomy and Applied Biology exam it is 26.3 (Tab. 8 Quater_S.I.Ca.S.).
The students of the 2020/21 cohort who regularly enrolled in the second year after the first year are 24, equal to 55.8% of the enrolled students.
Following analysis of the data reported by the GAQ, the GAQ members, meeting in the Councils of July 21, 2022, and September 13, 2022, to improve the percentage of students passing to the second year, proposed the following:
a) Invite, through the student representative, students who have difficulties in exam preparation to take advantage of teacher office hours;
c) Organize two meetings (in September/October) dedicated to first and second-year students to analyze the difficulties encountered in the study path;
d) Directly orient the entrance orientation more specifically.
Additionally, the student representative proposed the introduction of partial exams to increase the success rate in passing exams. The teachers welcomed the proposal positively.
The President recalls that, following the allocation of dedicated funds, calls for tutoring in subjects predominantly of the first year of the course were issued starting from the academic year 2022/23.
COHORT 2021-22
The students enrolled in the TESTA Course for the academic year 2021-22 were 42, of which 35 were pure enrollments and 1 was an incoming transfer (Tab. 1_S.I.Ca.S.). For the academic year 2020-21, 48 new careers were registered, but 1 student enrolled before January 31, 2021, withdrew, and 5 students transferred to other courses (Tab. 2, 2-bis_S.I.Ca.S.). Substantially, the enrolled students are stable in the first two years of the TESTA Course activation.
The students enrolled in the 2021-22 cohort are predominantly female (52.4%) compared to male (47.6%). 71.4% of the enrolled students are 19 years or younger, 21.4% are between 20-22 years old, 4.7% between 23-24 years, and 2.4% over 25 years (Tab. 3_S.I.Ca.S.). Compared to the 2020/21 cohort, these data show that the percentage of enrolled students aged 19 or younger has increased by 12%.
11.9% of the enrolled students come from the same municipality, 64.3% from another municipality in the province, 7.1% from another province in the region, and 16.67% from outside the region (Tab. 4_S.I.Ca.S.). The S.I.Ca.S. data in Table 4-Ter show that 35 students are from the Abruzzo region (83.3%), 2 from Puglia (4.8%), 1 from Marche (2.4%), 1 from Molise (2.4%), 1 from Basilicata (2.4%), 1 from Umbria (2.4%), and 1 from Calabria (2.4%). These data show that the percentage of students from other Italian regions has almost doubled compared to the 2020/21 academic year, increasing from 9.3% to 16.7%. Although the percentage of students from the same municipality has halved (from 34.9% to 11.9%), the percentage of students from another municipality in the province has almost doubled (from 34.9% to 64.3%), testifying to the intense orientation activity carried out in 2022.
The high school diploma obtained at the licei is held by 23.8% of the enrolled students (of which 11.9% hold the scientific high school diploma and 7.1% the classical high school diploma), at technical institutes by 50%, at magistral schools by 9.52%, and at other schools by 14.3% (Tab. 5 and Tab. 5 Bis_S.I.Ca.S.).
The high school diploma grade of 100 with honors is reported by 4.8% of the enrolled students, 100 by 16.7% of the enrolled students, between 80 and 99 by 47.6% of the enrolled students, and up to 80 by 31% of the enrolled students (Tab. 6_S.I.Ca.S.). Although the percentage of students from licei has decreased from 45.46% to 23.8% of the enrolled students, the percentage of students enrolled from technical institutes has significantly increased (from 31.82% of the 2020/21 cohort to 50% in the 2021/22 cohort).
The TESTA Course Council on September 13, 2022, notes that the trend of enrolled students has remained constant over the first two years of Course activation, with a prevalence of predominantly female enrolled students. The geographical user base has expanded to neighboring regions of Abruzzo, confirming that the entrance orientation activity carried out via teleconference in schools outside the region has made the Course known externally. The data also show that in the second year of activation, the percentage of students from licei has halved in favor of students from technical institutes. The Council proposed to the Entrance Orientation Committee to direct orientation towards institutions with a strongly scientific and environmental character.
PASSING TO THE SECOND YEAR COHORT 2021-22.
For productivity evaluation, type A, B, and C subjects are considered. The course productivity in the first year of study shows, in terms of CFU acquired by December 31, 2023, that the average CFU per student is 30 out of 60 CFU total offered in the first year (Tab. 7_S.I.Ca.S.).
In particular, 43.90% of students did not acquire any CFU, 17.07% acquired CFU between 6 and 20, 31.71% acquired CFU between 21 and 40, and 7.32% acquired CFU > 40 (Tab. 7-quater_S.I.Ca.S.).

The students of the 2021/22 cohort who regularly enrolled in the second year after the first year are 21, equal to 51.22% of the enrolled students.
These data show a high percentage of students who did not acquire any CFU despite the Course Council having:
a) invited, through the student representative, students who have difficulties in exam preparation to take advantage of teacher office hours;
b) organized two meetings (in September/October) dedicated to first and second-year students to analyze the difficulties encountered in the study path;
c) established the introduction of partial exams to increase the success rate in passing exams.
d) established tutoring in subjects predominantly of the first year of the course.

The percentage of students from technical institutes remains largely constant, around 44%.

The data also show that the percentage of students from licei has doubled compared to students from technical institutes due to orientation directed predominantly in licei.
Characteristics of the final exam The degree in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology is obtained after passing a final exam, which constitutes an individual training moment to complete the path. During the final exam, the student presents and discusses their thesis project, also of an experimental nature, related to the educational objectives of the Course, which is written under the supervision of a teacher of the Faculty. The final exam can be taken in English, and the final thesis can be presented in the same language.
Method of conducting the final exam The final exam can be taken in English, and the final thesis, whether compilative or experimental, can be presented in the same language.
However, a favorable and motivated opinion from the Course Council is required, which guarantees the possibility of effectively evaluating the thesis, thanks to the presence of sufficient competencies within the teaching body. In any case, the thesis and the thesis written in a foreign language must be accompanied by an adequate summary (abstract) in Italian.
The Degree Examination Committee is composed of a minimum of five and a maximum of seven members; it includes First and Second Class Teachers, Researchers, Contract Teachers, and professionals from external companies.
The final grade, expressed in hundredths, takes into account the weighted average of the grades obtained during the study course, plus:
A) a percentage up to a maximum of 10% in reference to the grade in hundredths obtained from the average of the career grades, and conditioned by the quality of the activity performed;
Additional points may be assigned by the Degree Committee:
B) 1 point if the student graduates during the course;
C) 0-1 point (at the discretion of the committee) if the student has had an international mobility during their study path;
D) 0-2 points for an experimental thesis.
The award of the honors (lode) will be at the discretion of the Committee, taking into account the candidate's previous career and the thesis work.
For the award of the honors, the Committee's unanimous decision is required. If the graduate has achieved, during the course, an average grade of at least 107/110 in the profit exams, the Committee may propose a mention for 'pregevole curriculum studiorum' to be approved unanimously.
The Degree Exam is normally held in the months of July, October, November, March, and April.
Procedures for requesting, characteristics, and obtaining the degree title.
The student must prepare a compilative or experimental thesis agreed with a Department teacher or from other Departments, or with a teacher from another Italian or foreign University, or with a researcher from other public or private institutions, following the signing of a convention or recognition of the visiting student status.
The thesis request must be submitted to the Course Director after acquiring at least 117 CFU, at the beginning of each month after all exam sessions, normally on the first Wednesday of March, April, May, June, July, September, October, November, and December. The supervisor and co-supervisor are appointed by the Course Council.
The discussion of a compilative thesis must take place at least three months after the appointment of the supervisor.
The discussion of an experimental thesis must take place at least six months after the appointment of the supervisor.
To be admitted to take the Degree Exam, the student must have acquired, in total, 171 CFU in the case of an experimental thesis, or 177 CFU in the case of a compilative thesis; must submit to the student office: - a request to the Rector at least 90 days before the Degree session - a final copy of the Thesis at least 15 days before the Degree session.
Summary of the technical report of the evaluation nucleus - SUA Sheet The design of the Course was carried out with appropriate timing and attention. The cultural and professional profiles of the figure the Course intends to form are clearly defined. The direct consultation of the stakeholders is adequate at the local level, although not entirely at the national level.
The functions and competencies are described with sufficient precision and consistency with the professional profiles. The path is sufficiently consistent with the professional profile.
The course provides an admission test: the necessary knowledge for admission are defined in detail, as are the modalities. OFA are correctly assigned in the main subjects (mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology) based on not reaching a minimum score in the corresponding questions of the test, and support courses are also provided for each subject.
The structural resources and teaching staff appear adequate. The monitoring of the Course is consistent with the University's AQ system.

Admission Requirements Required knowledge for admission Candidates who hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent under current regulations (art. 6, comma 2, D.M. 270/04) and who possess adequate preparation and are qualified for the admission exam may be admitted to the first-level Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Therapy (class L/SNT2). Admission to the Study Program is quota-driven in accordance with Law 264/99. The University, in implementing the Ministerial Decrees issued annually for admission purposes, verifies the adequacy of general culture and logical reasoning knowledge, as well as theoretical/practical knowledge and current regulations specific to the discipline and functional to subsequent professional application, and knowledge of scientific-mathematical culture, statistics, computer science, English, and human and social sciences. Admission to the Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Therapy (class L/SNT2) following transfer from a different Bachelor's Degree course (not Occupational Therapy, even if belonging to the same class or another study program at the same University) is possible within available places. Recognition of studies completed at other Italian Universities, as well as credits earned there, may be granted after review of the curriculum submitted by the originating University and the accredited course programs at that University. The admission test used to verify the possession of adequate knowledge and skills will be used to prepare the merit ranking and assign Additional Training Requirements (OFA). Specifically, admitted students who score below 25% of the maximum score in Biology and Physics on the entrance test will be assigned Additional Training Requirements (OFA) to be completed during the first year of the course with the relevant verification methods.

Admission Procedures Article 4 excerpt from the Occupational Therapy Course Regulations.
Required Knowledge for Admission Candidates who hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable according to current regulations (Article 6, Paragraph 2, Ministerial Decree 270/04) and who possess adequate preparation and are qualified for the admission exam may be admitted to the first-level Occupational Therapy Degree Course (class L/SNT2).
Admission to the Course is quota-controlled in accordance with Law 264/99. The University, in implementing the annual decrees issued for admission purposes, verifies the adequacy of general culture and logical reasoning knowledge, as well as theoretical/practical knowledge and current regulations specific to the discipline and functional to subsequent professional application, and knowledge of scientific-mathematical culture, statistics, computer science, English, and human and social sciences.
The admission test used to verify the possession of adequate knowledge and skills will be used for the preparation of the merit ranking and for the assignment of additional training obligations (OFA). Admission to the Occupational Therapy Degree Course (enabling the health profession of Occupational Therapist) is granted to candidates who rank favorably within the quota of students allocated. Students admitted to the Course who score below 25% of the maximum score in Biology and Physics on the entrance test will be assigned additional training obligations (OFA) to be fulfilled during the first year of the Course with the relevant verification methods. Fulfillment of OFA involves the assignment of training activities for each discipline in which the student has shown deficiency. Assessment will be conducted through the successful completion of a final exam requiring qualification to be taken within the first year of the Course and no later than the deadline for renewal of enrollment in the second year, with methods established by the Course Director and the instructors of the relevant courses. It is mandatory to complete the OFA activities, which are a necessary condition for passing the verification exam. Failure to fulfill OFA within the specified deadlines will result in automatic enrollment in the first year out of sequence. Completion of additional training obligations does not grant additional academic credits beyond those in the curriculum, and the related activities are not part of the study plan. For current regulations regarding additional training obligations (OFA), refer to Article 28 of the University Academic Regulations.
Admission to the Occupational Therapy Degree Course (class L/SNT2) following transfer from a different Degree Course not in Occupational Therapy (class L/SNT2), even if belonging to the same class or another course at the same University, is possible within available quotas. Recognition of studies completed at Degree Courses of other Italian Universities, as well as credits earned there, may be granted after review of the curriculum transmitted by the originating University and the syllabi of courses accredited at that University.

Admission Procedures Candidates may be admitted to the first-level Degree Course in Occupational Therapy (class L/SNT2) who hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable according to current regulations (art. 6, paragraph 2, DM 270/04), and who possess adequate preparation and are qualified for the admission exam.
The available places for the Occupational Therapy Degree Course (class L/SNT2) are determined annually by a decree of the Ministry of Education, University, and Research (hereinafter referred to as MIUR), in relation to the actual availability of teaching staff, suitable teaching and scientific facilities (classrooms, laboratories for practical exercises and biomedical research), and services operating within the local cooperating structures of the National Health Service, as well as in accordance with the University's proposal considering the sustainability of human and instrumental resources.
Access to the Study Course requires a national admission exam prepared by MIUR, consisting of a multiple-choice test on topics of general culture, logic, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. For admission to the courses, a general culture is required, with particular relevance to literary, historical-philosophical, social, and institutional fields, as well as the ability to analyze written texts of various types and aptitude for logical-mathematical reasoning, as specified annually in the call. Moreover, the required knowledge and skills refer to the preparation promoted by educational institutions organizing activities consistent with the Ministry's Programs, especially in preparation for the State Exams, and also relate to the scientific disciplines of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics. The content and format of the test are typically established annually by MIUR through a decree and specified each year in the University's competitive call.
Finally, the University offers preparatory courses for admission competitions to Health Professions, based on theoretical foundations, exercises, and simulations on the subjects specified in the call.
Admission to the Occupational Therapy Degree Course (class L/SNT2) following a transfer from a different Degree Course (not in Occupational Therapy, even if belonging to the same class) is subject to passing the admission exam and is possible within the available places.
Information on administrative procedures and required fees for registration in the admission test (if applicable) and for recognition of acquired credits is available on the University's website at the following link: www.unich.it
Program, Texts, and Objectives Communication Skills (communication skills)
At the end of the study program, Occupational Therapy graduates will be able to manage communication as follows:
- Establish a meaningful therapeutic relationship with the person, their family, and caregivers
- Establish effective collaborative relationships with other members of the healthcare team
- Use professional tools such as the rehabilitation record, clinical report, and rehabilitation project, drafting them clearly, concisely, and professionally
- Translate technical language in a way that is understandable even to those outside the professional field
- Use appropriate tools for scientific communication, also in English.
Communication skills will be developed throughout the entire educational path, particularly through the courses characteristic of the profession, seminars, laboratories, and clinical internships.
Teaching Tools: classroom activities, teaching laboratories, practical lessons in laboratories and/or equipped classrooms, Internship, reading and interpretation of international literature.
Assessment Methods (which can be conducted in person or exceptionally in virtual form): written reports on the communication aspects of the rehabilitation setting; briefings with tutors and the coordinator; oral and written presentation of projects; internship.

URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/618

Autonomy of Judgment (making judgments)
At the end of the training path, graduates in Occupational Therapy will be able to exercise decision-making and operational judgment autonomy in conducting the therapeutic process, using clinical reasoning as a method and reflecting on the social and ethical implications related to the application of knowledge and operational norms.
This autonomy will be realized in all phases of the Occupational Therapy rehabilitation process, particularly through the ability to:
- identify, through the evaluation of clinical data in the psychomotor, cognitive, functional and relational fields, the health needs of the subject in different life stages, also in relation to the presented psychological conditions;
- define functional prognosis and therapeutic goals
- choose and plan strategies, methodologies and techniques to promote health and well-being through the use of occupation and the involvement of the patient or caregiver,
- integrate the resources of the assisted person and the environment with individual and/or collective health needs,
- evaluate using appropriate outcome measures as the result of the intervention,
- compare and use the best scientific evidence, international guidelines, best practices and expert experience in the discipline.
- Autonomy of Judgment will be attained through the entire training path, particularly through the teaching specific to the profession, seminars and laboratories as well as through the clinical internship.
Verification method (to be carried out in person or exceptionally in virtual form): written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, clinical case discussions, definition of the Rehabilitation Plan/Program and completion of the clinical record.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI-PESCARA "GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO"
COURSE: [L644] OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY
SECTION: Orientation in Entry
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/618

Orientation in Entry The University "G. d'Annunzio", through its Orientation, Placement, Right to Study and Disability Sector, provides support to secondary school students in making the challenging choice of the most suitable academic course for their abilities, assisting them in university studies to prevent initial evaluation errors from causing delays or abandonment of the chosen path, and ultimately facilitating their entry into the job market and professions. Orientation encompasses a set of services offered by the University of Chieti-Pescara "Gabriele d'Annunzio" to improve students' relationship with the University, accompanying them throughout their academic journey from choosing a study path to entering the workforce through specific and targeted activities for prospective students, enrolled students, and graduates.
The service is coordinated by a delegate of the Rector for Orientation, appointed by the School of Medicine and Health Sciences (Prof. Giustino Orlando), assisted by the interim Sector Manager (Mr. Marco Costantini) and a delegate from the Department of the Course, appointed by the Department Director (Prof. Mirco Fasolo). Orientation services include periodic public presentations of the educational offer, inviting graduating secondary school students from the region and from out-of-region schools that request it, as well as participation in orientation fairs organized by various entities at the national level.
Services are offered by organizing presentations of the Educational Offer, coordinating University orientation with Department orientation, and involving secondary school students in meetings and seminars at school institutions:
- Open Days: Annual event held at the Chieti and Pescara campuses, inviting all secondary schools in the Abruzzo region and neighboring regions. During this event, the University presents its wide range of study paths within an Educational Offer structured into 4 main academic areas (Health, Scientific, Social, and Humanistic) and organized into 68 courses offered by 14 Departments.
- Student Fairs and Exhibitions: Events where direct meetings with Department and Course professors are possible to deepen knowledge of the University and understand its opportunities. The University organizes its own Student Fair but actively participates in Student Fairs organized by other cities throughout the academic year (e.g., Macerata, Fermo, Ascoli Piceno, Bari, etc.), as well as abroad (e.g., University of Tirana).
- School Meetings: Presentations of Courses and seminars organized by Departments or the Course itself to guide secondary school students in transitioning from graduation to university studies.
- Urban Box: The "d'Annunzio" University has signed an agreement with the City of Pescara for the use of the Urban Box in Piazza della Rinascita as a meeting point with young people and citizens. The Urban Box serves as a showcase facing the city of Pescara where the University's educational offer is presented interactively through videos, brochures, and staff.
- PNRR 2026 Orientation: Following requests from secondary schools to activate PNRR Orientation School-University agreements, orientation courses are offered at the University. From the start of the academic year until May, 15-hour orientation courses for different schools are scheduled, held in person and following two modalities: one day of course held at the Chieti campus, featuring a module explaining the university system and TOLC tests, and two separate modules presenting all Health and Scientific Area Courses. The second day of course, held at the Pescara campus, involves courses aimed at presenting Social-Humanistic Area Courses and all tools for choosing a university path. At the end of the course, the Almaorientati questionnaire is administered to better understand each student's profile. Based on the results, students can further explore their test outcomes with the support of experts from each of the four areas present at the Pescara campus.
- Universities Unveiled: CRUI has decided to establish the National Day of Universities on March 20, coinciding with International Happiness Day and within the Minerva Week, a period dedicated to celebrating knowledge and education. For this occasion, the University participated with meetings, workshops, and debates organized on campus open to all citizens.
Through collaboration with a group of professors, the orientation service is also responsible for producing both printed and online versions of the Student Guide, a useful information tool and first moment of self-orientation, as well as supporting secondary school students transitioning to university and new enrollees.
Course representatives, who participate in various orientation events held across the territory, invite graduating students and fourth-year secondary school students to complete the AlmaOrientati questionnaire available on the University Orientation portal, a useful tool to help future enrollees monitor their knowledge of the university world and reflect on self-orientation.
The University provides a free mobile app specifically developed to more easily access the Orientation Services offered by the University of Chieti-Pescara "Gabriele d'Annunzio". Ongoing orientation and tutoring Ongoing orientation is implemented through various actions. - ongoing orientation and monitoring of academic careers
- coordination of didactic-integrative and recovery activities where necessary.
