• Dott.ssa Maria Laura Di Loreto Nelle battute iniziali dell'incontro, il Prof. Cascavilla sottolinea l'importanza del ruolo del Comitato di Indirizzo nel consentire di raccogliere informazioni al fine di giungere ad una più solida valutazione della corrispondenza tra le competenze e le capacità che il mondo del lavoro richiede e i profili dei laureati.
In seconda battuta, informa il Comitato circa il buon andamento del Corso di laurea triennale in termini di crescita di immatricolazioni e iscrizioni, anche in considerazione dell'equilibrio dell'offerta didattica e della relativa sostenibilità del percorso di studi. In particolare, le iniziative di orientamento in ingresso, in itinere e in uscita hanno avuto un apprezzabile riscontro da parte degli studenti, in termini di partecipazione e soddisfazione.
Inoltre, il Presidente informa il Comitato della recente istituzione di un dottorato di ricerca in Social Sciences, finalizzato a completare la filiera della già ricca offerta didattico-formativa.
In merito alla offerta didattica, i membri esterni del Comitato di indirizzo, nonché la rappresentante degli studenti, evidenziano la necessità di un potenziamento delle attività laboratoriali e di tirocinio a fronte dell'andamento crescente degli iscritti e, pertanto, del conseguente bisogno di tenere in considerazione le nuove possibilità aperte dall'evoluzione del mondo del lavoro. In tal senso, da un lato è già in corso una attività di aggiornamento dei laboratori; dall'altro, si registra come la commissione tirocini sta procedendo alla revisione ed alla integrazione degli enti convenzionati.
l giorno 15 febbraio 2024, alle ore 15:00, si è riunito - presso lo Presidenza dei corsi di laurea socio-criminologici – Palazzina di Lettere e sulla piattaforma telematica Teams - il Comitato di indirizzo del Corso di laurea triennale in Sociologia e criminologia (L-40) con il seguente ordine del giorno:
1. Presentazione offerta formativa a.a. 2024/2025
Sono presenti: Proff. Cascavilla, Della Pelle, Antonilli, Ferrara, Dott.ssa De Girolamo (in presenza).
I docenti Tuozzolo, Cifaldi, Rossi, la Dott.ssa Di Renzo, il Dott. Vincenzo Circosta, il Dott. Ugo Terracciano, i rappresentanti degli studenti per i corsi di laurea triennale e magistrale Daniela Marcucci, Giulia Pestarini, Fiammetta Trisi ( a distanza).
Presiede la riunione il Professor Cascavilla.
Il Presidente ringrazia i partecipanti e ricorda la funzione del Comitato di indirizzo.
Si tratta di un organo previsto dal regolamento universitario, formato da docenti dei corsi di laurea, dai rappresentanti degli studenti e dai rappresentanti di istituzioni, aziende pubbliche e private, enti pubblici che hanno avviato un rapporto di collaborazione con i Cds, e che rappresentano strutture in cui i laureati dei Cds possono svolgere attività di tirocinio, ed esperienze post lauream.
Al fine di ridurre il gap esistente tra la fase di formazione universitaria e il mondo del lavoro, è stato istituto da regolamento universitario il Comitato di indirizzo, per offrire agli studenti la possibilità di spendere le abilità e le competenze, acquisiti nel percorso universitario, all'interno del mondo professionale, riducendo il divario tra momenti formativi di natura più teorica (università) e concretezza del mondo lavorativo. Secondo il regolamento è necessario riunire il Comitato di indirizzo almeno una volta l'anno, perché sia informato sulla programmazione dei corsi di laurea e possa formulare proposte utili per l'a.a. successivo.
Nel Comitato sono presenti diverse realtà, rappresentanti di enti pubblici e privati. Il Presidente dà lettura dell'elenco dei nominativi che compongono l'attuale Comitato di indirizzo.

• Dott.ssa Maria Laura Di Loreto Il Presidente ringrazia il Comitato per il lavoro svolto nel corso degli anni, per aver formulato proposte di miglioramento che il Corso di laurea ha recepito e messo in pratica. Attualmente i corsi di laurea triennale e magistrale ha una curvatura criminologica e sulla sicurezza, anche alla luce delle indicazioni del Comitato.
I nostri Cds risultano essere attrattivi per studenti provenienti da varie regioni italiane, da Nord a Sud.
Il Prof. Cascavilla declina, dunque, la proposta formativa per il nuovo a.a. 2024/2025, che non presenta sostanziali cambiamenti, in quanto i corsi risultano attrattivi e piuttosto richiesti. Il Corso di laurea in Sociologia e Criminologia è il secondo per numeri di iscritti tra i vari Cds di Ateneo, anche il Corso magistrale presenta un numero soddisfacente.
Dà quindi lettura degli insegnamenti previsti nel Cdl Triennale di Sociologia e Criminologia, sottolineando come presentino una determinata curvatura in modo che siano coerenti con gli obiettivi formativi del cds legati alla criminalità e alla sicurezza.
Dà lettura anche degli insegnamenti del Corso di Laurea magistrale in Ricerca sociale, politiche della sicurezza e criminalità interclasse.
Chiarisce al Comitato la funzione dei laboratori professionalizzanti previsti nel percorso, ovvero di essere attività che orientano gli studenti verso il mondo professionale. Gli studenti, infatti, hanno la possibilità di mettere a frutto le conoscenze teoriche nel mondo professionale, grazie alla presenza di professionisti che svolgono i laboratori.
Dà lettura dei laboratori attivi nel corrente a.a.
L'Ateneo ha fornito alcune indicazioni circa l'attivazione dei laboratori professionalizzanti, al fine di evitare una eccessiva frammentazione. Se si prevede di introdurne di nuovi, l'Ateneo suggerisce di eliminarne altri.
Il prossimo a.a. non prevede sostanziali modifiche nell'attivazione dei laboratori.
Il Prof. Cascavilla dà la parola al Prof. Della Pelle per alcune integrazioni.
Il Prof. Della Pelle informa il Comitato di indirizzo dell'attivazione del dottorato di ricerca, giunto al secondo anno, che sarà proposto anche per il prossimo. Illustra la sua articolazione in tre percorsi, di sociologia generale, sociologia della devianza e del crimine, politico- filosofico. Sottolinea come rappresenti non solo una possibilità per gli studenti di proseguire con un ulteriore percorso di formazione ma anche di attivare dottorati in convenzione con enti pubblici, i cosiddetti dottorati industriali, i quali permettono di conseguire il titolo durante il percorso lavorativo. Invita, quindi, i rappresentanti del Comitato a proporre studenti che possono partecipare al bando o ad attivare percorsi di dottorato industriale. Ricorda, inoltre,
al Comitato anche la possibilità di convenzionarsi per tirocini curriculari rivolti a studenti della triennale e magistrale.
Il Professor Cascavilla precisa il fatto di essere consapevoli come Cds che la nostra offerta formativa, pur essendo di tutto rispetto, presenti il limite di non prevedere master, necessari per creare un ulteriore collegamento tra il mondo della formazione universitaria e quello professionale, per il quale occorre una formazione specifica che il corso di laurea non può dare offrire per vocazione a studi generali. Non è stato possibile attivare master fino ad ora in quanto si è stati impegnati nella trasformazione del Corso magistrale in interclasse e nel dottorato, auspicando in un futuro prossimo di poter dedicare tempo ed energie alla formulazione di proposte di master.
Il Prof. Cascavilla invita i presenti a intervenire per integrazioni e proposte.
La Dott. Trisi si congratula per i risultati raggiunti, per il numero degli iscritti e per il fatto che si tratta di corsi (triennale e magistrale) atipici a livello nazionale. In merito ai laboratori professionalizzanti, sottolinea come siano maggiormente centrati su devianza e diritti, mancando un laboratorio che orienti al lavoro in carcere e alla professionalità presenti. Pertanto, propone di attivarne uno specifico di orientamento alle varie professionalità in carcere, tenendo conto della previsione di assunzione di diversi operatori e dei numerosi concorsi che saranno banditi.
Il Prof. Cascavilla sottolinea l'interesse degli studenti verso il mondo carcerario e il desiderio di spendere il titolo in tale ambito. Informa i presenti del risultato raggiunto da una dottoranda, la dott.ssa Di Cesare, la quale è risultata vincitrice di un concorso nell'amministrazione penitenziaria come funzionario giuridico-pedagogico a tempo indeterminato. La proposta della Dott.ssa Trisi sarà presa in considerazione.
Il Dott. Terracciano ritiene fondamentale un orientamento in criminologia applicata in ambito professionale, in quanto base essenziale per l'attività di criminologo. In merito ai master, come membro dell'Associazione di criminologi informa i presenti dell'organizzazione di un master propedeutico alla certificazione da criminologo che si può acquisire con norma UNI. Si rende disponibile ad attivarlo presso l'Università d'Annunzio.
Il Prof. Antonilli, in relazione alla proposta avanzata dal Dott. Terracciano, sottolinea la validità della proposta e gli sforzi che il Cds sta mettendo in atto per la sua attivazione. In tal senso si sta cercando una più ampia collaborazione da parte degli uffici, avendo riscontrato una certa freddezza iniziale da parte dell'Ateneo.
Il Prof. Cascavilla evidenzia la necessità di attivare il master quanto prima, per evitare sovrapposizioni con ulteriori proposte che potrebbero essere avanzate da altri Cds. Potrebbe essere necessario attivarlo in modalità online, tramite l'università telematica, qualora l'Ateneo dovesse farne richiesta. Informa i presenti della volontà da parte del Rettore di istituire un master in Scienze forensi, con curvatura giuridica per ruoli ruoli di consulenza in tribunale, per il giudice.
Il Prof. Antonilli ribadisce la necessità di ricevere l'appoggio di professionisti AICIS in quanto la norma prevede l'attribuzione del 50% di ore a docenti interni e il restante 50% a esterni. Sarebbe opportuno vagliare la possibilità di attivare una sorta di convenzione con l'associazione che ha già creato un percorso formativo coerente con gli obiettivi della norma e fare uno studio di fattibilità anche alla luce del nuovo regolamento di Ateneo sui master.
La dott.ssa Di Renzo informa i presenti di essere in pensione dallo scorso anno ma le è stata data la possibilità dal questore di seguire studenti per il tirocinio. A breve è in programma un'altra visita presso la Leonardo. I ragazzi molto entusiasti con operatori polizia scientifica, oltre all'ordine pubblico e alla violenza di genere, come sostegno e prevenzione. Suggerisce di focalizzare attenzione sulla prevenzione e sul ruolo dei centri per riabilitazione e sostegno per uomini maltrattanti. Si attiverà per attivare convenzione.
Il Prof. Cascavilla informa i presenti dell'attivazione del laboratorio con la Leonardo tramite il Dottor Sergola in questo anno accademico o per il prossimo.
Dottor Circosta afferma di aver lavorato 4 anni con il Dottor Terracciano per elaborare la norma UNI e di essere stato docente nel corso attivato su criminologia. Sottolinea la difficoltà di reperire collaboratori, e le grandi difficoltà che incontrano nel mettere in pratica conoscenze.
I Laboratori dovrebbero essere pensati come fucine per sporcarsi le mani, traducendo la conoscenza accademica in pratica. Suggerisce di concentrarci su come si deve fare, sulla pratica, operatività. Mancano le figure di Security manager che siano in grado di fare risk assesment di origine criminoso e Analisi di rischi in criminologia urbana.
Il Prof. Cascavilla chiede ai rappresentanti degli studenti di intervenire.
Giulia Pestarino, rappresentante degli studenti, dichiara di non avere nulla da aggiungere.
Daniela Marcucci, rappresentante degli studenti, dichiara di non avere nulla da aggiungere, se non in merito ai tirocini. Alcune attività nell'elenco non corrispondono agli interessi del corso di laurea. Chiede di aggiornare elenco.
Il Prof. Cascavilla ringrazia i presenti per la partecipazione e la proficua collaborazione. La seduta è tolta alle 16.30
Dati di ingresso, di percorso e di uscita In relazione al flusso degli immatricolati registrati nel 2022/2023, si registra un numero costante di immatricolati (454 contro i 492 del precedente a.a) di cui 381 (437 nel 21/22) immatricolati puri. Si assiste quindi alla prosecuzione della tendenza positiva degli ultimi anni.
Relativamente alla tipologia di diploma superiore, per l'a.a. 2022/2023 il 40% ca. (lieve decremento) è in possesso di un diploma liceale, il 26,2% (lieve aumento) di un diploma magistrale, il 21,1 ca. (lieve decremento rispetto al 21/22) di uno tecnico, il 2,8% (dato inferiore al 6,7% del precedente anno) da un diploma professionale. Il diploma è stato conseguito con una votazione 'fino a 80' dal 54,8% ca. (dato lievemente superiore al 52% dell'anno precedente) e con una 'fra 80 e 99' dal 37,4%. Il 6,1% ca. ha ottenuto una votazione pari al 100 (nel 21/22 il dato si attestava sull'8% ca.).
Il 63,8% (precedentemente il 68,9%) degli iscritti proviene da regioni diverse dall'Abruzzo, l'8,1% ca. (il 17,8% nel 21/22) proviene da altro Comune della provincia.
L'80% (precedente rilevazione 84,5% ca.) (dati PQA agosto 2023) si laurea con una votazione fino a 105/110 e il 13,4% ca. (nel precedente anno, il 10,3%) si laurea con una votazione compresa tra 105 e 110.
Per quanto concerne le proposte di miglioramento, in relazione alla sostenibilità del corso di laurea e tenuto conto di un significativo numero degli ingressi, si presenta la necessità di una opportuna programmazione finalizzata a un incremento del numero dei docenti.

I dati di ingresso, di percorso e di uscita verranno discussi nel primo Consiglio di corso di laurea utile, presumibilmente entro la prima metà di settembre 2023.In seguito, si potrà procedere con l'inserimento dell'allegato del verbale.
Caratteristiche della prova finale La prova finale prevede l'elaborazione scritta di una ricerca relativa alla riflessione critica sulla letteratura concernente uno specifico tema d'indagine o relativa alla delineazione di un progetto di ricerca e/o di un progetto operativo finalizzato alla realizzazione di un determinato intervento sociale. In ogni caso lo studente dovrà dimostrare buona capacità di riflettere criticamente sul materiale bibliografico di riferimento ed autonoma capacità di utilizzare tale materiale al fine di costruire la propria tesi e di saper utilizare metodi e strumenti di ricerca e di programmazione di interventi in ambito sociale.
Modalità di svolgimento della prova finale La prova finale prevede l'elaborazione scritta in lingua italiana (o - previa approvazione del consiglio di corso di laurea - in altra lingua) di una ricerca relativa alla riflessione critica sulla letteratura concernente uno specifico tema d'indagine o relativa alla delineazione di un progetto di ricerca e/o di un progetto operativo finalizzato alla realizzazione di un determinato intervento sociale. In ogni caso lo studente dovrà dimostrare buona capacità di riflettere criticamente sul materiale bibliografico di riferimento ed autonoma capacità di utilizzare tale materiale al fine di costruire la propria tesi e di saper utilizzare metodi e strumenti di ricerca e di programmazione di interventi in ambito sociale.
La prova finale consisterà nella valutazione dell'elaborato presentato dallo studente e compilato con l'assistenza del docente della materia corrispondente all'argomento prescelto.
Come deliberato Consiglio di Cds nella seduta del 16 luglio 2018 lo studente non espone oralmente i contenuti della tesi di fronte all'intera commissione ma sarà premura del relatore verificare la capacità del candidato di argomentare il tema trattato e dimostrare un buon accesso alle fonti bibliografiche consultate.
La valutazione sarà effettuata dalla commissione tenendo conto dell'elaborato presentato, delle fonti consultate, dei dati raccolti e della congruità della metodologia applicata in caso di tesi sperimentale, delle capacità dimostrate dal candidato, della valutazione del docente della materia corrispondente all'argomento prescelto.
La Commissione conferisce una votazione che va da 0 a 8 punti aggiuntivi rispetto al punteggio di base derivante dalla media ponderata dei voti riportati in occasione del sostenimento degli esami curriculari, potendosi riconoscere la distinzione della lode in presenza dell'unanimità di consenso della commissione.
Inoltre, potrà essere attribuito n. 1 punto aggiuntivo qualora il laureando abbia svolto un periodo di studi all' estero ovvero in uno degli scambi previsti all'interno del Progetto Erasmus.
Nello specifico il Consiglio di Cds nella seduta del 16 luglio 2018 ha deliberato di:
'non far esporre più oralmente i contenuti della tesi difronte all'intera commissione',
'1. La tesi, una volta approvata dal relatore (che giudicherà anche la capacità del laureando di esporne oralmente i contenuti), sarà valutata da una apposita Commissione.
2. La Commissione di esami di tesi verrà convocata, in successione, due volte:
a) In una prima riunione, i membri della Commissione, ai quali il laureando dovrà far pervenire almeno sei giorni prima della riunione il proprio elaborato, dopo aver appreso il giudizio del relatore, stabiliranno il voto di laurea.
b) Nel corso di una riunione pubblica la Commissione renderà noti i voti di laurea proclamando i nuovi dottori in Sociologia e Criminologia'.
Argomenti trattati nelle tesi di laurea:
Violenza di genere Politiche di sicurezza nazionale ed internazionale Esecuzione della pena Nuove tecnologie e mutamento sociale Rapporto tra diritti e società Globalizzazione Sintesi della relazione tecnica del nucleo di valutazione Il Nucleo di Valutazione esprime parere favorevole in merito alla fattibilità tecnica della proposta di modifica, discussa e approvata nella consultazione con le organizzazioni rappresentative a livello locale della produzione, servizi, professioni.
Sintesi della relazione tecnica del nucleo di valutazione - Scheda SUA Il Nucleo di Valutazione esprime parere favorevole in merito alla fattibilità tecnica della proposta di modifica, discussa e approvata nella consultazione con le organizzazioni rappresentative a livello locale della produzione, servizi, professioni.

Teaching Method Conventional Verification of knowledge required for access S  Course instructors View list Admission requirements Required knowledge for access Regarding curricular requirements, all individuals holding a secondary education diploma obtained in Italy or abroad and recognized as suitable according to current regulations may access the Social Service Degree Course (L-39).
Additionally, good knowledge of spoken and written Italian language, good logical reasoning ability, basic knowledge in social science and contemporary culture is required.
The methods for verifying such knowledge and abilities will be determined in the course's didactic regulations.
Any detected educational gaps will result in the assignment of Additional Educational Obligations (OFA) to be fulfilled after enrollment, during the first year of the course, following the methods specified in the Course's Didactic Regulations.
Admission methods Regarding curricular requirements, all individuals holding a secondary education diploma obtained in Italy or abroad and recognized as suitable according to current regulations may access the Social Service Degree Course (L-39).
To assess adequate personal preparation, the Department Council appoints a Committee that verifies the possession of required knowledge through an interview.
If the Committee considers the candidate's knowledge level sufficient, it issues an aptitude assessment allowing enrollment.
Diplomates who achieved a grade at least equal to a minimum threshold to ensure possession of the required criteria and preparation are exempt from the interview. This minimum threshold is set at 70/100.
If this threshold is not met, the candidate must undergo a qualifying interview conducted by the Committee responsible for verifying the necessary knowledge.
Any detected educational gaps in one or more of the following study areas:
a) Basic knowledge in social science and contemporary culture (SSD SPS/07),
b) Approach to the scientific methodology of social science (SSD SPS/07),
c) Communication and logical argumentation (SSD SPS/08)
will result in the assignment of Additional Educational Obligations (OFA) to be fulfilled after enrollment, during the first year of the course, through verification tests or interviews conducted by the respective instructors of the aforementioned study areas.
OFA are considered fulfilled if students who did not pass or did not undergo the interview have earned at least 18 CFU in foundational and characteristic courses during the first year, allowing enrollment in the second year.

Program, texts and objectives Note regarding selected sectors and credits for basic activities The breadth of the basic field 'Historical-anthropological-philosophical-pedagogical disciplines' is determined by the need to activate the required courses in order to provide an integrated spectrum of formative knowledge related to the profile of a social worker capable of combining an organic vision of contemporary issues and welfare interventions in their various historical-anthropological and philosophical-pedagogical variations.
Note regarding selected sectors and credits for characteristic activities It is considered appropriate to include the sectors IUS/09 among legal disciplines and M-PSI/05 among psychological disciplines for greater flexibility in pursuing the educational objectives.
Communication skills
The graduate in Social Service must have acquired the ability to:
- communicate with users and colleagues using appropriate language;
- structure the reception of individuals, families and groups in services;
- transmit social information and communications appropriate to the target audience;
- relate and document regarding the performance of the profession (relations, reports, analysis documents);
- identify appropriate communication methods for each specific operational situation;
- structure effective relationships with educational, supportive or promotional purposes for the individual in different life stages, for the family and for the community;
- establish correct communication within the institutional context for hierarchical and functional aspects;
- structure an interview setting for analyzing needs and assessing requirements;
- promote network work by demonstrating ability to build community networks;
- use communication techniques related to prevention, promotion and health education;
- be competent in listening for the protection of citizens' rights;
- be competent in managing information regarding services;
- be competent in using information technologies.
Communication skills will be acquired through theoretical courses in sociology, pedagogy, psychology, and professional methodology, as well as through internship.
The acquisition of behavioral competencies will be verified through teaching activities, by tutors during the internship, and through final assessment.

Autonomy of judgment (making judgements)
The graduate possesses solid theoretical and practical knowledge enabling the development of skills and abilities for collecting and interpreting social data to determine autonomous judgments.
Autonomy of judgment is monitored through:
- verification methods, oral and/or written, planned during and at the end of courses;
- internship activities verification through presentation and discussion of a report by students;
- final exam verification through discussion of a compilation and/or experimental work. Training periods assistance Administrative contact: Cinzia Colangelo (ufficio.tirociniclass@unich.it)
The Social Work Study Course provides curricular internships for 9 CFU in the field of Social Service and Social Assistance professions. These activities complete the theoretical and practical training required by the study program through direct contact with occupational realities where students will practice their profession. For the internship, the Study Course has specific agreements with public or private entities operating in the social intervention, socio-assistential, and socio-health sectors. The entities and organizations where students complete their internships are primarily those with a socio-health focus, socio-assistential welfare, local welfare, and more generally those operating in the welfare sector.
The Study Course assists students in completing their internships through a dedicated service that handles signing new agreements and collects and analyzes evaluation forms completed by the tutor to assess the effectiveness of the internship.
Assistance for internship completion includes:
1) Reception in Front Office and Back Office with stakeholders involved in the internship activity;
2) Promotion of new agreements;
3) Support and maintenance of relationships with agreed entities;
4) Collection and management of forms and documentation related to internship activation;
5) Coordination with the external supervisor of the hosting entity/organization;
6) Assistance/accompaniment to the intern for the elaboration of the internship training project by the responsible Academic Tutor.
All Course Council members serve as academic tutors for various internships. All necessary information and documentation for activating and managing internships are provided through a dedicated section on the Course website, which also lists the agreed entities (https://class.unich.it/pagina-stage-e-tirocini-1063).
The Course has over 300 active agreements with various local entities, national associations, cooperatives, including the following: ASL 1 of Avezzano-Sulmona-L'Aquila, ASL 2 of Lanciano-Chieti, Chieti Municipality, Chieti Prefecture, ANFFAS, Pescara Municipality, Pescara Province, Union of Municipalities of Vomano, Basilicata Region, various juvenile prisons, ASL of Benevento, and numerous Italian municipalities.
Between January and December 2023, 134 students started their internship, none conducted abroad.
The 2022 data from the University's teaching application services on graduates indicate a rating of 3.09 (scale 1-4) for the university's support in internship completion and a satisfaction rating of 3.71 for the internship experience.
A satisfaction questionnaire for internships will be developed subsequently for internal use by students.

Workplace Accompaniment
2024- B5   WORKPLACE ACCOMPANIMENT Contact: Professor Francesco Ferzetti (francesco.ferzetti@unich.it)
Workplace accompaniment activities include both specific initiatives developed by the Study Course and activities carried out in coordination with the University's 'Placement & Career Service' Division (previously 'Orientation, Tutoring and Placement, Right to Study and Disability'). This Division manages the intervention lines provided by the post-graduation Orientation program called 'START', which offers various services managed through the online job placement platform (http://job.unich.it/placement/): PWI internships, employment placements, transnational mobility actions. At University level, the service organizes weekly workplace and entrepreneurship orientation meetings, company presentations, and recruitment days. The University's Workplace Orientation and Placement Manager is Dr. Annalisa Michetti (0871-3556345; annalisa.michetti@unich.it), while the University's Delegate is Professor Davide Quaglione (until July 26, 2023, the Delegate was Professor Mario Luigi Rainone). The orientation desk is located at the Chieti Campus (placement@unich.it). The Department of Business Economics' contact for exit orientation and placement activities is Professor Federica Ceci (Coordinator of the Placement Commission until February 2024), while the contact for exit orientation and placement activities is Professor Francesco Ferzetti until February 2024, replaced by Professor Roberto Veraldi. The Study Course's Exit Orientation and Placement section, in close synergy with the Course's Steering Committee, organizes events to facilitate meetings between students and the workplace, including organizing thematic seminars and interventions by local professionals, managing internships and stages within intra-EU mobility such as the Leonardo Project. Additionally, the Department proposes specific internal seminars within the Course, primarily within the 'Useful Knowledge for Entry into the Workplace' teaching, with sector experts.
Another initiative is the Social Work Day organized in partnership with the Professional Order of Social Assistants, whose date varies annually. The event, (https://class.unich.it/avviso-class-social-work-day-cds-in-servizio-sociale-6595), held on March 19, 2024 at the Pescara Campus of d'Annunzio University, saw over 200 participants including Students and Social Assistants, as well as Colleagues from the Course.
The effectiveness of these initiatives is monitored by the Commission through the following indicators for 2023: the percentage of employed graduates one year after graduation is 60% of respondents for 2022, and 80% of respondents three years later (source Anvur-Almalaurea). These figures correlate with positive feedback from students through annual quality forums and representatives in AQ bodies, highlighting strong satisfaction with placement initiatives.
Additionally, within the Department, various webinars were organized to guide students in understanding effective CV writing techniques, communication and employability skills, and other specific social area events. These seminars were held from March 2023 to May 2023.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI-PESCARA GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO

Student opinions The statistical data provided by the Quality Assurance Office of the University, based on 1,491 questionnaires for the academic year, regarding student opinions on courses taught by the Social Service Study Program, considering the particular circumstances experienced and the slow recovery, show results in line with previous years and, in any case, quite good. The satisfaction rating, measured on a scale from 1 to 4, averages 3.40 overall, which is a significant increase compared to the University's average of 3.31 and the Social Area average of 3.33. The score confirms a positive trend in the effectiveness of the training path, which has been maintained over the years and is generally higher than the University average. Considering the particular circumstances experienced by our Universities, this should be considered an excellent result.

Regarding teaching effectiveness, the course records a positive figure of 3.56, while the University average is 3.49 and the Social Area average is 3.52.

The data thus reveal rather positive student opinions:
- Regarding interest in the topics of the courses in the Social Service Degree Program, the rating shows a high score of 3.51, compared to a University base of 3.43 and a Social Area average of 3.44;
- As for preliminary knowledge, the data show that they were sufficient for understanding the topics covered in the exam program, with a score of 3.29;
- The study load required by the various courses is proportional to the assigned credits (3.40);
- Teaching materials (indicated and available) are adequate for studying the subject (3.50), while the Social Area average is 3.44 and the University average is 3.39;
- Regarding the delivery of courses, they were conducted consistently with what was declared on the Study Program's website (3.57);
- Class schedules for lectures, exercises, and other teaching activities are respected (3.59);
- Examination methods were clearly defined (3.54);
- Teachers stimulate/motivate interest in the discipline (3.52);
- Teachers present topics appropriately according to the complexity of the respective subjects (3.53);
- Teachers are available during lectures and/or office hours to clarify topics covered (3.64).

The data confirm an upward trend compared to the previous year and, in any case, a positive trend both in University performance and in Social Area courses.

Within the Study Program, the content of the Syllabus was also evaluated, which was the subject of specific meetings and discussions, and was discussed in various Study Program Councils.

Student opinions have always been communicated and discussed in the Degree Program Councils (e.g., Degree Program Council of September 14, 2021; Degree Program Council of September 13, 2022; and September 11, 2023).

Overall, student opinions tend to confirm the effectiveness of the training path.

NO CRITICITIES ARE EVIDENT THAT WOULD REQUIRE URGENT IMPROVEMENT ACTIONS, EVEN THOUGH CONTINUOUSLY PLANNING, THROUGH SPECIFIC DEPARTMENT COMMISSIONS, ACTIONS TO STRENGTHEN SERVICES BENEFITING STUDENTS.

The Degree Program, however, to manage any emerging criticalities, through the Course President, accepts student complaints via the following communication channel: presidenza.serviziosociale@unich.it

Opinions of graduates B7 GRADUATE OPINION The data used are derived from AlmaLaurea processing (updated to April 2023) regarding graduates' opinions in the 2022 calendar year, integrated with data provided by the University's Statistics Division.

98.4% are overall satisfied with the Study Program (98.6% the previous year; 89.8% University average), and of these, the majority (64.5%) are decidedly satisfied (41.3% University average).

Specifically, 98.6% consider the teaching load overall appropriate (100% the previous year; 88.7% University average), and 79% consider the examination organization overall satisfactory (76.3% the previous year; 79.8% University average). 93.6% appreciate the relationship with teachers overall (94.4% the previous year; 87% University average). 93.4% of respondents consider classrooms adequate (84.3% University average), 65.7% consider IT equipment adequate (56% University average), and 81% consider laboratories adequate (73% University average). Almost all respondents (97.8%) appreciated the library services overall (89.3% University average).

The majority of respondents (77.4%) would enroll in the same University for the first level (88.9% the previous year; 64.7% University average), expressing satisfaction with the training path.

The majority of respondents (74.3%) are satisfied with career orientation initiatives, with 28.6% decidedly satisfied and 45.7% more or less satisfied. In conclusion, given the trend, NO CRITICITIES ARE EVIDENT THAT WOULD REQUIRE URGENT IMPROVEMENT ACTIONS, EVEN THOUGH CONTINUOUSLY PLANNING, THROUGH SPECIFIC DEPARTMENT COMMISSIONS, ACTIONS TO STRENGTHEN SERVICES BENEFITING STUDENTS.

The data were discussed in the Degree Program Council of September 11, 2023.

The data provided by AlmaLaurea regarding graduates' opinions highlight, in the 2021 graduation year, qualifying aspects related to the effectiveness of the training path.

A large part of respondents declared overall satisfaction with the Study Program, indicating constant attention to students (98.6% of students, AlmaLaurea data).

Overall, the data collected from the surveyed group allow for a more than satisfactory evaluation (also compared to University data); this highlights a high level of satisfaction and effectiveness of the Study Program.

All respondents expressed a positive judgment regarding satisfaction with the Study Program followed, which is also evident from the table provided, indicating that the Study Program has excellent attractiveness motivated by positive judgments on the variables examined and should prompt reflection on possible future investments in terms of human capital for the sustainability of the Degree Program and the overall organization of services offered.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The training path provided allows for the acquisition of skills and knowledge applicable:
- in the realization of services and interventions in the social field;
- in the planning of interventions, including counseling and mediation;
- in the organization of interventions and services in the social field,
- in the methods of data collection and interpretation,
- in the methods of using evaluation systems.

The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is achieved through attendance at the planned training activities and through internship activities.

Verification of these abilities is carried out through oral and/or written tests. During exams and the final thesis, the ability to present, communicate, and critically argue thesis topics is also evaluated.

Learning skills (learning skills)
During the training path, graduates develop learning abilities through the processing of information acquired via activation of their interpretive schemes and reasoning in a plural paradigmatic way.

Graduates must have developed learning abilities that allow them to continue studying independently in their specific fields of interest.

Since social interventions, which constitute one of the main fields of interest for the Social Assistant, require not only already acquired knowledge but also the ability to analyze individual problems and construct an applicable intervention model in specific situations, Social Service graduates must be able to:
- seek necessary information to solve problems or uncertainties regarding professional practice, critically selecting sources;
- structure circular learning environments;
- study independently;
- learn in the work group;
- update theoretical knowledge through consultation and analysis of scientific publications, also using databases and retrieving information available on the internet, while critically examining them;
- achieve sufficient knowledge and methodological skills to continue the study and cultural growth path independently (Master's Degree, University Specialization Courses, University Master's Degrees).

Learning ability is evaluated through verification methods during training activities, integrating knowledge acquired during specific activities with those gained through personal study, evaluating the critical contribution demonstrated during the internship, as well as verifying the ability developed during the final project activity.

Knowledge and understanding (knowledge and understanding)
Graduates will achieve:
- professional knowledge of sociology and social service methodology;
- professional knowledge in legal, statistical, information, ethical, philosophical, psychological, historical disciplines;
- professional knowledge applied in interventions and services in the social field.

Teaching methods for achieving the expected results include lectures and internships.

Methods for verifying learning outcomes include:
- oral and/or written exams, scheduled during and/or at the end of courses;
- internship activities through presentation and discussion of periodic reports (direct and indirect internship) by students;
- final exam through discussion of a written report.

Organizational structure and responsibilities at University level
2024 -
The Quality Assurance Office plays a central role in promoting the culture of Quality and Quality Assurance (QA), ensuring compliance with the Quality Assurance Requirements set forth in Annex C of Ministerial Decree 30 January 2013, No. 47.

For the QA of Study Programs, in particular, it organizes and verifies the continuous updating of information contained in the SUA-CdS of each Study Program of the University; oversees the regular conduct of QA procedures for teaching activities in accordance with planned and declared procedures; regulates and verifies periodic Review activities for Study Programs; evaluates the effectiveness of improvement interventions and their actual consequences; ensures the correct information flow to and from the Evaluation Committee and the Parity Committees of teachers and students.

For the QA of departmental research, in particular, it verifies the continuous updating of information contained in the SUA-RD of each Department; oversees the regular conduct of QA procedures for research activities in accordance with planned and declared procedures; ensures the correct information flow to and from the Evaluation Committee.

The Quality Assurance Office is composed of the Rector's delegate for 'Quality', a full-time professor of the first rank who has opted for full-time work, responsible for overseeing the Office's activities, along with three full-time professors belonging to the following ERC (European Research Council) domains: Physical Sciences & Engineering; Social Sciences & Humanities; Life Sciences.

Link https://pqa.unich.it/pqa/struttura-organizzativa-e-responsabilita-livello-di-ateneo

Organization and responsibilities of QA at Study Program level
2024 -
D2   QA OF THE STUDY PROGRAM Responsible for ReAQD-D: Prof. Daniela Di Berardino The Department of Business Economics has established within it a system of bodies and committees involved in the Quality Assurance process of Study Programs and in managing the primary processes of the Study Programs affiliated with the Department.

This system is structured into bodies with specific competencies and responsibilities for QA, being involved in monitoring the primary processes connected to teaching. These bodies are listed below:

Course President   Prof. FRANCESCO FERZETTI Responsibility: coordinates the Study Program's QA system and oversees compliance with obligations set by specific regulations, with the collaboration of the Quality Assurance Committee/Group, the Parity Committee of Teachers and Students (CPDS), in accordance with what is indicated by the University's central bodies on QA and the guidelines of ANVUR. The President, with the collaboration of the QA Group, leads the cyclical and annual Review of the Study Program, drafting the Annual Monitoring Sheet (SMA) and the Cyclical Review Report (RRC), and proceeds with the insertion of the SUA-CdS, with the collaboration of the QA Group. According to annual deadlines, it handles teaching coverage and redefines the training path and objectives, based on periodic consultations with social partners. Finally, it is responsible for promoting a quality-oriented culture within the Study Program Council.

Quality Assurance Committee/Group and Review Group Members: the Course President, the Coordinator and QA Representative at the Department of Business Economics (Prof. Daniela Di Berardino), Department professors (Prof. Maria Teresa Giusti and Prof. Stefano Camillo Pasotti), a student representative, a technical-administrative staff representative (Cinzia Colangelo).

Responsibility: The QA and Review Group oversees the Study Program's quality management policy; specifically, the coordinator manages all quality activities and the specific committees established within the Department for monitoring the primary processes of the Study Program. The coordinator also maintains direct relations with the Quality Assurance Office and the Parity Committee of Teachers-Students. The Course President is constantly updated on the activities of the Department committees. The QA Group as a whole oversees compliance with the quality policy, regulations, and provisions, in line with the Quality Assurance Office's guidelines and ANVUR's lines, proceeding with periodic monitoring of indicators, analysis of criticalities, evaluation of possible improvement actions, convening active Department committees for information on requirements from AVA 3. The QA Group collaborates in drafting the SUA-CdS, SMA, and RRC.

Parity Committee of Teachers-Students Composition: the Committee Coordinator and Study Program professor (Prof. Antonio D'Andreamatteo), a Study Program professor, and a student representative.

Responsibility: The committee is responsible for monitoring the teaching offer, teaching quality, and contextual services provided to students by teachers and structures, with particular emphasis on criticalities, which are periodically communicated to the Course President, the Study Program Council, and the Department's Teaching QA Representative.

Study Program Council Composition: professors responsible for courses and representatives of enrolled students, elected according to the procedures set by the University's General Regulation.

Responsibility: the Council deliberates on the content of the SUA, the Annual Monitoring Sheet (SMA), and evaluates and deliberates on the related improvement proposals identified by the Course President and the QA Committee; periodically, it deliberates on the content of the Cyclical Review Report (RRC); collaborates in implementing the Study Program's quality improvement policies.

The quality policy in the Study Program is also exercised through decentralized activities within the committees activated in the Department as follows:
- Teaching Committee: members are professors responsible for the scientific areas represented in the training path; it is responsible for harmonizing teaching programs and evaluating the quality of the teaching offer, as well as verifying the completeness of syllabi inserted by teachers;
- Orientation Committee (divided into entry, in-course, exit, and placement): responsible for evaluating student opinions on tutoring initiatives, monitoring careers, welcoming and directing new students, monitoring the effectiveness of curricular internships and placement, planning and evaluating the effectiveness of services supporting entry into the job market;
- International Relations Committee: coordinate services for student mobility, provide support and orientation for Erasmus students;
- Relations with the Territory Committee, Steering Committee, and Course President: monitor employment effectiveness, consult social partners, redefine the teaching offer, activate agreements;
- Communication Committee: coordinate contextual services supporting students, update information documentation on the Study Program (student guide, Study Program functioning, e-learning platform, social networks, Department website), manage relations with media;
- Credit Recognition Committee: verify access and admission requirements to the Study Program. The teaching secretariat and the Department's internship office also collaborate in acquiring information.

Program of work and implementation deadlines for initiatives
2024 -
D3   PROGRAMMING OF ACTIVITIES
The Quality Assurance Committee meets periodically, according to the schedule summarized in the attached model, to carry out the following activities:
- Within the appropriate timeframes for inserting information into the SUA-CdS (February-April; July-September), for the SMA (October-December), and for the RRC (at least 3 months before internal deadlines), proceed with hearing the specific Department Committees regarding the implementation of QA within the Study Program;
- Within the appropriate timeframes for inserting information into the SUA-CdS (February-April; July-September), for the SMA (October-December), and for the RRC (at least 3 months before internal deadlines), proceed with analyzing and evaluating interventions aimed at continuous improvement of the Study Program in various organizational aspects, monitoring teaching indicators, with particular reference to student, graduate, and candidate opinions, contextual services, external effectiveness of the Study Program, Erasmus path, effectiveness of curricular internships, and results produced by the actions taken.
The reference indicators are drawn from the Department Strategic Plan (% students out of course contacted; % recovered out of course, enrolled, internationalization), from internal surveys by the Internship Office and the Orientation Committee (student opinions; opinions of organizations and companies; career monitoring, quality forum outcomes), and from processing provided by the University's Applied and Teaching Sector (enrollments, career monitoring, student opinions, employment).

- Within the appropriate timeframes for inserting information into the SUA-CdS (February-April; July-September), final collegial meetings for discussing frameworks and drafting the SUA;
- Between February and May, coordinate with the Course President to redefine specific training objectives of the Study Program, based on consultations with social partners, for defining the requirements necessary for teaching coverage and programming the teaching offer. Based on indications from the Evaluation Committee and the Teaching Delegate, the Department QA Representative will interact with the Course President before approving the teaching offer to allow timely verification regarding the Study Program's sustainability and the coherence of training objectives with the planned offer, also verifying the effectiveness of elective courses in the Study Program, with biennial checks;
- By the annual deadline set by the Quality Assurance Office (October-December), at least two meetings to analyze SMA indicators and evaluate causes and improvement proposals;
- Periodically, verify the correctness and proper insertion of syllabi, in concert with the Teaching Committee;
- Periodically, through the Coordinator of the Quality Assurance Committee/Group and Review and the Course President, promote a quality culture within the Study Program, both within Councils and through periodic communications to Department committees, and participate in training events related to Study Program quality requirements.

Improvement initiatives emerging from periodic meetings are periodically highlighted in the Study Program Council to plan improvement actions, as evidenced by the minutes of the Study Program Council meetings.

The Quality Assurance Committee meets periodically, according to the schedule summarized in the attached model, to carry out the following activities:
- Within the appropriate timeframes for inserting information into the SUA-CdS (February-April; July-September), for the SMA (October-December), and for the RRC (at least 3 months before internal deadlines), proceed with hearing the specific Department Committees (orientation and placement, teaching, international relations, relations with the territory, communication, credit recognition) regarding the implementation of QA within the Study Program;
- Within the appropriate timeframes for inserting information into the SUA-CdS (February-April; July-September), for the SMA (October-December), and for the RRC (at least 3 months before internal deadlines), proceed with analyzing and evaluating interventions aimed at continuous improvement of the Study Program in various organizational aspects, monitoring teaching indicators, with particular reference to student, graduate, and candidate opinions, contextual services, external effectiveness of the Study Program, Erasmus path, effectiveness of curricular internships, and results produced by the actions taken. The reference indicators are drawn from the Department Strategic Plan (% students out of course contacted; % recovered out of course, enrolled, internationalization), from internal surveys by the Internship Office and the Orientation Committee (student opinions; opinions of organizations and companies; career monitoring, quality forum outcomes), and from processing provided by the University's Applied and Teaching Sector (enrollments, career monitoring, student opinions, employment).

- Within the appropriate timeframes for inserting information into the SUA-CdS (February-April; July-September), final collegial meetings for discussing frameworks and drafting the SUA;
- Between February and May, coordinate with the Course President to redefine specific training objectives of the Study Program, based on consultations with social partners, for defining the requirements necessary for teaching coverage and programming the teaching offer. Based on indications from the Evaluation Committee and the Teaching Delegate, the Department QA Representative will interact with the Course President before approving the teaching offer to allow timely verification regarding the Study Program's sustainability and the coherence of training objectives with the planned offer, also verifying the effectiveness of elective courses in the Study Program, with biennial checks;
- By the annual deadline set by the Quality Assurance Office (October-December), at least two meetings to analyze SMA indicators and evaluate causes and improvement proposals;
- Periodically, verify the correctness and proper insertion of syllabi, in concert with the Teaching Committee;
- Periodically, through the Coordinator of the Quality Assurance Committee/Group and Review and the Course President, promote a quality culture within the Study Program, both within Councils and through periodic communications to Department committees, and participate in training events related to Study Program quality requirements.

The Quality Assurance Committee concludes the work at 17:45.

Prof. Roberto Veraldi Meeting of February 7, 2023

The Consultation Committee of organizations representing service production and professions for verifying competencies, employment, and professional opportunities of graduates of the Study Program in Social Service (L-39) met on February 7, 2023, at 15:00 in Room 4 of the Viale Pindaro Teaching Complex of the University of Chieti.

The committee was attended by some social assistants representing organizations. In addition to the Presidents of the Social Service Degree Program, Prof. Roberto Veraldi, and the Master's Degree Program in Policies and Management for Welfare, Prof. Francesco Ferzetti, were present Dr. Giuseppe Viani, a social assistant invited, Prof. Vincenzo Corsi, Prof. Sabrina Speranza, Prof. Luana Di Profio, and student representative Vittoria Rosato, who requested justification for the absence of the other two colleagues Julia Durantini and Lucia Di Felice. The Regional President of the Social Assistants' Order of Abruzzo, Dr. Amalia Di Santo, requested to be considered absent with justification due to unavoidable institutional activities with the entire Order Council. The Student Representative of the Master's Degree in PMW was absent with justification.

The teaching offer for the 2023-2024 academic year was first presented to the Consultation Committee members, noting that the courses provided are consistent in terms of competencies acquired by students and employment and professional opportunities for graduates.

Regarding this, reference is also made to recent AlmaLaurea data, according to which graduates express very positive opinions regarding the training path followed. All present members of the Consultation Committee agree on the excellent employment results and professional opportunities for Social Service graduates, on the validity of the training path, and on the competencies transmitted in the disciplines specified in the study plan.

It is also observed from various parts that in the job market, the demand for Social Assistant professional figures is increasingly high, although not always adequately remunerated. It is nonetheless a growing professional reality. Social Service graduates employed use the professional competencies acquired during the training path to a high degree, confirming the coherence between the Study Program's teaching offer and the professional job market demand. The Committee members agree with this interpretation and do not report criticalities.

The importance of precise knowledge of the Deontological Code, serious application in the internship, and consistency in applying work methods that the Social Assistant must always have in mind when carrying out professional activities is also emphasized. Code, internships, and methods are widely covered in the courses taught in the Study Program. Equally important is the knowledge of foreign languages and intercultural knowledge, offered in the Study Program in terms of English and French, as well as demo-ethno-linguistic-anthropological disciplines, economic and social policy, relational techniques, and European legislation and services for persons, and given the pervasiveness of the internet, knowledge of the digital society.

The Consultation Committee finally notes that there is full coherence between the teaching offer, competencies acquired by students, and employment and professional opportunities for Social Service graduates.

The meeting of the Social Service Degree Program Consultation Committee ends at 15:30.

Entry, Path, and Exit Data C1
Entry The data acquired on August 28, 2023, at the Statistics Section provided by the University's Quality Assurance Office show a decline in enrollments for the Study Program, decreasing from 141 units in the 2020/21 academic year to 119 in the 2021/22 academic year and 102 in 2022/23. The Sicas System also shows 4 entry transfers and 1 incoming transfer, 2 outgoing transfers, and 6 withdrawals. The total number of enrolled students corresponds to 386 units, of which 67% are in course.

The percentage of incoming students from the Abruzzo region increases significantly, rising from 67% of the previous academic year to 81%, reducing the attractiveness of students from outside the region, particularly from Southern regions.

35% of new students have obtained a diploma from technical and professional institutes, followed by high school graduates (27%) and magistral graduates (25%). However, the percentage of new students who obtained a diploma with a grade of 80 or lower increases (63%), followed by the 80-99 range (30%). The attraction of graduates with a grade of 100 or higher remains negligible (7%). This data requires reflection on the knowledge possessed by new students at entry.

PATH The data provided by the Quality Assurance Office and integrated with those from the SICAS system, updated to June 2023, refer to students in the 2021/22 cohort.

50% of students in the cohort are women, and 50% are 19 years old or younger. However, a good incidence of students aged 20-22 years (23%) and over 25 years (19%) is also noted.

The renewal rate for the second year increases from 59.8% to 70%, and of these, 24% have earned more than 40 CFU, 15% have earned no CFU, and 32% are inactive, exactly in line with the previous cohort's trend.

On average, students in the cohort take 4 exams, achieving an average grade of 28, and the percentage of students earning the required CFU increases from 42% to 44%. Approximately 40% of students in the cohort earn 21-40 CFU per year. This data highlights an improvement in career regularity and learning quality. However, the number of dropouts remains significant and merits reflection by the Study Program Council. Specifically, of the students enrolled in 2019/20, 57 students dropped out of the Study Program without renewing their enrollment, but the number rises to 96 for students enrolled in 2020/21 and slightly decreases to 85 for students enrolled in 2021/22. The economic crisis following the pandemic's impact on continuing studies should also be considered.

EXIT The graduates in the 2022 calendar year number 66, of which 48% are in course, a value in contraction compared to the 64% of the previous calendar year. Of these, 26% achieved a grade of 110 or higher, but 53% fall into the grade range below 105.

These data, although partial, have been subject to analysis and evaluation by the Study Program Council on September 13, 2022, and discussed in the Council held on September 11, 2023.

Entry The data acquired in August 2022 at the Statistics Section provided by the University's Quality Assurance Office show a slight decline in enrollments for the Study Program, decreasing from 141 units in the 2020/21 academic year to 119 in the 2021/22 academic year. The total number of enrolled students rises to 427 units, of which 70% are in course. 67.5% of new students come from the Abruzzo region, while the attractiveness of students from outside the region decreases slightly to 32% compared to 37% in 2020/21. This polarization is confirmed, primarily related to the regional user base and Southern regions, with no foreign students. New students mainly come from magistral institutes and similar (42%), followed by high schools (29%) and technical institutes (26%), confirming the historical trend.

52.9% of new students obtained a diploma grade of 80 or lower, while only 8% achieved the maximum diploma grade. This data requires reflection on the knowledge possessed by new students at entry.

PATH Extracurricular The data provided by the Quality Assurance Office and integrated with those from the SICAS system and the monitoring of profit exams as of August 2022, highlight for the 2020/21 cohort that 59.8% of enrolled students continue to the second year, and of these, 24% have earned more than 40 CFU, 29.5% have earned 21-40 CFU, 30% have earned 6-20 CFU, and 15% have earned no CFU. For this cohort, 42% of the required CFU have been earned by enrolled students. These data indicate a deterioration compared to the 2019/20 cohort, which had a second-year continuation rate of 79%, with a higher incidence of those who earned more than 40 CFU (41%). Regarding the trend of completed cohorts, for the most recent observable cohort, there was 1 outgoing transfer, 3 transfers from other Social Area courses, and 3 explicit withdrawals, data in contraction compared to the past. However, the number of dropouts remains significant and merits reflection by the Study Program Council. Specifically, of the students enrolled in 2019/20, 57 students dropped out of the Study Program without renewing their enrollment, but the number rises to 96 for students enrolled in 2020/21. The pandemic's impact on continuing studies, including the economic impact of the subsequent crisis, should also be considered. The average number of exams taken is about 4, with 40% of CFU earned compared to the required. The SICAS system notes some inconsistencies due to the longer observation period: for the 2019 cohort, the percentage of earned CFU compared to expected is 69%, while for 2020 it rises to 76%.

EXIT The data of graduates in the 2021 calendar year rise to 96 students, of which 64% graduated in course, a value in significant increase compared to 2020 (42%) and 13% in the first year out of course. Of these, 19% received the honor declaration, 35% achieved a graduation grade between 110-105, and the remainder achieved a grade below 105.

These data, although partial, have been subject to analysis and evaluation by the Study Program Council, as evidenced by, for example, the minutes of September 14, 2021. For 2022, the reference minutes are from the Council held on September 13, 2022.

Characteristics of the final exam The final thesis requires the presentation of a written report of a maximum of 50 pages (approximately 1,500 words per page), also in digital form, personally prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor. The report must concern a research on the literature related to the chosen topic, with possible case analysis and/or an intervention project.

Final exam procedure The degree is awarded upon passing a final thesis exam, which is assigned 6 CFU.

The final thesis requires the presentation of a written report of a maximum of 50 pages (approximately 1,500 words per page), also in digital form, personally prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervisor. The report must concern a research on the literature related to the chosen topic, with possible case analysis and/or an intervention project.

After passing all exam tests of the training path and earning all required credits, the student will proceed to the final thesis exam, discussing in front of the Committee a written report, consisting of a critical review of the literature or a field research of a project or analytical type, in one of the disciplines present in the path followed and characteristic of the chosen study direction.

The final thesis and the presentation of the respective report can be carried out in a foreign language upon favorable and motivated opinion of the Study Program Council, ensuring the possibility of effective evaluation due to sufficient competencies within the teaching body. In any case, the report written in a foreign language must be accompanied by an adequate summary in Italian.

The graduation exam is public and takes place according to a predetermined program, with each candidate having an average exam duration not exceeding twenty minutes, of which part is dedicated to presentation and part to discussion.

For the evaluation of the final exam, the student's academic record is taken into account, using the average as a base to which additional points may be added, up to a maximum of 7 points.

The score variation from minimum to maximum will also consider qualitative variables that will be evaluated case by case by the Committee.

Candidates are evaluated with a grade expressed in hundredths, taking into account the overall academic performance, with possible unanimous mention of the honor; the minimum score to pass the final exam is 66/110.

The Committees for evaluating final exams are appointed by the Department Director. The judging Committees consist of at least five and no more than seven members, including the president.

Admission Procedures
1. The required entry knowledge is identified and described in the Study Course Regulations and publicized during the entrance orientation activities conducted by the CdS (see Section B5 of the SUA CdS) and in a dedicated section of the CdS website: https://scuolaeconomia.unich.it/index.php?gruppo=1270.
2. To facilitate the verification of the required entry knowledge, the CdS has implemented an self-assessment system: interested students may take a verification test by answering questions from previous years' entrance tests, published in a dedicated section of the CdS website: https://scuolaeconomia.unich.it/index.php?gruppo=1270. The online verification system, prepared by GAQ, will provide students not only with the total score achieved but also specific indications regarding the areas (logic, foreign language, text comprehension, or general culture) where difficulties may arise.
3. The possession of essential initial knowledge is verified through the administration of an entrance test (PDF attachment).
The entrance test for verifying students' knowledge - prepared by a committee composed of CdS teachers - is divided into 4 parts, totaling 31 questions. The first part, concerning the understanding of a legal text, requires answering 6 questions; the second part involves answering 10 questions on contemporary history and contemporary law; the third consists of 10 questions on linguistic logic, while the fourth includes 5 questions on English language.
Failure to complete the entrance test or obtaining a score below the annual threshold set by the CdS Council will result in the assignment of OFA (Additional Educational Obligations), which the student will fulfill by attending an 8-hour introductory course on the study of legal and economic sciences, logic, and legal argumentation, with dates, methods, and content to be determined by the CdS.
For 2023:
- 19 April (16:00-18:00)
prof. Pietro Masala 'Introduction to Constitutional Law' (online lecture)
- 27 April (11:00-13:00)
prof. Francesco Montanari 'Law and Economics' (online lecture)
- 4 May (11:00-13:00)
prof. Francesco Montanari 'Further on Law and Economics' (online lecture)
- 11 May (11:00-13:00)
prof. Vincenzo Acciaro 'Introduction to Computer Science' (online lecture)
OFA will also be considered fulfilled by passing a minimum of 18 CFU related to courses in the first year of the study plan, within basic and characteristic subjects — by October 31 of the calendar year following the enrollment year, for full-time students, and by October 31 of the second year following enrollment, for part-time students.
In case of failure to fulfill OFA within the specified deadlines, students will not be able to earn exams from the second and third years unless they have passed the required 18 CFU.
Students take the entrance test in a computerized manner at the beginning of the first semester. For the 2023-2024 academic year, 86 students participated in the test conducted in the computer lab on November 10, 2023.
4. The results of the entrance tests are communicated individually to participants by the same computerized system at the end of the test. The academic manager and CdS teachers, who assist participants during the test, provide immediate clarifications regarding identified deficiencies and the support activities organized by the CdS (Entrance Orientation and In-Process Orientation and Tutoring - as per relevant Sections B5 SUA - and OFA Recovery Course). The test results are processed in aggregated and anonymous form by GAQ (as per PDF attachment).
Out of a total of 31 questions, the minimum number of correct answers was 18 (58% of questions) and the maximum was 30 (97% of questions).
Thus, all students who participated in the test provided a number of correct answers exceeding the 50% threshold.
5. Organization of the OFA Recovery Course Following the results of the entrance tests and the verification conducted at the Student Secretariat, the CdS decided (Council resolution of February 17, 2023) to organize an 8-hour introductory course on the study of legal and economic sciences, logic, and legal argumentation for OFA recovery (Additional Educational Obligations). The recovery course will be taught by professors Montanari, Acciaro, and Masala and will conclude with a verification interview. Interested students will be contacted individually by academic tutors (via email) to inform them of the start of the recovery course and invite them to participate. The schedule of the recovery course will also be published on the bulletin board and the CdS website: https://scuolaeconomia.unich.it/index.php?gruppo=1270:
Interested parties will be reminded that OFA will also be considered fulfilled by passing a minimum of 18 CFU related to courses in the first year of the study plan, within basic and characteristic subjects, by October 31 of the calendar year following the enrollment year, for full-time students, and by October 31 of the second year following enrollment, for part-time students.
6. OFA Lectures 2024
Verification was also conducted at the Student Secretariat regarding first-year enrollees who should have taken but did not take the 2023 entrance test. Twelve students were identified who must fulfill OFA according to the terms, methods, and content set by the CdS. The OFA fulfillment course will take place in April-May 2024. (See Council resolution SeGi 21 February 2024).

Program, texts and objectives Communication skills
The graduate
• knows and is able to use the main communication techniques, in order to fully and effectively present the legal and administrative-management issues to be examined;
• is able to effectively use, in written and oral form, the legal language of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian.
Communication and relational skills are developed, in particular, during participation in seminars, exercises and group work, organized to stimulate discussion among students, mainly dedicated to the presentation and discussion of legal and administrative-management issues and to the elaboration of the most appropriate operational solutions. The acquisition of the aforementioned communication skills also occurs during the internship and through the activities carried out by the student for the preparation and discussion of the final exam.
Knowledge of at least one European Union language, with particular attention to legal language, is imparted through specific training activities and its acquisition is verified through the relevant suitability tests.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [639L] LEGAL SERVICES FOR BUSINESS
TYPE:
CURRICULUM:
SECTION: Autonomy of judgment
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/569

Autonomy of judgment (making judgements)
The graduate
• is able to use acquired knowledge, experiences and available data to provide the most appropriate legal and organizational-management solutions for the specific contexts in which they are called to operate: administrations, businesses, third sector organizations and international organizations;
• is able to guide the choice of appropriate contractual types for different subjective and objective situations, suggesting the necessary obligations;
• is able to promote the extrajudicial resolution of business disputes: mediations, conciliations and arbitrations.
Autonomy of judgment is developed, in particular, through guided discussion of practical application cases and research, and through the conduct of exercises and seminars organized to allow active student participation, with students called upon to express their viewpoint; as well as during internship and traineeship activities and through the work carried out for the preparation of the final exam.
In the aforementioned activities, the acquired autonomy of judgment is verified through the assessment of the degree of autonomy and critical abilities demonstrated in the use of analytical tools, in the selection of reference theoretical frameworks and in the proposed operational solutions, as well as through the appreciation of participation in group work, which allows for student comparison.

Ongoing orientation and tutoring The ongoing orientation and tutoring activity is implemented through:
1. Support tutoring carried out by all faculty members of the degree program, typically during office hours, aimed at assisting students in resolving their issues (e.g., organizing meetings or short recovery courses for groups of students in difficulty, suggestions regarding study methods, clarifications on program content and exam topics);
2. Identification of ongoing faculty tutors: Prof. Puoti, Nepa, and De Santis, and the Dean of the degree program, Prof. Serpe, to whom students can turn for personalized tutoring services (e.g., advice on selecting elective exams, guidance on career path options, stage selection, requests and proposals for professional seminars);
3. Identification of the academic manager (Dr. Morelli) - Office hours MONDAY and TUESDAY from 9:00 to 11:00 – activities: study plan assistance; reconstruction of the curriculum path in relation to the absence or containment of academic debts; coordination with master's degree courses at UdA or affiliated; application of the agreement with the Labor Consultants Order; information on the University's placement service, etc.;
4. Activation of tutoring service entrusted to doctoral students and master's degree students GIURINN, respectively, Dr. Filippo Matrisciano (June-December 2023), and students Gaia D'Averio (June-October 2023) and Raffaele Spina (June-October 2023) carried out their orientation and assistance activities for a total of 300 hours in the 2022/2023 academic year.
5. The degree program relies on disability services provided by the University, the Orientation, Tutoring, and Study Rights for Students with Disabilities Sector (interim Sector Head: Dr. Marco Costantini/email: servizio.disabilitaedsa@unich.it).
For the submission of a request for disability services (disability/DSA-BES), please refer to the following link:
https://orientamento.unich.it/servizi-gli-studenti/disabilita-e-dsa The request can be completed by the student and sent to the Study Rights and Disabilities Sector at email: servizio.disabilitaedsa@unich.it using the institutional email (name.surname@studentiunich.it).
The Sector will process the requests as soon as possible. During the first meeting, the available supports will be shared in relation to the diagnosis, educational needs, and individual characteristics of each student.
After the student submits the request and the Sector approves it, assignment to the CON_TE_STO Service proceeds:
- if the student is assigned to disability/invalidity services, the contact is: disabilita.contesto@unich.it
- if the student is assigned to DSA/BES services, the contact is:
dsa.contesto@unich.it
(telephone: 0871 3556009 (Fridays from 10:00 to 12:00).
6. For the 2023/2024 academic year, the degree program has established, to counter and resolve the student dropout rate—as highlighted by the analysis of student career data conducted by the Quality Assurance Group, particularly noted in the transition from the first to the second year—to intervene as follows:
a) Analyze student productivity data provided by the University via the 'Student Career Monitoring' platform, accessible at https://ingrid.unich.it, to identify students with significant delays in achieving the required CFU and exams where they face greater difficulties;
b) Identify, for every 10 first-year students, a reference tutor among the faculty members of the degree program whose task is to constantly monitor (through in-person meetings; email exchanges; online discussions) the progress of their academic path. This action has been regularly carried out by the designated faculty members.
During 2023, for students in difficulty, the Quality Assurance Group (GAQ) planned, with the support of faculty, student tutors, and administrative staff, the following countermeasures:
x. Widespread dissemination (website and degree program bulletin board, in-class information) to all students regarding the ongoing tutoring activities carried out by academic tutors-doctoral students and faculty members (for the first year: Prof. Serpe and Gambini and De Lucia; for subsequent years: Prof. Puoti, De Santis, and Nepa) – and by the academic manager (Dr. Morelli);
xi. Ongoing tutoring service provided by the academic office and designated faculty members, and support tutoring carried out by all first-year faculty members of the degree program;
xii. The tutoring service will be enhanced with the support of two new disciplinary tutors for Private Law and Political Economy courses (Call for selection for student collaborations with University services for peer tutoring in the 2023/2024 academic year), whose task will be to guide students in difficulty during exam preparation;
xiii. Among the initiatives undertaken, it is particularly noted that:
- extraordinary exam sessions were scheduled in October, March, and April windows;
- for most courses in SEGI, intermediate and/or partial assessments are planned, allowing students to organize their study and final assessments according to their specific needs;
- Based on productivity data for students in difficulty (44 for the first semester/2022-2023), collective meetings were held with students in difficulty to follow up and identify the reasons behind difficulties in passing exams, then offering them greater study support. Subsequently, students in difficulty (13 for the second semester/2023) were contacted by phone to invite them to individual meetings (as per the attached schedule). Drs. de Lucia and Nepa specifically managed this initiative.
Information on the initiatives is available on the degree program website: https://scuolaeconomia.unich.it/index.php?gruppo=1270 and on the social media channels (Facebook and Instagram) of the degree program.
