Orientation and ongoing tutoring B5-ORIENTATION IN ITINERE APRIL 2024
The CdS, through a Specialization Course (CP) established ad hoc, has trained and continues to train nursing tutors with pedagogical skills. The tutor's role is to accompany the student throughout their training path and guide them in the best acquisition of professional competencies across various nursing areas. The characteristic training activity takes place under agreements activated with Entities and Structures of the SSN and private organizations at the local and national level. This is also aimed at offering preferred paths for professional choices applicable in the workplace. Additionally, ongoing orientation is expressed through multiple delivery methods: all teachers fulfill this role during their office hours, while, as previously mentioned, specific reference figures (nursing tutors) have been trained for students to approach in case of need. The names of the nursing tutors are listed in the Administration section, 'Information'.
The nursing tutors, in turn, relay emerging issues to the Teaching Directors, who are the reference figures for characteristic activities: Dr. Daniela Daniele (Chieti teaching pole), Dr. Paola Mosca (Pescara teaching pole), Dr. Luciana Potalivo (Vasto teaching pole).
The Nursing CdS has promoted the activation of a CP in Clinical Tutor for all graduates in Health Professions. Indeed, in February 2019, with Decree R. 183/2019, the admission call for the CP in 'Clinical Tutor for Health Professions' A.Y. 2018/2019 was published. The Course aims to train professionals capable of supporting and guiding students in the degree courses of Health Professions. The Specialization Course's objective is to: develop the pedagogical approach and learn tutorial methods applicable during the internship.
The Course responds to the Dublin Descriptors, fostering the connection between the University and Health Companies. The trained professional figures can find opportunities in Training Operative Units, company training paths, Assistive Operative Units, and within Health Professions Degree Courses.
The CdS, through the Teaching Director of the Chieti teaching pole, Dr. Daniela Daniele, and the nursing tutor, Dr. Antonio Di Paolo, has published the CP via posters on the official website of:
- ASL LANCIANO-VASTO-CHIETI,
- AUSL PESCARA
- OPI PESCARA
- OPI CHIETI. Fifty-two applications were received, 22 beyond the maximum allowed number, demonstrating the CP's attractiveness.
DESCRIPTION OF THE TUTORING SYSTEM Clinical contexts require students, at the end of their three-year degree program, to possess competencies for effectively managing care complexity. Therefore, in the training context, students must be guaranteed the opportunity to experiment with managing dynamic and unpredictable situations. The tutoring system is designed to guide and support students throughout their training path, based on a fundamental principle:
IF THE STUDENT HEARS, HE FORGETS; IF HE SEES, HE REMEMBERS; IF HE DOES, HE UNDERSTANDS.
Simulation is a strategy that allows reproducing real and complex situations, requiring students to immerse themselves acting 'as they are' in risk-free scenarios for both patient and operator. Mechanical manikins are used for training exercises, enabling skill development. In response to simulation, students demonstrate:
- Applying systematic evaluation learned in lectures
- Acting with critical thinking and decision-making skills
- Implementing technical-management interventions
- Coordinating with other operators
- Managing emotions arising from the situation.
In 3-hour laboratories, a group of 10 students simulates a clinical scenario. The scenario reproduces a ward room where the manikin is the patient, two students are nurses, and the laboratory tutor, through care requests, adds realistic aspects to the simulation; the remaining students act as observers. In relation to parameter modifications or descriptions, students are called to collect data, assign meaning, and interact in a coordinated manner to choose and implement interventions. At the end of the simulation, the tutor guides reflection on the concluded experience. The laboratory demonstrates a multidimensional learning opportunity as it allows students to experiment with technical/operational learning while simultaneously developing the dimension of simulated clinical evolution (by the manikin) and the management/emotional dimension (simulated by the tutor/actor). The combination of elements (manikin, tutor, and students) is the most appreciated aspect by students, as the simultaneous experience of technical/management activities, management/organizational aspects, and the tutor's ability to foster total engagement place the student in a realistic, challenging situation to test how tensions and emotions in specific contexts may affect the outcome of care gestures and decisions.
CLINICAL INTERNSHIP The tutoring activity for students is a continuous path defined by internship sites and concludes when the student achieves the predetermined objectives. Student assignment to the internship site is the responsibility of the Teaching Director of the CdS in collaboration with the tutors and is communicated via email to the interested parties within one week before the start of each clinical internship period. Clinical internship programming and assignments are formulated based on the progression of theoretical content, the training objectives set by the curriculum, and differentiated by academic year.
In the first year of the course, students complete internships only in specific Operative Units (Medicine, Surgery, Residential Care Structures, Territorial Services), where, respecting the theoretical concepts learned in the classroom and with specific learning objectives, they acquire indispensable technical and relational competencies in nursing. Additionally, through this path, students begin to orient themselves within the complex healthcare organization context.
First-Year Students - First Placement The internship placement is contingent upon participation in preparatory activities: laboratories, exercises, and training interventions related to risk prevention and safety in internship sites.
A few days before the clinical internship begins, a meeting is held with students to illustrate documents accompanying them during the internship. Specifically, the following are presented and discussed:
- Behavioral norms to adopt during the clinical internship, including in case of injury
- Logbook for certification of internship attendance.
Following the student meeting, a further meeting is organized per Hospital Pole, in coordination between the CdS Chair and the Health and Nursing Direction, where, in the presence of students, tutors, and coordinators, additional information on the clinical internship's execution, organization, hospital organizational chart, and its representatives is provided.
Second and Third-Year Students From the second year of the course, students, leveraging a broader knowledge base and experience, are progressively assigned to other Operative Units: Cardiology, Dialysis, Day Hospital, Operating Room, Oncology Day Hospital, Digestive Endoscopy, and Maternity-Infant Area. In response to specific situations or learning needs identified during formative evaluations, the Teaching Director may consider personalizing clinical internship paths to facilitate achieving the set objectives and performance levels.
The curriculum includes theoretical training in Critical Area and Psychiatric Area during the third year, after which students are assigned to DSM Services and Reanimation, Intensive Therapy, and Emergency Department Operative Units and the 118 service.
Before the end of their training path and during the second or third year, each student is guaranteed the opportunity to repeat the internship in the basic Operative Units visited in the first year (Medicine and/or Surgery). The second placement in these Operative Units allows students, based on greater experience and acquired knowledge, to practice care planning for medical or surgical clinical cases and collaborate in executing complex techniques.
At the end of each internship period, students are invited to attend a meeting with the reference tutor for an open discussion on the experience, encountered issues, clarifications, and/or proposals.
If the performed path and achieved learning are unsatisfactory, the student is offered to integrate deficient phases and repeat the field experience.
INJURY DURING INTERNSHIP The student is insured by 'G. d'Annunzio' University of Chieti-Pescara for injuries.
The insurance policy covers students during their stay at internship sites for the period scheduled by the CdS.
In case of injury due to traumatic causes or infection risk, the student must follow the Hospital Company's procedure.
In all cases, the student must go to the Emergency Department of the internship site, after notifying the Nursing Coordinator of the assigned Operative Unit and the reference tutor; the Emergency Department prepares a triplicate report, one copy of which is delivered by the hospital to INAIL, and the remaining two copies are given to the student.
The Teaching Director certifies the sequence of events and delivers the report and the event certification to the student.
The student keeps a copy for themselves, delivers one copy to their Laboratory Tutor, who retains it in the student's personal file, and finally, it is the student's responsibility to submit all original documentation to the Competent Offices of the University. To verify the satisfaction level of tutoring and internship activities, the CdS has, for several years, prepared a customer satisfaction questionnaire completed by graduating students before the practical licensing exam. Responses to the questionnaire questions have been analyzed and presented in graphs (SEE ATTACHMENT SATISFACTION LEVEL OF GRADUATING STUDENTS).
On May 15, 2020, after multiple online meetings via Skype with the Teaching Directors of the three poles and Dr. Iannone, aimed at evaluating suitable methods for conducting professional training laboratories and internships during the COVID-19 health emergency, the CdS Chair published the following document:
NURSING CdS GUIDELINES FOR RESUMING PROFESSIONAL TRAINING INTERNSHIP AND LABORATORY ACTIVITIES Given the health emergency related to COVID-19, to resume the professional internship and laboratory activities as soon as possible, a new programming is necessary to ensure the continuation of all students' training paths.
Specifically, in line with the recommendations of the Ministry of University and Research Decrees No. 12 of April 9, 2020 and No. 58 of April 29, 2020, and the Guidelines of the Permanent Conference of Health Professions Degree Classes, while respecting the University's regulations, the CdS has temporarily organized an 'alternative' method for conducting internships and laboratories. Specifically:
- FIRST YEAR: While frequencies to ADOs (which were to be completed in the second semester) have already been recognized, from June onward until in-person activities can resume, sessions on the TEAMS platform will be organized for some of these activities, with participation considered as 'distance internship': 8 hours of internship per activity.
Additionally, synchronous and interactive sessions on the TEAMS platform will be held, where designated tutors will ensure the achievement of training objectives using the following tools:
  briefing, debriefing;
  discussion of clinical cases and ethical issues;
  resolution of exercises/problems with guidance/supervision.
For these activities, if the clinical case discussion, in the presence of the tutor and Teaching Director, receives a positive evaluation, 20 hours of internship will be recognized.
Finally, the laboratory will continue and be completed, with attendance recognized only for 100% participation. The scheduled calendar will be modified.
- SECOND YEAR: While frequencies to ADOs and seminars (which were to be completed in the second semester) have already been recognized, from June onward until in-person activities can resume, sessions on the TEAMS platform will be organized for some of these activities, with participation considered as 'distance internship': 6 hours for ADOs and 8 hours for seminars.
Internship meetings will be conducted via dedicated TEAMS sessions, with the following methods:
  briefing and debriefing sessions
  development of clinical cases, which, after student elaboration, will be discussed on the platform in the presence of the tutor and Teaching Director.
A positive evaluation of the clinical case by the tutor and Teaching Director will result in 40 hours of internship.
Finally, the laboratory will continue and be completed, with attendance recognized only for 100% participation. The scheduled calendar will be modified.
- THIRD YEAR: While frequencies to seminars (which were to be completed in the second semester) have already been recognized, from June onward until in-person activities can resume, sessions on the TEAMS platform will be organized for some of these activities, with participation considered as 'distance internship': 8 hours of internship.
For internships, TEAMS sessions will be scheduled, including:
  discussion of clinical cases
  briefing, debriefing sessions
  critical analysis of scientific literature
  discussion of ethical issues For internships conducted online, 40 hours of internship will be allocated only if the tutor and Teaching Director provide a positive evaluation.
Finally, the laboratory will continue and be completed, with attendance recognized only for 100% participation. The scheduled calendar will be modified.
- OUT OF COURSE: Students are required to participate in the activities as scheduled to reduce training debt.
Activities will be planned and communicated shortly by the Teaching Directors of the three teaching poles to the respective student representatives, clarifying doubts and providing further details.
For participation in FAD Courses organized by ISS and made available to students, 20 hours of internship are recognized (recognition is contingent upon submission of the participation certificate).
For any volunteering activities performed in support of healthcare structures (Ministry of University and Research Decree No. 12 of April 9, 2020), 4 hours of internship are recognized per day of presence.
Finally, all students are reminded that to enroll in the internship exam, in addition to completing all hours, verification and declaration by the tutor, followed by the Teaching Director's declaration, are indispensable.
A student's inability, for any reason, to submit the internship logbook to the tutor will prevent them from taking the exam.
If a student loses their internship logbook, it is essential to file a loss report with the competent authorities and immediately inform the tutor and Teaching Director.

These data, however, must be monitored in subsequent analyses. Additionally, it is noted that the percentage of students who acquired at least 40 CFU exceeds the geographical area values and the average of non-online universities. In this regard, the training activity for teaching staff on learning processes and innovation of teaching methodologies, which the CdS has planned and implemented through two seminars/webinars by Prof. Nardi on September 29 and October 22, 2021, followed by six teaching laboratories (three dedicated to MODULE 1   CONDUCTING THE LESSON in May 2022 and three to MODULE 2   VERIFYING AND VALUING LEARNING in June and July 2022), is highly appropriate.
The CdS consistently promotes orientation and tutoring activities aimed at enhancing dialogue with students to achieve greater regularity and performance. In this context, the Chair requested grants for peer tutoring activities from the Prevalent Department (DMSI). Peer tutoring activities refer to activities aimed at guiding and assisting students throughout their studies, as provided for in Article 13 of Law 341/1990; the public selection is open to capable and meritorious students of the University of Chieti-Pescara, enrolled in the first and second year of the Master's Degree Course in Nursing and Midwifery, for the purpose of carrying out activities for students enrolled in the Nursing Degree Course. Eight students from the Master's Degree Course in Nursing and Midwifery responded to the notice. The committee responsible for evaluating requirements and qualifications sent the merit ranking to DMSI. Tutors will be assigned students experiencing difficulties in their study path.
The CdS utilizes, based on the Ateneo Quality Office's recommendations, in collaboration with the Information Systems Unit U-Gov Didattica e Ricerca, the dynamic dashboard named UdA in Numeri accessible at https://ingrid.unich.it to monitor student careers and evaluate the percentage of students with struggling careers.

Assistance for Training Periods B5-ASSISTANCE FOR THE EXECUTION OF TRAINING PERIODS ABROAD (INTERNSHIPS AND PLACEMENTS) ACADEMIC YEAR 2023-2024
The execution of external training periods (internships and placements) concerns both in-course training and the preparation of the thesis/final exam when it is experimental, at the Convened Structures (AASSLL, DSB, Hospice, INAIL, Penitentiary Institutes, CIM, SERT, etc). Assistance is delegated to Tutors, thesis supervisors, and the Chair of the Course Council with the assistance of the three Academic Directors of the Poles, who manage institutional relations with the convening and/or hosting entities.
In addition to ASL 02 Lanciano-Vasto-Chieti and AUSL of Pescara, the healthcare structures where the professional internship is carried out are:
- Villa Pini D'Abruzzo Nursing Home Chieti, contact: Dr. Annamaria Di Giandomenico
- Villa Serena Nursing Home Città Sant'Angelo, contact: Dr. Donatella Candeloro
- G. Spatocco Nursing Home Chieti, contact: Dr. Luigi Zappacosta
- Pierangeli Nursing Home Pescara, contact: Dr. Luigi Zappacosta
- Assisted Healthcare Residences: United Assistance Institutes 'S. Giovanni Battista' Chieti, contact: Dr. Martina Marini
- Elderly Care Home: Compassionist Sisters of Mary Service 'Chieti Scalo', contact: Sister Maddalena, Superior, Sister Valentina, and Nurse Daniele Gasbarri
- Rehabilitation Center for Neurological and Motor Disorders Foundation Institute 'Santa Caterina' Francavilla al Mare, contact: Dr. Simonetta Di Nardo
The structures must:
- address situations or processes related to the competency profile specified in the internship project in relation to the academic year
- provide contact persons and internship guides
- collaborate with the Academic Director in monitoring learning.
In the structures listed above, during the Academic Year 2018/2019, approximately 50 students completed their internship.
The link http://www.med.unich.it/corsi-di-laurea/infermieristica/sezione-qualita reports the results of the evaluation of internship sites by our students.
During the Academic Year 2017/2018, ADO activities were carried out for third-year students by the Italian Military Health Service INTERFORZE (A.N.S.M.I.), coordinated with Dr. Corrado Picone, Vice-President of the National Commission for Major Risks and Major Emergencies and Responsible Commissioner for the Interregional Grouping Abruzzo-Marche-Molise:
March 16, 2018 'Armed Forces in Rescue Operations. Prevention and Safety in Hostile Environments: Activities of the State Police'
March 23, 2018: 'Pediatric/Neonatal Extra-Hospital Emergencies. Organization of Medical Rescue in Major Emergencies'
April 20, 2018: 'Emergency Communication: Military Aviation on the Front Line. Major Events: State Police Intervention'
May 4, 2018: 'Nuclear-Biological-Chemical-Radiological Risk. The Carabinieri and the 2017 Snow Emergency'
May 18, 2018: 'Military Aviation in Managing Major Emergencies. The Carabinieri in Natural Disasters'
These activities stimulated some students who chose to complete an internship period aimed at finalizing their thesis within the Military Health Service.
A thesis titled 'THE COMPETENCIES OF THE MILITARY NURSE' was discussed in the April 2019 session by student Miriana Forlano with Dr. Carlo Della Pelle as supervisor and Dr. Corrado Picone as co-supervisor.
Noteworthy is the interest shown by some second and third-year students who attended the HATRANUS II conference, Prevention and Safety: Territorial and Health Emergency, held at the Rectorate Auditorium of 'G. d'Annunzio' University, Chieti Campus on May 29, 2019, organized by the Chair of the Master's Course in Medicine and Surgery, Prof. Muraro, with the collaboration of Dr. Picone.
Some students from the Nursing Course Council wished to speak personally with some speakers and establish contacts for potential employment opportunities within the Military Health Service. Attached is the PDF file of the program and photos taken during the conference.

In the structures listed above, during the Academic Year 2019/2020, approximately 30 students completed their internship before the lockdown due to the Covid-19 health emergency.
On May 11, 2020, the Chair communicated that on February 26, 2020, the School of Medicine and Health Sciences signed an agreement with Medicasa Italy, founded in Milan in 1993, specialized in designing and providing Home Care on behalf of ASL, operating throughout Italy to offer a wide range of home services. With over 20 years of experience, Medicasa provides competent and qualified staff to assist patients in their homes. Nursing Course Council students can: complete internships to gain knowledge about the professional role in the territory and the techniques and services performed at home; learn the main characteristics of the home care plan; observe and practice the relational aspects of a successful helping relationship between professional and patient/caregiver.
The Chair and Academic Directors visited the Pescara office at Via Alcide De Gasperi on January 10, 2020, and highly appreciated the organization of the activities carried out by the Cooperative.
Due to the lockdown, it was not possible to start the activities in 2020. However, on March 23, 2021, the Chair confirmed to Medicasa contact Dr. Giuseppe Di Maggio the availability of the Academic Directors of the Chieti and Pescara Poles to send students for ADI (Integrated Home Care) activities.
Academic Year 2021-2022
The Chair of the Course Council received a convention request from Ms. Antonietta Cataldo, Administrative Director of the Social Cooperative Residence Fraternitas of Castel Frentano. The Academic Directors expressed a favorable opinion, and on April 14, 2022, the signed documentation was received from Ms. Cataldo. The Chair of the Course Council arranged for the convention to be signed by the President of the School of Medicine and Health Sciences, Prof. Liborio Stuppia.
Another convention will be signed with the Social Cooperative La Rondine, which provides medical, nursing, rehabilitative, and specialized services at the user's home through Integrated Home Care (ADI). The service objectives include: improving quality of life by keeping elderly, disabled, and patients with certain conditions at home, reducing hospitalization rates by promoting discharge (protected discharge), avoiding improper admissions, and qualifying care in the territory. La Rondine has provided the service in the Lanciano-Vasto territory since 2005; since August 2016, the service has been extended to the Chieti territory.
Additionally, on April 8, the Chair met with the manager and a medical director of the Don Orione facility in Pescara to sign a convention allowing students from the Course Council to expand their internship activities. The facility provides services in various fields: rehabilitation, diagnosis and treatment, and specialized medicine.
Academic Year 2022-2023
During the Academic Year 2022-2023, conventions with Cireneo and the Padre Alberto Mileno Foundation were renewed, and new conventions were activated with RSA Santa Rita, San Giovanni, and San Vitale.
Academic Year 2023-2024
Thanks to student Agnese Iezzi's request to write a thesis on the nurse's role in multicultural contexts in Emergency projects and Dr. Fabio Rossi's availability, the Chair of the Course Council organized a Teams call on February 16, 2024, with Emergency representatives to discuss the possibility of signing a convention for the student's internship activities. During the meeting, the activities carried out in Emergency's Italian centers were presented, and Agnese had the opportunity to outline the objectives of her thesis project. Dr. Gianfilippo Pascolini, Administrative Coordinator of the ITALIA PROGRAM, expressed full willingness to contact Agnese to begin collecting her logistical needs and provide useful support to start a 6-month internship.
More and more students are requesting the possibility to carry out some clinical internship activities in facilities near their residences. In particular, in recent years, the number of students from cities in the Teramo province has increased. Regarding this, on July 23, 2021, the Chair, together with Prof. Angelo Di Iorio and Dr. Francesco Delle Monache, Head of Medicine at Teramo Hospital, met with the ASL Teramo leadership to discuss the possibility of signing a convention and providing students and trainees the opportunity to attend the Organizational Units of the affiliated structures. By the end of 2023, an agreement was finally drafted based on which students who make a motivated request can complete their internship, in agreement with the Professional Academic Directors, at the facilities affiliated with ASL Teramo.
International Mobility Assistance
The University of G. d'Annunzio has obtained the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) 2014-2020, certified by the European Commission (EACEA (Education, Audiovisual and Culture Executive Agency)), based on the Erasmus Policy Statement, a necessary document that grants the right to participate in the new Erasmus+ Program 2014/2020. The objective of the new Program is to encourage international mobility for over four million people (double the previous amount) with European funding (2014/2020) for study and training periods abroad. The University's International Relations Office organizes student and faculty mobility through meetings aimed at promoting participation and subsequently guiding selected students.
The link related to information on international mobility (Students - Erasmus, Overseas, Visiting Students, Seminars/Training Abroad - Traineeship, Non-Teaching Staff, Faculty) Erasmus+ for Study, Erasmus+ Traineeship, Erasmus Incoming Students, International Conventions, Opportunities is the following: https://www.unich.it/didattica/international/mobilita.
At the link https://www.unich.it/didattica/international/mobilita/studenti/erasmus, the following information can be found:
ERASMUS CHARTER FOR HIGHER EDUCATION (ECHE), EUROPEAN POLICY STATEMENT, ERASMUS PARTNER UNIVERSITIES - Programme Countries - K 103, University Regulation for International Mobility, Conversion Tables/ECTS Grading System.
Additionally, to optimize resources, the competent office has set up and activated email boxes for specific Erasmus-related inquiries:
  INCOMING:
incoming@unich.it
  OUTGOING:
outgoing.chieti@unich.it
A Bilateral Agreement is a mutual commitment agreement between partner universities, providing for student mobility for specific internship programs at the Course Council's training poles; this clinical activity is coordinated by the Academic Director of the Pole who assigns a specific tutor to the student.
The Nursing Course Council has delegated, for assistance and Erasmus agreements, as well as for managing related documentation, in collaboration with the University's URI service, Dr. Gabriella Mincione (gabriella.mincione@unich.it), who was replaced in the Academic Year 2018/2019 by Dr. Giulia Renda (giulia.renda@unich.it).
Every Academic Year, the Erasmus Plus Traineeship call is published at the following link: http://unich.traineeship.it/.
Within the Erasmus+ Program, the Erasmus Traineeship Program (only internship) aims to promote the activation of internships at companies or training and research centers in one of the participating European countries. Erasmus students have the opportunity to acquire specific skills and a better understanding of the socio-economic culture of the host country, with the support of preparatory or updating courses in the host country's language (or the working language), ultimately aiming to promote the mobility of young workers throughout Europe.
The training internship is intended for students/graduates and doctoral candidates of G. d'Annunzio University Chieti-Pescara. Candidates must be winners of an internship mobility grant before the thesis defense. The thesis defense cannot take place during the internship period: mobility must be carried out entirely before or entirely after the thesis defense.
During the Academic Year 2016-2017, the Nursing Course Council welcomed, within the Erasmus Plus traineeship program (only internship), two students from the Riga Medical College of the University of Latvia.
In the same Academic Year, three students from the Nursing Course Council of G. d'Annunzio University Chieti-Pescara completed a 9-month period at the Spanish University of Huelva within the Erasmus Plus study program.
During the Academic Year 2017-18, the Nursing Course Council, within the Erasmus+ (PLUS) study program, received two students from the Spanish University of Jaen, while one of our students departed for the same university. In the same Academic Year, a student from the Nursing Course Council of G. d'Annunzio University Chieti Pescara was awarded a study mobility period at the University of Huelva.

Through the Erasmus program, it is possible to fund the organization of a BIP, obtaining up to €6,000 for the coordinator.

University of Jaen (Spain).
Sivas Cumhuriyet University (Turkey), Klaipeda University (Lithuania), and Calisia University Kalisz (Poland) responded positively.
The chosen topic has the following title: The Multidisciplinary Role of Health Care Professionals in Integrated Care Between Hospital and Territory.
The planned activities are: Lectures by experts. Meetings with stakeholders and local actors. Meetings with the local community. Design and processing activities.
Expected learning outcomes: At the end of the program, students are expected to: Share issues related to territorial healthcare assistance; Stimulate reflection on new models and paradigms for the concept of Community Health Houses; Develop architectural models based on adaptation to environmental aspects, reduction of anthropic impacts, reuse of existing heritage, etc. Comparison and discussion of topics through seminar activities; Lectures and dialogues with experts; Drafting of a design program starting from comparison with stakeholders and territory actors; Construction of future design scenarios at different scales; Presentation and dissemination of the project idea.
In-person work at the Chieti Campus will begin on June 17 and end on June 21, while online activities will start on July 1 with pre-recorded lectures and end on July 12 with the final lecture and discussion of the work.

The President reports that on September 15, 2020, the Academic Senate and the Board of Directors deliberated on the timing and modalities for resuming teaching activities related to the so-called Phase 3 of the Covid-19 emergency. Specifically:
LECTURES
- Start of lectures For all Study Courses:
  lectures for semester courses: start Monday, October 12, 2020
  lectures for annual courses: Monday, November 3, 2020
- Modalities of delivery / live lectures and recordings Lectures for courses delivered to the maximum extent in university classrooms, ensuring that in-person teaching is always accessible remotely. However, on November 12, 2020, due to the increase in infection rates, new provisions in compliance with Regional Council President's Decree No. 92 of October 26, 2020, and the explanatory note of October 30, 2020, suspended all in-person lectures.
Lectures were held exclusively in a remote format.
Subsequently, in compliance with the DPCM of January 14, 2021, starting from February 1, 2021, lectures for courses were delivered to the maximum extent possible in university classrooms, but always accessible remotely.
Final graduation exams were conducted according to the student's chosen modality - either in-person or online - following the application of currently in-force protocols (PREVIOUS EMAIL SUBMISSION TO THE STUDY COURSE SECRETARIAT AND TO THE SUPERVISOR PROFESSOR AT LEAST FIFTEEN DAYS IN ADVANCE).
Written profit exams were conducted online, applying the currently observed operational protocols.
Oral profit exams were conducted according to the student's chosen modality - either in-person or online - following the application of currently in-use operational protocols (PRE-ANNOTATION OF REQUEST ON ESSE3 AND EMAIL SUBMISSION TO THE PROFESSOR AT LEAST FIVE DAYS IN ADVANCE).
Finally, new provisions in compliance with Regional Council President of Abruzzo Decree No. 7 of February 12, 2021, effective from February 12, 2021, until further notice, indicate the suspension of in-person lectures, profit exams, and final theses.
Therefore, remote delivery will be implemented.
With Decree-Law No. 111 of August 6, 2021, new provisions were adopted for the start of the 2021/2022 academic year, considering the new epidemiological context and the vaccination plan's progress. Initially, Article 1, paragraph 1, reaffirmed the principle - which all universities had already followed during the previous academic year - of prioritizing in-person teaching and curricular activities.
To this end, the President of the Nursing Study Course and the teaching representative communicated the new provisions to all teachers and students:
a) use of respiratory protection devices, except for individuals with conditions or disabilities incompatible with such devices and for sports activities;
b) recommended maintaining a minimum interpersonal safety distance of one meter, ensuring the widest possible in-person participation in teaching and curricular activities, taking into account structural and logistical conditions of the buildings;
c) prohibited access or staying in university premises for individuals with respiratory symptoms or body temperature above 37.5°C.
It is also noted that the Decree-Law introduced important changes, in particular:
- from September 1, 2021, until December 31, 2021, all university staff, both teaching and administrative, must possess and present the Green Pass COVID-19;
- failure to comply with these obligations results in the staff being considered unjustifiably absent, and from the fifth day of absence, depending on the characteristics and specifics of the work performance of teaching staff versus administrative staff, the employment relationship will be suspended without payment of salary or any other compensation;
- from September 1, 2021, until December 31, 2021, university students must also possess the Green Pass COVID-19 for participation in in-person teaching and curricular activities;
- the obligation to possess the Green Pass COVID-19 does not apply to teaching and administrative staff, as well as students, exempt from the vaccination campaign based on a medical certificate issued according to criteria defined in a Ministry of Health circular;
- universities conduct checks regarding possession of the Green Pass COVID-19 according to modalities to be indicated in a subsequent DPCM and, in any case, according to organizational choices of each university, while respecting privacy regulations and handling data contained in the Green Pass COVID-19 within the scope of the law's intended purpose;
- checks on university students regarding possession of the Green Pass COVID-19 are conducted on a sample basis and according to modalities determined by each university;
- such checks are the responsibility of university authorities, meaning, as per Article 2, paragraph 1, letter b) of Law No. 240 of 2010, the Rectors and their delegates as per each university's organization for control.
On January 7, 2022, following the pandemic evolution, it was decided that exams could be taken in a mixed modality.

On April 13, further provisions were communicated as follows:
"Following the provisions of Decree-Law No. 24 of March 24, 2022 'Urgent measures for overcoming the measures to counter the spread of the Covid-19 epidemic', consequent to the cessation of the emergency state - which has suspended the Covid-19 emergency from April 1, 2022 and indicated a gradual return to normality - and the subsequent indications from the Minister of University and Research, the indications approved at the Academic Senate meeting of September 16, 2021, regarding the organization of teaching activities for the first semester of the 2021/2022 academic year are confirmed, with some modifications only regarding profit and graduation exams."
In brief:
The delivery modality of teaching activities in the second semester will remain unchanged from the first semester:
All university teaching activities, whether lectures or practical activities (internships, laboratories, seminars, exercises), are delivered in-person, with rotation for larger courses, in compliance with measures contained in the safety protocols adopted by the university and compatible with available space.
Until the end of second-semester lectures, remote access will be guaranteed for students unable to attend university premises due to the health emergency or unable to book a classroom seat.
Regarding exam and graduation sessions, starting from May 1, 2022:
Exam sessions are held in-person, with appropriate scheduling if overcrowding risks incompatible with interpersonal distancing are present. However, exam sessions can still be conducted remotely for the reasons specified by the Academic Senate at the September 16, 2021 meeting, when the student makes a documented request via email to the professor at least five days before the exam date.
Final graduation or diploma exams are primarily conducted in-person, with appropriate scheduling if overcrowding risks incompatible with interpersonal distancing are present.
Up to five accompanying persons (manned with FFP2 respiratory protection devices) may attend in-person graduation sessions, up to classroom capacity, always ensuring compliance with interpersonal distancing obligations.
However, graduation sessions can still be conducted remotely when the student makes a motivated request via email to the Study Course Teaching Secretariat at least fifteen days before the start date. Remote access will also be guaranteed to allow family members who could not attend to follow the thesis discussion and proclamation of graduates.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI-PESCARA GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO
COURSE: [L603] NURSING
SECTION: Student opinions
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/613

Student opinions OBJECTIVES OF THE SURVEY The survey of opinions from enrolled students represents:
-the fulfillment of the legal obligation set forth by Law 370 of 1999 and subsequent amendments
-an opportunity to acquire the level of student satisfaction regarding the structural and organizational resources provided by the University, the organization of teaching activities, the methods of conducting lessons, the content of courses, as well as the competencies of teachers.
The usefulness of the survey increases with a higher rate of evaluated courses, hence the need to sensitize teachers and students about the importance of evaluation.
SURVEY TOOLS The University's unified questionnaire, used since the academic year 2013/14, is the one proposed in the AVA Document of January 28, 2013, with minor modifications, and consists of 10 questions. The scoring scale adopted for the response options of the questions is that proposed by CNVSU and also suggested by ANVUR, ranging from a minimum of 1, corresponding to the judgment 'definitely no', to a maximum of 4, corresponding to 'definitely yes', with two intermediate evaluations: 2, equivalent to 'more no than yes', and 3, equivalent to 'more yes than no'. In the online survey, an additional section was added to the questionnaire for collecting free student comments.
The details of the data are reported in the attached PDF (ANALYSIS OF STUDENT OPINION DATA TABLE B6 2023).
ANALYSIS OF STUDENT OPINIONS A.Y. 2022/2023 VS A.Y. 2021/2022
In A.Y. 2022-2023, the average value attributed to the Course of Study increased compared to A.Y. 2021-2022 (3.42 vs 3.35).
ANALYSIS CONDUCTED BY THE JOINT TEACHER-STUDENT COMMISSION Analysis and proposals on management and use of questionnaires regarding student satisfaction During the past year, it emerged from discussions with students that there is a functional issue with the platform for collecting student opinions, which does not allow disaggregated compilation of integrated courses, i.e., the possibility to express an opinion on each individual teacher composing the integrated course, and provides different compilation options depending on whether access is via fixed computer or smartphone, from the website or through the app. Since the vast majority of students access via smartphone, a method that allows for reduced compilation, there is a concrete risk that judgments cannot be detailed optimally and that certain specific situations may be missed in the survey. These issues were brought to the attention of the PQA during the meeting held on November 11, 2022. Therefore, the compilation of this table is carried out with the awareness that the results to be analyzed may be unreliable.
The number of completed evaluation forms was only slightly lower than that of A.Y. 2019-2020, and significantly lower than the previous year (7,512 vs 11,011), covering 51% of courses and 80% of teachers. The average score was 3.35, the highest of the three years considered.
Strengths: Compared to the previous two years, a significant improvement in teaching quality was noted, with 22% rated as Class A (compared to 5.17% and 2% in the years 2019-2020 and 2018-2019, respectively), 77% as Class B, and only 1 out of 118 courses as Class C. No course was rated as Class D.
Weaknesses: The questions with the lowest scores were D1: 'Are the preliminary knowledge possessed sufficient for understanding the topics covered in the exam program?' and D3: 'Is the study load required by the course proportional to the assigned credits?' confirming the initial cultural difficulties noted in previous years and accounting for the necessary effort to address existing gaps and progress in building the cultural background necessary for the nursing profession. In this regard, since these difficulties were also noted in previous years, several initiatives have been implemented; for details, refer to the discussion in Table D.
Additionally, following the changed context resulting from the pandemic event, our University has adhered to a request from the Didactic Commission of CRUI that requires the collection of opinions on Distance Learning, therefore this year, for the first time, the PQA has prepared a new report dedicated to opinions collected on Distance Learning.
Considering the abrupt change in lifestyle and personal interaction and teaching methods, the questionnaire reveals an overall satisfactory management of teaching activities during the pandemic emergency, with 86% of students reporting overall satisfaction.
Indeed, despite the vast majority of lessons being held remotely (78%), and most students (69%) following lessons exclusively remotely, most teachers (57%) opted for synchronous methods to maintain virtual contact with students.
The platform provided by our University for distance learning is Teams, and 90% of lessons were held on this platform, with lessons recorded in 70% of cases. Students also rated teachers highly on their ability to manage the digital medium, with 89% of evaluations indicating teachers were comfortable with it.
It is important to note that students' living and study conditions were significantly influenced by the possibility of attending remote lessons: less than half of students (47%) resided in the city where the course is based and could interact directly with teachers; for others, communication and exchange were primarily through the Teams platform or emails.
Despite the comforting fact that 79% of students had a private space to attend lessons and 67% had a personal computer, a notable figure is that 23% of students, nearly a quarter, attended lessons on smartphones, and 15% were unable to satisfactorily access teaching activities due to insufficient digital tools and internet connection.
The opinions of graduating students were also examined. The Graduating Students Opinion Survey collects the opinions of all students who submitted a graduation application in the three sessions (summer, autumn, and extraordinary) of A.Y. 2020/21. The questionnaire used is the one proposed by ANVUR (Form n.5), appropriately remodeled and integrated with additional questions to provide a comprehensive view of the adequacy of facilities (classrooms, equipment, and support services) and the overall experience of their training path.
The evaluation given by graduating students for A.Y. 2020/2021 can be considered generally positive, with an average score of 3.21, slightly higher than the previous year but slightly lower than the average scores of the Health Area and the University (respectively 3.29 and 3.23).
WEAKNESS: The question with the lowest score was D3: 'Is the overall organization (schedule, exams, intermediate and final) of the courses in the reference period acceptable?' which received a rating of 2.98, indicating students' clear request for greater attention to the organizational management of the complex set of activities they are required to undertake.
SOLUTION: This point has been addressed over the past two years by the responsible parties of the various poles, who also had to manage additional difficulties related to the pandemic concerning internships, through a reorganization of the lesson and internship calendar. In future questionnaires, we will be able to assess the effectiveness of the changes implemented.
As a pilot this year, a questionnaire for evaluating the Internship experience was also administered to students.
The results were interesting and stimulated new reflections: 100% of students believe the Internship was effective in improving competencies, technical, relational, and educational skills, and 70% of students reported being very or extremely satisfied with the experience, confirming the enormous professionalizing and developmental value always attributed to internships within the Course of Study. New reflections were stimulated by discussions with students about the tutorial model they encountered, the advantages and disadvantages of different situations.
These reflections led to a request from the student body for greater interaction between the Course of Study and the heads of host departments to agree on an organized tutorial model that serves as a clear reference point for students and optimizes the learning process while simplifying the work of structured nurses acting as tutors.
From interaction with the student body, two additional critical points worthy of attention emerged: 1- a high rate of lesson postponements and non-compliance with the didactic calendar issued at the start of the semester, postponements and absences that compromise the student's proper preparation; 2- the presence of teachers who have not demonstrated full mastery of the courses assigned to them.
Proposed solution: The joint commission proposes that Professor Mincione take responsibility for interacting with the student body and involved teachers to agree on a resolution method for the reported issues.
Analysis and proposals on the validity of assessment methods for knowledge and skills acquired by students in relation to expected learning outcomes.
Programs and examination methods for each course in the study plan are available online (UdA Homepage, Teaching, Teaching Activities, Department of Medicine and Aging Sciences, Nursing Course of Study, link to Course of Study site: https://scuolamedicina.unich.it/corsi-di-studio/infermieristica-l603). In most individual course sheets, there is consistency between the methods, teaching tools described, and expected learning outcomes; others are found to be non-conforming in methods and topics. Teachers have been invited to update syllabi according to new regulations, particularly by completing the Sustainability section. In this section, it is required to verify how topics covered in the course relate to the United Nations 2030 Agenda Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
WEAKNESS: Sample checks have revealed that not all syllabi have been entered, some are incomplete.
PROPOSAL: It is proposed to entrust the Didactic Directors of the Training Poles and the subcommittees that have already analyzed the programs in the three locations, and therefore have a precise overview of the situation, with a stricter control of syllabi entry. Regarding this proposal, during 2023, the Didactic Directors of the three poles completed a comprehensive revision of the Nursing discipline syllabi and uploaded them to the dedicated platform.
The analysis conducted will be included in the agenda of the Course of Study Council meeting in October 2023.
At the same time, to evaluate potential weaknesses and obtain suggestions for improving our students' training, it will be proposed to the Council that students themselves use the link https://www.unich.it/parla-con-noi ANALYSIS OF STUDENT OPINIONS A.Y. 2021/2022 (as of July 31, 2022) VS A.Y. 2020/2021

ANALYSIS OF RESULTS FOR THE YEAR 2022
The satisfaction level regarding the evaluation of equipment for other teaching activities increased (laboratories and practical activities 77.8% in 2021 vs 79.4% in 2022); the evaluation of the study load being appropriate to the duration of the course also increased compared to 2021 (from 74.7% in 2021 to 77.5% in 2022). The percentage of students who found the exam organization satisfactory remained stable (from 77.7% in 2021 to 77.5% in 2022). The use of computer stations decreased from 70.6% in 2021 to 65.9% in 2022. This likely reflects the greater availability of personal computers among students. Indeed, the evaluation students give to computer stations is very positive. Therefore, they appreciate the service even though they do not use it much (from 48.3% in 2021 to 66.7% in 2022).
The evaluation of library services increased (from 88.5% in 2021 to 91% in 2022); the percentage of students satisfied with interactions with professors in general also increased (from 88.8% in 2021 to 91.2% in 2022).
The evaluation of classrooms increased (82.7% in 2021 vs 88.3% in 2022).
Satisfaction with the degree course increased (from 93.5% in 2021 to 95.6% in 2022) but remains high compared to other courses of the same class at the university (90.6% in 2021).
The percentage of students who would enroll again at the university improved. Specifically, the percentage of students who would enroll in the same course at the university increased from 58.8% in 2021 to 68.1% in 2022.
The analysis of the data will be discussed at the Course Council meeting in October 2023.

acquiring professional skills is relevant (88.2%); there should be consistency with studies (83.4%); there should be the possibility to best use acquired skills (80.2%); they are interested in working in the public sector (89.3%); they want to work full-time (85%); they are willing to work in their province of residence (65.2% vs 72.8% compared to 2017), to work in a European country (49.7% vs 44.9% of 2017). These last two data indicate that nursing graduates are aware of the difficulty of entering the job market in Italy and are willing to choose European countries to practice their profession.
Learning Skills
Nursing graduates must develop the following self-learning skills:
- develop skills for independent study;
- demonstrate the ability to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activities as a source of new learning;
- develop the ability to pose questions related to the exercise of their activity, formulating relevant questions at the right time, place, and to the right interlocutors;
- demonstrate the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning;
- demonstrate the ability to self-assess their competencies and outline their development and learning needs;
- demonstrate the ability for collaborative learning and sharing knowledge within work teams;
- demonstrate the ability and autonomy to seek necessary information to solve professional practice problems or uncertainties, critically selecting primary and secondary research evidence sources.
Teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- problem-based learning (PBL);
- use of cognitive maps;
- use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- laboratories for bibliographic research methodology (paper and online);
- guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in Italian and English.
Evaluation tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- project work, report on specific research mandates;
- tutorial supervision on the internship path;
- active participation in work and debriefing sessions;
- punctuality and quality in presenting documents.
Brief Course Description The Study Course (Course) in Nursing aims to ensure students acquire adequate mastery of general scientific knowledge, methods, and content, oriented towards acquiring the most specific knowledge and professional skills, traceable to abilities and skills of understanding applied, in autonomy of judgment, in collaboration with other healthcare professionals, in managing nursing care for individuals and the community.
To be admitted to the Course, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another recognized foreign degree. The training potential of the Nursing Course for the 2021/2022 academic year is 245 (two hundred forty-five), plus 5 (five) places, of which 3 (three) for non-EU foreigners residing in Italy and 2 (two) for non-EU foreigners residing abroad. In the number of places reserved for non-EU students (non-EU) residing abroad, none are reserved for Chinese students participating in the 'Marco Polo' program.
The sustainability of the Course is related to the actual availability of human resources, teaching staff, and support staff, suitable structures and equipment (classrooms, laboratories for exercises, simulations, and biomedical research), services, and Complex Operational Units contracted with the National Health Service, as well as private healthcare structures in the territory. Teaching and internship activities are organized at the Chieti, Vasto, and Pescara training poles in the respective Healthcare Companies, under the responsibility of a teaching director of maximum qualification in the professional field, appointed based on curriculum evaluation by the Course Council. Access to the Course, whose modalities will be indicated annually on the university website (www.unich.it), is subject to passing a national admission test. For greater teaching effectiveness, adequate knowledge of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics is required for access, as defined by Article 4 (OFA) of the Course's Academic Regulations. To obtain the degree, the student must have earned 180 CFU, including all theoretical and practical teaching activities and the final qualifying exam. The normal duration of the Course is three years. Longer durations may be provided for part-time students, as per Article 17 of the current Course Academic Regulations. Those who obtain the degree are awarded the academic title of Doctor in Nursing.
External Effectiveness C2, 2023
C2 EXTERNAL EFFECTIVENESS The analysis of data on the employment status of 2021 graduates at one year (2022 survey updated to April 2023, see attached file) indicates that:
the number of graduates is 192, increasing from the 2021 survey (173); the percentage of graduates enrolled in a second-level degree increases from 6.9% to 16.4% in 2022; the employment rate slightly decreases from 91.4% to 90.0% in 2022; the percentage of employed graduates who use acquired degree skills to a high degree decreases from 92.4% to 89.8%; the average net monthly salary is comparable (from 1,647.00 to 1,638.00 euros). There is a slight decrease in satisfaction with the work performed (from 8.5 in 2021 to 8.1 in 2022).
Overall, the data analysis shows that external effectiveness is significantly higher than for the same type of course at the university.
The data will be discussed at the Course Council meeting in September 2023.
From the consultation of AlmaLaurea data (see attached file), covering the survey years 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020 (with graduates being 180 vs 165 vs 162 vs 212 vs 209), the RESPONSE RATE was respectively 72%, 78%, 76.5%, 76.9%, 73.2%; in all years, women represent the majority, although in 2018 the gap with male graduates narrows to 66% compared to 73% the previous year.
Nurses graduate during the course, although the average duration in years has slightly increased from 2016 (3.5 vs 3.9), and they are relatively young: 24.3 years. The average degree grade for the three years considered is 105.4/110.
Regarding post-graduation training, in the last three years, the percentage of those enrolled in a second-level degree has visibly increased from 0.8% in 2016 to 9% in 2018, then decreased to 5.5% in 2019, and increased again to 9.8% in 2020; the motivation for enrolling in a second-level degree is: in 2016, 100% was driven to improve their cultural training, decreasing to 66.7% in 2017, 54% in 2018, 33% in 2019, and 20% in 2020; simultaneously, the percentage of those choosing the Master's to improve job prospects and because a second-level degree is necessary for this purpose has increased over the years.
Considering the section 'Characteristics of current work', permanent employment has further decreased in 2019 compared to 2018: specifically, permanent employment decreased from 14.6% in 2018 to 12.9% in 2019 and to 11.5% in 2020, increasing the non-standard work type from 68.5% in 2018 to 75% in 2019 and to 77.9% in 2020: this data can be explained by the increase in outsourcing of services by healthcare companies, involving cooperatives and temporary agencies.
The average weekly working hours respect the sector collective labor agreement (36).
Our graduates work predominantly in the private sector until 2019 (70.7% in 2019, 73% in 2018 and 2017, 50.5% in 2016), while in 2020 the health emergency due to the Covid-19 pandemic caused a trend reversal in favor of the public sector (in 2020, the percentage is 51.9% in public and 44.3% in private). Thus, in 2019, private sector work decreased from 70.7% to 44.3%.
The geographical area where nurses find employment one year after graduation, with a gradual increase, is Southern Italy, the region of origin of half of the students enrolled in the Course (Puglia is the leading region).
A data certainly worth highlighting is that nursing graduates have been appreciated abroad, especially in Great Britain: in 2016, the share was 12%. However, from interviews, the percentage decreased in 2017 to just over 1.0%, increased to 4.2% in 2018, dropped to zero in 2019, and slightly rose to 0.8% in 2020.
The net monthly salary of over 1300 euros, despite high professional responsibilities, is still above the national average of 990 euros (ISTAT, 2018). In 2020, the net monthly salary rose to 1595.00 euros.
Additionally, the skills acquired with the degree are used to a high degree by 77.5% in 2018 (comparable to previous years); in 2019 it was 81%, and in 2020 it was 85.5%.
The university training is considered 'very appropriate' and gradually increases from 2016 to 2019 (84 vs 86.5 vs 86.5 vs 90.5) with a decline to 84.7% in 2020: probably the decline recorded in 2020 is due to the effects of implementing distance learning due to the Covid-19 health emergency. Indeed, at the end of February 2020, the Study Courses for Health Degrees and Master's Degrees underwent important changes in teaching, laboratory, and professional/internship activities due to the emergency situation. Immediately, the DPCM of April 10, Article 1, Paragraph k,1 stated that internships for Health Professions could continue. However, while teaching activities resumed almost immediately in distance mode, laboratories and professional/internship activities were suspended throughout Italy, mainly due to joint decisions by Healthcare Companies/Universities as emerged from a survey conducted by the Permanent Conference of Health Degree Classes.
The internships for Health Degree and Master's Degree Courses constitute the indispensable part of the training of future health professionals because they are capable of generating and consolidating the expected competencies at an initial and advanced level and developing a solid professional identity through learning processes from experience, practice, and anticipatory socialization to work. For its indispensability and relevance (=60 CFU for Bachelor's Degrees, 30 CFU for Master's Degrees), the internship has always been carried out 'in person' for the entire scheduled hours.
Restarting internships in a profoundly changed context and re-proposing, where necessary, a suitable part in distance mode requires a comprehensive vision capable of guiding unprecedented choices to ensure learning experiences of quality generating competencies no less than those acquired 'in person'. The Permanent Conference has developed guidelines aimed at suggesting a range of opportunities and diversified approaches capable of stimulating different learning styles and student needs, avoiding further isolation. Moreover, the guidelines were fundamental to ensuring, where possible, a coordinated preparatory phase among all Course Councils of the same university through inter- or intra-departmental systems to guarantee a harmonious approach towards companies, while respecting different specificities.
The last observed variable is 'EFFECTIVENESS OF THE DEGREE AND SATISFACTION WITH CURRENT WORK', where the effectiveness of the degree in the work performed, measured with the judgment 'very effective/effective' in 2020, was 97.7%, in 2019 it was 95.7% vs 96.6% in 2018.
SATISFACTION WITH THE WORK PERFORMED, on a scale of 1-10, is above 7.5 in the analyzed years (in 2018: 7.9, in 2019: 7.7, in 2020: 8.4), indicating full alignment between the study course and the actual work performed.
Specific Course Objectives and Training Path Description The graduate, at the end of the three-year path, must be able to:
- manage with autonomy and responsibility interventions aimed at prevention, care, assistance, and safeguarding the health of the assisted person, family, and community;
- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, and elderly) with acute and chronic respiratory problems, cardiovascular problems, metabolic and rheumatic problems, acute and chronic renal problems, acute and chronic gastrointestinal problems, liver problems, neurological problems, oncological problems, infectious problems, orthopedic and traumatological problems, obstetric-gynecological problems, hematological problems, behavioral and cognitive alterations, and situations of discomfort/disturbance;
- assess and manage nursing care for chronic patients and disabilities in all ages;
- manage perioperative nursing care;
- ensure safe administration of therapy and monitor its effectiveness;
- perform nursing techniques learned and defined by the Course standards with skill and ability;
- activate decision-making processes based on the general and clinical conditions of the patient, altered parameter values, reports, and laboratory tests;
- manage diagnostic pathways ensuring adequate patient preparation and subsequent monitoring;
- integrate nursing care into multidisciplinary care projects;
- assess the problems of the assisted person through structured and systematic techniques and modalities, identifying alterations in functional models (activities and exercise, perception and maintenance of health, nutrition and metabolism, elimination model, rest and sleep, cognition and perception, concept of health, role and relationships, coping and stress management, sexuality and reproduction, values and beliefs);
- activate and support, individually or in collaboration with other healthcare professionals, the residual capacities of the person to promote adaptation to limitations and alterations caused by illness and changes in lifestyle;
- identify the nursing care needs of the person and their related reactions to illness, treatments, institutionalization, changes in daily activities, and perceived quality of life;
- define the priorities of interventions based on nursing needs, organizational needs, and optimal use of available resources;
- design and implement, in collaboration with other professionals, information and health education interventions for risk factor control aimed at the individual and the community;
- evaluate the results of the provided care and adapt the nursing planning based on the evolution of the patient's problems;
- manage and organize nursing care (including night shifts) for patients;
- distinguish nursing care needs from other assistance needs, differentiating the contribution of support staff from that of nurses;
- assign and supervise assistance activities to support staff;
- manage paper and computer-based information systems supporting care;
- document nursing care provided in accordance with legal and ethical principles;
- ensure patients and significant persons receive relevant and updated information about their health status;
- prepare conditions for the discharge of the assisted person, in collaboration with team members;
- ensure continuity of care between different shifts and services;
- use professional integration tools (meetings, team meetings, case discussions);
- work integrated within the team respecting competence spaces;
- ensure an effective physical and psychosocial environment for patient safety;
- use practices for protection against physical, chemical, and biological risks in the workplace;
- adopt manual handling precautions for loads;
- adopt infection prevention strategies (standard precautions) in hospitals and community settings;
- monitor and vigil the clinical and psychosocial condition of the patient, identifying early signs of worsening;
- activate necessary interventions to manage acute and/or critical situations;
- identify triggering factors for reactivation in chronic patients;
- activate and manage a therapeutic and supportive relationship with the user, their family, and significant persons;
- manage care processes respecting cultural, ethnic, generational, and gender differences;
- support, in collaboration with the team, the assisted person and family in the terminal phase and grief;
- activate informal care networks to support the user and family in long-term care projects.
TRAINING PATH:
1st year - aimed at providing knowledge in basic, biomedical, and preventive hygiene disciplines; the foundations of the professional discipline, also in a psychopedagogical context, as indispensable requirements to face the first internship experience aimed at orienting the student to the reference professional areas and acquiring basic prevention and assistance competencies;
2nd year - aimed at clinical knowledge and preventive and assistance interventions, designed to address priority health issues in medical and surgical areas, specialized and integrated areas, maternal-infant areas, and oncological areas, focusing on acute and chronic disease phases, supporting educational and psychosocial aspects. Simulation experiences in nursing laboratories and internships in contexts where students can experiment with acquired knowledge and techniques are provided;
3rd year - aimed at specialized in-depth in neurological and mental health areas and acquisition of knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice and ability to integrate within work teams and in more complex organizational contexts. The relevance of internship experiences increases, and students can gradually assume greater autonomy and responsibility under expert supervision. Additional training activities are provided, including internships in excellence structures to support thesis preparation and develop methodological skills in scientific and nursing research.
This curricular logic has been concretized in the growth of credits assigned to clinical internships from the 1st to the 3rd year of the course.

The President directly and/or indirectly, in official meetings of the Technical Planning Committee (CTP) and the Course Council, consults social partners (Students, Directors of Healthcare Companies, Internship Coordinators, Nursing Managers, and Professional Colleges).
The CTP exercises the following instructional functions towards the Course Council or deliberative functions on specific mandates:
1. identifies the training objectives of the core curriculum;
2. aggregates training objectives into teaching courses that are functional to the Course's training purposes;
3. identifies with Teachers the appropriate teaching methodologies for achieving individual teaching objectives;
4. organizes, at the beginning of each Academic Year, the offer of optional teaching activities and proposes their activation to the Course Council.
The CTP also:
- discusses with teachers the modalities for preparing formative and certificative assessment tests, consistently with the predefined training objectives;
