Program, textbooks, and objectives Official teaching and assessment languages.
ENGLISH
Specific educational objectives.
The objective of the Master's Degree Course in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services is to train professionals with solid skills in Information Engineering and specific preparation in one of the areas into which the broad disciplinary sector of telecommunications is divided. Starting from a solid foundation in mathematical-physical and engineering disciplines, prerequisite for admission to the course, the program proceeds to deepen the theoretical-scientific aspects related to the characteristic disciplinary sectors and aims to provide the knowledge and skills necessary to develop advanced design capabilities with reference to systems characterized by a high degree of complexity and requiring innovative solutions at the product and/or service level.
In line with recent years' evolution and considering the relevant professional fields, the study program proposes a privileged educational path for the characterization, design, and management of ICT infrastructures ("pervasive ICT infrastructures") that support the most modern network applications (broadband services for users, industrial automation, automotive, advanced building systems such as smart buildings, power grids, etc.). In essence, the focus is on the increasingly pervasive, complex, and heterogeneous network infrastructure that underpins the IoT (Internet-of-Things) paradigm and the world of networked systems and cyber-physical systems.
Assuming mastery of the basic topics of signals, systems, and telecommunications networks, the curriculum offers:
- Courses in the disciplines characteristic of Telecommunications Engineering, listed below: digital transmission systems, propagation and communication channel modeling, wireless communication systems, architectures and protocols for broadband and software-defined networks, photonic networks, signal processing and multimedia applications, remote sensing systems, antenna systems and electromagnetic design techniques, metropolitan and access network design;
- Courses in related or complementary engineering fields, such as: digital electronic systems, software engineering, embedded software architectures, stochastic models for networks and methods for resource control and optimization, models and methods for the environmental impact of radio systems, cybersecurity in ICT;
- Specific deepening of basic disciplines, such as combinatorial mathematics, coding theory, cryptographic algorithms, operations research and optimization;
- Additional opportunities for students to choose training activities, including strengthening foreign language knowledge, acquiring professional content (for which the course offers a structured offer, especially in the field of cybersecurity), and deepening aspects of business organization (individually or combined with field experiences through internships in Italian or foreign companies and foreign universities).
The study path is characterized by the combination of theoretical and methodological aspects related to telecommunications systems with advanced skills in modern HW and SW technologies for the development and implementation of solutions. It is worth noting that this study program has already anticipated current trends by introducing an embedded systems module for some time. The study program includes project work and the explicit presence of an advanced laboratory module with an adequate number of credits during the second year.
Curricula have been defined with the general objective of capturing a trend in the telecommunications field to differentiate based on a greater focus on technological aspects and, in general, a closer proximity of topics to the physical level on one hand and a certain propensity to oversee the network and service sectors enabled by these on the other.
The Master's Degree in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services concludes with a final project, involving a significant design and/or research activity, demonstrating mastery of the topics covered, the ability to work independently, and an adequate level of communication skills.
For both the final internship and the execution of project works in the regular activities of various modules, the study program offers a wide range of opportunities in telecommunications laboratories (also hosting the Local CISCO Academy for CISCO certification), DEWS Excellence Center laboratories, electromagnetic compatibility laboratories, HW/SW platforms and photonic systems laboratories, optics and photonics laboratories. It is important to highlight the possibility of involving students in a large number of research projects at DISIM, ensuring the opportunity to conduct experimental activities in advanced contexts. Additionally, internships are available with a large number of partner companies in Italy (e.g., Leonardo, Thales Italia, Thales Alenia Space, Telespazio, TIM, Wind Tre, etc.) and abroad (e.g., ABB in Sweden, Nokia-Siemens Networks in Denmark, etc., also through ERASMUS Traineeship). Finally, it is possible to complete the internship at foreign universities under ERASMUS agreements (e.g., KTH Stockholm, University of Aalborg, Technical University of Berlin, Instituto Superior Técnico in Lisbon, ENST in Rennes, AGH Krakow, Polytechnic University of Catalonia), with which collaborations are ongoing for the award of double degrees.
In general, student mobility experiences within ERASMUS and ERASMUS Placement agreements are encouraged.
Finally, initiatives have been launched aimed at i) increasing the degree of internationalization, ii) organizing research-oriented training, iii) formalizing initiatives for integration into the job market through apprenticeship for higher education. Regarding the first point, the Study Program has offered to host foreign students within ERASMUS, ERASMUS Mundus (e.g., Euroweb), and TEMPUS mobility programs and has provided the entire teaching activity in English since the 2015-2016 academic year, with full openness to international student recruitment. Regarding point iii), an apprenticeship program with companies has been activated and made operational.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The training path offered by the Master's Degree in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services aims to provide students with the knowledge and tools to understand and address issues related to telecommunications engineering, from both the technological and service perspectives.
The Master's graduate will have acquired at the end of the training path:
- The foundational knowledge of telecommunications engineering and design methodologies, through the fundamental courses in the characteristic sectors ING-INF/03 and ING-INF/02;
- More advanced topics in the ICT field to understand the most relevant scientific developments through advanced courses in the characteristic sectors;
- Tools and methodologies more oriented towards transmission and signal processing chains; or, skills necessary for the design and management of modern telecommunications networks and the development of services enabled by next-generation networks; or skills for the design and management of next-generation networks through an international training path, depending on the chosen curriculum;
- Interdisciplinary knowledge and transferable skills through courses in related or complementary fields.
The teaching path includes frontal lectures and classroom exercises, laboratory activities, and expert seminars, as well as individual study. The verification of learning outcomes is primarily conducted through written and/or oral exams, possible laboratory tests, and the development and presentation of group projects across multiple modules. Finally, the path concludes with the evaluation of the final exam by a graduation committee. Through these assessments, students' understanding, problem-solving abilities, and communication skills are evaluated.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate will be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to define and solve complex design problems and to develop and configure complex telecommunications networks, also considering economic and organizational implications. The achievement of the ability to apply knowledge occurs through critical reflection on the texts proposed for individual study and the execution of numerical and practical laboratory exercises and individual or group projects involving bibliographic research and the use of simulation and/or professional development environments.
III - Independent judgment The Master's graduate will be able to analyze, interpret, and describe complex telecommunications engineering problems, even based on limited or incomplete information. They will also be able to evaluate the social and ethical implications related to the application of their knowledge and judgments. They will be able to integrate and use the necessary knowledge to form their judgment on topics related to their specialization and develop a sufficient degree of creativity to define innovative solutions and approaches.
This educational objective is pursued, in particular, through teaching courses and project works, encouraging meetings and discussions with professionals promoted through seminars, conferences, and the completion of the Master's thesis. The thesis represents the moment when the student confronts contexts characteristic of telecommunications engineering, developing original and innovative ideas, taking on the task of illustrating and supporting their validity during the discussion.
IV - Communication skills The Master's graduate will have developed the ability to communicate and express without ambiguity in English the development and conclusions of their analysis or design work, as well as the context of the related knowledge.
They will be able to engage with interlocutors, specialists, and non-specialists on topics related to the different disciplines covered by the study program, identify problems, and communicate solutions using appropriate arguments and language for different circumstances.
They will have developed relational skills that facilitate teamwork, as well as the ability to carry out coordination actions.
These objectives will be pursued during regular teaching activities (encouraging active student participation), during assessment sessions (primarily conducted orally and in writing with 'open' responses), and through group projects requiring relational and seminar presentations. Finally, the final exam involves a discussion, in a debate format with a committee, of a thesis developed independently under the guidance of a faculty advisor. In this case, not only the content of the thesis but also the candidate's synthesis, communication, and presentation skills are evaluated.
V - Learning ability At the end of the training process, the graduate will have developed learning abilities enabling them to independently approach the study of engineering and basic disciplines, even those not included in their curriculum. This ability, which will be well motivated through the encouragement of awareness of the need for continuous training as an integral part of future professional activity, will allow the graduate to independently and profitably pursue further studies (Master's and PhD) and update and refine their knowledge through self-directed learning.
The development of learning ability is pursued within individual teaching modules through emphasis on methodological aspects and encouragement of individual in-depth study of specialized texts, standardization documents, and scientific literature: the care of these aspects is inherently included in project works and, finally, in the preparation of the Master's thesis, which stimulates the ability to acquire new skills through independently conducted research and studies.
The verification of learning abilities is an integral part of individual exam sessions and the final exam.
Professional role in the workplace.
Professional role in the workplace:
The graduate in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services from the University of L'Aquila is characterized by the combination of i) knowledge of the most modern communication techniques and architectures and ii) skills in terms of modeling, simulation, emulation, and implementation capabilities in various operational environments, with particular reference to emerging technologies and next-generation networks and services.
Based on the acquired preparation, the professional profile for Master's graduates in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services allows them to undertake tasks related to advanced design, planning, and management of complex systems and provides the foundation for operating in the field of innovation and development of new solutions, basic and applied research for the development of telecommunications technologies, next-generation networks, and innovative services. A natural career perspective is therefore represented, within various companies, by research and development laboratories and areas of design, planning, and management of telecommunications systems, offering access to the highest levels of technical career progression. Additionally, the Master's Degree provides stimuli and motivations for access to second-level Master's courses, as well as Research Doctorate courses, thus favoring a stronger orientation towards the performance of research and innovation activities.
Skills associated with the role.
1) Dimensioning, planning, and management of telecommunications networks, in relation to architectural aspects and programmability of modern networks; in this regard, skills acquired in the Telecommunications Networks modules and partly related to certifications (e.g., CISCO and Juniper) are particularly applicable,
2) Design and management of information security and protection aspects, referring to modules related to cryptography and ICT security and partly related to certifications (e.g., SPLUNK);
3) Design and modeling of digital transmission systems on physical carriers (copper and optical fiber) and radio;
4) Design and deployment of radio networks in various technologies;
5) Design, simulation, and development of microwave systems, with particular reference to radio frequency chains and antennas, MIMO systems, and beamforming techniques;
6) Methods and techniques for signal processing for telecommunications and for sound and image processing;
7) Design and modeling of Software Defined Networks and Software Defined Radio solutions;
8) Analysis of main vulnerabilities related to ICT security and corresponding countermeasures;
9) Evaluation of the compatibility of radio communication installations with environmental impact regulations for electromagnetic fields.
Professional title conferred.
Career opportunities:
The reference business field consists of companies that design and/or produce systems and devices for telecommunications, network operators managing complex telecommunications systems, and companies and entities providing services through the use of telecommunications systems. It is important to emphasize that the structure of the training path and the content of the specialized modules have been conceived to provide graduates with in-depth knowledge and appropriate design methods in sectors of great relevance in modern telecommunications: radio access technologies (e.g., mobile communications) and broadband interconnection technologies, optical technologies, remote sensing and applied electromagnetism systems, networking and internetworking technologies, programmable radio and network devices. Special attention is given to the integration between telecommunications technologies and the Internet world, which is closely connected to the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) scenario and the pervasive use of such technologies in all productive sectors and social life. This approach corresponds to the intention of providing graduates with broad employment prospects across the national and European territory. On the other hand, it aims to satisfy the significant recruitment needs of major companies in the Abruzzo region, in a context undergoing strengthening. In this framework, company internships also aim to facilitate the future graduate's integration into the job market and may evolve, in some cases regulated by specific agreements with companies engaged in further specialization and corporate training.

Program, Texts, and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN
Awarded Degree. Master's Degree in LITERARY AND CULTURAL STUDIES
Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's Degree course in Literary and Cultural Studies, fully aligned with the professional profiles and employment opportunities anticipated for its graduates, aims to provide students with philological-literary, linguistic, and historical tools that enable them to develop a deep understanding of the complexity and problematic nature of texts, literary and non-literary, which will be comprehended, analyzed, and interpreted through the critical use of bibliographic tools within their area of expertise. Most disciplines are therefore literary, critical-literary, and linguistic-philological. Complementing these are historical, philosophical, anthropological, and geographical disciplines.
Starting from a broad foundation of fundamental courses in literary, philological, and linguistic culture, and from the substantial overlap of applied methodologies, two curricula are proposed, focusing on the peculiarities of the ancient world and the modern and contemporary era, respectively. In particular, the classical curriculum track prioritizes the learning area related to the philological and historical Greek and Roman context, enhanced by courses in literary and ancient historical areas, as well as medieval and modern; the modern curriculum track is aimed at understanding and comprehending the Italian literary landscape and linguistic evolution, within the broader context of Italian, European, and extra-European historical-cultural development.
The study plan concentrates most of the core examinations in the first year, reserving student-selected courses for the second year, thus allowing students to dedicate a significant portion of their time to research and thesis writing, which is allocated 30 CFU. Affine courses are also included in the first year; they allow a certain degree of flexibility, enabling students to deepen a specific area and/or fulfill requirements for a particular teaching category.
Teaching activities are organized on a semester basis; in addition to frontal lectures, seminars and integrated activities are provided to stimulate students' critical participation and deepen specific interests; up to 6 CFU are also allocated for internships and trainings.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The knowledge forming the core of the course relates to text interpretation procedures, acquired through courses in literary and general linguistics (L-FIL-LET and L-LIN/01). A strong support for historical, geographical, anthropological, and aesthetic-philosophical contextualization, as well as for acquiring technical skills, will come from the sectors M-GGR, M-DEA, M-FIL, M-STO, and L-ANT, depending on the chosen curriculum. The acquisition of these skills is assessed for students of both curricula through written or oral reports presented by students in individual courses, through the final exam of each course, and through the final exam.
Finally, graduates will acquire knowledge and skills aimed at using the main computer tools and telecommunication systems. This objective is achieved by including in both curricula, among the affine courses, the sector ING-INF/05, Information Processing Systems.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies, within their field of study and in a research context, is able to best utilize and independently apply the available research tools, master different critical methodologies in the study of texts (from linguistic and philological analysis to historical and cultural analysis), and identify and develop original research topics.
Additionally, the graduate will be able to apply methods and tools for linguistic, philological, and historical analysis of texts, literary and non-literary; and interpret them in their multiple aesthetic, cultural, and symbolic aspects. This competence will be useful for understanding and valuing literature and generally humanistic knowledge in the current global context, where cultural production and all imagery take diverse forms and are transmitted through increasingly complex technological media.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding must also rely on adequate linguistic skills (at least B2 level) in at least one European Union language besides Italian; and, finally, may rely on adequate computer skills.
- To achieve the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, attention is directed towards the methodological and practical aspects of acquired knowledge. Students will be constantly confronted with recent scientific results through the use of simulation strategies that explicitly require the application of practical and problem-solving skills. Knowledge and skills, regarding text interpretation procedures, are acquired through courses in the sectors L-FIL-LET and L-LIN/01. A strong support for historical, geographical, anthropological, and aesthetic-philosophical contextualization, as well as for acquiring technical skills, will come from the sectors M-GGR, M-DEA, M-FIL, M-STO, and L-ANT, depending on the chosen curriculum. This will primarily be possible through frontal lectures and exercises; participation in seminars or workshops, bibliographic research on specific and complex topics; use of databases, dictionaries, etc. This will enable students to formulate informed and conscious judgments, develop independent reflections, and apply acquired knowledge in an original manner. This independence of judgment will also positively impact the student's future professional activities.
- The verification of the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding occurs concurrently with the verification of knowledge and understanding, specifically through written or oral reports presented by students within individual courses, the final exam of each course, and the final exam, which carries significant weight. The final exam requires the preparation of a thesis to be discussed before a committee that forms a judgment based on the student's academic record and the discussion itself.
- The verification of the ability to apply B2 level linguistic skills in at least one foreign language will occur through the certification of training credits in the activity “Additional Language Knowledge.” Finally, the ability to use computer tools may be assessed, in addition to the qualification in “Computer and Telecommunication Skills,” through the exam of the course in the sector ING-INF/05, Information Processing Systems, included among the affine courses.
III - Autonomy of Judgment Starting from the interpretation of acquired knowledge (fundamental notions and methods within various humanities disciplines), through diverse analytical and comparative tools, Master's graduates in Literary and Cultural Studies develop the ability to formulate independent opinions and judgments. Critical reading of texts and contexts thus translates into a methodological thinking attitude that will allow them, in the future and generally, to analyze reality critically and reflect coherently on social, ethical, and political issues. In particular, knowledge of the ancient world and its texts, in the case of the classical curriculum, facilitates understanding current themes and problems rooted in our cultural tradition of Greek and Roman antiquity. Graduates in the modern curriculum can interpret and understand today's texts and events, often stemming from the most recent cultural history of our country.
- To achieve autonomy of judgment, dialogic and interpretative methodologies, both written and oral, will be encouraged. Specifically, the described abilities, such as independently interpreting the results of textual and literary analysis, grasping the meaning of a series of information, and interpreting texts using contextual elements, synthesizing analysis results, etc., will be verified through written reports, synthetic works, and short essays, as well as through the work presented in the final exam. The aim is to encourage active participation from each student and foster the development of judgment autonomy based on critical re-elaboration of acquired knowledge. In this sense, specific exercises will be prepared on texts and sources of particular relevance (linguistic, literary, historical, etc.), high-value scientific conferences and seminars will be organized by national and international experts; students will be enabled to prepare original and methodologically correct reports. Knowledge and skills will be verified through exam assessments, including the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills At the end of the training path, Master's graduates in Literary and Cultural Studies acquire the ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, information, ideas, problems, and solutions, to both specialist and non-specialist audiences. They must be able to use discipline-specific terminology as well as translate specialized topics into more accessible forms. This objective is primarily supported by linguistic and literary training activities, mastery of a European language (in addition to Italian), study abroad stays, and acquisition of computer skills for humanities fields. Clarity in exposition, synthesis ability, and argument coherence are required during disciplinary exams, seminar activities involving the preparation of short papers and oral presentations in class during courses, discussion moments often present in frontal teaching activities, and the written preparation of the final exam.
- The verification of achieved communication skills occurs through passing exams distributed across the academic year sessions; during other training activities, chosen based on the curriculum, involving public oral presentations, written works in the form of short papers, descriptive, summary, and explanatory texts; and through the final exam. Additionally, communication skills at least B2 level in a foreign language will be certified through a specific language test at the University Language Center or through credit recognition for certifications issued by accredited bodies. The ability to communicate using current information technologies will be verified, in addition to the qualification in “Computer and Telecommunication Skills,” through the exam of the course in the sector ING-INF/05, Information Processing Systems, also during laboratory, seminar, and internship activities that involve the use of common word processing, data entry and processing, interactive, and multimedia presentations.
V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies, upon completion of the university path, will have developed the ability to independently use strategies for careful text exegesis (not only literary) to identify their various components, which in turn allow their contextualization within historical and cultural frameworks. The course of study also enables its graduates to develop learning abilities suitable for pursuing further training paths: specialized internships, research doctorates, or related or divergent Master's degrees. In fact, teachers of each discipline not only transmit updated content and use new research tools but also stimulate cultural awareness and a high degree of student autonomy in seeking objects of interest, integrated study paths, and their own forms of expression.
The verification of achieved learning abilities, in addition to throughout the course via passing exams, is subject to specific evaluation within the final exam.
Function in the Workplace.
Function in the Workplace: The Master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies will be able to perform various functions, differentiated based on the different knowledge and skills deepened in the two curricula provided by the Course. The figure of the Editorial, Documentary, and Cultural Services Operator, in fact, depending on the deepened knowledge and skills in the two paths, can be specified as follows:
1. Editorial and Documentary Services Operator. In reference to this figure, the Master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies will be able to perform functions such as:
- editor, chief editor, publisher in publishing houses, radio-television newsrooms, magazines and newspapers, both in print and online (after passing the professional aptitude exam for access to the profession of journalist);
- library and archive manager, document system manager, consultation, loan, and access service manager.
2. Cultural Services Operator. In reference to this figure, the Master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies will be able to perform functions such as:
- promoter, organizer, and manager of conferences and cultural events for the transmission and dissemination of humanistic knowledge in public and private institutions;
- promoter, organizer, and manager of events within the fields of arts and entertainment.
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Competencies Associated with the Function: The functions that the Master's graduate in Literary and Cultural Studies can perform are linked to various competencies. Each curriculum allows for the deepening of knowledge and skills more targeted to specific functions, professional opportunities, and employment prospects.
In reference to the functions related to the Editorial and Documentary Services Operator: solid and deep philological, linguistic, and humanistic competencies in the fields of Greek and Latin languages and literatures and the political, social, and artistic history of antiquity (classical curriculum); solid and deep philological, linguistic, and humanistic competencies in the field of Italian literary history (viewed in its relationship with the overall historical and cultural development) and Italian linguistic history, integrated within the broader context of Italian, European, and extra-European historical-cultural development (modern curriculum); linguistic skills at least B2 level in at least one European Union language besides Italian; advanced skills in text management and interpretation; critical use of bibliographic tools and multimedia sources; high conceptual processing and argumentative, expository, and explanatory text production abilities; solid document classification competencies; full mastery of common word processing, editing, and typesetting programs.
In reference to the functions related to the Cultural Services Operator: solid and deep philological, linguistic, and humanistic competencies in the fields of Greek and Latin languages and literatures and the political, social, and artistic history of antiquity (classical curriculum); solid and deep philological, linguistic, and humanistic competencies in the field of Italian literary history (viewed in its relationship with the overall historical and cultural development) and Italian linguistic history, integrated within the broader context of Italian, European, and extra-European historical-cultural development (modern curriculum); linguistic skills at least B2 level in at least one European Union language besides Italian; advanced skills in text management and interpretation; critical use of bibliographic tools and multimedia sources; high conceptual processing and argumentative, expository, and explanatory text production abilities; event planning, direction, and realization capabilities; solid organizational and responsibility competencies in the fields of theater, cinema, and entertainment; full mastery of common word processing, editing, and typesetting programs.
Additionally, the Master's degree in Literary and Cultural Studies allows for the acquisition of competencies and CFU useful for pursuing further paths as provided by current regulations in training and access to the roles of secondary school teachers.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
- Publishing houses and editorial service agencies; private companies and public institutions operating in the publishing field; print and online newspapers; radio-television broadcasters;
- Public and private research and study centers;
- Institutions dedicated to the conservation of documentary assets and archival research (libraries, archives);
- Public and private entities in the cultural services sectors; Italian and foreign cultural institutions interested in promoting a more widespread knowledge of Italian literary production, past and present;
- Entities and organizations operating in the fields of arts and entertainment;
- Italian companies in international relations.

Master's Degree in PREVENTIVE AND ADAPTIVE MOTOR SCIENCES Specific educational objectives.
The course aims to train autonomous professionals regarding decision-making and continuous updating capabilities, competent in the fields of the class, capable of interacting with various professional groups concerned with human health, with specific focus on primary and secondary prevention and motor rehabilitation, particularly in the elderly and/or disabled population.
The training path includes the following objectives:
1. Full mastery of advanced theoretical foundations of human movement and its control in different ages and health conditions, considering gender specifics;
2. Full mastery of techniques (including functional assessment, adaptive motor activities, motor rehabilitation, recovery of motor skills) of physical exercise and related indications based on documented evidence of effectiveness;
3. Mastery of language and knowledge necessary for effective collaboration with health professionals, considering specific health conditions (including therapies) of subjects, the need for individual secondary prevention, rehabilitation, and motor skill recovery programs, and the use of physical exercise within therapeutic plans and lifestyle modification;
4. Full competence in controlling risks related to physical activity in relation to hygiene and safety of environments, modification of unhealthy or dangerous behaviors, and correct procedures for approaching individuals or groups;
5. Full competence in methodologies for promoting physical activity and healthy lifestyles, enhancing individual and collective resources, in the general population and in groups such as the elderly, in school, work, or community settings to achieve maximum health levels;
6. Mastery of language and knowledge necessary for collaboration with social services operators for the use of motor activities as a factor of social integration and inclusion;
7. Full communication competence in both social and individual/small group contexts as a tool to complement motor exercise techniques and health promotion methodologies;
8. Full competence in designing, implementing, and evaluating motor activity programs for individuals or groups, in relation to different health conditions, age, gender, in the aforementioned contexts, with particular reference to scientific documentation of results.
The training path includes lectures, theoretical-practical activities, optional training activities, seminar activities, internships, and training stages.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The Master's program in Preventive and Adaptive Motor Sciences provides advanced knowledge on:
- Theoretical foundations of human movement, particularly in the elderly, disabled individuals, and subjects with pathologies;
- Molecular and morpho-functional bases of aging, chronic-degenerative cardiovascular and metabolic conditions;
- Pathophysiology of aging and models of chronic-degenerative and metabolic conditions, mechanisms of action of main therapeutic schemes used;
- Indications and effects of physical exercise in healthy subjects and the above conditions, based on documented evidence of effectiveness;
- Principles and methods of first aid, also in relation to assessing exercise intensity in special conditions;
- Techniques of physical exercise in relation to different indications, functional assessment, biomechanics in motor disability, rehabilitation techniques, posturology;
- Methods and techniques for risk control in motor activity;
- Methods and techniques of communication, group management, and counseling applied to the management of motor activities;
- Effect of physical exercise on common psychological discomfort conditions;
- Social impact of motor activities;
- Methodologies for designing, directing, implementing, and evaluating motor activity programs.
Specific understanding capabilities include:
- Scientific literature relevant for critical deepening of topics, preparation of the final thesis, and professional updating;
- Anamnesis as summarized by the subject or health professionals (medical and/or psychological areas) for individualized motor activity planning;
- Common tools (questionnaires) for detecting and assessing health status and physical exercise in epidemiological studies.

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Upon completion of the course, the Master's graduate in Preventive and Adaptive Motor Sciences will be able to:
- Independently analyze the starting condition of a subject using anamnestic methods, functional tests, and appropriate instrumentation, considering both motor performance and lifestyle;
- Independently plan and manage motor activities suitable for the subject's condition, ensuring safety regarding health, environmental, and behavioral risks;
- Direct motor or sports instructors, provide consultations to physical education teachers, and manage facilities aimed at achieving well-being through movement;
- Integrate into multidisciplinary health teams, understanding the limits of autonomous competence of each involved profession, and contribute to the group's objectives.

III - Judgment Autonomy The Master's graduate is able to independently address problems related to the design, implementation, and evaluation of motor activities based on received training and by researching scientific literature for new problems or proposing new strategies.
The Master's graduate contributes autonomously to multiprofessional groups concerned with human health.
The Master's graduate is able to evaluate their own work using guidelines and other criteria defined by the scientific community.

IV - Communication Skills Communication skills are specifically addressed in the training path. In particular, the Master's graduate is able to communicate effectively using various techniques, English language, computer tools, and basic multimedia techniques, at social and small group levels. They are able to use counseling to encourage adherence to motor activity and lifestyle modification programs. They effectively use communication to manage teams of collaborators.
The Master's graduate is able to use scientific communication tools to present their results and interact within study and/or research groups.

V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate is able to select sources for professional updating in line with scientific research progress; they are able to select and undertake master's courses, specialization, and advanced training courses, etc.
The Master's graduate is also able to follow doctoral research courses and address innovative scientific studies collaboratively.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
The Master's program in Preventive and Adaptive Motor Activities prepares an autonomous professional in the design, implementation, and evaluation of motor activities in any context (from fitness to activities for disabled individuals, for example, in school, recreational, social support, sports, and health facilities), also, where necessary, in multiprofessional groups for managing health issues using motor activity.
The profession of expert in motor activities is not regulated.

Master's Degree in NURSING AND MIDWIFERY SCIENCES Specific educational objectives.
Graduates in the Master's degree class in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences must achieve the following specific educational objectives:
1. In accordance with Article 6, paragraph 3 of Legislative Decree 30 December 1992, No. 502 and subsequent amendments and additions, and in accordance with Law 10 August 2000, No. 251, Article 1, paragraph 1, they possess advanced cultural and professional training to intervene with high-level competencies in care, management, training, and research processes in one of the fields relevant to the various health professions included in the class (Nurse, Midwife, Pediatric Nurse).
2. Master's graduates develop, following appropriate professional experience and acquired methodological knowledge, an integrated approach in the design and management of training and research processes specific to their professional fields.
Upon completion of the two-year course, the Master's graduate is able to:
1. Evaluate the potential and limitations of professional theories and models for their application to care and improvement of the quality of the organizational and professional context.
2. Adopt behaviors consistent with the ethical, deontological, and legal dimensions of care for individuals with health needs.
3. Evaluate the health needs of the individual and the community in relation to the responses of health and social services.
4. Plan, coordinate, manage, and verify health, nursing, and midwifery systems.
5. Analyze, organize, manage, and verify operational systems of health professional services.
6. Design and implement evidence-based innovative care models for the prevention and management of priority health issues of the individual and the community.
7. Transfer results of scientific research into nursing and midwifery care.
8. Evaluate methods and tools for analyzing and assessing the health status of the subject for the purpose of delivering nursing and midwifery care.
9. Integrate scientific, clinical-educational, and managerial knowledge in responding to specific health needs of the individual and the community.
10. Deepen and critically evaluate theoretical and empirical knowledge from various disciplinary fields for application to nursing and midwifery care.
11. Assume leadership in professional activities and in interdisciplinary and organizational contexts.
12. Design, evaluate, and manage interventions for the development of professional competencies in basic and continuous training.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences possesses high-level competence in the field of nursing clinical practice and service management. Demonstrates ability to identify and classify health phenomena and issues and propose developments for nursing and midwifery services.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences is able to expertly apply nursing culture in service management with mastery of methods and tools; develops and applies innovative ideas for quality and development of the service and professional offer.
III - Judgment autonomy The Master's graduate in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences is skilled in integrating knowledge to manage complexity, even in multi-professional settings. Uses analytical and review methodologies to produce independent hypotheses and original proposals in planning, implementation, and evaluation of processes, interventions, and outcomes.
IV - Communication skills The Master's graduate in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences is competent in using effective communication in the professional context with various stakeholders. Maintains a professional approach in their activities, demonstrating judgment autonomy and ability to integrate within the multi-professional team.
V - Learning ability The Master's graduate in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences demonstrates the ability to learn and persist in updating professional culture and context, introducing innovation into professional activities.
Workplace function.
Workplace function:
Master's graduates in the LM/SNT1 class are already qualified professionals authorized to practice the professions of Nurse, Pediatric Nurse, or Midwife. The Master's program provides the legal requirement to compete for senior/director roles in services related to health professions. Additionally, the Master's Degree in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences is the requirement to assume the following functions within the reference degree class: technical-practical coordinator, teacher, didactic tutor.

Roles President MARIO GIANNONI Program, Texts and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages. ITALIANO Degree Awarded. Master's Degree in SCIENCES OF HEALTH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROFESSIONS Specific Educational Objectives. Graduates of the Course with a unified path must achieve the following specific educational objectives:

Master's graduates in the Sciences of Health Technical Assistance Professions aim to become holders of advanced cultural and professional training to intervene with high-level competencies in assistance, management, training, and research processes in one of the fields relevant to the various healthcare professions included in the class. Graduates will be able to express advanced assistance, educational, and preventive competencies in response to priority health issues of the pediatric, adult, and geriatric population, as well as quality service issues. Based on acquired knowledge, they will be able to consider, in the programming and management of healthcare staff, both the needs of the community, the development of new work organization methods, technological and information innovations (including tele-assistance or tele-education), and the planning and organization of pedagogical-training interventions, as well as the harmonization of operational standards with those of the European Union. Graduates must develop, following experience gained through appropriate professional activity, an integrated approach to organizational and management issues in healthcare professions, qualified by mastery of healthcare management techniques and procedures, respecting their own and others' competencies.

Management:
- Coordinate simple and complex organizations using tools and measures for planning, human resource management, and accounting in business economics;
- Develop leadership capabilities;
- Identify environmental risk factors, assess their health effects, and plan protective interventions in the workplace;
- Manage work groups and apply appropriate strategies to promote multi-professional and organizational integration;
- Ensure or maintain quality certification;
- Manage technical staff rotation across different functions to enhance staff valorization;
- Collaborate in cost-benefit analysis of various assistance procedures.

Research:
- Conduct systematic bibliographic research, including through databases and their periodic updates;
- Perform literature reviews, including systematic reviews, aimed at producing scientific articles;
- Collaborate in quantitative and qualitative research projects.

Professional:
- Verify the application of research results for continuous improvement of healthcare activities;
- Practice in compliance with key legislative norms governing healthcare organization, as well as ethical and professional responsibility norms;
- Collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines;
- Design and develop automation in assistance processes while safeguarding the specific professionalism of individual operators;
- Develop proposals to enhance patient and operator safety.

Training:
- Promote technical staff updates by fostering dynamics that enhance productivity without inducing demotivation or dequalification among professionals;
- Manage continuous training and updates for healthcare staff;
- Participate in and observe management, conduct, and programming processes for bachelor's, master's, and first and second-level master's programs;
- Design and implement, in collaboration with other professionals, educational and supportive interventions for individuals and communities to manage risk factors and health issues.

The course aims to provide conceptual and methodological models for the four competency areas of the Master's graduate.

Professional Area:
- Communicate clearly on organizational and healthcare issues with colleagues and users;
- Critically analyze ethical and professional aspects of healthcare professions from a multi-professional integration perspective.

Management Area:
- Apply principles and methods of healthcare economics and planning, administrative and labor law;
- Deepen leadership and service management strategies, including human resource management, organizational integration tools, and quality performance evaluation.

Training Area:
- Develop pedagogical models, enhance teaching capabilities for specific professional roles within tutorial and internship coordination in complementary and ongoing basic training;
- Deepen the design and management of basic and advanced training systems, teaching methods, and group training management to activate specific training events for technical healthcare professions.

Research Area:
- Understand statistical methods to apply them within healthcare research contexts.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Master's graduates must be able to:
- Interpret epidemiological and experimental statistical data to analyze complex phenomena and problems in healthcare and technical healthcare professions;
- Analyze the organization of healthcare systems, particularly European ones, programming and funding modalities, and service organization;
- Interpret principles of healthcare, administrative, and labor law to understand their application in managing healthcare services, work processes, and professional relationships;
- Possess knowledge and skills to create effective learning environments in professional contexts and training settings, both basic and advanced, and in continuing education;
- Deepen teaching and tutorial methodologies to implement teaching strategies based on educational theories and evidence-based practices;
- Possess knowledge to analyze training needs of technical healthcare professions, formulate learning objectives, select appropriate learning activities, design, and implement training paths relevant to the professional context;
- Apply knowledge of work psychology and sociology to understand the complexity of work processes in healthcare organizations, necessary integration systems, and multi-professional interactions in healthcare.

Knowledge and understanding will be acquired through attending lectures, role-playing, problem-solving, exercises, seminars, and guided and independent personal study.

Assessment of learning outcomes will primarily occur through oral and/or written exams, in-course or final written assignments with in-depth analysis of acquired knowledge.

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Master's graduates must be able to:
- Apply theoretical, operational, and research models within technical healthcare professions;
- Apply evidence-based practice methodology to evaluate effectiveness;
- Use effectiveness and efficiency indicators to analyze ethical, legal, and professional implications in work practice;
- Take responsibility for the quality of their professional practice;
- Apply knowledge to analyze work processes in healthcare organizations, personnel management strategies, and professional accreditation systems to promote team integration in services for achieving safe, effective, and efficient performance;
- Harmonize contributions from different professions engaged in technical assistance;
- Apply evidence-based guidelines to make decisions;
- Apply leadership and management theories to develop collaborative alliances between different healthcare professions in their work context;
- Apply pedagogical knowledge to conduct teaching, tutoring, and training design activities;
- Critically evaluate scientific articles, consult and manage databases, and conduct periodic updates;
- Manage information systems for services, acquiring IT skills.

Teaching tools aimed at achieving these abilities include lectures, problem-solving, small group practical activities, seminars, and individual study.

These abilities will be assessed through written and/or oral certification exams and practical tests.

III - Judgment Autonomy Master's graduates must be able to:
- Demonstrate the ability to make decisions, express functional and assistance judgments through reflective practice;
- Predict and evaluate the effects of their decisions and activities, assuming the consequent responsibility;
- Participate in research activities to understand or contribute to technical assistance advancements;
- Formulate independent reflections through multidisciplinary scientific, legal, ethical, and professional discussions.

Teaching tools aimed at achieving these abilities include student essays presenting the phases of building an intervention project in technical assistance, demonstrating the ability to analyze, manage, and interpret data with autonomy and competent logic.

IV - Communication Skills Master's graduates must be able to:
- Apply language analysis and communication style skills to provide appropriate information to users of all ages and their families within the technical assistance process and/or with other healthcare professionals in appropriate verbal, non-verbal, and written forms;
- Communicate effectively with verbal, non-verbal, and written methods to convey evaluations and decisions in interdisciplinary technical assistance teams, considering the specificities of different professional roles;
- Demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing;
- Demonstrate basic communication skills and appropriate attitudes for conducting training, teaching, and instruction activities for the assisted population, healthcare professionals, and students at various levels;
- Implement educational interventions for individuals, families, and groups to promote healthy behaviors;
- Recognize and respect individual and cultural differences in all professional interaction moments.

Knowledge and understanding mentioned above will be acquired through attending lectures, exercises, seminars, and guided and independent personal study.

Written and oral communication skills, including in English, will be particularly developed during internship activities and through classroom presentations of individually or group-developed assignments.

Assessment of these skills occurs through in-course evaluations of case presentations and situations performed by students in plenary sessions. Final assessment is based on a written thesis followed by an oral discussion of the objectives achieved, supported by IT equipment.

V - Learning Ability Master's graduates must be able to:
- Evaluate their performance based on professional practice standards and organizational criteria, continuously identifying their educational needs in relation to the nature and complexity of problems to address and the strategies to manage, to realize their professional improvement plan;
- Independently adopt effective strategies for continuous learning throughout their professional life, both formally and informally, through further training paths;
- Use information systems, software, and complete databases to collect, organize, and catalog information; identify a problem, conduct a literature review on the topic, critically analyze the problem and current knowledge, develop a strategy to apply research in practice, and facilitate the dissemination of research results;
- Attend further advanced training paths oriented toward research, healthcare management, and educational methodology.

These abilities are acquired through frontal activities, internships, seminars, and in-depth projects and individual study activities within research methodology and thesis preparation.

Assessment of these abilities occurs through the development of a problem, data collection and evaluation based on the assigned context, and critical analysis of relevant scientific publications.

They may find employment in programming and managing healthcare staff, developing new work organization methods, and coordinating technical practice activities of bachelor's degrees. Acquired methodological knowledge enables intervention in specific training and research processes of the class.

Master's Degree in SCIENCES OF DIAGNOSTIC HEALTH TECHNICAL PROFESSIONS
Specific Educational Objectives.
The educational objectives are achieved through an advanced path aimed at providing knowledge/skills in the following disciplinary areas, with particular reference to the training of the specific professional figure in the technical-diagnostic field:
-biomedical, biological, medical, and surgical sciences (with in-depth study of related disciplines, such as biochemistry, clinical biochemistry, and clinical molecular biology, anatomy and histology, general pathology),
-biomedical laboratory sciences and techniques, medical imaging radiology and radiotherapy, neurophysiopathology and audiological sciences (with in-depth study of related disciplines, such as clinical pathology, pathological anatomy, biomedical laboratory sciences, imaging diagnostics and radiotherapy, neuroradiology, applied medical sciences, locomotor system diseases, nursing sciences, neuropsychiatric and rehabilitative techniques, otorhinolaryngology, audiology),
-legal, economic, and healthcare management sciences (with in-depth study of related disciplines, such as law, economics, business, general and applied hygiene),
-prevention sciences and healthcare services (with in-depth study of related disciplines, such as internal medicine and legal medicine),
-preliminary, computer, statistical, and demographic sciences (with in-depth study of related disciplines, such as computer science, information processing systems, and medical statistics),
-human, psychopedagogical, and anthropological sciences (with in-depth study of related disciplines, such as psychology and sociology of cultural and communication processes).
The training activity is primarily structured into integrated courses, aimed at providing a unified and, at the same time, multidisciplinary approach to achieve the objectives. Teaching methods include various types of activities (e.g., lectures, seminars/conferences, discussion groups, internship).
At the end of the program, the graduate will be able to:
-apply biological, medical, and biomedical knowledge/skills to the professional field of diagnostic health technical sciences;
-apply, within healthcare structures, the technical knowledge/skills relevant to the specific professional figure and appropriate for making decisions regarding the organization and management of healthcare services provided by technical-diagnostic personnel;
-understand the actions of healthcare personnel in their global dimension, i.e., ethical, social, and moral;
-contribute to the design and implementation of systems for the processing of scientific data, as well as their management and utilization in various healthcare application contexts;
-utilize, for the organization of healthcare services and management of available human and technological resources, the necessary skills in healthcare economics and business organization, also evaluating cost/benefit ratios;
-employ, in the area of healthcare service organization, methods and tools of research;
-plan and improve activities aimed at enhancing the resources (human, technological, informational, financial) available in healthcare structures;
-program and implement training interventions for updating and continuous education related to the reference healthcare structures;
-enhance, within tutorial and internship coordination activities in training, complementary and continuous teaching abilities for the specific professional figure;
-instruct on legal aspects related to normative, administrative, and jurisdictional competencies;
-communicate clearly with colleagues and users on organizational and healthcare aspects.
EDUCATIONAL PATH The educational path, conducted over 2 years with 120 ECTS, is designed to provide knowledge/skills in the fields of biological and biomedical sciences, technical-diagnostic sciences; legal, economic, and management sciences; prevention and healthcare services sciences; statistical, demographic, and computer sciences, particularly applied to healthcare management; psychology and sociology, as well as the principles of professional discipline, which are required to undertake internship experiences aimed at acquiring competencies in the reference sectors (e.g., laboratory medicine sciences and applied medical sciences), as well as guiding students toward their professional fields. Specialist in-depth activities are also provided, particularly for acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice, teamwork in complex organizational contexts, and scientific research methods to support the final thesis.
During the two years, optional training activities (AFO) are also available for student choice, as well as other training activities divided into further activities (e.g., laboratory or computer-based) and acquisition of English language skills at B2 level.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The graduate must be able to demonstrate knowledge in various disciplinary areas, aimed at in-depth study and understanding:
-of the organization of the organism, fundamental pathogenic and biological defense processes, interpretation of main pathogenic mechanisms and diagnostic method results;
-of health determinants, dangers, and risk factors, prevention strategies, protection systems, interventions to safeguard health and safety, organization of the National Health Service, importance and utility of acting in compliance with regulations and guidelines, also in relation to bioethical issues connected to research and experimentation,
-of techniques and methodologies used in different medical sectors (laboratory, imaging diagnostics, neuroscience, and otorhinolaryngology) for diagnostic purposes and interpretation of the clinical significance of results, risk management methods, structural and functional organization of technical-diagnostic services, data processing methods, human resource management for service optimization, methods of accessing and using scientific information for research activities,
-of psychological mechanisms and related study methods, associated with sociological knowledge of cultural and communication processes for understanding work relationships, integration areas, and interdependence with other operators, professional autonomy in healthcare, also in relation to service users,
-of computer science methods and data processing systems applied to healthcare service management, networks, main statistical methods, correction models, statistical models for epidemiological analysis,
-of the English language, aimed at understanding international scientific literature in the reference field.
Internship is provided, supervised by a tutor, in healthcare structures contracted with the University or university laboratories/structures. Optional training activities and other student-choice activities are also provided.
Teaching Tools, Methodologies, and Training Activities to Develop Expected Outcomes:
-lectures; -guided reading and application; -demonstrations, diagrams, and graphic materials; -construction of cognitive maps; -case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; -exercises and simulations; -internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes:
-written and oral exams, staged case tests, project work, reports; -structured objective station exam; -class discussions; -evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and professional practice reports).
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The graduate in Sciences of Diagnostic Health Technical Professions:
-uses biological, medical, and biomedical knowledge in relation to the human organism within the specific work context;
-applies methodological and technical-diagnostic skills for managing subsequent phases of the analytical process in the fields of Laboratory Medicine, Imaging Diagnostics and Radiotherapy, Neuroscience, and Otorhinolaryngology;
-applies hygienic-preventive knowledge to prevention and collective/individual protection strategies; legal and organizational knowledge to the management of healthcare services, particularly technical-diagnostic services; statistical and computer knowledge to statistical methods and data processing, specifically in the healthcare context;
-uses psychosocial disciplinary knowledge for analyzing psychological and social mechanisms underlying communication processes in the workplace and interaction with users;
-integrates knowledge and skills by collaborating to maintain high quality and safety standards in various technical-diagnostic healthcare disciplines;
-utilizes English language for understanding scientific literature and updating, also internationally, in the field of technical-diagnostic services.
Teaching Tools, Methodologies, and Training Activities to Develop Expected Outcomes:
-lectures; -guided reading and application; -demonstrations, diagrams, and graphic materials; -construction of cognitive maps; -case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; -exercises and simulations; -internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes:
-written and oral exams, staged case tests, project work, reports; -structured objective station exam; -class discussions; -evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and professional practice reports).
III - Judgment Autonomy The graduate in Sciences of Diagnostic Health Technical Professions:
-demonstrates ability to account for one's actions during professional practice in accordance with the professional profile;
-uses critical thinking to deliver effective technical-diagnostic performances;
-assumes responsibility for one's actions in relation to work activity goals and priorities;
-demonstrates ability to consider other operators in the exercise of one's actions;
-applies ethical principles in professional behavior.
Teaching Tools, Methodologies, and Training Activities to Develop Expected Outcomes:
-case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; -internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility; -debriefing sessions to reflect on and reprocess professional practice experiences.
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes:
-written and oral exams, staged case tests; -evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice); -structured objective station exam.
IV - Communication Skills The graduate in Sciences of Diagnostic Health Technical Professions:
-employs listening and appropriate communication skills with users and various healthcare professionals using different communication forms: written, verbal, and non-verbal;
-establishes effective relationships with other professionals;
-demonstrates ability to transmit and manage information within one's work context;
-demonstrates ability to use information and computer technologies in one's work context;
-establishes professional and collaborative relationships with other healthcare professionals, aware of the specificities of different professional roles.
Teaching Tools, Methodologies, and Training Activities to Develop Expected Outcomes:
-videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives, and testimonials; -case and relational situation discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; -internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and debriefing sessions to reflect on and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes:
-observation of film or written frames, dialogues with structured grids; -evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports); -structured objective station exam with simulations on relational skills.
V - Learning Ability The graduate in Sciences of Diagnostic Health Technical Professions:
-demonstrates ability in self-assessment of one's skills and outlines personal development and learning needs;
-exhibits proficiency in planning, organizing, and developing one's actions;
-demonstrates ability in collaborative learning and sharing knowledge within work teams;
-develops independent study skills;
-demonstrates ability to seek necessary information to resolve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, critically selecting secondary sources (guidelines, systematic reviews) and primary sources (research studies).
Teaching Tools, Methodologies, and Training Activities to Develop Expected Outcomes:
-problem-based learning (PBL); -use of cognitive maps; -use of self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment; -research methodology workshops for printed and online literature; -guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes:
-project work, reports on specific research mandates; -tutor supervision of the internship path; -active participation in work and debriefing sessions; -adherence to deadlines and quality in the presentation of deliverables.
Work Context Function.
Work Context Function:
Master's graduates in Sciences of Diagnostic Health Technical Professions develop, following experience gained through professional practice, an integrated approach to organizational and management problems of healthcare professions, characterized by mastery of healthcare management techniques and procedures. Activities are expressed through the coordination of simple and complex organizations, using tools and measures for planning, human resource management, accounting in business economics; development of leadership capacity; identification of risk factors to assess their effects on health and implement protection interventions in work environments; management of work groups and application of appropriate strategies to promote multiprofessional and organizational integration processes; care for achieving and maintaining quality certification; organization of technical staff rotation between different functions to enhance their value; collaboration in cost/benefit analysis processes of various care procedures.
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Competencies Associated with the Function:
Verify the application of research activity results for continuous improvement of healthcare activities; operate in compliance with main legislative norms regulating healthcare organization as well as professional ethical and responsibility norms; collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines; design and develop automation in care processes while safeguarding the specific professionalism of each operator; develop proposals to increase patient and operator safety; ensure technical staff updates, promoting dynamics among various professionals that enhance productivity without inducing demotivation or dequalification; ensure continuous training and updates for healthcare staff; observe and participate in management, conduct, and programming processes of degree or master's courses; design and implement, in collaboration with other professionals, educational and support interventions for self-management and control of risk factors and health issues for individuals and communities; communicate clearly regarding organizational and healthcare issues with colleagues and users; critically analyze ethical and professional aspects of healthcare professions from a multi-professional integration perspective; apply principles and methods of healthcare economics and planning, deepen legal aspects (e.g., administrative and labor law); deepen leadership and management strategies for human resource services, organizational integration tools, and performance quality evaluation; develop pedagogical models, enhance teaching skills for the specific professional figure within tutorial and internship coordination activities in complementary and continuous basic training; deepen the design and management of basic and advanced training systems, teaching methods, and training group management to activate specific training events for health technical professions.

The acquired methodological knowledge also enables intervention in specific training and research processes of the class.
