ENGLISH Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in MATHEMATICAL ENGINEERING Specific Educational Objectives.
The evolution of the scientific, technological, and economic context requires professional figures capable of addressing increasingly complex problems with an integrated approach between mathematical modeling and the use of computational resources.
The Master's Degree in Mathematical Engineering embraces this challenge and aims to train graduates with a broadly multidisciplinary profile and characterized by a solid theoretical-methodological preparation in mathematical modeling and scientific computing.
The solid theoretical training will be accompanied and made concrete through knowledge and experience in at least one application domain, within engineering or sciences, and integrated with the ability to communicate and interact with experts in engineering, physical and natural sciences, economics, and social sciences. Internships and thesis work at research laboratories and companies will constitute an additional element of training, allowing the practical application of problem-solving skills developed and knowledge acquired.
The specific educational objectives of the study path are as follows:
- Ability to flexibly and rigorously address complex problems in a multidisciplinary context through the construction of mathematical models and their numerical resolution using computational resources for scientific computing;
- Ability to evaluate which resolution techniques and computational and technological tools to use, developing an engineering approach aimed at solving a problem in the most efficient way possible;
- Ability to communicate and interact with experts in at least one application domain, understanding the main issues and specific terminology.
Graduates of this program will have a training that enables them to successfully enter the business world or continue studies in a research doctorate in modeling and computational fields.
The courses offered during the program are organized into various areas:
- Theoretical Training: Completion of foundational mathematical and engineering training;
- Mathematical Modeling, aimed at deducing, from the application problem, the appropriate mathematical model for describing the phenomenon and analyzing the solutions from qualitative and quantitative perspectives;
- Numerical Simulation, focused on describing approximation and numerical integration methods and methodologies for representing numerical solutions;
- Scientific Computing: Courses in this area will provide knowledge on hardware and software technology for scientific computing, advanced and parallel programming, management of large data volumes, as well as efficient algorithm design.
- Applications: Courses will be provided in various application areas, both introductory to the issues of the area and applying the acquired methodological knowledge to such areas.
The study paths will emphasize different aspects of methodology, creating professional profiles more focused on scientific computing or more oriented towards modeling in engineering and sciences. In the second year, students will acquire knowledge in a specific application domain proposed by the course and the ability to apply methodological tools in that domain, both through specific courses and through internship and thesis work.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the educational process, students will have acquired:
- A deep knowledge and clear understanding of the methodological foundations of Mathematical Engineering;
- A taste for study and the ability to generally apply the principles and methods of Mathematics and Physics;
- Sensitivity to adapt their application to the specific difficulties of the problem to be solved, the desired solution accuracy, technological aspects, and the sustainable time and financial investment.
The methodological training and necessary information to enable students to acquire the above knowledge are distributed in a coordinated and progressive manner within the courses and other educational activities proposed by the study program. In particular, the methodological foundations and principles of mathematics and physics are acquired within the mathematical, physical, and computer science disciplines (Mathematical Analysis, Numerical Analysis, Mathematical Physics), while aspects related to their application in concrete problems are more extensively treated within engineering disciplines (Automatic Control, Information Processing Systems, Fluid Dynamics) and more application-oriented mathematical disciplines, particularly in the field of Numerical Analysis. The verification of knowledge and understanding is conducted in an integrated manner within all the profit assessments provided during the study program.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the educational process, students will have acquired the ability to:
- Design/develop models, both through courses related to mathematical disciplines (Mathematical Analysis, Mathematical Physics) and through engineering disciplines, particularly in the field of Fluid Dynamics;
- Manage complex systems, particularly through courses in the fields of Automatic Control and Information Processing Systems;
- Formulate and solve problems in new and emerging areas of specialization, particularly in aspects related to scientific computing and "big data," through courses in the fields of Numerical Analysis and Information Processing Systems;
- Perform a connecting role between traditional engineering professionals and experts in other disciplines, thanks in particular to the coexistence within the study path of basic training activities in mathematical disciplines with an eye toward their possible applications, and engineering training activities with a strong modeling focus.
The verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through written and/or oral exams provided for profit assessments, particularly through exam exercises in disciplines that include a project activity, and for other educational activities through the final exam.
III - Judgment Skills At the end of the educational process, students will have acquired the ability to manage the complexity typical of problems in Mathematics and Engineering during the development of all design, implementation, and management activities of complex systems. They must therefore be able to formulate critical judgments and evaluations even based on limited or incomplete information.
Specific skills must be developed in the field of design: ability to use their knowledge to design solutions to complex problems, even little known or interdisciplinary; creative ability for developing innovative and original approaches; ability to interact with social and cultural processes; ability to operate under uncertainty.
Achieving this objective is particularly delegated to the preparation and writing of the final thesis, which must be configured as the result of a personal re-elaboration of the curricular content acquired.
The verification of judgment skills is carried out through written and/or oral exams provided for profit assessments, particularly through exam exercises in disciplines that include a project activity, and for other educational activities through the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills At the end of the educational process, students will have developed:
- The ability to clearly and logically communicate process and design choices, as well as the underlying scientific approaches, to mathematical and/or engineering interlocutors;
- The ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects, mathematical and/or engineering, involved in the development of systems of interest;
- Communication skills both towards the international scientific community and towards different social components, even non-experts;
- The ability to coordinate an interdisciplinary team;
- Language skills and knowledge that enable international openness.
These skills are developed during regular educational activities, for some of which a presentation before an interdisciplinary committee is required.
The verification of communication skills is carried out through written and/or oral exams provided for profit assessments and other educational activities, particularly through the final exam.
V - Learning Ability At the end of the educational process, students will have acquired:
- Awareness of the need for continuous learning, to be pursued autonomously throughout their professional career;
- The ability to autonomously acquire new technical and scientific knowledge related to the course topics based on scientific and technical literature in the specific field.
These abilities develop primarily during individual study of the topics covered in lectures and exercises. The preparation of the Master's thesis also involves consulting technical and scientific literature in the field.
The verification of learning abilities is carried out through profit assessments and other educational activities, particularly through the final exam.
Work Context Function.
Work Context Function:
Graduates of Master's Degree programs in this class combine in-depth knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences, with particular reference to physics, with advanced knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of engineering in general.
They possess advanced skills to address experimental, computational, technological, economic, and epistemological problems related to the construction, validation, and use of models; they are therefore capable of using such knowledge and skills to identify, interpret, describe, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems. They are also equipped with knowledge in the field of business organization (business culture) and professional ethics.
Associated Skills for the Function.
Associated Skills for the Function:
Advanced innovation and design, particularly regarding the definition and validation of models and calculation procedures, with particular reference to one or more technological sectors. Graduates in Mathematical Engineering can perform high-responsibility functions in development and design centers, public and private, in advanced technological sectors of industry, computing laboratories, and companies providing data processing and development of numerical calculation codes for industry.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Career Prospects:
The main career opportunities include:
- Engineering companies engaged in both consulting and research and development activities;
- Companies or public bodies managing services;
- Manufacturing companies producing and integrating complex systems;
- Software companies dedicated to modeling and simulation;
- Research institutes and laboratories in the fields of engineering and applied mathematics.

Roles Study Plan Approval Coordinator LAURA TARANTINO, MATTIA D'EMIDIO, GIACOMO VALENTE President LAURA TARANTINO Programme, Texts, and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages. ENGLISH Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's Degree Course in Computer Engineering aims to create highly qualified professionals for the analysis, design, implementation, and management of computer systems, applications, and services based on the use of highly complex technologies, through the application of the most modern tools. Consequently, this course enables the acquisition of a solid preparation capable of fully responding to the continuous innovation needs that require a high degree of specialization and, if necessary, an interdisciplinary approach.
To appropriately pursue the specific educational objectives, the Study Course is structured into curricula that provide distinctive competencies for the training of various professional profiles, representing distinct variations of a unified project.
Specifically, the unified project aims to provide the following common competencies and abilities to all curricula: analysis, design, implementation, and management of computer systems, applications, and services based on the use of highly complex technologies, based on the Internet and the Web, robotics, and artificial intelligence, through the use of the most modern tools. Additionally:
- as a designer within the information technology field, the Computer Engineering graduate will possess deep knowledge and understanding of topics such as: design and implementation of enterprise information systems, automation of services in public and private entities, design of architectures and networked information systems;
- as a designer within the computer engineering field, the Computer Engineering graduate will possess deep knowledge and understanding of topics such as: design of dedicated (embedded) hardware/software (HW/SW) systems and systems with close interaction with the external environment (cyber-physical), advanced architectures of information processing systems, design and analysis of high-performance and/or low-energy consumption processing systems.
The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering is therefore able to understand, use, and innovate the most advanced computer technologies (HW/SW), and is thus capable of both mastering the increasingly rapid developments in the ICT sector and applying their knowledge to the numerous application fields where computer technologies can be utilized. Indeed, such graduates possess a thorough preparation in engineering sciences and basic sciences, enriched by specific computer knowledge and appropriate design capabilities, enabling them to interact with specialists from various sectors.
DESCRIPTION OF THE STUDY PATH The Study Course offers instruction in English and is structured into curricula. It includes a core of common characteristic courses applicable to all curricula, representing the fundamental characteristics of the Computer Engineer professional profile. Specifically, each curriculum includes additional characteristic courses specific to that curriculum, a set of related and integrative courses, typically methodological and foundational with a broad scope, to allow a comprehensive engineering perspective on problems, and finally a set of elective courses to enable flexible and interdisciplinary in-depth study of the most interesting topics.
In particular:
- the common core of characteristic courses provides competencies on aspects such as: design methodologies, specifically focused on innovation, fundamentals of algorithms and data structures, software engineering, development infrastructures, databases;
- the in-depth studies targeted at the information technology profile provide additional competencies on aspects such as: algorithm engineering, big data processing, distributed systems, methods and measures for Information Technology, software development technologies;
- the in-depth studies targeted at the computer engineering profile provide additional competencies on aspects such as: embedded systems and automation topics, such as system identification, data analysis, and modeling of hybrid systems;
- the mathematical in-depth studies, appropriate for each curriculum, enable the acquisition of necessary competencies on aspects such as: mathematical modeling of real problems, coding methodologies for information transmission and protection, discrete optimization, evaluation of problem-solving algorithms;
- the engineering in-depth studies, appropriate for each curriculum, are predominantly focused on electronics and telecommunications, providing competencies on aspects such as: analysis and design of digital circuits, telecommunications networks, wireless communication, cybersecurity, cloud computing, Internet of Things;
- the computer science in-depth studies cover more formal aspects related to: artificial intelligence, machine learning, software architecture, and software quality.
Finally, it is emphasized that the Computer Engineering Study Course is characterized by a strong presence of practical, project-based, and laboratory activities, which constitute a fundamental, defining, and indispensable element, prioritizing an interdisciplinary approach. The Study Course also offers the possibility to complete internships, traineeships, and theses at companies and public and private administrations, including research and technological institutions. These activities are an integral and qualifying part of the educational path and facilitate the transfer of skills from the University to companies and public and private administrations.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The Master's graduate of this Study Course must possess knowledge and understanding of the main methodologies, even advanced, necessary to correctly describe and model engineering-type problems requiring solutions typical of a Computer Engineering expert. Such knowledge is initially provided by an adequate number of courses in the characteristic fields. The knowledge is complemented by further courses selectable in the related engineering fields. In particular, the emphasis placed on the ability to formulate problems rigorously using the most appropriate mathematical models has led to the inclusion of applied mathematical content in the Study Course. Moreover, to allow students a full understanding of typical issues within the entire ICT field, various contents offered by related courses in the ING-INF and INF fields are included in the study plan. Additional credits in free-choice subjects allow students to deepen the engineering topics they find most interesting and consistent with their desired professional profile.
Students also have the opportunity to choose various types of professional seminars conducted by industry professionals or external lecturers, where the understanding acquired during the studies is tested on specific professional topics.
The verification of knowledge and understanding is conducted in an integrated manner within the framework of all assessment methods provided by the individual courses.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The Master's graduate of this Study Course, based on the chosen curriculum, will be able to apply the acquired knowledge to achieve the following objectives:
- to formulate real problems using mathematical models, and to identify the most suitable model for the problem at hand;
- to apply knowledge related to modern design, development, and implementation methodologies for software systems, including both established and emerging technologies, for managing the entire development lifecycle, quality monitoring, and maintainability;
- to design, develop, and validate dedicated ("embedded") systems and information systems based on joint hardware/software (HW/SW) design techniques;
- to create user-system interaction environments, having full knowledge of human-computer interaction issues;
- to create information systems that include interconnected components, computer networks, and intelligent, robotic, and/or autonomous entities;
- to design and implement web/mobile/cloud-based applications;
- to design, implement, and experimentally validate efficient, centralized, and distributed algorithms for computational problems of various types;
- to engineer algorithms and computing systems in relation to performance, scalability, and processing of heterogeneous and massive data, also considering big-data analysis and processing techniques, as well as machine learning and artificial intelligence methodologies;
- to design and maintain complex databases, knowing the main technologies for fault-tolerance and distribution support;
- to manage cybersecurity issues related to heterogeneous information systems.
These objectives are achieved by providing solid methodological foundations through more theoretical courses, as well as by having students work on project-based activities through a certain number of courses that include practical examination types. In such courses, students, working in groups, conduct project activities involving the realization or computer simulation of algorithms, complex software systems based on different technologies and architectural types, interactive systems, complex databases, and dedicated hardware/software systems. Additionally, within these activities, students experience group work dynamics and are trained in writing technical reports and presenting the results obtained. This allows students to enrich typical engineering hard skills with highly applicable soft skills in the workplace context.
III - Judgmental Autonomy Thanks to solid methodological preparation and laboratory activities, graduates will acquire the ability to analyze the results of project experiments and simulations, and to evaluate both the suitability of models and/or procedures in the application context and the impact of the conceived information solutions, regarding technical aspects, organizational aspects, ethical implications, and potential socio-economic reflections. These abilities will enable them to interact with other professional figures, even in interdisciplinary contexts, and to make decisions to solve problems that may arise in the field of Computer Engineering in line with the chosen path.
The achievement of this objective occurs through individual and group study, participation in laboratory project activities, writing reports on project activities, and the work of preparation and writing of the final thesis, which must be the result of personal re-elaboration of the acquired curricular content.
The verification of judgmental autonomy is carried out through individual or group reports (particularly in the context of disciplines that include project activities) and written and/or oral examinations provided for the courses, and for other educational activities, through the final examination.
IV - Communication Skills The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering must acquire the appropriate language to express issues in the discipline, both at a general and specialist level, and, more generally, communication skills that enable:
- coordinating and participating in project, research, and development groups in the field of Computer Engineering
- effectively interacting with specialists from different application sectors to understand their specific needs in the development of supporting information tools
- planning and conducting training in the field of Computer Engineering
- organizing the results of one's work in an effective communication format
- clearly and comprehensively describing complex technical-scientific solutions and aspects of computer technology, even in forms suitable for dissemination, with particular attention to corporate and social communication. These objectives require the development of technical-scientific writing and oral presentation skills, also using modern multimedia presentation technologies, which are developed throughout the study path within the regular educational activities, through discussion and comparison moments in group work, and refined in seminar activities and project and thesis presentations, as well as during the preparation of the final examination.
The verification of communication skills is carried out through written and/or oral examinations provided for the courses, through project activities and the associated technical reports required in some courses, and for other educational activities, through the final examination, which provides a comprehensive evaluation not only of the content of the work but also of synthesis, communication, and presentation abilities.
The instruction offered in English provides students with continuous linguistic experience preparatory for interaction in professional contexts, even international. The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering thus acquires the ability to understand and express the English language, in written and oral form, at least within their technical-scientific context.
V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering must possess learning abilities that allow them to update and absorb technological innovations in the field of Computer Engineering. In particular, they must be able to autonomously acquire new specialized technical knowledge from the scientific and technical literature of the field, both within the topics deepened in the study path and in other areas of Computer Engineering, in response to various application needs.
Such learning abilities develop during individual study of the topics covered in lectures and exercises, as well as through laboratory activities, carried out individually and/or in groups.
The verification of learning abilities is carried out through written and/or oral examinations provided for the courses and other educational activities, through project activities and the associated technical reports required in some courses, and through the final examination. The development of the thesis, in particular, involves autonomous processing of the technical and scientific literature of the field.
Professional Role in the Workplace.
Professional Role in the Workplace:
The Computer Engineer trained by this Study Course possesses a high professional qualification and a profound foundational culture, with an aptitude for innovation, multidisciplinary work, and creativity. These competencies enable them to play an active and critical role in the evolution of information processing systems, computer technology, and its applications, meeting the needs and challenges of a rapidly evolving society, supporting and promoting change with awareness of technology's impact on the socio-economic context.
This professional figure will therefore be able to both understand technological evolution in the field and contribute to it, and will be capable of performing functions of analysis, design, development, and validation of complex/innovative software applications and systems, both in centralized and distributed environments, and for both fixed and mobile devices.
The Computer Engineer is, first and foremost, a designer of devices and systems, with an aptitude for creating hardware and software systems that find applications in industry and the public and private service sectors. They can design and implement integrated hardware and software systems for a wide range of dedicated applications (e.g., embedded applications). They are able to adopt modern methodologies and technologies for the design of information processing systems and their data models; for the design of interactive applications that optimize usability and user experience; for intelligent systems and decision support systems; for web-services projects and necessary architectures. They can design, implement, analyze, and engineer efficient computational algorithms, even for highly complex problems. They are able to develop: applications that leverage modern cloud architectures for big-data processing and storage; mobile and pervasive applications. They possess knowledge to appropriately evaluate and integrate available technologies for system and service implementation. They are able to apply information security principles in the design of devices and systems. They can carry out research activities in the fields of information and communication technologies (ICT).
Associated Competencies.
The Master's Degree in Computer Engineering provides advanced competencies in the design and implementation of information processing systems in their broadest sense, with specific skills in the use of innovative technologies, evaluation of adequacy from the perspective of computational performance, maintainability, usability, scalability, and security of the systems themselves.
In particular, the course provides specific competencies in the following areas:
- software design: knowledge of design, development, and implementation methodologies for software systems, including both established and emerging technologies, for managing the entire development lifecycle, quality monitoring, and maintainability;
- design, development, and validation of dedicated ("embedded") systems and information systems based on joint hardware/software (HW/SW) design techniques;
- creation of user-system interaction environments, knowledge of human-computer interaction issues;
- implementation of information systems that include interconnected components, computer networks, and intelligent, robotic, and/or autonomous entities;
- design, development, and testing of web/mobile/cloud-based applications;
- analysis and understanding of the structural design, quality, and performance of complex information systems;
- design, implementation, and experimental evaluation of efficient, centralized, and distributed algorithms for computational problems of various types;
- engineering of algorithms and computing systems, evaluation of issues related to performance, scalability, and processing and storage of heterogeneous and massive data;
- analysis and processing of big-data, application of machine learning and artificial intelligence methodologies;
- design of cloud-based information systems capable of leveraging modern parallel and cluster-based computing infrastructures;
- designing and maintaining complex databases, knowing the main technologies for fault-tolerance and distribution support.
- management of cybersecurity issues related to heterogeneous information systems.
Professional Title Awarded.
Employment Opportunities:
The Master's graduate in Computer Engineering can perform the various duties indicated above, also in a coordinating role. Such functions can be carried out in manufacturing or service companies, public administrations, in free profession, or in self-initiated entrepreneurial activities, in research centers.
Professional figures in the field of Computer Engineering appear in numerous statistics as highly sought after and well-paid in the industrial sector, both nationally and internationally. Indeed, recent ISTAT employment rates three years after graduation (AlmaLaurea data, 2020) reveal that 100% are employed (94% working, 4% pursuing doctoral/master's courses). An excellent employment condition thus emerges.

Program, Texts, and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's Degree course in Management Engineering offered by the University of L'Aquila, in accordance with the Qualifying Educational Objectives of its Degree Class, is characterized by specific educational objectives through a common section (including the majority of CFU for characteristic and related/interdisciplinary training activities) and two distinct curricula that allow a specialized approach in terms of designing production and logistics systems for the first and managing production, organizational, and logistics systems for the second.
The specific educational objectives and descriptions of the areas of specialization related to the common section and the two curricula are described below.
Regarding the common section, it aims to achieve the following educational objectives:
a) analyze, interpret, and describe complex problems in companies based on an interdisciplinary perspective that involves sharing approaches, tools, and techniques from both characteristic scientific disciplines (Technology and Processing Systems, Mechanical Industrial Plants, and Economic-Management Engineering) and related/interdisciplinary fields (Mechanical and Thermal Measurements, Information Processing Systems);
b) identify and implement innovative technical, organizational, and management solutions based on an interdisciplinary approach to complex issues typical of Management Engineering, with particular focus on manufacturing companies;
c) consider technological, sectoral, organizational, and management contextual factors during analysis, definition of alternatives, selection of the best option, and its implementation;
d) possess advanced knowledge in analyzing and evaluating company costs as a support for decision-making processes based on technical, technological, organizational, and management variables;
e) have adequate knowledge of production and logistics systems and organizational and logistics processes to enable further specialization in one of the proposed curricula.
The educational objectives of the common section are achieved through a combination of courses related to characteristic and related/interdisciplinary fields. Specifically, referring to the first (characteristic fields), topics related to operations management and supply chain management are distributed between the first and second year of the Master's Degree course, while topics related to decision-making alternative evaluation based on advanced costing systems are concentrated in the second year. In the first year, there is also an in-depth study of industrial quality management to promote a more comprehensive interdisciplinary vision. Regarding the related/interdisciplinary fields, the focus is on topics related to creating and managing databases and managing industrial instrumentation.
Regarding the first of the two curricula, it is specifically focused on the design of production and logistics systems, therefore, building on the educational objectives of the common section previously described, it enables the achievement of the following specific educational objectives:
a) develop the ability to design complex systems through innovative solutions derived from interdisciplinary approaches integrating some of the characteristic scientific disciplines (Technology and Processing Systems and Mechanical Industrial Plants) with related/interdisciplinary fields (particularly Mechanical and Thermal Measurements);
b) develop advanced theoretical and experimental capabilities in simulating and validating projects related to production and logistics systems.
To achieve these specific objectives, courses related to the learning areas of processing technology (including more innovative ones, such as additive manufacturing) and industrial plant safety are provided in both years of the course. Integrating the competencies from the common section learning areas with those described above allows for the development of the ability to design production and logistics systems and validate them, even through simulation.
The curriculum focused on managing production, organizational, and logistics systems in manufacturing and service companies adds to the educational objectives of the common section the following elements:
a) develop the ability to analyze, evaluate, and select alternatives and implement innovative management solutions based on an interdisciplinary approach grounded in some of the characteristic scientific disciplines (Mechanical Industrial Plants and Economic-Management Engineering) and related/interdisciplinary fields (particularly Information Processing Systems);
b) develop the ability to design and implement simulations of integrated management solutions that specifically consider human resource dimensions and environmental sustainability management.
The additional educational objectives pursued within this second curriculum are achieved through the inclusion, in the first and second years of the Master's Degree course, of additional courses related to economic-management topics, with particular focus on financial management, human resources, and environmental sustainability. Integrating the content of these courses with those in the common section enables the development of competencies to identify innovative management solutions and implement them after simulating their effects.
Regardless of the chosen curriculum for specialization, the Master's Degree course in Management Engineering offered by the University of L'Aquila promotes fluent use of the English language, taking specific account of the typical terminology of industrial and service companies.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the Course, the student will have acquired primarily:
- knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to data collection and analysis phases;
- knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to evaluating possible alternatives and defining the optimal solution;
- knowledge of methods and techniques for managing production, organizational, and logistics systems;
- knowledge of techniques for processing and validating performance evaluation indicators of management processes;
- knowledge of systems for evaluating the impact of business systems in terms of economic, environmental, and social sustainability.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the Course, the student will have acquired primarily:
- ability to initiate and implement decisions, even in non-deterministic contexts;
- ability to measure, detect, classify, and analyze data necessary to support business decisions;
- ability to develop, implement, and manage organizational, management, production, and technological innovation processes;
- ability to evaluate opportunities for improving the economic, environmental, and social sustainability of production and management systems.
III - Judgment Skills It is noted that the development of judgment skills, communication abilities, and learning capabilities is encouraged through interaction with the instructor and other students during teaching activities. In particular:
- during lectures, students are stimulated to acquire knowledge and understanding;
- during interaction with students, decision-making situations are proposed to develop the ability to understand and identify appropriate solutions;
- during participation in guided exercises and group work, communication and thesis support abilities are developed;
- during preparation of written reports (also in groups), synthesis and application abilities are promoted.
At the end of the training process, the student will be able to formulate independent critical judgments, even based on limited or incomplete information. In this sense, they will consider the priorities they deem most appropriate, either autonomously or in cooperation. In particular, the Master's graduate in Management Engineering:
- is able to retrieve and select the necessary information to resolve a problem involving technological, plant, organizational, and management aspects simultaneously;
- is able to interpret and evaluate the results of an improvement process (product/process innovation, logistics, management control) to be implemented in a company, taking into account the company's specificities (e.g., size, sector, ...);
- has the ability to analyze and decide on high-impact strategic business issues such as production capacity sizing and technical, economic, and financial evaluation of investments;
- is aware of the responsibilities that engineering solutions may have in terms of economic, environmental, and social sustainability.
These abilities will be developed through the analysis of practical cases treated during studies, as well as through the retrieval and processing of information necessary for the preparation of the thesis. The achievement of these abilities will be assessed in the final exams and during the discussion of the final thesis.
IV - Communication Skills At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- ability to communicate clearly and argue with specialists and non-specialists of different cultural backgrounds (technological, organizational, economic) and different levels of business responsibility;
- ability to integrate into work groups, also with coordination functions;
- ability to clearly and effectively present and describe problems and their engineering solutions;
- ability to communicate effectively with industrial sector representatives at both national and international levels.
These abilities are developed during the planned teaching activities and through cooperation and discussion in group activities. The verification of these abilities is assessed in group activities, exams, and the final presentation.
V - Learning Ability At the end of the training process, the student will have acquired:
- awareness of the need for continuous learning, to be pursued autonomously throughout their working life;
- ability to autonomously acquire new knowledge, both technical and scientific, necessary for improving and managing processes and economic aspects.
This ability derives from the consolidated learning methodology acquired during the course of study. The verification of this ability is conducted in exams, in the retrieval and consultation of scientific and technical literature, and in the preparation of the final thesis.
Workplace Function.
Workplace Function:
The Master's Degree course in Management Engineering has been active for twenty years and has trained approximately 500 Master's graduates.
The Master's Degree in Management Engineering formed at the University of L'Aquila has a strong industrial vocation, allowing it to operate in service companies as well, thanks to a general vision of processes and an interdisciplinary and multifunctional approach.
The Management Engineer formed at the University of L'Aquila is able to leverage economic, managerial, and engineering skills to define and implement organizational, operational, and technical business procedures with an integrated vision, making necessary changes to optimize processes (organizational, production, logistics) to balance efficiency, effectiveness, and profitability with an innovation-oriented approach.
Starting from a solid common base of knowledge and skills typical of industrial systems engineering, through the two specific training paths described earlier, the Master's graduate in Management Engineering from the University of L'Aquila can specialize in the design phase of production and logistics systems or in the management of management processes, with particular attention to organizational, production, and logistics processes.
Regarding the design of production and logistics systems, the Master's graduate in Management Engineering from the University of L'Aquila can perform the following tasks:
- design of production systems with particular reference to plant companies;
- design/redesign of logistics systems within manufacturing companies and engineering consulting;
- design/redesign of technological cycles within manufacturing companies, also using innovative production technologies.
Regarding the management of organizational, production, and logistics processes, the Master's graduate in Management Engineering from the University of L'Aquila can perform the following tasks:
- organization and management of production and support activities (e.g., maintenance, production management);
- organization and management of supply chain management activities (e.g., procurement, industrial and distribution logistics);
- design and management of systems for analyzing operational, economic, and financial performance (e.g., management control, financial management);
- design and management of organizational and information systems.
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Competencies Associated with the Function:
The study program is designed to train professionals capable of operating with a high level of specialized skills, even within multidisciplinary teams, in the characteristic fields of Management Engineering, referring to the design and/or management of business systems, whether in the production of goods or the provision of services.
More specifically, Master's graduates who have successfully completed the curriculum related to the design of production and logistics systems will have acquired the following knowledge and competencies enabling them to perform the previously indicated professional roles:
- Knowledge of the principles of production plant design
- Knowledge of production process technologies
- Knowledge of quality management systems in manufacturing companies and services
- Ability to measure, detect, classify, and analyze data necessary to support business decisions
- Ability to analyze and interpret the functioning of complex production systems
- Ability to plan, manage, analyze, and implement new production methodologies aimed at optimizing the operations cycle
- Ability to contribute to the introduction of innovative methodologies in the production field
Regarding Master's graduates who have successfully completed the curriculum related to the management of organizational, production, and logistics systems, they will have acquired the following knowledge and competencies enabling them to perform the previously indicated professional roles:
- Knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to data collection and analysis phases to support the identification of possible alternatives
- Knowledge of decision-making systems with particular attention to evaluating possible alternatives and identifying the optimal solution for managing organizational processes
- Knowledge of management and control systems for operations
- Knowledge of quality management systems in manufacturing companies and services
- Knowledge of systems for detecting, analyzing, and evaluating the performance of organizational processes
- Ability to measure, detect, classify, and analyze data necessary to support business decisions
- Ability to analyze and interpret the functioning of complex management systems
- Ability to address and solve new or less deterministic problems typical of organizational systems in which they are called to operate
- Ability to plan, manage, analyze, and implement new organizational and management methods aimed at optimizing business processes
- Ability to contribute to the introduction of innovative techniques and tools for managing business processes
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
The uniqueness of the Management Engineer, their flexibility and transversality allow for identifying a plurality of sectors and professional roles in which to carry out their duties. Graduates find natural employment in any manufacturing and service company, regardless of the specific sector of activity and company size. Graduates also find employment in consulting firms, public utility service companies (e.g., transportation, healthcare, telecommunications), and public administration. After passing the State Exam and registration with the appropriate register, they can engage in freelance activities. The solid knowledge and skills developed and the interdisciplinary vision acquired during the study path finally enable the Master's graduate in Management Engineering from the University of L'Aquila to pursue entrepreneurial paths even in sectors with a high level of technological innovation.

ITALIAN Degree Awarded. Master's Degree in ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING Specific Educational Objectives. The objective of the Master's Degree Course in Electronic Engineering is to train an Engineer capable of designing and developing advanced electronic technologies and systems, applicable in various contexts. The specific characteristic distinguishing the educational objectives of this Master's Degree is considering electronic systems in their complexity and entirety, also taking into account issues related to the design and realization of their components (both hardware and software). The Master's Degree in Electronic Engineering provides the necessary skills for this professional figure, deepening topics related to information and communication technologies. Thus, the study program, based on the fundamentals of mathematics, physics, computer science, and electronics already possessed by students from their first-level degree, deepens and develops their application potential, directing teaching towards the design and management of electronic systems. Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The Master's Degree Course in Electronic Engineering is founded on the methodological rigor of scientific disciplines. The graduate dedicates significant time to personal study, knows the fundamental aspects of theories, even more recent ones, underlying Electronic Engineering, integrating knowledge acquired during the first-level degree with methodological and theoretical deepening. The graduate must be able to define appropriate models suitable for interpreting and describing problems related to the field of electronics, electromagnetism, and electronic measurements. They must also master the theoretical-scientific aspects of Information Engineering to identify, formulate, and solve innovatively problems related to the collection, processing, storage, and utilization of information in complex and distributed systems using various technologies. The Master's graduate in Electronic Engineering must be able to develop original and innovative technical solutions based on known solutions through scientific literature. In this way, they can effectively contribute to research or project groups, even international ones, operating on topics related to the curriculum and independently develop their thesis. Teaching methods and tools are those described in the educational objectives. Verification of learning outcomes is primarily through written and/or oral exams concluding with a grade, which may include laboratory tests. II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The didactic approach of the Master's Degree Course in Electronic Engineering aims to encourage active participation and autonomous elaboration by students. Therefore, the graduate is able to apply acquired knowledge for analyzing and designing information acquisition and processing systems, which are crucial in today's communication society. In particular, the autonomous elaboration of knowledge is entrusted to personal deepening, to assess the student's mastery of acquired knowledge, enabling them to find appropriate technical solutions for the design, sizing, and maintenance of information systems. Assessments (written and oral exams, reports, and seminar presentations of project works) require students to demonstrate mastery of topics, tools, methodologies, and critical autonomy. The final exam represents the culmination for refining and verifying acquired skills, adding potential insights related to innovation and research. III - Independent Judgment The Master's graduate in Electronic Engineering must have the ability to analyze and design complex systems, evaluating the impact of electronic solutions in the application context, both in technical and organizational aspects. Characteristic courses, particularly those with a more applied and professional focus, allow through individual and group exercises to develop the ability to select, process, and interpret data for analyzing different systems contributing to information processing. Study plans include activities where students can apply theories presented, possibly through comparison with external professionals from companies, agencies, or organizations in the electronics sector. Consequently, relational and teamwork skills, the ability to select relevant information, and awareness of the social and ethical implications of study activities will be developed. The educational objective will be pursued, in particular, through teaching courses and project works, encouraging meetings and discussions with professionals promoted through seminars, conferences, and the Master's thesis. The thesis represents the moment when the student confronts contexts characteristic of Electronic Engineering, autonomously developing original and innovative ideas, taking responsibility for illustrating and supporting their validity during discussion. IV - Communication Skills The Master's graduate in Electronic Engineering must be able to interact with specialists from different application fields to effectively understand the terms of intervention of electronic systems in various contexts. The graduate must be able to clearly and comprehensibly describe technical solutions and aspects of electronic and electromagnetic nature. In particular, they must be able to train collaborators, coordinate, and participate in project groups in the electronics and information industry, plan and conduct training. These objectives will be pursued through regular teaching activities (encouraging active student participation), during assessment (primarily oral and written with open-ended responses), and through group work requiring seminar presentations. Finally, the final exam involves discussing, in a debate with a committee, a thesis developed autonomously under the guidance of a supervisor. In this case, evaluation is not only on the content of the thesis but also on the candidate's synthesis, communication, and presentation skills. V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate in Electronic Engineering, as a result of the didactic approach and methodological rigor of the entire study program, is able to autonomously acquire new technical-scientific knowledge related to the course topics, starting from technical-scientific literature in the specific field of Information Engineering. Verification of learning abilities will be an integral part of individual exam assessments and the final exam. Function in the Workplace. Function in a workplace: The main functions performed by the Master's graduate in Electronic Engineering are related to innovation and production development, advanced design, planning, programming, and management of complex systems. Activities in free profession are also provided, both in manufacturing or service companies and in public administrations. Skills Associated with the Function. Skills Associated with the Function: In addition to the specific skills of the professional figure, the Electronic Engineer is characterized by: - Aptitude for developing and continuously updating technical knowledge; - High organizational capacity; - Creativity, initiative, and autonomy in performing their activities; - Propensity for teamwork; - Relational skills to collaborate and interact with experts from different disciplines; - Ability to work towards goals; - Attention to detail and rigor, even in respecting safety and environmental requirements; - Flexibility and adaptability to various situations; - Aptitude for working in an international context and interacting with people of diverse cultural backgrounds. Professional Status Conferred by the Degree. Employment Prospects: Employment prospects for Master's graduates in Electronic Engineering are expected in manufacturing or service companies, public administrations, research institutions, and free profession. Typical professional fields for Master's graduates in Electronic Engineering include: - Advanced design; - Applied and industrial research; - Product and process innovation. As application fields, the following can be cited: - Microelectronic technologies, enabling the integration of an increasing number of functions in circuits with reduced surface area and decreasing power consumption; the evolution of these technologies has significant importance, decisively influencing information processing capabilities and thus the power of applications; - Nanoelectronic technologies, aiming to make a significant leap in quality, taking inspiration from reaching the physical limits of microelectronics to introduce new generations of devices and functions; - Optical technologies, now indispensable for mass information transmission, but rich in applications in many fields; - Measurement and monitoring instrumentation, crucially linked to the 'hardware' quality of its circuit components, with applications in almost all technological fields; - Remote sensing, significantly based on the ability to process electromagnetic data and knowledge of the physical structure of the transmission medium and the objects to be detected; - High-frequency techniques (RF and microwave), used not only in all radio communication systems, both fixed and mobile, but also in industrial, medical, and scientific applications; - Study of electromagnetic interference, crucial in the design of compact circuits and high-transmission information systems, as well as in the integration of different systems based on electrical operation, coexisting in the same environment; - Sensing technology, a rapidly growing sector that essential integrates the sensor itself with the necessary electronics for correct data interpretation and transmission. Among employment prospects in the information sector, the following can be identified: electronic industries; aerospace industries; component manufacturing industries; public and private entities; as well as more traditional industrial sectors where modern analog and digital electronics constitute a significant part of production activities; research institutions operating in advanced electronic fields.

ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING Specific educational objectives.
The Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering aims to train technicians with high-level university education and skills to develop and manage complex activities related to the design and innovation of scientific and technological research, and to promote research in a broad technical-scientific field. It aims to build upon the foundational and engineering preparation required for admission to the course, providing focused training on the scientific disciplines specific to Electrical Engineering, without neglecting content from related or complementary cultural areas.
The educational objectives include developing professional skills regarding:
- design of systems and management of processes related to the production, transformation, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy;
- design and control of electrical machines and power converters, devices and systems for electric mobility, industrial automation, and home automation;
- measurement and monitoring of electrical systems;
- modeling and analysis of electromagnetic emission phenomena in electrical systems.
Achieving these objectives is pursued through a structured educational activity comprising teaching modules, including classroom lectures, laboratory exercises, and individual study or practice. These modules lead to credits earned by passing examinations.
The Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering may offer multiple study paths to organize the provided competencies in specific or emerging areas of Electrical Engineering, such as renewable energy and distributed generation, electric mobility, industrial automation, and home automation.
The disciplines included in the study path focus on typical areas of Electrical Engineering: electrical systems for energy, converters, electrical machines and drives, electrical engineering, electrical and electronic measurements; these activities may be complemented by transversal disciplines such as automation and computer science, or integrated with specific study paths such as electronics, telecommunications, energy and mechanical systems, transportation.
The study path is organized to coordinate and progressively distribute methodological training and knowledge within the context of the courses and other educational activities provided by the study program.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding During the educational process, Master's graduates in Electrical Engineering acquire in-depth knowledge in the disciplinary area characteristic of electrical energy:
- knowledge and understanding of the methodological and design foundations of Electrical Engineering;
- knowledge and understanding of the different components of the production, conversion, transmission, distribution, and utilization chain of electrical energy;
- knowledge and understanding of the technologies and components for electrical systems serving civil and industrial automation plants;
- knowledge and understanding of the technologies and components for electric mobility;
- knowledge and understanding of measurement and analysis methodologies for electrical quantities;
- knowledge and understanding of issues related to electromagnetic emissions in electrical systems.
Such knowledge is integrated, also depending on the teaching plan and the learning areas identified annually by the Didactic Area Council, with transversal disciplinary competencies such as automation and computer science, or integrated with respect to the strictly electrical field, such as electronics, telecommunications, energy and mechanical systems, transportation.
The training aims to provide a broad spectrum of multidisciplinary knowledge enabling the development of the strategic vision necessary to successfully address the technological and socio-economic challenges of the future of electrical energy, both in traditional contexts and in more emerging areas of smart cities and technologies for sustainable and eco-compatible development, from the use of renewable energy sources to electric mobility, to distributed generation systems.
The core educational activities are based on disciplines specific to the electrical energy field, specifically ING‐IND/31 ‐ Electrical Engineering, ING‐IND/32 ‐ Converters, Electrical Machines and Drives, ING‐IND/33 ‐ Electrical Systems for Energy, ING‐INF/07 ‐ Electrical and Electronic Measurements.
The integrative or related educational activities are identified within the disciplines ING-INF/01 - Electronics, ING-INF/03 - Telecommunications, ING-IND/13 - Mechanical Engineering for Machines, ING-IND/09 - Energy and Environmental Systems, ING-IND/17 - Industrial Mechanical Plants, ICAR/05 - Transportation, ING-INF/04 - Automation, ING-INF/05 - Information Processing Systems.
Additional knowledge and skills include mastery of foreign language, both technical and colloquial.
The tools implemented to achieve the stated educational objectives include theoretical lectures and classroom exercises, practical laboratory activities, individual and/or group projects, training for using instrumentation and calculation software, seminars and educational visits, training internships and orientation, individual study and self-learning activities, thesis work.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Upon completion of the educational process, Master's graduates in Electrical Engineering will be able to:
- develop mathematical models and simulate the behavior of electrical systems for the production, transmission, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy;
- develop procedures and guidelines for energy efficiency and monitoring of civil and industrial plants;
- apply optimized design methods for electrical plants and machines, aimed at energy saving and sustainable development;
- solve problems related to the management and control of automation systems;
- model and design components and systems for electric mobility.
The acquired skills will enable them to address even complex problems in contexts that are not well-defined or with contradictory specifications, or with constraints unrelated to the strictly scientific/technological issues typical of a purely theoretical context.
Master's graduates in Electrical Engineering will be able to manage all phases of evolution of an electrical process and/or system, from research and development, through detailed design and implementation phase, to system management/supervision; they will be able to use laboratory tools and equipment and define test and measurement protocols; they will be able to use computer aids for collecting textual and numerical information, processing calculations and simulations, as well as for preparing final technical documentation; they will be able to work in teams and interact with subjects and structures in the workplace; they will be able to express themselves in both technical and colloquial foreign language.
Verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through written and/or oral examinations, results of classroom or laboratory exercises, internship activity reports, individual and/or group project reports, tests using instrumentation, computer aids, and calculation software, and the discussion of the thesis.
The level of mastery of the acquired knowledge is particularly evaluated in project-type activities and in the preparation of the final thesis, where the application and critical analysis of the acquired information and knowledge, personal initiative, and the ability to address and solve problems are rigorously tested, also in extra-university contexts, promoting activities at companies, professional offices, and external bodies, national or international.
III - Judgment autonomy Master's graduates must have the ability to design and conduct analytical investigations, using models and even complex experiments, knowing how to critically evaluate the obtained data and draw conclusions. Master's graduates must also have the ability to investigate the application of new technologies in the field of Electrical Engineering.
The teaching approach includes that theoretical training is accompanied by examples, applications, individual and group work, and verifications that encourage active participation, propositional attitude, and the ability for autonomous processing.
IV - Communication skills Master's graduates must be able to effectively operate as a project leader and/or group leader, which may consist of people competent in different disciplines and at different levels. The Master's graduate must be able to work and communicate effectively in broader national and international contexts.
The teaching approach includes in (some) core courses involving project activities and thesis work, applications and verifications that encourage active participation, propositional attitude, and the ability to communicate the results of the work performed.
V - Learning ability The Master's graduate must possess a learning ability that enables them to effectively address the changing work-related issues connected with technological innovation and changes in the economic and productive system.
They must also be aware of issues such as risk and change management. Finally, they must be able to recognize the need for autonomous learning throughout their life.
The Master's Degree courses use teaching methodologies such as analysis and resolution of different and complex problems, integration of various disciplines, and group discussion; these methodologies foster the acquisition of competencies related to learning and adaptation. Other useful tools for achieving these abilities are the thesis, which requires the student to measure and understand new information, and the possible internship carried out in a laboratory or in an industrial production context.
Workplace function.
Workplace function:
The Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering trains technicians with high-level university education and skills to design and manage complex activities related to the design and development of scientific and technological innovation, and to promote research in a broad technical-scientific field.
The received training enables the electrical engineer to interact with professionals of different cultural backgrounds, lead group work, and operate in the workplace with autonomy and flexibility while respecting professional ethics, even at an international level.
Competencies associated with the function.
Competencies associated with the function:
Master's graduates in Electrical Engineering possess:
- technical, economic, and managerial skills in the field of electrical energy systems: plants for production from conventional and renewable sources, transmission, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy, monitoring and diagnostics of networks and consumers, energy saving;
- skills regarding the technologies and components for electrical systems serving civil and industrial plants, in automation and home automation systems, in electrical systems for mobility, in plants for distributed electrical generation;
- skills regarding measurement and analysis methodologies for electrical quantities: monitoring of plants and machines for industrial production, transmission, processing, and management of measurement information;
- skills in design, sizing, and control of electrical motors, electromechanical actuators, and power electronic systems;
- skills regarding issues related to electromagnetic emissions in electrical systems: generation of disturbances, electromagnetic compatibility, rejection and immunity.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The employment opportunities for Master's graduates in Electrical Engineering include manufacturing or service companies, public administrations, research bodies, as well as self-employment. Regarding the latter, the study program prepares for the profession of engineer, Section A, Industrial Sector, Specialization Electrical.
Typical professional activities for Master's graduates in Electrical Engineering are:
- design of components, devices, and electrical and electronic power systems;
- management and operation of production and industrial transformation processes;
- management of technical offices in manufacturing companies, tertiary sectors, services, and public administration;
- technical and managerial activities in companies operating in the energy and transportation sectors.
Additionally, the specialized knowledge acquired on different themes of the electrical energy value chain offers Master's graduates a wide range of work possibilities in the emerging sectors of smart cities and technologies for sustainable and eco-compatible development, from the use of renewable energy sources to electric mobility, to distributed generation systems.
Master's graduates who have sufficient credits in appropriate disciplinary sector groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in the admission tests for secondary teaching training paths.
