ITALIAN, ENGLISH
Specific Educational Objectives.
Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Structural and Construction Engineering have in-depth knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences and are able to use this knowledge to interpret and describe complex engineering problems, adopting a systemic vision and an integrated and multidisciplinary approach. In this context, the professionals the Course aims to train apply existing knowledge in the fields of design, construction, refunctionalization, and recovery of structures, constructions, and civil works at the building scale, considering also economic, energy, and environmental sustainability aspects; they assess risks associated with natural events in relation to design, planning, realization, refunctionalization, recovery, management, and monitoring of structures and constructions; they adopt advanced technological solutions, also for the progressive physical-digital transformation of existing systems; they design and manage highly complex experiments, as well as physical, mathematical, and numerical models for simulating and designing complex civil works; they supervise and direct such activities.
In particular, the choice of specific courses allows the acquisition of competencies related to:
- programming and management of complex systems;
- planning, design, construction, management, and monitoring of civil and industrial structures, with particular reference to seismic risk protection of building and monument heritage;
- assessment of safety and functionality requirements of civil works, considering also degradation and aging processes of components and exposure to extreme natural and anthropogenic events;
- maintenance, recovery, and requalification of building heritage, with particular reference to the ability to adapt civil engineering works and systems to evolving boundary conditions and service requirements, considering short, medium, and long-term dynamics;
- valorization and requalification of building heritage;
- modeling and management of structures and constructions and their life cycle using modern representation techniques;
- advanced design in the field of support and foundation structures.
The achievement of these objectives is pursued through a structured educational activity composed of teaching modules, including classroom lectures, laboratory exercises, and individual study or practice, leading to credits earned through passing examinations. Activities are designed to stimulate teamwork and communication skills.
The educational path for obtaining the Master's Degree in Structural and Construction Engineering therefore includes training activities, also offered in English, balanced across disciplines related to the completion of specific preparation in Civil Engineering disciplines and integration with related cultural areas.
In particular, two areas of in-depth study are provided:
- Basic Training Deepening Area: aimed at reinforcing and expanding knowledge and methodological tools in Civil Engineering disciplines and integration with related cultural areas.
- Engineering Training Deepening Area: aimed at providing knowledge and methodological tools in the fields of design, construction, management, and monitoring of both ordinary and special structures.
The disciplines included in the educational path focus on typical areas of Civil Engineering, such as Structures in Seismic Zones, Structural Design, and Prefabricated Structures, Foundations, Concrete Technology, Structural Theory, Risk Assessment, etc.; depending on the chosen options, these activities are complemented by the study of other disciplines such as Structural Dynamics, Stability and Bifurcation of Structures, Bridge Construction, Masonry Structures, Timber Structures, Finite Element Structural Analysis, Steel Structures, Viscoelastic Structural Analysis, Technical Architecture, Site Organization, Recovery of Existing Heritage, Building Information Modeling, etc.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding
Master's graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering will develop competencies and understanding that, on one hand, extend and consolidate those acquired in basic disciplines during the first-cycle degree. On the other hand, they will be able to generate original ideas and successfully address complex engineering problems, especially in innovative contexts and applied research on structures and civil constructions, with a particular focus on works realized at the building scale. These educational objectives will be achieved through classroom lectures, practical exercises, and participation in seminars conducted by university professors, guest professors, and industry professionals. Additionally, guided visits to construction sites and points of interest, together with the use of various departmental laboratories, will complete the Course's training strategy.
The educational path includes distinctive activities within the disciplinary field of Civil Engineering, with particular reference to the scientific-disciplinary areas of Science and Technology of Structures (ICAR/08 and ICAR/09), Technical Architecture (ICAR/10), and Geotechnics (ICAR/07), integrated synergistically with related cultural areas.
Knowledge and skills are assessed in an integrated manner within the context of all profit examinations provided in the study path, which include written and oral exams. During these assessments, both theoretical preparation and the ability to process information, especially in design contexts, will be analyzed.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding
Master's graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering, thanks to the course's teaching approach promoting active participation and students' ability to independently process information, will be able to use acquired knowledge for the design, planning, realization, refunctionalization, management, and monitoring of materials, structures, and constructions. These competencies develop in linear and non-linear contexts, with particular attention to innovative structural technological components and systems. Such abilities are acquired through exercises, usually monographic and design-oriented, which also encourage group interaction skills, as well as laboratory activities.
The assessment of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding occurs through written and/or oral and/or practical technical examinations scheduled for the courses. This evaluation process focuses particularly on examinations of disciplines that include design activities. For other training activities, verification occurs through the final examination.
III - Judgment Autonomy
Master's graduates must possess, at the end of the study course, personal judgment autonomy regarding decisions to be made in the phases of design, planning, realization, refunctionalization, management, and monitoring of materials, structures, and constructions, both in linear and non-linear fields, with particular attention to innovative structural technological components and systems. They will therefore be able to make autonomous decision-making responsibilities and actively participate in the design process in interdisciplinary contexts.
Advanced critical reasoning skills will also be developed through progressive involvement in research activities, analyzing and interpreting experimental data, theoretical results, and models.
Throughout the educational process, students will acquire the ability to solve advanced engineering problems through the development of design applications, predominantly within courses in the second year.
The assessment of achieved judgment autonomy will be conducted progressively in profit examinations, in the development of design applications, and in the preparation and discussion of the final thesis.
IV - Communication Skills
The ability to communicate the objectives and methods of realizing complex designs is essential for effective integration into the professional world.
Therefore, it is important for the Master's graduate to possess appropriate communication tools and have verified mastery through targeted simulations.
The Master's degree course will therefore provide all tools to consolidate and further develop students' communication skills, both written and oral, as well as communication through graphical representation and the use of information and telecommunication tools.
At the end of the educational process, students will have developed:
- the ability to clearly and logically communicate process and design choices, as well as the underlying scientific approaches, to both specialist and non-specialist audiences;
- the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects, specialists and non-specialists, involved in the development of civil engineering systems, in the field of structures and constructions (public bodies, companies, design offices, etc.);
- communication skills, also in English, both towards the scientific community and towards different social components, even non-experts;
- both the ability to work autonomously and the ability to work as a member of a group with diverse competencies, depending on the project development needs;
- the ability to coordinate a group, even with an interdisciplinary character.
These objectives will be pursued through classroom lectures and exercises, also conducted in English, requiring students in various courses, seminars, and the final thesis defense to present both oral and written and/or computerized versions of their work, also using audiovisual means.
The assessment of communication skills will occur in profit examinations, intermediate tests, seminars, and the final degree examination.
V - Learning Ability
The Master's degree course will provide students, in addition to specific knowledge, a methodological approach to study that will enable them to pursue subsequent studies (Master's and Doctoral programs) profitably and equip future professionals to independently embark on a continuous learning process.
The Course's objective is therefore to offer a work method, as well as specific knowledge. This objective will be pursued through the alternation of traditional training moments (classroom lectures) with others more dedicated to developing self-organization, critical synthesis, and personal research abilities (internships, thesis).
Verification will occur through profit examinations and the discussion of the final degree examination.
Professional Function in Work Context.
Professional Function in Work Context:
The professional profile of graduates is particularly characterized by the following functions, without claiming completeness, in a work context:
- design, realization, management, and control of complex building systems;
- planning, design, construction, management, and monitoring of civil and industrial structures, with particular reference to seismic risk protection of building and monument heritage;
- advanced design and realization of support and foundation works;
- site management for the realization of complex civil and industrial structures and constructions;
- refunctionalization and recovery of building systems;
- coordination of activities aimed at managing and monitoring structures and constructions in relation to associated systems;
- risk assessment and evaluation of effects of natural events such as earthquakes;
- valorization and requalification of building heritage;
- analysis and development of innovative structural technological components and systems;
- modeling of the static and dynamic behavior of materials and structures, in linear and non-linear fields.
The daily activities of the graduate may be carried out in collaboration with other professional figures involved in the civil construction chain (Civil Engineers with different specializations, Environmental and Territorial Engineers, Building Engineers, Architects, Planners, etc.), also in a coordination role.
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Competencies Associated with the Function:
To perform the functions and activities associated with the professional profile, students in Structural and Construction Engineering will acquire specific knowledge, skills, and competencies. In particular, graduates, for example:
- are able to coordinate design, construction, management, and monitoring teams for complex civil structures, constructions, and works;
- know and understand from a technical perspective aspects related to the effects of realizing structures and civil works;
- are able to solve complex problems related to the design, refunctionalization, and recovery of civil structures and works, considering also economic, energy, and environmental sustainability aspects;
- are able to assess risks associated with natural events in relation to design, planning, realization, refunctionalization, recovery, management, and monitoring of structures and constructions;
- are able to adopt advanced technological solutions, also for the progressive physical-digital transformation of existing systems;
- are able to design and manage highly complex experiments, as well as use physical, mathematical, and numerical models for simulating and designing constructions and structures;
- are able to adapt their actions in response to the evolution of methods, techniques, tools, and technologies;
- are able to interact with other professional figures involved in the civil works and construction chain and operate in interdisciplinary contexts.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
The professional profile and employment and career prospects for graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering are a direct consequence of consultation with stakeholders and analysis of sector studies.
The Course's objective is to train Structural and Construction Engineers who can practice the profession in the field of Civil Engineering with reference to the design, planning, realization, refunctionalization, management, and monitoring of materials, structures, and constructions, both in linear and non-linear fields, with particular attention to innovative structural technological components and systems. This is consistent with the University Strategic Plan 2020-2025, which includes promoting the quality of educational offerings with paths aligned with the needs of individuals and society.
The profession falls under the ISTAT category "Civil Engineers and Similar Professions."
It is emphasized that access to the profession, as indicated by current regulations, is subject to passing the State Examination for the qualification to practice as a Civil and Environmental Engineer.
Employment prospects relate to typical areas of Civil Engineering, with particular reference to structures and constructions. Professional opportunities for graduates range from the classic figure of a self-employed engineer working in medium/large companies to managerial roles in design companies, construction firms, central and peripheral bodies of the State, Regions, and Municipalities. In particular, possible professional opportunities for graduates can be listed, without claiming completeness, as follows:
- public offices for planning, management, and recovery of civil structures;
- companies, entities, consortia, and agencies for management and control of civil works;
- professional offices operating in the field of design, refunctionalization, recovery, and monitoring of civil works;
- construction and maintenance companies for civil works.
Continuation of studies in specific research doctorates represents an additional, albeit particular, employment prospect for graduates.

ITALIAN, ENGLISH Specific Educational Objectives.
Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Infrastructure Engineering have in-depth knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences and are capable of using this knowledge to interpret and describe complex engineering problems. In this context, the professionals that the Master's Degree aims to train apply existing knowledge in the fields of design, construction, and maintenance of complex transportation systems, roads, railways, airports, ports, bridges, canals, dams, and water intake structures; design solutions to prevent, control, or remediate the negative environmental impacts of human activity; address the prevention and remediation of hydrogeological instability and slope instability, river basin management and governance; conduct research on the technological characteristics of specific materials and processes; define and design standards and procedures to ensure the functionality and safety of infrastructure; oversee and direct such activities.
In particular, the choice of specific courses allows the acquisition of competencies related to:
- planning, design, implementation, management, and monitoring of infrastructure systems;
- technical evaluation of complex aspects related to the realization and/or refunctionalization of infrastructure works;
- solving complex problems related to the design and implementation of infrastructure works;
- analysis and evaluation of urban and territorial systems and acquisition of planning techniques and tools at all scales;
- assessment of risks associated with natural events, such as earthquakes, floods, landslides, in relation to the complex aspects concerning the design, planning, implementation, refunctionalization, management, and monitoring of infrastructure.
The achievement of these objectives is pursued through a structured educational activity composed of teaching modules, including classroom lectures, laboratory exercises, and individual study, leading to credits earned through passing examinations.
The educational path for the Master's Degree in Infrastructure Engineering therefore includes training activities, also offered in English, distributed evenly across disciplines related to the completion of specific preparation in Civil Engineering disciplines and integration with related cultural areas.
Two learning areas are therefore provided:
- Area of Deepening of Basic Training: aimed at reinforcing and expanding knowledge and methodological tools in Civil Engineering disciplines and integration with related cultural areas.
- Area of Deepening of Engineering Training: aimed at providing knowledge and methodological tools in the fields of design, construction, management, and monitoring of infrastructure and infrastructure systems.
The disciplines included in the educational path are also chronologically structured to first complete the basic preparation in the field of Infrastructure Engineering, monitoring, and related risks, and subsequently develop concepts and methods for the design, construction, management, and monitoring of infrastructure and infrastructure systems. The disciplines cover typical sectors of Civil Engineering, such as hydraulic and port constructions, concrete technology, structural theory, bridge construction and monitoring, transportation technology and economics, infrastructure and territory monitoring, etc.; depending on the individual student's choices, these activities are complemented by the study or deepening of other disciplines such as constructions in seismic zones, seismic risk assessment and statistical tools for infrastructure design, wood constructions, finite element structural analysis, steel constructions, foundations, site organization, applied geology, geomatics, urban planning, BIM, etc.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Master's graduates in Infrastructure Engineering will have knowledge and understanding that, on one hand, extend and strengthen the basic sciences acquired in the first-level education, and on the other hand, allow them to develop original ideas and solve complex engineering problems even in an innovative context and applied research on civil infrastructure. These results will be achieved through lectures, exercises, participation in seminars conducted by university professors, visiting professors, and professionals from the workplace, as well as guided visits to construction sites and points of interest. The use of numerous departmental laboratories completes the educational strategy of the Master's Degree.
The educational path includes characteristic activities of the Civil Engineering discipline, particularly in the scientific fields of Construction Science and Technology (ICAR/08 and ICAR/09), Hydraulic Constructions (ICAR/02), Transportation (ICAR/05), Topography and Cartography (ICAR/06), Geotechnics (ICAR/07), and their mutual integration with related cultural areas.
The verification of knowledge and understanding is conducted in an integrated manner within all the profit assessments provided during the course (exams, written and oral, where both theoretical preparation and the ability to develop design are evaluated).
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Master's graduates in Infrastructure Engineering, following the course's didactic approach aimed at stimulating active participation and autonomous elaboration by students, will be able to apply acquired knowledge for the planning, design, analysis, implementation, monitoring, and refunctionalization of civil infrastructure works, as well as the assessment of risks associated with natural events and the development of mitigation strategies. These abilities are acquired through exercises, typically monographic and design-oriented, which also stimulate the ability to interact in groups with other students, as well as through laboratory activities.
The verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through written and/or oral and/or technical-practical examinations as part of the profit assessments, particularly through design-oriented exam exercises for disciplines that include a design activity, and for other training activities, through the final examination.
III - Judgment Autonomy Master's graduates must possess, at the end of the course, personal judgment autonomy regarding decisions to be made in the phases of civil infrastructure implementation.
They will therefore be able to make autonomous decision-making responsibilities and actively participate in the design process in interdisciplinary contexts.
Advanced critical reasoning abilities will also be developed through progressive involvement in research activities, through the analysis and interpretation of experimental data, theoretical results, and models.
Throughout the educational process, the student will acquire the ability to solve advanced engineering problems through the development of design applications, primarily within courses in the second year.
The evaluation of the achieved ability and judgment autonomy will be carried out progressively in the profit assessments of courses, in the development of design applications, and in the preparation and discussion of the final thesis.
IV - Communication Skills The ability to communicate the objectives and implementation methods of projects, even complex ones, is essential for effective integration into the professional world.
It is therefore important for the Master's graduate to possess appropriate communication tools and to have verified mastery through targeted simulations.
The Master's Degree will therefore provide all the tools to consolidate and further develop students' communication abilities, both written and oral, and communication through graphical representation, as well as the use of information and telecommunication tools.
At the end of the educational process, the student will have developed:
- the ability to clearly and logically communicate process and design choices, as well as the underlying scientific approaches, to both specialist and non-specialist audiences;
- the ability to manage relationships with the plurality of subjects, specialists and non-specialists, involved in the development of Civil Engineering infrastructure (public bodies, companies, design offices, etc.);
- communication skills, also in English, both towards the scientific community and towards different social components, even non-experts;
- both the ability to work autonomously and the ability to work as a member of a group with diverse competencies, depending on the development needs and the inherent complexity and interdisciplinarity of the infrastructure design and implementation;
- the ability to coordinate a group, even with an interdisciplinary character.
These objectives will be pursued through lectures and exercises, also conducted in English, requiring students in various courses, seminars, and the final thesis examination to present both oral and written/informatic reports of their work, also using audiovisual means. The evaluation of communication skills will occur in profit assessments, intermediate tests, seminars, and the final degree examination.
V - Learning Ability The Master's Degree will provide students with, in addition to specific knowledge, a methodological approach to study that will enable them to pursue subsequent studies (Master's and Research Doctorate) profitably and equip future professionals to independently pursue a continuous process of professional growth, updating, and learning.
A goal of the Master's Degree is, among others, to offer a work methodology, as well as specific knowledge. This goal will be pursued through alternating traditional educational moments (lectures) with others more dedicated to developing self-organization, critical synthesis, and personal research abilities (internships, thesis).
Verification will occur through profit assessments and the discussion of the final degree examination.

Roles Responsible for Approving Study Plans STEFANO DI GENNARO President STEFANO DI GENNARO Program, Texts, and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ENGLISH Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's Degree in Control Systems and Automation Engineering aims to train professional figures possessing broad and solid competencies in Information Engineering, through which they can receive, manage, and contribute to the innovation of automation systems while operating safely in national and international contexts.
The Degree Course pursues the objectives characteristic of the Class by training designers of automatic control systems and systems for industrial automation, for the energy transition and for electric mobility. To appropriately pursue the specific educational objectives, the Study Course will be structured into curricula that provide distinctive competencies for the training of such designers and represent distinct variations of the unified project.
As an automatic control systems designer, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering will have a deep knowledge and understanding of topics such as modeling, identification, analysis, control, and optimization of systems, in complex contexts such as robotics or dedicated electronic devices (or 'embedded'), and will have excellent capabilities to apply such knowledge and skills to design, manage, and supervise automated control systems.
As a designer in the field of industrial automation and the energy transition, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering will acquire advanced competencies and design capabilities in Information Engineering, including automatic control, artificial intelligence, and machine learning, in Electrical Energy Systems technologies, in Computer Science, and in Industrial Communications, and will have knowledge and capabilities in power electronic converters, electric machines and drives for industrial applications, electric propulsion, and electric energy generation from renewable sources; models and methods for the analysis, simulation, and control of electrical, electromechanical, and electrochemical systems controlling energy, both in deterministic and stochastic contexts; artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques for Industry 4.0 and advanced control of energy systems; design and programming techniques for distributed and embedded information systems for industrial applications; systems and techniques for communications in industrial, smart grid, and automotive contexts.
Finally, as a designer in the field of electric mobility, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering will be trained to acquire advanced knowledge and capabilities in Information Engineering, particularly in modeling, identification, analysis, and synthesis of controllers, optimization, implementation of controllers on dedicated digital devices (embedded), and electrical technologies for automotive mobility, such as control of electric motors, power actuators, batteries, and energy optimization of the vehicle system.
Prioritizing an interdisciplinary approach and pursuing a method where future designers are placed at the center of the educational process, with teaching and assessment being closely and continuously connected through formal and informal assessment methods measuring the learning process throughout the educational phase, the Study Course will enable future designers to acquire knowledge and skills with:
- mathematical in-depth studies appropriate for each curriculum;
- broad knowledge of the Automation field for all curricula, with appropriate declination of knowledge in other fields characteristic of the Class, tailored to each curriculum;
- solid knowledge of the theoretical and practical aspects of engineering sciences, electrical and electronic systems used in the generation, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy for energy control and energy efficiency.
The characteristic course programs developed by the Study Course, aimed at achieving the aforementioned competencies, capabilities, and skills, include:
- models and methods for the analysis and simulation of systems in both deterministic and stochastic contexts;
- data analysis and filtering techniques;
- models and techniques for static and dynamic optimization;
- computer modeling and simulation of dynamic systems;
- analysis and control of robotic systems;
- modeling and control algorithms and verification for hybrid systems;
- methods for implementing control algorithms on dedicated systems (embedded);
- analysis and design of power electronic converters for automation and control of energy produced from renewable sources, distribution networks, and electrical systems for mobility.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The graduate in this Degree Course (CdS) must possess knowledge and understanding of the main methodologies and technologies, even advanced, necessary to correctly describe and model engineering problems requiring solutions typical of Control Systems and Automation Engineering experts.
To this end, the necessary knowledge to understand, analyze, and design solutions to typical Control Systems and Automation Engineering problems is provided through a substantial number of credits in characteristic fields. Additionally, to rigorously formulate problems using appropriate mathematical models, and to understand problems of different types within Information Engineering, suitable mathematical knowledge and knowledge of various related engineering disciplines have been provided. Furthermore, through freely chosen courses, students can deepen the engineering topics they find most interesting. Finally, students can complete their training through additional activities such as internships and traineeships at companies, public or private entities, professional orders, as well as specialized courses conducted by industry professionals, where the understanding acquired during studies is tested on specific business topics. The verification of knowledge and understanding is conducted comprehensively within the framework of all assessments provided by individual courses.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The graduate of this CdS will be able to apply the acquired knowledge and understanding to achieve the following objectives:
- formulate real problems using mathematical models, and identify the most appropriate model for the problem (static or dynamic, stochastic or deterministic, continuous or discrete);
- analyze requirements for control and automation systems, and evaluate compliance with requirements and specifications;
- design and implement estimation and control systems;
- build mathematical models of physical systems for simulation and verification of control algorithms, with particular reference to industrial issues;
- implement the hardware and software of energy production control systems and industrial automation systems;
- identify and use algorithms for problem resolution, define and evaluate innovative algorithms.
These objectives are achieved by providing solid methodological foundations through more theoretical courses, as well as proposing project-based activities through courses that include practical exam assessments where students, working in groups, must conduct a project activity involving the realization or computer simulation of control algorithms for various problems arising in interdisciplinary contexts requiring automation solutions, such as those encountered in industrial environments (electric machines and drives for industrial applications, electric propulsion, and electric energy generation from renewable sources, power electronic converters, electrical systems, energy systems, electromechanical and electrochemical systems controlling energy, etc.).
III - Judgment Autonomy Thanks to solid methodological and disciplinary preparation, as well as laboratory activities, graduates will acquire the ability to analyze project results, experimental or simulation outcomes, and assess the suitability of a certain model, procedure, or system. This will enable them to interact with other professional figures and make decisions to solve problems in the context of Control Systems and Automation Engineering.
Achieving this objective is particularly delegated to the preparation and writing of the final thesis, which must be the result of personal elaboration of the curricular content acquired.
The assessment of learning and judgment autonomy is conducted through written and/or oral exams, as required for passing course exams, through project-based exam assessments, and for other educational activities through the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills Graduates, during their studies, through exam assessments and final exam preparation, acquire the appropriate language to express themselves verbally, in writing, and multimedia on disciplinary issues, both at a general and specialist level. This communication ability will be continuously assessed in exam assessments, particularly in the final exam. The ability to understand and express, at least within their technical-scientific context, will also be required.
These communication skills are developed through regular educational activities and various discussion and comparison moments (seminars, conferences, guided visits, etc.).
The assessment of communication skills is conducted through written and/or oral exams provided for course exams and other educational activities, particularly through the final exam.
V - Learning Ability Graduates must update and absorb technological innovations in the field of information engineering and automation, train colleagues, participate in research and development groups in the information and automation industry, and contribute to foundational training in the information and automation sector.
These learning abilities are primarily developed through individual study of topics covered in lectures and exercises. The development of the final thesis involves independent processing of technical and scientific literature in the field.
The assessment of learning abilities is conducted through written and/or oral exams provided for course exams and other educational activities, through project-based activities in some courses, and through the final exam.
Professional Function in Work Context.
Professional Function in Work Context:
This Study Course aims to train the professional figure of a control systems and automation engineer. The main functions this professional figure will perform, depending on the distinctive competencies acquired in the different curricula into which the Study Course will be structured, are those of control systems engineer, engineer in the field of industrial automation and energy transition, and engineer in the field of electric mobility. These functions are appropriately tailored to different work contexts.
Associated Competencies for the Professional Function.
Associated Competencies for the Professional Function:
The graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering trained in this Study Course is an expert capable of analyzing problems and situations in interdisciplinary contexts requiring automation solutions. Additionally, they will possess high and diverse competencies in Information Engineering, enabling them to successfully address the main challenges present and future in the fields of industrial automation, energy transition, and electric mobility, crucial for the ecological transition in the sustainable mobility sector.
More specifically, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering is an expert capable of analyzing problems and situations in interdisciplinary contexts requiring automation solutions. They can define requirements and specifications for automation devices (microprocessor-based dedicated systems, robotic systems, control or monitoring centers, etc.). They can design and evaluate automation solutions using computer simulations. Their strong methodological preparation allows them to explore innovative automation solutions. Such an engineer can also perform management functions for automation systems, deeply understanding their operational mechanisms. They will have the ability to analyze system quality and performance, identify potential issues and criticalities, and propose solutions.
In their role as control systems engineer, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering will be able to use modern techniques and tools for the efficient design of components, systems, and processes in automation, also leveraging competencies in mathematical modeling for the analysis and simulation of processes and control systems. They may also perform verification and validation of automatic system performance, conduct experiments, and analyze and interpret their data.
The knowledge provided by the courses offered enables the graduate to analyze and understand automation and control systems designed and implemented by others, and critically evaluate their suitability in relation to application, quality, and performance.
The acquired knowledge will allow the analysis and understanding of industrial issues and the proposal of automatic solutions, defining the models to be used in:
- design and programming of automated or robotic systems;
- design of continuous or event-based automatic control systems;
- design and development of "embedded" systems;
- sales and support of automation systems.
In the context of the energy transition and industrial transformation, according to the "Industry 4.0" paradigm where the knowledge required from automation engineers is rapidly changing and becoming more specialized in enabling technologies related to information technology, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering is trained as a high-level professional with high and diverse competencies in Information Engineering, enabling them to successfully address the main present and future challenges in the fields of industrial automation and energy transition.
In their role as intelligent systems engineer for automation and energy control systems, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering acquires, with rigorous methodology and also from an applied perspective, the most advanced competencies in Information Engineering necessary to successfully perform the profession of an automation engineer specialized in energy system control.
To achieve these objectives and to prioritize an interdisciplinary approach, the educational path develops:
- appropriate mathematical in-depth studies;
- solid knowledge of the theoretical-scientific aspects of engineering sciences, with particular attention to information engineering;
- solid knowledge of Automation, Electrical Energy Systems technologies, Computer Science, and Communication Technologies.
In their role as control systems engineer in the field of electric mobility, crucial for the ecological transition in the sustainable mobility sector, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering is an expert in electric propulsion systems, with advanced knowledge in the field, preparing them for the imminent challenges of electric mobility. Such a graduate acquires not only a solid foundation in the main areas of control and electric vehicles but also solid knowledge of electric vehicle components and advanced specialization in energy storage systems, electric propulsion control systems, and electric mobility control, or integrated control systems for electric mobility. To this end, students are trained to be experts capable of analyzing issues related to mobility and electric vehicle components in interdisciplinary contexts requiring automation expertise in relation to electric mobility. They can define requirements and specifications for automatic devices for electric mobility and evaluate and compare different methodological and technological solutions available for this purpose. Such a graduate combines methodological aspects with technological aspects to implement innovative solutions in the field of electric mobility.
The graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering trained in this Study Course will be able to:
- analyze client needs and related issues, define requirements and specifications for applications and systems (such as embedded dedicated systems, robotic systems, control or monitoring centers, etc.);
- use modern techniques and tools for the efficient design of components, systems, and processes in automation, also leveraging competencies in mathematical modeling for the analysis and simulation of processes and control systems;
- perform verification and validation of automatic system performance, conduct experiments, and analyze and interpret their data;
- understand and manage complex automatic systems, analyzing their quality, identifying criticalities when necessary, and proposing solutions.
Finally, as common skills and capabilities applicable to all the above-described functions, the graduate in Control Systems and Automation Engineering possesses competencies that can be applied to a much broader range of other engineering and economic contexts. Such a graduate can therefore be employed in various industrial and economic sectors, given the relevant training for today's high-tech companies, where the ICT component is becoming increasingly important. Such a graduate acquires competencies related to:
- in-depth scientific and technical knowledge of control engineering and the ability to effectively use this knowledge;
- the ability to work both independently and in multidisciplinary teams, interacting effectively with specialists from various domains;
- the ability to communicate effectively in an international context;
- the ability to adopt the most suitable methodologies for the issues at hand and select the necessary technological components to implement the proposed solution;
- the ability to transfer high-tech methodologies from university to industry.
Professional Title Awarded.
Career Prospects:
Numerous career opportunities exist for graduates in Control Systems and Automation Engineering.
The main career opportunities for graduates in Control Systems and Automation Engineering are represented by industries, particularly in technologically advanced sectors that produce products including dedicated control subsystems or automation components (such as logic and control units, electronic control units, dedicated systems, data acquisition and processing units), as well as by industries, companies, or entities in different sectors that operate or provide services through the use of information and automation systems (e.g., in the production and distribution of goods and services, energy, public administration, finance, communications, transportation, maintenance, quality control).
Among the main sectors of companies interested in graduates in Control Systems and Automation Engineering are: electronics, electromechanics, automotive, aerospace, energy, chemical, machinery and automation equipment, computer components, measurement devices, bioengineering.
In their role as intelligent systems designer for automation and energy control systems, the main career opportunities for graduates in Control Systems and Automation Engineering are in companies operating in technologically advanced sectors that design, produce, and/or manage systems for automation and/or energy control, electronic industries, companies and entities operating in multiple sectors that operate and/or provide high-technology services using advanced energy systems and complex communication and information processing systems, companies operating in the production and distribution of electricity, including from renewable sources, public administration, finance, transportation, maintenance, and quality control.
In their role as control systems designer in the field of electric mobility, the main career opportunities for graduates in Control Systems and Automation Engineering are represented by industries, particularly those in technologically advanced sectors that produce products including control subsystems in the electric and hybrid automotive field (logic and control units, electronic control units, dedicated systems, data acquisition and processing units), with both national and international industrial prospects.

ITALIAN Degree Awarded. Master's Degree in CHEMICAL ENGINEERING Specific Educational Objectives. The Master's Degree in Chemical Engineering trains highly qualified technicians capable of addressing the design, development of process and technical-scientific innovation. The training builds upon the foundational engineering preparation required for admission to the course and, in harmony with the relevant ministerial declaration LM22 and the guidelines of the European Federation of Chemical Engineers (EFCE), strongly emphasizes the specific characteristics of the location. The student is thus effectively involved in the knowledge transfer process developed by research on key themes of modern chemical engineering. The educational path is structured into teaching modules, with classroom lectures, laboratory exercises, and individual or group study, with assistance from the teaching staff. Students earn credits associated with modules by passing the exams. The chronological structure of the educational path, detailed in the table of training activities, assists the student in their cultural growth and gradually develops professional autonomy. To this end, even the disciplines taught in the first year of the course, aimed at consolidating knowledge of the key themes of chemical engineering, use the "homeworking" tool. The disciplines of the second year structure the maturity of students, guiding them more decisively towards the design aspects of the profession. The degree course may offer multiple educational paths that provide teaching on transversal themes in harmony with the internationally recognized figure of the modern chemical engineer. Disciplines are provided to guide students towards biotechnological industrial processes, renewable energy chains, new materials, resource reuse, the design of ecologically sustainable plants, and the environmental control of industrial wastewater.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Master's graduates in the course of the educational process will acquire all the necessary knowledge for understanding the fundamental principles of Chemical Engineering, which form the unified structure of the study program. They will be able to identify and master knowledge related to the design and sizing of equipment and process plants; industrial instrumentation and process control; process analysis and simulation.

These knowledge will be developed harmoniously through strong integration with cross-disciplinary competencies aimed at stimulating an interdisciplinary approach and extrapolation of their knowledge to complex systems/situations and innovative sectors.

The student's knowledge and understanding are achieved through characteristic courses, active participation in exercises, seminar cycles, internships, as well as through individual and group study.

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the educational process, Master's graduates will be able to apply their knowledge to formulate, elaborate, synthesize, and solve complex problems in Chemical Engineering and related industrial and interdisciplinary sectors. Thus, they will be capable of planning material and energy balances governing the operation of units, processes, and chemical plants; elaborating calculations for sizing and verifying the operation of individual equipment and equipment systems; developing modeling, design, and management of chemical and energy processes; choosing and using, among available operations and processes, those most suitable for sustainability and environmental protection in relation to industrial activities in general and the chemical industry in particular.

Verification of learning outcomes is primarily carried out through written and/or oral exams. Additional significant verification moments include in-progress self-assessment tests conducted on digital platforms and spaces, online applications, and digital devices, laboratory experiences, internship reports, individual and/or group project reports with presentations, and in the final exam.

III - Independence of Judgment The Master's graduate in Chemical Engineering develops the ability to analyze and design complex production systems and processes, evaluating their characteristics, benefits, and potential damages that may arise from their development. The application-oriented courses received during studies enhance the student's independence of judgment and ability to make strategic decisions, supplementing any information gaps through experimentation and simulation under conditions close to real ones.

To achieve this, the Master's degree in Chemical Engineering is structured with a didactic approach that combines theoretical training with examples, applications, individual and group work, and verifications that encourage active participation, propositional attitude, and autonomous processing.

To facilitate the achievement of full professional judgment autonomy, the study program offers students many opportunities to interact with external professionals working in companies, agencies, or organizations in the field of Chemical Engineering or related sectors.

IV - Communication Skills The Master's graduate in Chemical Engineering acquires the ability to lead work groups and projects involving competent people from different disciplines and levels. The progressive development of this ability is monitored by the study program, which encourages students to present and synthesize the results of their study and thesis work, and to understand the state of the art of the topics addressed.

The Master's graduate in Chemical Engineering is able to clearly and comprehensively describe solutions and technical aspects of their field, argue and defend their technical choices, communicate results to the scientific community and non-specialist social parties, train collaborators, and participate in project teams coordinating their activities.

V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate in Chemical Engineering possesses a learning ability that enables them to effectively and flexibly address work-related issues connected with technological innovation and changes in the economic and productive system. The Master's graduate in Chemical Engineering has developed, as a result of the didactic approach and methodological rigor of the entire study program, the ability to autonomously acquire new technical-scientific knowledge related to the topics of the course itself, starting from the specific sector literature or related sectors. This is due to the fact that they are fully aware of the necessity of autonomous learning throughout their life, for the growth of their skills and knowledge.

The disciplines studied during the Master's degree in Chemical Engineering are delivered using approaches that induce the ability to identify, define, analyze, and solve different and complex problems through in-depth, personally guided by the teaching staff. Particularly useful for this purpose are the thesis and any internships carried out in laboratories, industrial production contexts, and design companies, initial self-assessment tests, and intermediate verification tests conducted through digital platforms, online applications, and digital devices, individual and/or group project reports with presentations.

Professional Role in Work Context.

Professional Role in Work Context:
The Master's graduate in Chemical Engineering at the University of L'Aquila possesses solid foundations in cross-disciplinary and professional specialized sciences, enabling them to interpret, describe, formulate, and solve complex problems. Typical tasks performed in the work context include the design, operation, and control of equipment and plants in the chemical, environmental, biotechnological, and new materials sectors, continuously paying attention to sustainability themes in environmental, economic, and social aspects and safety. They will collaborate with all technical-scientific and organizational-management professional figures involved in modern production contexts, managing international relationships at both interpersonal and business levels. They will be immediately capable of assuming medium-level coordination roles. Possesses the fundamental approach to undertake further professional growth and training paths that could lead to higher responsibility roles.

Competencies Associated with the Role.

Competencies Associated with the Role:
The preparation received during the Master's degree in Chemical Engineering develops balanced competencies and skills between specialized and cross-disciplinary knowledge. They will routinely be exercised to work effectively in groups including professionals from different cultural contexts. The Master's Chemical Engineer, thanks to the ability to define, model, and solve complex problems, will perform coordination activities in the fields of applied research and industry, innovation, sustainable development, and production.

Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.

Employment Opportunities:
Master's graduates in Chemical Engineering will work in the professional fields of applied research and innovation, development and production, advanced design, and planning, both in the private sector and in public administrations, as well as in independent practice. In particular, for the exercise of independent practice, it is necessary to pass the state exam for the qualification as an Engineer and to register with the relevant professional register.

Master's graduates in Chemical Engineering will find employment in the chemical and process industry, food, pharmaceutical, and biotechnological industries, companies for the development and transformation of polymeric, ceramic, glassy, and composite materials, engineering, plant, and environmental services companies, companies and public bodies in the role of environmental, water, and energy managers, applied research centers, industrial laboratories, and public administration structures responsible for energy, environmental, and safety governance. These skills can also be expressed in independent or subordinate consulting activities within manufacturing or service companies, or in public administration.

Program, textbooks, and objectives Official teaching and assessment languages. ENGLISH Degree awarded. Master's Degree in COMPUTER SCIENCE Specific educational objectives.

The Master's Degree Course in Computer Science is characterized by a strong autonomous project activity of the student, aimed at developing their ability to judge and solve problems. The competencies provided by the Master's Degree Course mainly concern distributed systems and mobile applications, computer networks, advanced algorithms, artificial intelligence, and the analysis and development of complex software systems. The Course, through a constant analysis, aims to both receive and anticipate the prevailing needs of the market. The Master's Degree Course intends to introduce students to the most advanced and frontier topics of Computer Science, both in scientific and applied contexts. According to the Course's vision, the Master's graduate in Computer Science is poised to be a protagonist of technological innovation on an international scale.

In practical terms, the Course aims to provide in-depth theoretical, methodological, and professional competencies in relevant areas of Computer Science: graduates will be able to conceive, analyze, specify, develop, verify, and maintain software systems, configure and manage network services and telematic systems, and develop and manage complex information processing systems and installations.

The Course places particular emphasis on the importance of internationalization, and for this purpose, all mandatory courses in all curricula are taught in English. It is also possible for interested and deserving students to spend one of the two years of the Course at a foreign university in place of the courses offered by our campus, within specific agreements with foreign universities. Such students may obtain a foreign degree in addition to the degree awarded by our University upon completion of the program. The list of partner universities and the calls regulating access to the mobility program and selection procedures will be published annually in the Course's Educational Offer and/or Study Plan, available on the Course's website.

Currently, the following pathways are available:
- Standard, to be completed entirely at the L'Aquila campus;
- International Double Degree jointly with the University of Nice (France), named UBIDIS;
- International Double Degree jointly with the Universities of Malardalen (Sweden) and VU-Amsterdam (Netherlands), named GSEEM.

Additionally, excellence pathways are being designed and implemented, also in collaboration with the Gran Sasso Science Institute http://www.gssi.infn.it/index.php/it/.

Regarding the quality of the educational process, it is noted that the Master's Degree Course holds the "GRIN Badge." The GRIN Badge, awarded annually since 2004 in collaboration between GRIN (Computer Science Group - the association of university professors of computer science) and AICA (Italian Association for Computer Science and Automatic Computing), certifies the quality of content in Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Computer Science (classes L-31 and LM-18). The results of the content quality certification process are available online at http://grin.informatica.uniroma2.it/certificazione. This certification is based on criteria defining how much and which computer science is taught, how much relevant mathematics is taught, and how many permanent computer science faculty members are present. The detailed certification rules are available at http://www.grin-informatica.it/opencms/export/sites/default/grin/files/RegoleCertificazione2012.pdf

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Graduates must possess a deep knowledge and understanding of essential mathematical and computer science concepts for the analysis and design of complex information systems. Such knowledge includes advanced algorithms and data structures, formal methods and verification of complex software systems, design and optimization of networks, telematic systems and applications, artificial intelligence, advanced software engineering, and web engineering. Graduates must also possess a deep understanding of Computer Science and related fields, from fundamental to the most innovative and advanced. Based on this knowledge, graduates must be able to independently understand principles and solutions related to complex information technology applications, even if not covered during the course due to recent developments or specific contexts. In summary, graduates must have:
- Knowledge and understanding of advanced mathematical and computer science concepts underlying complex information systems;
- A deep understanding of Computer Science and a systematic comprehension of key aspects and concepts related to it;
- The ability to independently understand and influence the latest developments in the field and innovative and specific applications.

In each of the curricula, these objectives are achieved through the study of dedicated courses (characterizing, related, and integrative) totaling over 80 CFU.

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Graduates must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis and development of advanced information and telematic systems and solutions. In particular, they must be able to analyze complex information technology problems, evaluate corresponding solutions, and propose new solutions appropriate to their level of knowledge and understanding, which may involve interdisciplinary approaches and interventions beyond their specialization. Analysis involves identifying the problem, clearly defining specifications, examining possible solution methods, selecting the most appropriate methodologies and technologies, and applying them correctly. Graduates must be able to use a variety of methods, including mathematical analysis, computational modeling, or practical experimentation, to design and implement complex information solutions, whether working independently or directing or collaborating with computer science and non-computer science graduates and professionals. In summary, graduates must have:
- The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve complex information technology problems using classical or advanced methods;
- The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to analyze information products, processes, and methods, even at high complexity;
- The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to develop and implement complex solutions and advanced projects meeting defined or partially specified requirements;
- An understanding of design methodologies and the ability to use them.

These objectives are achieved through dedicated courses and a substantial set of advanced courses that allow students to apply acquired knowledge through practical projects, both independently and in group work.

III - Judgment Autonomy Graduates must have acquired a high capacity for critical reasoning, identifying the most appropriate methods to analyze and solve complex information technology problems and design advanced systems, understanding the limits of their knowledge, and independently conducting investigations appropriate to their level of knowledge and understanding. Such investigations may involve bibliographic research, regulatory studies, and database searches. They may also involve designing and conducting experiments, interpreting data, and simulating at the computer, and where necessary generating the development of original theoretical and practical solutions, even extending the frontiers of acquired knowledge in relevant fields. Regarding the information technology profession, graduates must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to develop theoretical-practical skills for solving problems, conducting investigations, and implementing complex information solutions, even coordinating and directing different work groups. These skills may include knowledge, use, and awareness of advanced hardware and software processes and equipment, experimentation, use of scientific and technical literature, and other information sources. Graduates must also be able to recognize the broader non-technical implications of information technology practice, including ethical, commercial, and industrial aspects. In summary, graduates must have:
- The ability to use appropriate methods to conduct theoretical or applied research or other complex investigations on relevant technical topics, leveraging references to scientific and technical literature, regulations, databases, and other information sources;
- The ability to lead work groups for the implementation of complex information technology projects;
- The ability to design and conduct appropriate experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions;
- The ability to choose and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods combining theoretical and practical aspects;
- An understanding of applicable techniques and methods and their limitations;
- Awareness of the non-technical implications of information technology practice.

In addition to dedicated courses and project activities, these objectives are also achieved through internships and direct placements in work contexts, as well as training activities related to the final exam.

IV - Communication Skills Graduates must:
- Be able to effectively operate individually, as members of a group, and as coordinators or leaders of groups;
- Be able to use methods to communicate effectively with the computer science community and, in general, with society;
- Possess the necessary skills to integrate and organize activities within collaborative projects;
- Possess the necessary skills to acquire problem requirements through interaction with clients, transfer specific knowledge to colleagues, and present and communicate results effectively;
- Be able to effectively use, in addition to Italian, the English language both in technical-scientific contexts and for general information exchange.

These objectives are achieved through training activities involving group work, writing project reports in English, and finally preparing the written and oral presentation of the final exam.

V - Learning Ability Graduates must have acquired the ability to study scientific topics, even in relation to different and advanced contexts, to effectively integrate received knowledge. They must also be able to understand the limits of their knowledge and have skills in identifying relevant scientific literature, textbooks, other sources, and materials for further study. These abilities must enable graduates to effectively pursue higher-level training paths, such as doctoral studies or second-level master's degrees, and managerial careers requiring a high degree of autonomy and updating skills. Graduates must also have the ability to read and learn in English. The learning ability is continuously monitored during the course through performance assessments and exams focusing on knowledge acquired primarily through independent study. English is learned in dedicated courses and through progressive use of the foreign language in learning.

Role in the Workplace. Roles in the Workplace:
Computer Specialist Programmer: knowledge of main algorithmic methods and programming languages related to advanced and innovative applications, including network applications, mobile applications, and applications involving artificial intelligence. Web Programmer: knowledge of main languages related to Internet and mobile applications. System Administrator: knowledge of main operating systems, their applications, and possible evolutions. Network Designer: knowledge of main systems, protocols, and network applications. Software Project Designer and Coordinator: knowledge of the most advanced elements and methods of Software Engineering. Database Designer and Database Management Systems Designer: knowledge of main formalisms and languages for defining and using databases, knowledge of possible future developments. Database Administrator: knowledge of main DBMS. Training Technician: general knowledge acquired in the Master's degree. Marketing Specialist: knowledge of main information systems and their industrial and commercial applicability. Researcher: advanced knowledge acquired in the Master's degree within basic and applied contexts. Entrepreneur (especially for innovative start-ups): ability to apply their skills innovatively to create and commercialize new applications.

Skills Associated with the Role. Skills Associated with the Role:
Computer Specialist Computer Science and information technologies are now pervasive and widely applied in almost all fields. In the future, the perspective is that of further expansion of domains and application methods. Consequently, the Master's graduate in Computer Science can find employment in Companies and Entities developing new information applications, as well as in those that merely apply and manage them. In general, the occupational and professional fields for graduates of this class are those of conceiving, designing, organizing, implementing, managing, and maintaining information systems (with specific attention to advanced application areas, new theoretical and technological developments with focus on reliability, performance, and security, and today also on Information Ethics). Graduates are prepared to work in companies producing information systems, networks, and mobile applications, as well as in companies, public administrations, and, more generally, in all organizations using information systems. Master's graduates in Computer Science will be able to access coordination and managerial roles, as well as roles related to basic and applied research in both industrial and research institutions. They may also find employment opportunities in teaching at training institutions. Additionally, the international pathways GSEEM and UBIDIS provide specific competencies in advanced fields, applicable both in Italy and abroad.

Professional Status Conferred by the Degree. Employment Opportunities:
Computer Specialist Employee at a Private Computer, ICT (Information and Communication Technology) company or other sectors where Computer Science is applied (virtually all sectors). Employee at a Public Administration with a role in developing or managing information systems. Entrepreneur in the computer or ICT field or in sectors where these disciplines play a significant role. ICT Consultant. Teacher or researcher at training institutions or public or private research centers.
