ENGLISH Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in Physics Specific Educational Objectives.
The educational objective of the Master's degree course is to train a physicist with a solid foundational preparation and adequate specialized preparation in one of the current fields of physics through a specific curriculum, in line with the objectives of Class LM-17.
The specific educational objectives to be achieved are a) mastery of the scientific method obtained through a solid cultural preparation in classical physics and modern physics and its theoretical, experimental, and applied aspects present in the Department;
b) in-depth knowledge of modern physics and corresponding specific knowledge related to the chosen educational path.
c) in-depth knowledge of modern instrumentation and experimental techniques, data collection and analysis procedures, and formulation and solution of models, also through numerical simulation;
d) ability to use acquired knowledge for the utilization and design of sophisticated measurement instruments or for modeling complex systems in various fields of Physics present in the Department, as well as in areas beyond the scientific field;
e) fluent use of the English language, both written and oral, with reference to disciplinary and technical lexicons.
To achieve these objectives, the educational path includes completing the foundational training through a set of mandatory characteristic courses primarily in the first year, complemented by thematic laboratory courses. Specialized training in specific areas is mainly provided in the second year through various curricula and the completion of the Master's thesis. The specialization areas are related to the research themes present in the Department.
The study program, delivered in English and therefore accessible to Italian and international students based on international agreements, reflects the nature of current cutting-edge scientific research and aims to provide students with skills useful for operating in an international context.
External internships at companies and research laboratories, or internal internships within research groups, are provided as preparation for the Master's thesis and subsequent integration into the job market.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The educational path allows consolidation of knowledge of modern physics, including Quantum Mechanics applied to Matter Physics and Nuclear Physics, Quantum Electrodynamics, and Atmospheric and Space Plasmas Physics, as well as knowledge of frontier and cutting-edge topics in the chosen field.
The Master's degree includes over 45 CFU of characteristic courses, including advanced experimental/laboratory/computational techniques, in addition to advanced theoretical topics and their application in diverse contexts.
In particular, at the end of the educational path, the Master's graduate in Physics will achieve:
Knowledge:
- Excellent knowledge and understanding of theoretical/mathematical formalisms in the field of quantum physics, including relativistic quantum physics, statistical physics, and their implications in various physics sectors
- In-depth knowledge of the physical principles of the main experimental investigation techniques and the subsequent data collection and analysis, with applications related to the most recent methodologies adopted in different contexts
- Knowledge of cutting-edge research topics with applications to specific research areas
- Knowledge of frontier topics in related fields chosen by the student
- Knowledge of numerical calculation techniques for data processing and simulation of complex physical systems
Skills
- Ability to understand complex physical/mathematical formalisms in various sectors
- Ability to understand scientific articles and specialized scientific literature
- Ability to understand mathematical models applicable to real physical problems
- Ability to understand and recognize the laws governing the dynamics of physical phenomena in different sectors through interdisciplinarity;
- Ability to understand the physical mechanisms underlying advanced experimental measurement techniques;
Learning Methods: Dedicated courses (characteristic, related, and integrative), dedicated seminar activities, internal internships or external internships, group work (team work), final thesis work.
Assessment Methods: Individual exams with written and oral final exams.
Optional intermediate assessments for partial evaluation or feedback.
All courses in the educational path include a final exam with written and/or oral components. In laboratory courses, students are guided through activities involving the independent setup of experimental apparatus, data acquisition, analysis, and processing of both experimental and numerically simulated data. In some courses, typically advanced laboratory and specialized second-year courses, the final exam may be taken by presenting a student-developed project with discussion.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the educational path, the Master's graduate in Physics will have achieved the following skills:
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge in different contexts and perceive the interdisciplinary value of theories and experimental methodologies learned;
- Ability to set up an experimental apparatus for measurements applicable in scientific research;
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge to frontier research in one's own field and other fields;
- Ability to apply acquired knowledge to frontier research;
- Ability to apply, develop, and conceive advanced computational techniques;
- Ability to model a physical system into a mathematical model;
- Ability to solve complex problems through analytical and/or numerical resolution of equations and optimization techniques;
- Ability to clearly and thoroughly communicate results and reasoning to both experts and non-experts, in written and oral form;
- Ability to transfer physical-scientific knowledge to third parties
- Ability and flexibility to apply the tools of reasoning and the scientific method in any other area
Learning Methods:
The block of approximately 40 CFU of common courses provides an adequate interdisciplinary perspective for applying knowledge; in most courses, theoretical lectures are accompanied by classroom exercises or individual work; projects in advanced courses provide learning opportunities for methodologies of scientific work presentation; the thesis work and final exam consolidate these skills in a medium-term project; laboratory courses provide necessary knowledge for designing and using appropriate measurement apparatus to solve the problem at hand; external internships provide opportunities to apply acquired skills in contexts outside the university (research laboratories and/or high-technology industries).
Assessment Methods:
All assessment methods involve applying knowledge to previously unaddressed problems, stimulating initiative and evaluating the student's independent work.
III - Autonomy of Judgment Studying the scientific method applied to the physical world develops the Master's graduate's autonomy of judgment, particularly regarding:
- Formulating critical reasoning
- Critically analyzing a physical phenomenon in light of collected data/evidence
- Critically comparing one's own theoretical predictions and/or numerical and/or experimental results with those available in the relevant scientific literature, retrieved from databases and bibliographic research
- Conducting a critical and motivated analysis
Learning Methods:
These abilities are acquired through the analysis and interpretation of experimental data, their critical comparison with theoretical results and models, under the supervision of faculty involved in relevant research activities.
In specialized courses, students are continuously encouraged to deepen their understanding through different texts and original scientific articles.
Assessment Methods: Evaluation of these competencies is conducted through in-course and final assessments within the proposed courses and the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills At the end of the educational path, Master's graduates in Physics will have acquired the following communication skills:
- Ability to sustain a scientific discussion supported by relevant and pertinent scientific arguments
- Ability to use computer tools to present a scientific topic and sustain a scientific discussion in front of experts, based on valid, convincing, and pertinent arguments
- Ability to present research results to both expert and non-expert audiences, choosing the appropriate language and presenting the most relevant aspects in both cases.
Learning Methods: Training activities involving the presentation of physics topics (essays and seminars within various courses), in English, culminating in the presentation related to the final exam.
Assessment Methods: Evaluation of presentation ability, ability to justify scientific conclusions, and ability to sustain a scientific debate during oral exams and thesis presentations, all conducted in front of a faculty committee.
V - Learning Ability During the educational path, students acquire advanced autonomous learning skills in Italian and English, being prompted to conduct bibliographic research (texts and scientific articles in English) and select relevant material by critically comparing and evaluating different sources.
Graduates are also able to construct complex reasoning and modify standard proofs to adapt to new situations that may arise even in non-strictly scientific contexts.
Graduates finally gain an understanding of the limits of their knowledge and the ability to identify relevant textbooks, sources, and scientific articles for further study.
This path provides them with the ability to independently pursue further studies (PhD and second-level Master's in Physics and technical/scientific disciplines) and to effectively utilize training opportunities in potential technical/industrial work environments.
Learning Methods: Students progressively acquire these abilities in specialized courses and in the preparation for the Master's thesis.
Assessment Methods: Topics covered in various courses are proposed for independent study and assessed during exams or in-course assessments.
Work Context Role.
Work Context Role:
The Master's graduate in Physics is able to operate with broad autonomy, also assuming project and structural responsibilities, in public and private research contexts, national and international, and in public and private companies operating in technologically advanced sectors.
The solid scientific preparation, familiarity with mathematical models, computer tools, and experimental apparatus enables physicists to access design and analysis roles across a wide spectrum of applications, even not directly related to physics, and to interact constructively with other professional figures such as engineers, managers, and information technology specialists.
The Master's graduate in Physics can participate in and/or coordinate technological research and development activities, for example by designing sophisticated measurement instruments and/or activities of modeling complex physical systems and processes, can carry out activities of promoting and developing scientific and technological innovation, can perform management and design activities of technologies, and can exercise high-responsibility functions in sectors such as industry, environment, health, cultural heritage, and public administration.
They can assume roles such as technologist, project leader for development and research activities, laboratory technician, developer of scientific and industrial software, head of computing centers.
Physicists can also perform managerial and/or expert roles in Regional Environmental Protection Agencies (ARPA) and in industrial research laboratories. Physicists can also perform design and analysis functions in computational activities requiring knowledge of mathematical models and in the field of programming and information and communication technologies.
Associated Role Competencies.
Associated Role Competencies:
The theoretical and experimental competencies acquired by the Master's graduate in Physics are broad and generally develop reasoning flexibility and the ability to adapt the scientific method to a wide range of work requirements, including
- Competencies in all aspects of classical and modern physics with a strong inclination for in-depth study
- Ability to use the scientific method
- Ability to coordinate work groups in scientific research
- Ability to use complex measurement apparatus and interface them with computers for optimizing and automating measurements
- Ability to effectively communicate on scientific topics even in English.
Additionally, the Master's graduate may acquire, depending on the selected path and specific thesis work, interdisciplinary competencies in electronics, applied mathematics, data analysis, and numerical calculation, which can be applied in various work contexts.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
The Master's Degree in Physics constitutes the primary training channel for a physicist to exercise a highly specialized scientific profession with broad employment opportunities in public sectors (educational and research centers, national and international laboratories, institutions and agencies in scientific fields) and private sectors (technology, micro-electronics, software, nano-technology, energy, and finance companies).
The Master's physicist is able to work with broad autonomy, assuming project and structural responsibilities, using specific competencies for modeling complex systems in basic and applied sciences; therefore, they can hold high-level positions in scientific/technological areas.
The Master's Degree in Physics is also the foundation for a career oriented toward specialized professions in education and research and constitutes a preferred qualification for entry into the Research Doctorate program.

ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in PHILOSOPHY Specific educational objectives.
The Master's Degree in Philosophy aims to provide an in-depth knowledge of the various disciplines that belong to philosophical knowledge or interact with it. Such knowledge is largely obtained through the direct study of philosophical texts, both historical and contemporary.
Acquisition of this knowledge enables students to develop transversal logical-argumentative skills applicable in various contexts, and to become adept at solving complex problems, particularly when these problems are of a cultural, political, or social nature. The course also aims to equip students to effectively transmit philosophical and historical-philosophical knowledge to others.
Ample space is dedicated to courses within the Philosophy Institutions area and to those within the History of Philosophy area. Courses in the Philosophy Institutions area specifically aim to provide logical-argumentative skills, training students to reason on complex general and abstract issues, while also considering their reflections on contemporary society and culture. Courses in the History of Philosophy area specifically aim to bring students into contact with historical philosophical texts and train them to independently understand and interpret such texts, thereby extracting relevant content for analyzing general and complex problems and communicating such content to others.
Additionally, to broaden students' knowledge in disciplines other than philosophy but connected to it, and to particularly enable students to recognize the relevance of philosophy for public and social issues, courses in the Classical, Historical, Anthropological, and Political-Social Disciplines area are also present.
An extensive range of courses in related activities is also proposed, allowing students to tailor their study path according to their specific interests, particularly deepening disciplines that lend themselves to interdisciplinary connections with philosophy.
Other training activities aim to ensure linguistic and computer skills necessary to acquire the above knowledge, accessing texts not available in Italian and using appropriate computer tools; linguistic and computer skills are also useful for deploying the above skills in an international environment and through appropriate computer tools. Other training activities also aim to connect students with the world of work.
A relatively high weight is finally attributed to the final exam, which allows, through the elaboration of a written text, to rigorously and systematically deepen the chosen topic.
The courses in the core disciplines prevail in the first part of the course, while in the second part more space is given to courses in related disciplines and to courses chosen by the student, thus ensuring in this second phase the possibility for each student to tailor their path through choices regarding the courses to follow.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Upon completion of the Master's Degree in Philosophy, students achieve the following knowledge and understanding:
a) know the key concepts of different methodological approaches to philosophy;
b) know the logical-argumentative tools that allow evaluation and formulation of philosophical and non-philosophical arguments;
c) understand complex reasoning on general and abstract issues, typically discussed in philosophy;
d) have in-depth knowledge of some of the most important texts in the history of philosophy;
e) know some important long-term themes that characterize the history of philosophy;
f) understand the relevance of philosophical themes and arguments for understanding and transforming contemporary society;
g) identify the connections between philosophical disciplines and non-philosophical disciplines dealing with social, cultural, and scientific issues.
Objectives a), b), and c) will be achieved in particular through courses in the Philosophy Institutions area, which include the study of texts illustrating the contents of various philosophical disciplines and active re-elaboration of such contents, also through the preparation of seminar reports and short written works.
Objectives d) and e) will be achieved in particular through courses in the History of Philosophy area, which include the study of texts of significant importance in the history of philosophy and exegetical and historiographical works that allow recognition of long-term themes. Active re-elaboration of such contents is also expected, also through the preparation of seminar reports and short written works.
Achieving objective f) requires knowledge also related to non-philosophical disciplines studying society, its political organization, and historical processes influencing it. This objective will be achieved in particular through courses in the Classical, Historical, Anthropological, and Political-Social Disciplines area.
Achieving objective g) requires knowledge also related to disciplines other than philosophy, of a scientific, historical, linguistic, geographical, and socio-economic nature. Such knowledge is obtained in particular through courses falling under related activities, structured to allow students to exercise individual choices.
To ensure broad access to updated knowledge, teaching tools in languages other than Italian are also used (textbooks, critical editions, monographs, scientific articles, specialist contributions in print and digital format).
Finally, the acquisition of knowledge related to various philosophical disciplines or connected to philosophy is promoted through active participation of students in research seminars and conferences organized by teachers. Such participation is recognized as additional training activities, according to modalities determined by the Didactic Area Council.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding At the end of the study path, students acquire the following disciplinary competences:
a) evaluate the validity of complex arguments from a logical point of view;
b) formulate arguments supporting their own philosophical positions;
c) illustrate complex philosophical theories;
d) are able to independently understand and interpret classical philosophical texts;
e) are able to effectively present philosophical theories, contents of philosophical works, and long-term themes of the history of philosophy;
f) are able to apply abstract philosophical theories to socially, politically, and culturally significant themes, interacting them with approaches from other disciplines;
g) are able to read and understand philosophical texts in at least one foreign language other than Italian.
Acquisition of these competences occurs through active practice during courses. During courses – both in the Philosophy Institutions area and in the History of Philosophy area – students are asked to express reasoned opinions on the theories considered and on the interpretation of texts read, thus training competences a) and d). In short written works and oral presentations in class, as required by some courses' assessment methods, competences a), b), c), and e) are particularly trained.
The final exam (both for the preparation work and for the writing of the thesis) is then an opportunity for more extensive and articulated development and deployment of competences b), c), and e), and when the chosen topic is relevant to social and cultural themes, competence f). In general, all courses pay attention to discussing applications of theories and texts considered to cultural and social issues relevant to contemporaneity, thus developing competence f). Courses in the Classical, Historical, Anthropological, and Political-Social Disciplines area particularly contribute to acquiring competence f).
For competence g), several courses include the study of texts in languages other than Italian. Additionally, the acquisition of linguistic knowledge is part of other training activities, contributing to competence g).

III - Judgment autonomy At the end of the Master's Degree in Philosophy, students acquire the following transversal competences related to judgment autonomy:
1) are able to autonomously express reasoned preferences for certain theoretical options and practical choices;
2) are able to autonomously and critically evaluate information and opinions presented to them, identifying strengths and weaknesses in how they are motivated;
3) are able to autonomously apply philosophical interpretations to concrete problems, especially if they have cultural, political, or social implications.
To achieve these transversal competences, supplementary readings are suggested within different courses, oriented by their own philosophical preferences and aimed at providing tools to justify them (contributing to competence 1). Individual study in a public discussion context is also valued, promoting and valuing group discussions within individual courses, where the arguments of the teacher and other students are subjected to critical scrutiny and objections (contributing to competence 2). Attention is also paid in all courses to noting possible applications of discussed theories to cultural, political, and social problems (contributing to competence 3).
The choice of the topic for the final exam is then a moment when students exercise their judgment autonomy, under the guidance of the chosen teacher, also in light of their preference for a certain approach to philosophy, a philosopher, or a historical-philosophical theme matured during the study path.

IV - Communication skills Upon completion of the Master's Degree in Philosophy, students acquire the following transversal competences related to communication skills:
1) are able to communicate complex topics clearly in written and oral form, focusing on the most important aspects;
2) are able to use computer and telecommunication tools for conveying cultural content;
3) are able to use, particularly to receive and transmit cultural content, at least one European language other than Italian.
Transversal competence 1) is promoted within some courses by requiring the writing of concise, clear, and effective short essays and the delivery of seminar presentations within courses, making them accessible to other students. In particular, the difficulty and abstraction of philosophical topics to be presented provide an opportunity to train competence 1) so that it can later be applied to extra-philosophical and more concrete topics. The final exam is also a way to train this competence, both for the preparation of the written thesis and for its oral presentation.
Transversal competence 2) is promoted by including optional computer and technology training activities (both within courses and within other training activities). Additionally, in the preparation of written works and oral presentations within different courses and in the preparation of the final exam, the use of technological tools useful for effective written and oral presentation of cultural content is required; the use of appropriate bibliographic tools for retrieving texts to be studied is also required.
Transversal competence 3) is promoted by including within different courses the study of texts in a European language other than Italian. This is required in a more extensive form also for the preparation of the thesis for the final exam, when the chosen topic requires it. Additionally, other training activities include activities related to further linguistic knowledge.

V - Learning ability Upon completion of the Master's Degree in Philosophy, students acquire the following transversal competences related to learning ability:
1) are able to continue independently in research, strengthening both their philosophical and non-philosophical preparation;
2) are able to learn by interacting with others in a dialogic and collaborative context.
To strengthen transversal competence 1), all courses include forms of individual study and teachers recommend additional readings beyond the syllabus, to be carried out autonomously. The choice of the topic for the final exam is based first on individual preferences and thus involves the assignment of a personalized bibliography of texts to be studied autonomously, with the aim of bringing the student closer to the dimension of philosophical research, where learning occurs autonomously.
Discussion opportunities during lectures and during student seminars within different courses contribute to strengthening transversal competence 2). Participation in research seminars and conferences organized by teachers (and classified as other training activities according to modalities defined by the Didactic Area Council) exposes students to a dialogic and collaborative research context, contributing to strengthening competence 2).

Workplace function.
Workplace function:
1) Specialist in philosophical disciplines:
The specialist in philosophical disciplines conducts research activities in the philosophical field, tailored according to various sub-areas of competence. They can develop research projects, advance and develop interpretative hypotheses regarding the underlying philosophical implications of general issues discussed in various intellectual and cultural contexts, consider developments in modern science and concepts, trace sources and historical origins of public discussions. For this purpose, they will be able to publish and formulate arguments and criteria to distinguish between various hypotheses; draft research reports; produce informative and scientific publications; coordinate projects at national, European, or international levels, research groups, and activities aimed at disseminating research results.
2) Political and social consultant:
The political and social consultant analyzes political and socio-economic phenomena, highlighting dynamics and paying particular attention to their medium or long-term developments and their ethical and social implications; examines central issues in public debate and highlights factors to consider when addressing them; develops comparative evaluations between various available intervention lines, taking into account both feasibility criteria and social and cultural considerations; develops intervention proposals and provides consultancy regarding the elaboration of medium and long-term strategies in light of opportunities or problems associated with current trends in political, social, and economic fields related to the transformation of contemporary society.

Competences associated with the function.
Competences associated with the function:
1) Specialist in philosophical disciplines:
To perform the indicated functions, the Philosophy graduate will have specialized knowledge in the philosophical field as well as logical and argumentative skills that guarantee the ability to understand and interpret cultural, ethical, political, and aesthetic phenomena, recognizing possible implications at both theoretical and practical-social levels, having acquired a panoramic view of the history of philosophy. Additionally, the specialist will be able to master and demonstrate competences regarding the methods proper to philosophical analysis; will have the ability to develop or assist in drafting rigorous research projects coherent with the topics addressed; will exhibit transversal relational, communicative, organizational, and managerial competences that will enable them to interact with experts from various sectors, fostering knowledge transfer and creating synergies.
2) Political and social consultant:
To perform the indicated functions, the following are required: multidisciplinary competences, concerning both philosophical disciplines and social and political sciences; ability to critically examine complex political and socio-economic phenomena and recognize both their dynamics and possible developments as well as their social, historical, and political implications; ability to analyze and interpret empirical data using advanced computer tools; logical-argumentative skills; transversal relational, communicative, and organizational competences.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
1) Specialist in philosophical disciplines:
Public or private entities, institutions, and research centers operating at local, national, or international levels in the cultural and research world. Additionally, graduates who obtain sufficient credits in appropriate sector groups may, according to current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths.
2) Political and social consultant:
Local, national, and international public institutions and bodies; research centers of political parties and social and trade union organizations, interest groups, and category associations, Italian and international non-governmental organizations and third-sector organizations.

ENGLISH Specific educational objectives.
The Study Program (SP) for the Master's Degree in Applied Data Science trains a professional figure, the Applied Data Scientist, capable of operating within medium/large organizations as a central role in work groups responsible for framing analysis problems, planning, and managing the acquisition of large data streams (i.e., "big data"), such as those related to market research or genome sequencing. The Applied Data Scientist will be able to identify, represent, acquire, manage, and analyze such data, originating from specific application areas, using quantitative methodologies, mathematical-statistical-computer techniques, and computer tools, effectively communicate analysis results contributing to tactical and strategic decision-making, and produce knowledge and value.
The Study Program provides:
-in the field of Information Technology, foundational methodological knowledge for data processing and analysis, computer skills oriented towards Data Science and Big Data, programming, databases, machine learning, and data mining, and data security skills;
-in the statistical-mathematical field, mathematical skills for Networks and Decision-making, probability, statistics, and statistical learning skills, decision-making and optimization models skills, applied to the management, processing, and analysis of data of various nature;
-in the Legal and Business field, knowledge of economic and legal aspects of data processing and use, business skills for organizational processes in the presence of Big Data;
-in the Linguistic and Social field, skills for social analysis and identification of ethical issues arising from data acquisition, management, processing, and use, as well as skills to address logical-epistemological problems posed by data and their representation useful for managing, processing, and analyzing textual data.
The Study Program will provide related, integrative, and transversal skills enabling graduates to effectively communicate and operate in multi- and interdisciplinary groups to understand sector needs and suggest effective solutions, communicate analysis results compellingly, including through advanced visualization techniques, and evaluate the legal, ethical, and social implications of adopted methodologies and processes, while staying updated on developments in information technology and data science.
The Study Program offers teaching in English and is characterized by a strong presence of laboratory activities, which constitute a fundamental, defining, and indispensable element. Additionally, the Study Program includes practical activities where acquired theories and methods are applied, conducted in specific laboratories.
The Applied Data Science Program also offers the possibility to complete internships, traineeships, and theses at companies and public and private administrations, including research and technological institutions characterized by advanced data processing and use. These activities are an integral and qualifying part of the training path and facilitate the transfer of skills from the University to companies and public and private administrations.
DESCRIPTION OF THE TRAINING PATH The Study Program is designed to train experts in data processing, analysis, and use within specific application domains. Among the application domains of interest may be considered life sciences; digital services for citizens; process and product innovation for companies and public and private administrations, including research and technological institutions. For each domain, a specific curriculum is activated.
The curricula share a common initial training path and then differentiate by providing tools suitable for generating, processing, and analyzing data related to the application area to which the curriculum refers. The common path is predominantly composed of mandatory courses aimed at providing and/or standardizing foundational methodological knowledge for data processing and analysis, knowledge related to data security issues, as well as business, legal, and linguistic knowledge regarding data and data representation. Particular emphasis is placed on technological knowledge for Big Data processing and legal and philosophical knowledge necessary to understand and address ethical and legal problems related to data processing and use in respective application areas, and to evaluate the legal, ethical, and social implications of methodologies and processes used.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The Master's graduate in Applied Data Science knows the techniques of Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, and Mathematics relevant for data processing, analysis, and visualization.
Knows the methods of data generation and collection and has the ability to understand possible sources of uncertainty compromising data quality.
Knows data analysis techniques and has the ability to understand how to apply them to data from different domains and application sectors.
Knows computer tools and software platforms for data processing and has the ability to understand issues related to data and software system reliability and security.
Knows mathematical-modelling tools necessary to understand how to use data to optimize processes in companies, institutions, and public administrations and improve offered products and services.
Knows data representation techniques and visualization tools for effective communication of data and analysis results.
Knows the legal regulations regarding data collection, processing, and use as well as ethical aspects of data use in the various application domains considered by the Study Program.
The teaching methods and tools through which the expected outcomes are achieved are frontal lectures, group or individual project and laboratory activities, or the final exam.
Verification of knowledge and understanding is carried out through written and oral exams and evaluation of the products from project, laboratory, and final exam activities.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The Applied Data Science graduate is able to collect, classify, and analyze data in various application domains. Is able to assess data quality and identify the most suitable computer tools for their processing, also with reference to security management.
The graduate is capable of applying acquired mathematical-modelling skills and using data to improve products and services offered by companies, institutions, and public administrations.
Knowledge of data regulations enables the graduate to design and conduct experiments, interpret results, and, where necessary, develop original solutions and methodologies respecting relevant regulations and ethical principles. Understands and evaluates ethical and legal impacts connected to data processing and use.
Is able to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed solutions, communicate, also in English, and effectively operate with experts from different application sectors to understand sector needs and suggest effective technical solutions.
The Applied Data Scientist, thanks to the interdisciplinary nature of their training, is able to coordinate multidisciplinary projects based on massive data use.
The teaching tools through which the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is achieved are exercises and project activities where students must apply learned methods and techniques, as well as internships and the final exam.
The teaching tools through which the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is verified are:
- passing exams with written and oral tests, also related to project activities where students must apply learned methods and techniques;
- evaluation of reports and products resulting from group work, internships, or final exam.
III - Judgment Autonomy Master's graduates in Applied Data Science acquire a high capacity for reasoning and critical judgment, enabling them to identify the most appropriate models and techniques for managing and analyzing data related to organizational processes and activities to extract new knowledge and value.
Applied Data Scientists have the ability to evaluate the impact of proposed solutions in the application context, both regarding technical and organizational aspects. They are finally able to identify and evaluate broader non-technical implications of Applied Data Science, such as those in ethical, legal, economic, and industrial fields.
Acquire the ability to understand the limits of their own knowledge and identify potential methodological tools to complement their skills.
To foster graduates' judgment autonomy, an active learning method will be adopted including i) laboratory activities and in-depth study of specific case studies, ii) internships and direct placements in work contexts, iii) practical training activities related to the final exam preparation.
The evaluation of the student's ability to express independent judgments is conducted through oral exams and analysis of personal products produced both within individual modules and the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills The Applied Data Scientist
- communicates clearly the results and the most appropriate strategic lines resulting from data analysis, also through appropriate visualization of results;
- presents the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed solutions in technological, economic, and legal terms;
- fluently uses English, both written and oral, including disciplinary terminology;
- communicates information, ideas, problems, and solutions to interlocutors with different levels and areas of specialization, using appropriate linguistic tools;
- effectively communicates with group members, especially when serving as coordinator or group leader;
- possesses the communication skills necessary to acquire problem requirements through interaction with clients and domain experts.
These objectives are achieved through training activities involving group work, the preparation of reports in English both in written and oral form for projects, and finally through the preparation of the written and oral presentation of the final exam.
Verification of these objectives is carried out through passing exams and evaluation of reports and products resulting from group work, internships, or final exam.
V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate in Applied Data Science
- possesses the learning abilities necessary to continue studying in a self-directed or autonomous manner, as well as to independently update knowledge as required by the continuous evolution of technology, social, legal, economic, and productive systems;
- is able to read and understand university and post-university level scientific texts, use technical manuals for using software of different types and applications;
- is able to pursue post-university studies, such as second-level master's degrees, research doctorates, and/or careers in research;
- has the ability to read and learn in English.
Learning ability is acquired and verified during the study program through the execution and evaluation of individual and group applied projects, or the original final exam prepared by the student. In preparing the final exam, the student is free to choose the methodologies and technologies to use.
Professional Role in Work Context.
Professional Role:
The Master's graduate in Applied Data Science occupies high-level technical and/or managerial roles as Applied Data Scientist, Data Analyst, Data Manager, and Data-Driven Decision Maker, as well as supporting roles for specialists in data management, processing, analysis, and modelling or technical figures in specific application fields. They can operate in contexts requiring the use of computer, mathematical, statistical techniques, and data processing methods, in the tertiary sector and public administrations, in industrial and business sectors, and in scientific, technological, and application sectors such as biological and health care and business.
They are a professional figure responsible for data collection, analysis, processing, interpretation, dissemination, and visualization activities of quantitative or quantifiable organizational data for analytical, predictive, or strategic purposes. In their work, this professional identifies, collects, prepares, validates, analyzes, and interprets data related to various organizational activities to extract information (synthesis or derived from analysis), also through the development of predictive models to create organized knowledge systems, with the aim of creating new knowledge and value, improving processes and/or products, and potentially defining new ones.
Associated Professional Competencies.
The Applied Data Scientist is able to:
- identify, classify, and process data owned by an organization within a specific application domain, paying attention to data quality and regulations governing their processing;
- identify which data should be acquired outside the organization and the respective acquisition methods, also in economic and legal terms;
- apply relevant Computer Science, Statistics, and Mathematics techniques for processing large data volumes and formulating innovative, qualitative, and quantitative responses to complex problems requiring a multi- and interdisciplinary approach;
- explore, validate, model, and analyze data to add value to the organization, both in terms of process and product;
- identify and use the most effective software, hardware, and network infrastructures for (big) data processing, and manage issues related to their reliability and security;
- effectively communicate data and analysis results, both in written and oral form, also through advanced visualization and information representation techniques;
- understand problems and evaluate ethical and legal impacts connected to data processing and use;
- demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed solutions;
- communicate, also in English, and effectively operate with experts from different application sectors to understand sector needs and suggest effective technical solutions;
- continuously update and engage with the most advanced international realities in the field.
Professional Title Conferred.
Employment Opportunities:
Due to the variety of data types processed, employment opportunities relate to many sectors. The Applied Data Scientist occupies high-level technical and/or managerial roles in contexts requiring knowledge of computer science, mathematics, statistics, social sciences, and a deep, also legal, understanding of data processing and English. Thanks to their interdisciplinary nature, they can coordinate Data Science projects in various application areas.
Being multidisciplinary, their employment opportunities span multiple areas, including small and medium enterprises, large companies, consulting and research centers, Public Administration:
- Public and private entities
- Public and private research institutions
- Automated manufacturing industries
- Banking and Insurance institutions
- Public Administration
- Public and private health institutions
- Smart City service providers
- Tourism service providers
- Arts and culture service providers
- Transportation service providers
- IT sector companies
- Telecommunications sector companies
- Media
- Large Retail (GDO)
- E-commerce service providers
- Energy distributors (gas and electricity)
- Water distributors

[B4D] MEDICAL AND PHARMACEUTICAL BIOTECHNOLOGIES Master's Degree English Italian

Program, Texts, and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages. ITALIAN, ENGLISH

Specific Educational Objectives. The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology aims to train a professional figure with a solid cultural foundation and high levels of practical competence, who will be able to perform roles with responsible functions within the scope of competence as defined by current regulations, in research, scientific innovation, and the technical-productive development of biotechnology applications in medical fields, such as prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of human diseases, and in pharmaceutical fields, such as design, clinical testing, production, and surveillance/monitoring at various stages of production/authorization for use of drugs and biotechnological/diagnostic products.

The cultural, theoretical, and practical profile of the Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology is also suitable for access to higher levels of university and specialist education.

The educational objectives are achieved through an advanced training path that includes a common first year and a second year structured into differentiated curricula: the program is organized around cultural and methodological aspects of disciplines characteristic of Class LM-9 for Master's Degrees in Medical, Veterinary, and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology (the functional areas relevant to the course specificity are: Applied Basic Disciplines for Biotechnology; Morphology, Function, and Pathology of Cells and Complex Organisms; Common Biotechnology Disciplines; Laboratory Medicine and Diagnostics; Medical-Surgical Disciplines and Human Reproduction; Pharmaceutical Disciplines), complemented by knowledge and skills acquired through related and integrative training activities that develop specialized aspects of certain scientific fields not characteristic of Class LM-9, but consistent with the proposed objectives.

In particular, the educational objectives are achieved through advanced training that, in the common first year, will enable the graduate to possess:
- knowledge of the fundamentals and molecular, immunological, and physiological mechanisms underlying human diseases, both congenital and acquired, and competencies to design, develop, and apply strategies for scientific innovation based on qualitative/quantitative evaluation of physiological and/or pathogenetic determinants of biological processes of interest to humans;
- in-depth knowledge of the function and analysis of (macro)molecules and cellular processes in which they are involved; knowledge and mastery of the use of biochemical-molecular technologies and bioinformatics methodologies/tools for managing and accessing databases to adopt an interdisciplinary and holistic approach to studying complex biological systems, and through the management of DNA/protein engineering technologies and computational analysis technologies, to develop scientific innovations that evaluate the dynamic interactions through which biological macromolecules produce functional properties in living organisms;
- knowledge of principles for defining epidemiological investigation designs and ability to apply statistical methods in biomedical fields and epidemiological studies to acquire the scientific investigation method, mastery of principles of experimental design on biological systems, and competencies to organize and manage data from observational studies;
- knowledge of biotechnological methodologies applied to biological and chemico-toxicological analysis of drugs, diagnostics, vaccines, chemotherapeutics, and other biologically active molecules, and their valorization for therapeutic purposes;
- knowledge and methodological competencies for using advanced biotechnological technologies to study the morphology and function of cells and/or subcellular structures (also in relation to their organization into systems, organs, and organ systems) for understanding, manipulating, and dissecting complex biological mechanisms through research and experimental strategies, respecting bioethics principles, and based on more traditional systems (in vitro models) or more complex systems (in vivo models), to address specific biomedical questions, also with applied purposes in medical and pharmaceutical fields.

To ensure a scientific investigation method based on integrated approaches with complementary functions, these knowledge and competencies can be integrated, also through the specificity of related and integrative disciplines, with the fundamentals and conceptual and methodological principles of innovative and/or specialized techniques/approaches for dissecting biological phenomena related to gene evolution and, more generally, gene expression.

The first year will be completed by acquiring, within related and integrative activities, knowledge and methodologies for managing and valorizing intellectual property and projects resulting from scientific innovation.

In the second year, the Study Program will be structured into differentiated paths (curricula) that, deepening and integrating the professionalizing aspects already acquired in the first year, provide more specific knowledge and competencies for certain application/occupational areas of the Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology: the objective will be achieved both through certain scientific-disciplinary areas of the class, which already characterize the common path but contribute to the curriculum specificity, and through areas of the class (particularly Laboratory Medicine and Diagnostics, Medical-Surgical Disciplines and Human Reproduction, and Pharmaceutical Disciplines) to which different weight is assigned based on the specific competencies proposed in the curricula. The specialist nature of related and integrative activities may also contribute to the different curricular paths.

In detail, in the second year, the graduate acquires a solid cultural and methodological preparation through training paths with a more diagnostic and/or translational and/or pharmaceutical character.

The more diagnostic character of the training will be characterized, predominantly, by cultural and methodological aspects of disciplines mainly within the 'Laboratory Medicine and Diagnostics' and 'Medical-Surgical Disciplines and Human Reproduction' areas, focusing on knowledge and technologies, conventional and advanced, applied in various fields of laboratory medicine, used in professional practice in the diagnostic process, laboratory diagnostics, and the development of screening/validation and toxicological monitoring strategies for diagnostics, vaccines, and drugs.

The more translational character of the training will be characterized, predominantly, by cultural and methodological aspects of disciplines within the 'Medical-Surgical Disciplines and Human Reproduction' area projected towards transferring results of basic research to the development of diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic systems applicable in clinical practice, with particular attention to translational/clinical aspects of personalized medicine, diagnostics, and "molecular" therapies and/or biotechnology of reproduction and/or regenerative medicine: the training path enables the Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology to acquire competencies to operate/manage technologies, respecting the scope of competence and supporting medical/clinical professionals, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies applied in clinical practice.

The more pharmaceutical character of the training will be characterized, predominantly, by cultural and methodological aspects of 'Pharmaceutical Disciplines' with particular attention to fundamental aspects for managing the entire scientific and technical-productive development process of drugs and innovative biotechnological products: the pharmaceutical educational objective aims at learning more modern methodologies and techniques used in the "drug discovery" phase, industrial phase, and development and optimization of a drug, contributing to acquiring specialized competencies in research/innovation science and development in pharmaceutical and therapeutic fields.

The educational objectives are completed with practical-experimental activities, provided in various training units, training internships conducted at the University or at research institutions, universities, companies, or abroad (according to international agreements within the Erasmus program and/or agreements established by the University), and completion of a Laboratory Thesis presented in the final exam: the listed training experiences allow contextualizing acquired knowledge and competencies in a laboratory/production reality.

The training path provides flexibility in choosing courses among activities included in the University's training offer and seminar-type courses (with final assessment and according to the modalities specified in the Course Didactic Regulations), also in English, proposed by highly qualified internal/external experts, to integrate, in accordance with the Course's educational objectives, knowledge of advanced topics and specialized competencies.

Frontal lectures (in Italian and for some courses in English), didactic laboratories, consultation of teaching materials, understanding and critical analysis of scientific literature, in-depth/bibliographic research (also autonomous) on advanced scientific articles and texts, open group discussions on course topics, as integral parts of learning methods, and intermediate and final assessments and preparation/discussion of the Thesis, as verification methods, will contribute to developing/exercising/verifying the ability to learn and deepen, also autonomously, one's knowledge, autonomy of judgment, teamwork aptitude, acquisition of mastery and tools for communication, and ability to present/transmit/disseminate one's knowledge.

The training path includes, in Additional Language Knowledge, an English language course, at least B2 level, which ensures that students without these competencies at entry reach a level of English comprehension essential for both the training experience in English courses and for integrating communication skills in the language predominantly used in the international scientific field.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology training path is structured in activities that allow graduates to acquire:
Knowledge and Understanding
- statistical and epidemiological methods applied to medical-biotechnological sciences
- fundamentals and pathogenetic mechanisms of human processes of different origins, with particular attention to identifying potential targets for investigation and therapeutic strategies in acquired and genetic diseases;
- biochemical and molecular biology methodologies for studying/analyzing/characterizing biomolecules/macromolecules and bioinformatics methodologies for managing biological data in databases;
- mechanisms underlying drug/toxic interactions with biological systems and methodologies for biological and chemico-toxicological analysis for therapeutic and toxicological evaluation of drugs and xenobiotics;
- principles governing the management and valorization of innovation and intellectual property;
- principles and regulations underlying bioethics in the development of experimental protocols;
- advanced biotechnological technologies and experimental models for studying cell morphology and function and their organization into systems, organs, and organ systems.

In relation to the more diagnostic and/or translational and/or pharmaceutical character of the offered curricular paths
- cultural, molecular, and serological methods for diagnosing infections caused by pathogenic microorganisms in humans;
- clinical-diagnostic pathology and biochemico-molecular/omic technologies applied to the study of nucleic acids and proteins used in laboratory medicine;
- methodologies for producing biologically active molecules aimed at developing innovative drugs;
- different classes of therapeutic proteins, monoclonal antibodies, and innovative vaccines and methodologies for defining their pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic profile;
- different phases and biotechnological competencies required in the industrial production and marketing process of biopharmaceuticals;
- molecular analysis methodologies and advanced biomedical technologies applied in clinical practice in medical, toxicological, therapeutic, and reproductive fields (including cellular systems, bioartificial tissues, gene therapy, etc.).

Knowledge acquisition will be guaranteed by the following learning methods:
- Frontal lectures (also with computer support) of training activities (characteristic and related/integrative), some organized into teaching units, and teaching materials (textbooks, scientific articles/reviews, materials provided by the instructor).
- Didactic laboratories, provided in some teaching units or training units, with theoretical/practical lessons that may also involve the use of computer programs - Seminar-type courses (with final assessment) also in English, chosen by the student, for in-depth/integration of advanced topics in biotechnology/medical/pharmaceutical fields.

Knowledge acquisition will be verified through the following assessment methods:
- Final exam (written or oral) individual, aimed at verifying the knowledge expected in various training activities.
- Intermediate assessments provided in some teaching units/formation units for formative evaluation and/or feedback on expected learning outcomes.

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology training path is structured in activities that allow graduates to acquire:
- ability to apply key aspects of cell and molecular biology involved in human pathological processes of different origins to innovative approaches, especially in biomedical and clinical/specialized biotechnology development and in the design of biotechnological strategies in clinical/experimental and pharmacological fields;
- ability and competencies to recognize elements of innovation, limitations, and potential in biotechnology development projects and in the design and application of new diagnostic strategies;
- ability to critically analyze information provided by laboratory medicine;
- critical ability to process data in the application of molecular biology, biochemistry, and bioinformatics methodologies;
- ability to monitor advanced technologies applied in clinical/experimental fields and apply molecular and recombinant DNA and advanced biotechnological technologies for personalized diagnostic and therapeutic approaches;
- ability to evaluate respect for main bioethics aspects in the development of experimental protocols;
- ability to organize and plan research or biotechnological product development activities, demonstrating methodological application competencies;
- ability to competently evaluate the use of biopharmaceuticals, various phases of clinical and validation testing, and discuss key aspects leading to specific choices;
- ability to integrate biological, physiological, pathological, statistical, analytical, and legislative data in the application/design of biotechnological methodologies in biomedical, pharmaceutical, and clinical fields;
- ability to develop study methods and appropriate methodological paths, select and interpret data and information, and work towards specific goals;
- ability of judgment autonomy and self-education supporting the ability to operate with critical and motivated choices;
- ability to present/transmit/disseminate one's knowledge, actions, and information;
- critical and creative ability to plan strategies to be undertaken, identify suitable resources/approaches to apply, monitor the impact of actions taken to achieve specific goals or solve problems/questions.

Knowledge and understanding application ability acquisition will be guaranteed by the following learning methods:
- Frontal lectures on strategies and theoretical basis of biotechnological methodologies and/or advanced biotechnological approaches/models
- Laboratory activities (also with computer support), integral part of some teaching units/formation units, and preparation of the Thesis within a Research Project.

Knowledge and understanding application ability acquisition will be evaluated through the following assessment methods:
- Exam (written or oral): in the final exam, verifying acquired knowledge, the student's critical ability to interpret/comprehend/elaborate/discuss/analyze/choose/apply the knowledge acquired in various training units through the solution of practical/application questions. This assessment method may also be applied in intermediate assessments where provided in some teaching units/formation units.
- Thesis Evaluation: in the final exam, the critical ability and originality in the project/experimental approach and choice of investigation and methodological tools of the graduate contribute to the evaluation.

III - Judgment Autonomy The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology training path is aimed at acquiring the ability for independent reflection, critical sense, and observation spirit to ensure that the Master's graduate can exercise the profession in the various medical-pharmaceutical work contexts in which they may operate, fully autonomously, with consistency and responsibility.

The Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology is able to
- design and formulate hypotheses and independently identify the most suitable methodological approach to achieve the objective;
- use methodologies/procedures in the field of biotechnology and evaluate their applicability in different contexts;
- collect, analyze, interpret, and apply data in the considered 'systems';
- interpret sources and literature in the scientific field
- within the respect of one's own competencies and scientific-technological and ethical requirements, demonstrate critical ability to make effective and quality choices.

The educational objectives of the Course, both in more theoretical training activities and in more practical training activities; the rigor and variety of learning methods (frontal lectures, teaching materials, seminar courses) projected to provide tools for a critical approach to advanced topics in biotechnology/medical/pharmaceutical fields; interactive teaching involving discussions and comparisons based on also independent research, understanding, and elaboration of bibliographic materials from scientific literature; internship and didactic laboratory activities that, through a scientific and analytical approach, provide interpretative hypotheses to verify in relation to potentialities/limitations/limitations derived from contextual factors; participation in a Research Project as the subject of the Experimental Thesis represent the tools that will ensure, for the student guided by tutors/teachers/researchers, the development of critical sense, judgment autonomy, ability to sustain dialectical discussion on one's theses, even in collective contexts, decision-making ability, and ability to apply acquired knowledge consistently.

Written and/or oral verification exams, in-course tests, will provide feedback on the student's ability to understand/deepen/elaborate and critical ability to apply acquired knowledge to the planning and implementation of solutions to theoretical/practical/application questions in the medical-pharmaceutical field.

The final exam with evaluation of the critical ability and originality of the project/experimental approach of the student in preparing the Experimental Thesis within a Research Project will represent an additional method of assessing acquired judgment autonomy.

IV - Communication Skills The Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology acquires at the end of the training path:
- adaptable communication skills for both interlocutors of equal or different specialist preparation in the field and for different scientific/industrial/cultural contexts;
- ability to disseminate with linguistic property and synthesis the experimental data/results of one's activity and draft reports suitable for the operational contexts in which one operates;
- ability to manage tools for presenting scientific information;
- relational abilities in the context of discussions (also group), on projects/protocols/ experimental results, in biotechnology/industrial/biomedical contexts both national and international.

Acquisition of these skills will be developed/assessed
- in frontal teaching and practical laboratory experience, where the student is involved in sharing with colleagues and communicating with appropriate language
- in internships conducted in research laboratories/companies where the student can communicate with figures from different professional contexts;
- in seminar activities held by sector specialists (also in English)
- in the use of conventional teaching, learning, and verification tools (in oral and written form involving the student for developing communication skills and appropriate terminology) and more computer-based tools through multimedia systems (which, through the production of personal/group presentations, stimulate not only research, elaboration, and representation of knowledge, but also interpersonal communication);
- in the discussion of the Thesis and during the performance of verification tests where the student must use linguistic property, demonstrate mastery of appropriate terminology, and ability to present/transmit/disseminate one's knowledge.

Knowledge of the English language, included in the training path, will integrate the ability to communicate also in the language predominantly used in the international scientific landscape.

V - Learning Ability The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology provides tools to acquire study methods, critical ability, and learning suitable for relating to scientific, technological, and cultural issues in specialized biomedical, clinical, and pharmaceutical fields, even autonomously and with the ability to update one's knowledge on innovations, regulations, methods, technologies/tools constantly (through reading scientific articles, national and international bibliographic consultations, database and bioinformatics resource consultations, etc.), compare one's knowledge with experts in the field and/or related fields, and plan/elaborate/organize one's activity, both in the rapidly evolving professional reference world and in the context of third-level university training programs (PhD, Master's II level, Specialization School) with a flexible mindset, competence, and critical approach to knowledge.

The Study Program, through conventional teaching tools and/or computer and multimedia equipment, seminars, studies/reports/presentations, internships/laboratory exercises, tutorial activities, and experimental work in research groups offers culturally versatile experiences that foster and stimulate the development of critical ability and flexible learning skills, allowing the student to carry out/research and study on medical-pharmaceutical or related sectors and, in general, to continue autonomously the training and updating even after obtaining the degree.

In-course learning assessments (partial tests, PowerPoint seminar presentations, etc.), written and/or oral profit exams, and individual work for the preparation of the Thesis will allow verification of learning ability and the ability to update knowledge, also autonomously.

Work Function.
Work Function:
The medical and pharmaceutical biotechnologist can apply the acquired knowledge and competencies in research, development, production, and service areas within public or private structures and biotech companies.
- The biomedical culture on the relationship between structure/function of biological macromolecules and the human organism at different organizational levels and in physio-pathological conditions, and knowledge of advanced and specialized techniques fundamental in the fields of biotechnology applied to "human health", acquired also based on solid laboratory practical experience;
- The ability to apply knowledge of key aspects of cell and molecular biology, involved in processes of interest to humans and of different origins, to innovative approaches in scientific/technological development;
- The ability to integrate biological, biochemical, statistical, and analytical data for the design and/or application/transfer in clinical/therapeutic and diagnostic practice of methodologies and/or diagnostic, vaccine, and biotechnological drug products;
- The ability to apply advanced techniques in laboratory medicine for studying and analyzing "determinants" of physio-pathogenetic processes for diagnostic, preventive purposes, and monitoring/validating the effect of biopharmaceuticals, diagnostics, and vaccines;
- The ability to organize and manage observational studies in research, clinical/pharmacological testing, and quality control of products and services, and production processes;
- Knowledge of contextual cultures, with particular reference to the topic of intellectual property valorization;
allow the Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology to perform tasks that promote the development, scientific innovation, and technical-productive innovation of biotechnology applications in experimental, diagnostic, therapeutic, management, and production fields.

The acquired knowledge and competencies allow the medical and pharmaceutical biotechnologist to perform the following functions:
- organize, design with operational autonomy, and coordinate interdisciplinary research, basic and applied, aimed at expanding and innovating scientific knowledge and its application in scientific and technical-productive sectors such as chemical-pharmaceutical, therapeutic, and medical-diagnostic;
- organize and conduct laboratory activities, basic and advanced diagnostic investigations requiring the use of innovative biotechnological methodologies (molecular, genetic, cellular, omic, and bioinformatics);
- assist, within the scope of competence defined by current regulations, medical professionals in the development and testing of innovative diagnostic/therapeutic products involving manipulation of genetic material/biological material/engineered cells;
- develop, design, formulate, and test new biotechnological products and biopharmaceuticals based on chemical, biological, and toxicological aspects, collaborating in the management of innovation projects and marketing activities, in teams with other professionals with specific backgrounds for the discipline;
- participate and perform functions of evaluation, monitoring, and validation of clinical studies in various therapeutic fields according to current regulations;
- participate in the development and/or evaluation to proceed with patenting in the biomedical field;
- lead and coordinate programs for development, monitoring, and prevention and diagnosis through the management of advanced biotechnological/biomedical technologies;
- handle scientific dissemination and/or consultancy activities at public and private institutions/biotech companies.

Skills Associated with the Function.
Skills Associated with the Function:
The Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology has advanced knowledge and high levels of competence in promoting and developing scientific and technical-productive innovation of biotechnology applications in the medical and pharmaceutical field.

The Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology has:
- theoretical, scientific, and methodological knowledge for studying the morphology, function, and pathology of cells of complex organisms, knowledge of principles for defining investigation designs and mastery of technologies and principles of experimental design on biological systems, to design and develop experimental research using in vitro and in vivo models, for studying indicators of cellular and molecular pathogenic alterations in diseases, congenital or acquired, for developing/monitoring new biotechnological drugs, and, respecting the scope of competence and supporting medical/clinical professionals, to participate in translational projects;
- advanced knowledge and ability to apply principles of biochemistry, cell biology, molecular biology, and recombinant DNA for managing both technologies applied to laboratory medicine and technical-productive fields and advanced molecular technologies, to develop, validate, and apply investigation tools and treatments for pathogenic alterations in the human organism and to monitor, validate, and apply new cellular and/or molecular models in the biomedical field for preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic purposes;
- solid knowledge of analysis and function of biological macromolecules and cellular processes in which they are involved and biochemico-pharmaceutical competencies for formulating and designing, with advanced technologies and based on chemical/biological/toxicological foundations, biologically active molecules, drugs, vaccines, xenobiotics;
- mastery of bioinformatics methodologies for organizing/construction/access to databases, knowledge of advanced recombinant DNA, proteomics technologies, and competencies in pharmaceutical disciplines to collaborate, in concert with professionals in the medical, statistical, and chemical-pharmaceutical fields, in the development and validation of personalized therapies based on the use of new drugs targeting molecular screening from the most modern platforms and gene profiling technologies;
- knowledge of pharmaceutical marketing activities and knowledge related to managing intellectual property/projects of innovation, to disseminate scientific/technological information; to coordinate/participate in development and consultancy activities within surveillance programs; to design and develop biotechnological products and proceed with their application in industrial fields, collaborating/contributing to intellectual property valorization and management projects in the biotechnology area;
- ability for self-education and independent understanding and elaboration of sector scientific literature, supporting the ability to operate in professional contexts not only on standardized situations and models, but also to ensure critical input and continuous and motivated updating of theoretical/practical/application choices made;
- communication-relational ability in the biotechnology/pharmaceutical field that allows expanding the comparison with the research and national/multinational companies world, relating with healthcare professionals and/or specialists and non-specialists in biomedical/pharmaceutical fields, and disseminating scientific data.

Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
The employment prospects for Master's graduates in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology are in structures/organizations/areas with a predominant biotechnological, pharmacological, and biomedical character, both public and private, exercising their function autonomously and/or supporting other professional figures.

In particular, Master's graduates in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology will exercise their profession in:
- Universities, Public and Private Research Institutes, Institutions (e.g., Ministry of Health)
- Structures of the National and Private Healthcare System
- Biotechnology and Service Companies
- Drug Industry and Regulation
- Diagnostic and Pharmaceutical Research and Industry
- Biotech Industry
- Companies for the development, commercialization, and management of biomedical equipment
- Bodies responsible for elaborating health regulations and monitoring clinical studies
- Patent Offices, Biotechnological Products, and Technology Transfer
- Scientific Publishing Companies;
- Scientific dissemination and information sectors

The Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology may also:
- proceed with the qualification process for teaching and, according to current regulations governing access to various competition classes, which may require integration of training with specific competencies, to exercise their professional function in educational institutions.

- pursue an Academic Career in Universities according to current regulations governing access.

According to current regulations, some professional roles, especially in the medical-health field and/or for higher levels of responsibility, require (in public sector and for some regions also in private sector), in addition to registration with the relevant professional register (see regulation for registration with the National Order of Biologists), also the possession of additional competencies acquired in post-graduate training programs, such as Specialization School in the Health Area for Non-Medical Professionals, professionalizing courses, Master's II level, PhD, etc., to which the Master's graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology can access.
