Master's Degree in BIOLOGY OF HEALTH AND NUTRITION Specific educational objectives.
The Master's Degree in Biology of Health and Nutrition aims to train experts with advanced and practical preparation in the field of biomedical sciences and nutrition sectors, combined with a thorough scientific and practical preparation in the disciplines that characterize the curriculum.
Theoretical preparation is complemented by particularly intensive practical experience. In the second year of the degree program, approximately half of the student's academic workload is focused on the thesis. The goal is to provide students, through significant experimental work in a laboratory, the opportunity to acquire both the necessary cultural tools and critical analysis skills required for research activities or to assume responsibility for projects and structures.
The educational path is structured into two curricula "Biosanitary" and "Nutrition" and is designed to achieve: - adequate cultural preparation in biological fields with training activities aimed at acquiring knowledge and tools in statistical, computer, chemical, biochemical, molecular genetics, pharmacological-toxicological, and anatomical-physiological-pathological disciplines, along with a good mastery of techniques useful for their understanding in various applications within biomedical research;
- solid knowledge of the properties of nutrients and non-nutrients contained in food and their potential modifications during technological processes, biochemical and physiological mechanisms of digestion, absorption, and metabolic processes related to nutrients, as well as the ability to evaluate, using the main laboratory techniques, body composition, metabolism, energy expenditure, and recognize the effects of quantitative and qualitative malnutrition.
- appropriate theoretical-practical preparation on investigation methods used in the biosanitary field, including supporting computer tools;
- knowledge of the influence of food on well-being and disease prevention, and safety levels during technological and/or biotechnological transformation, as well as toxicological levels, acceptable daily intakes, and assessable risks in the consumption of substances contained in or conveyed by the diet; knowledge of the pharmacology of nutrient substances, food supplements, various natural substances, minerals, and vitamins, effects of drugs on nutritional status and nutrient absorption, perception of taste, hunger and satiety, and mechanisms of malabsorption, as well as relationships between diet and drug action.
- adequate mastery of the scientific investigation method to enable participation in experimental design, and acquisition of a level of English language and scientific literature knowledge sufficient to use computer communication techniques and present results in an international environment;
- knowledge of the main industrial technologies applied to food preparation; knowledge of methodologies used in biochemistry, microbiology, genetics, pharmacology, toxicology, molecular biology, genetic and protein engineering, metabolic and nutritional analysis, as well as analysis and manipulation of biological macromolecules, cells, microorganisms, and complex organisms;
- knowledge of biological and quality control criteria and methods for conventional and/or bioproducts.
- the ability to hold responsible positions in both public and private sectors; having the cultural basis to access recognized Health Ministry Biosanitary Specialization Schools, necessary for a managerial career in public and private laboratory and biosanitary sectors, as well as PhDs in biomedical fields and Second-Level Masters.
For the educational purposes that qualify the study program, reference is made to the principles of European harmonization that encourage the alignment of graduates' competencies with the specific requirements identified by the Dublin Descriptors system according to the National Tuning Table (CBUI College) for class LM-6, as follows.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Acquisition of integrated cultural competencies related to biomedical, nutritional, and other applied fields; acquisition of advanced scientific preparation at morphological/functional, chemical/biochemical, cellular/molecular, physiopathological, microbiological, pharmacological-toxicological levels, and mechanisms related to physiology, pharmacology, pathology, and Nutrition.
Learning methodologies: The aforementioned knowledge and understanding are acquired through participation in lectures, exercises, and seminars, guided personal study, and independent study, as provided by the training activities.
Assessment of learning: The achievement of specific educational objectives for each teaching activity will be verified through written or oral exams containing questions designed to stimulate critical re-elaboration of knowledge.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Acquisition of in-depth multidisciplinary practical competencies for biological analysis, methodological, technological, and instrumental (instrumental methodology, analytical tools, data acquisition and analysis techniques, mathematical and computer support tools, scientific investigation method).
Learning methodologies: These competencies will be acquired in training activities related to the core, related, and integrative disciplines, conducted in classrooms, laboratories, and including independent study of research publications as well as practical application of scientific experiments under teacher guidance.
Assessment of learning: The application of acquired knowledge and understanding will be evaluated through problem-solving exercises, written and/or oral tests, laboratory experiences, and preparation and discussion of reports on experiments conducted.
III - Judgment autonomy Acquisition of conscious autonomy in areas related to project management, structural and personnel responsibility, identification of innovative development perspectives/strategies, and evaluation, interpretation, and re-elaboration of literature data, professional ethics, and critical and responsible approach even to bioethical issues.
Learning methodology: Judgment autonomy is developed particularly through exercises, seminars organized within core and related disciplines, emphasizing mastery in managing experiences and data obtained, and during the activity assigned by the supervisor for the final exam preparation.
Assessment of learning: The acquisition of judgment autonomy is verified through evaluation of the degree of autonomy and ability to work, also in groups, during ongoing activities and the final exam.
IV - Communication skills Acquisition of appropriate competencies and tools for communication, with particular attention to fluent practice in an EU language, specific focus on disciplinary terminology, preparation/presentation of research projects, leading research groups, and presenting research results.
Learning methodology: Written and oral communication skills will be developed in seminars, exercises, and training activities involving preparation of reports and documents and oral presentation of the same.
Assessment of learning: Exam tests and thesis presentation.
V - Learning ability Acquisition of abilities that promote continuous development and deepening of competencies, with particular reference to consultation of specialized databases, adoption of innovative technologies, and use of advanced knowledge tools for continuous knowledge updating.
Learning methodology: Learning abilities are acquired throughout the study process, particularly through individual study, preparation of individual projects, and activities for final exam preparation.
Assessment of learning: These abilities will be verified by passing the relevant exams. In particular, for the successful completion of the final exam, it will be required to demonstrate full acquisition of the required learning abilities.
Workplace function.
Workplace function:
The main competencies of the Master's Biologist in Health and Nutrition include:
- basic or applied research activities in biomedical fields in public or private research institutes;
- autonomous professional activities in nutrition and food safety sectors in health, public administration, and industry;
- programming of nutritional interventions for individuals and populations;
- promotion and innovation of scientific and technological activities in genetic and biological-molecular fields, cellular biology and technology, metabolic and nutritional evaluations, analysis and development of biomolecules for biomedical and industrial applications;
- research and marketing activities in the pharmaceutical industry (applied research, drug-clinical research, data control and management) and biomedical equipment industry;
- professional activities in public and private biological, microbiological, sero-immunological, genetic, pharmacological-toxicological, biochemical, and cytological laboratories for the identification of infectious pathogens and control and activity of antibiotics, hormones, sera, and vaccines;
- designing the development of biological and biochemical applications in healthcare;
- dissemination and educational activities related to neuroscience.
Competencies associated with the function.
Competencies associated with the function:
The graduate, after registration with the Register for the profession of biologist section A, may carry out professional activities under the title of biologist as listed in the main functions of the professional figure and the associated competencies.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Career opportunities:
The program prepares for the profession of biologist, biochemist, pharmacologist, bacteriologist, and similar, food biotechnologist, researcher, graduate technician, and similar.

ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in ENVIRONMENTAL BIOLOGY AND ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT Specific educational objectives.
The Master's Degree in Environmental Biology and Ecosystem Management aims to train environmental biologists and environmental experts with advanced preparation in the fields of analysis, management, assessment, and restoration of the environment, both in undisturbed conditions and in altered conditions due to specific human activities, climate change, or anomalous natural events. The educational objectives of the course consist of acquiring: advanced levels of knowledge of the biotic and abiotic components of ecosystems as a tool for correct integrated analysis of the ecosystems themselves; skills in collecting field and laboratory experimental data, with critical approach and interpretative capacity; ability to analyze data through statistical methodologies with the support of mathematical and computer tools, and critical interpretation of results; principles, methods, and tools for environmental resource and impact assessment, in compliance with current national and community regulations; knowledge related to mitigation and compensation of anthropogenic impacts on biodiversity and habitat rehabilitation; autonomy in implementing new conceptual models and methodological protocols for field and laboratory investigation; ability to hold responsible positions in management activities related to nature conservation and environmental quality control at national and international levels; mastery of written and oral English, in addition to Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons of professional figures operating in the environmental sector; high-level preparation for access to Research Doctorates and Second-level Master's Programs. The study program offers the possibility to choose between two educational paths. The first is predominantly oriented towards the analysis of the different biotic components of terrestrial ecosystems, including wetlands and inland waters. It is distinguished by a higher proportion of courses dealing with ecology and biomonitoring, also in sensitive habitats, and the effects of environmental impacts at different levels of biological organization. The second path is more oriented towards the analysis of phenomena at the broader ecosystem level and the management of territory from the perspective of conservation and environmental restoration. It is distinguished by courses dealing with environmental botany, environmental assessment techniques, forecasting tools, territorial planning tools, bioremediation, and solid waste treatment. The two curricula include common courses regarding environmental physics and chemistry, earth sciences, ecology of specific biocenoses, responses to environmental stress, biological conservation methods, and environmental economics.

Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate knows and/or is able to understand: field and laboratory tools and procedures for the detection and monitoring of biotic and abiotic components of natural and anthropized ecosystems; mathematical-statistical and computer tools for environmental data analysis; results of such analyses, which they are able to critically interpret; environmental assessment and territorial planning tools applied in compliance with current regulations; effects of different natural resource management methods; the English language, in addition to Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons of various professional figures operating in the environmental sector. These results will be achieved through the courses listed in the training activities table that cover environmental physics and chemistry, earth sciences, applied aspects of biological disciplines and ecology, methods for representation, analysis, and modeling of environmental data, and environmental assessment and territorial planning techniques. Verification of knowledge and understanding is carried out through passing exams and in-course assessments during field activities, laboratory exercises, and internship activities.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate is able to apply knowledge and understanding in a multidisciplinary professional context related to the study of biodiversity, its individual components, conservation, and management of natural resources, also in a broader context of territorial planning, environmental restoration, and assessment of environmental sustainability of plans and processes. In this context, the graduate can carry out both managerial coordination and management activities, as well as specific activities. The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is achieved through: group activities related to 'case studies' proposed within different training activities; field and laboratory exercises; internships and traineeships inside or outside the University. This ability is verified during the above activities and during activities aimed at writing the final thesis.

III - Judgment autonomy The Master's graduate possesses judgment autonomy regarding: selection of the most appropriate methodologies for biodiversity assessment, analysis, monitoring, and conservation, to be applied in different ecological and biogeographical contexts and in relation to different disturbance conditions; elaboration and interpretation of experimental data and reprocessing of literature data; use of appropriate criteria for applying sustainable development strategies in different territorial realities; management of projects, in relation to tools, means, and personnel involved; choices regarding ethical and deontological issues connected with nature conservation and management; application of current regulations in the context of biodiversity management and conservation while interacting with authorities responsible for controlling and managing natural heritage and territorial planning. The expected results are achieved and verified during training activities that propose 'case studies', field exercises, internships, and activities related to writing the final thesis.

IV - Communication skills The graduate acquires communication skills that are transversal to different professional figures operating in the environmental sector, enabling clear expression of concepts to both specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, both orally and in writing, at least in Italian and English. These skills are acquired and verified through: direct interaction between teacher and student during frontal teaching activities, field and laboratory exercises; writing of reports related to different teaching activities; preparation of oral and written exam tests; internal and external internship activities; activities for preparing the final exam and thesis discussion.

V - Learning ability The study program develops learning abilities that enable graduates to independently pursue further studies and begin a professional career in the fields of biodiversity conservation and management, territorial planning, environmental restoration, and environmental sustainability. These abilities are acquired during training activities through research and reading of the most recent specialist articles, brainstorming related to 'case study' objectives to be developed, and teacher encouragement to participate in national and international seminars and conferences. Learning abilities are verified during exercises, in-course assessments, and passing exams.

Work context function.
Work context function:
- Implementation and coordination of activities for planning, design, recovery, and management of natural and seminatural environments;
- Management and coordination in corporate policies related to achieving and maintaining environmental sustainability of works, plans, and projects;
- Census of animal, plant, and microbial natural heritage;
- Analysis and control of pollutants;
- Design and application of integrated terrestrial, aquatic, and atmospheric biomonitoring procedures;
- Realization and evaluation of environmental impact studies, strategic assessment, and environmental risk assessment;
- Preparation of thematic maps and forecasting tools aimed at territorial planning from the perspective of biodiversity protection in its entirety or of specific components;
- Basic or applied research activities.
The above-mentioned management and coordination functions, or specific functions, are typically carried out in an interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary context, in collaboration with other professional figures operating in the environmental sector.

Function-associated competencies.
Function-associated competencies:
The competencies commonly exercised in the work context include:
- Ability to implement conceptual models and scientific investigation protocols for specific biotic and abiotic components of the environmental sector and for the territory as a whole;
- Knowledge and ability to apply field and laboratory tools and procedures for the detection and monitoring of biotic and abiotic components of natural and anthropized ecosystems, and for assessing biological responses to environmental stress;
- Ability to analyze data using appropriate mathematical and computer tools, and critically interpret results;
- Knowledge and ability to apply what is required by national and community regulations regarding professional activities related to environmental management (e.g., environmental assessment techniques, territorial planning, waste treatment, treatment plants);
- Ability to assess resources and knowledge of the economic implications of different natural resource management methods, in the perspective of implementing interventions aimed at sustainable development;
- Ability to work autonomously in responsible and coordinating roles, and in synergy with other professional figures operating in the environmental sector;
- Adequate knowledge, in written and oral form, of the English language, in addition to Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons of various professional figures operating in the environmental sector.
The Master's program proposes two educational paths that provide partially differentiated competencies. One is primarily oriented towards the analysis and management of the biological component and basic and applied research, while the other is more directed towards the technical-assessment and management aspects of the territory as a whole.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
The Master's graduate can perform their functions as a self-employed professional or within public and private entities dealing with territorial planning, environmental quality control (pollutant analysis, terrestrial, aquatic, and atmospheric biomonitoring), biodiversity conservation, waste disposal, and bioremediation. Among these, we mention: entities specifically responsible for natural environment protection (Regional and National Parks, Reserves, WWF Oases, ARTA); Environmental departments of public entities (Ministries, Regions, Provinces, and Municipalities) and private or state-participating S.p.A. (Municipal Environmental Services, Drainage Consortia, Water and Treatment Plant Management Consortia, Optimal Territorial Areas). The scientific research sector also offers employment opportunities at Universities or research bodies (CNR, ENEA, etc.). Possession of the Master's degree allows enrollment in the registers of the following professions, following the successful completion of the relevant State Exam and/or internship, where required: biologist, agronomist, forester, geologist, landscape architect. Graduates with sufficient credits in appropriate subject groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths.

ITALIAN, ENGLISH Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in Administration, Economics and Finance Specific educational objectives.
The Master's degree in Administration, Economics and Finance aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of business and economic sciences to enable the graduate to fully understand the business phenomenon (also in the public sector context) in its multiple aspects (economic, business, financial) and the fundamental economic dynamics.
The Master's degree provides a systematic ability to analyze the company, both in its structural dimension and in its functional dynamics, as well as knowledge and methodologies necessary to carry out consultancy activities in administration and management of companies, as well as the free professions in the economic and business area.
The training path of the Master's degree in Administration, Economics and Finance is structured into five curricula to partially differentiate the training project (always characterized by a solid business and economic preparation, with courses also in legal and mathematical-quantitative areas) in order to allow the student to have, on one hand, a sufficient choice possibility (always within the indicated training project) and, on the other hand, a solid and in-depth preparation in a specific area among those covered by the training project. This option also enables the student to enter the job market with a robust preparation regarding the chosen areas.
One curriculum is dedicated to the knowledge of accounting, financial reporting, and business economic management topics, focusing on planning and management control topics. Consequently, the study path structure is particularly based on business area courses, especially the ssd sector of business economics, to provide a solid preparation regarding the sector disciplines, even integrated with basic knowledge of economic, mathematical, and legal areas.
Another curriculum is dedicated to preparing a graduate for free profession. For this purpose, a solid and in-depth knowledge of accounting and financial reporting topics is provided, with regard to carrying out free professional activities. This curriculum provides a study path structure particularly based on business area courses, especially the ssd sector of business economics, to provide a solid preparation regarding the sector disciplines, even integrated with basic knowledge of economic, mathematical, and legal areas.
Another curriculum is dedicated to preparing a Master's graduate to be an expert in management. For this purpose, a solid and in-depth preparation is offered on business management, marketing, organizational management, and human resource management topics; the study path aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of management topics and to focus attention on organizational management and human resource management topics. This curriculum provides a study path structure particularly based on management area courses, especially the ssd sector of business organization and business economics and management, to provide a solid preparation regarding the sector disciplines, even integrated with basic knowledge of economic, mathematical, and legal areas.
Another curriculum aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of topics related to economic market issues, with particular attention to financial markets. For this purpose, financial intermediation topics, particularly banking, and corporate finance topics, particularly for business entry, are particularly deepened. Additionally, the student acquires the necessary ability to analyze economic processes at the level of the economic system, a single production sector, or a company, to enable professional operation within public bodies and private companies that use economic analysis, information, and forecasting in their decision-making processes. This curriculum provides a study path structure particularly based on economic area courses, especially the ssd sectors of political economy, economic policy, public finance, and econometrics, to provide a solid preparation regarding the sector disciplines, even integrated with important business area courses and basic mathematical and legal area knowledge.
Another curriculum aims to tailor the competencies of the training project with particular regard to the economy and management of public administrations. For this purpose, a solid and in-depth knowledge of topics related to the direction and management of public administrations is provided. The student acquires the necessary ability to analyze the operational dynamics of public administrations, also in connection with ongoing economic processes, to enable professional operation within public bodies and private companies. This curriculum provides a study path structure particularly based on legal area courses (especially public law), to provide a solid preparation regarding the sector disciplines, even integrated with important business and economic area courses, as well as basic mathematical knowledge.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate in "Administration, Economics and Finance" acquires knowledge and understanding in the business and business economics field, with important legal and mathematical-quantitative knowledge, enabling them to know and understand business and economic dynamics and to address practical and theoretical problems in the mentioned fields. The methods through which the expected outcomes are achieved are those traditional to university teaching delivered through annual courses organized according to current regulations, and through the dissemination of teaching programs and recommended textbooks for exam preparation. Verification methods for achieving expected outcomes consist of an exam for each individual course. The decision on exam modalities (written or oral) is left to the course instructor, who annually, in the exam program, also indicates the modalities for conducting the final exam, which aims to verify the achievement of the set objectives, including the assignment of the CFU numbers required for the individual course and the awarding of a grade out of thirty attesting to the quality level achieved by the individual student.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance is able to apply, within professional and work fields, the acquired knowledge and understanding gained during studies, as well as apply the competencies developed to address theoretical and practical problems encountered in the work activities they are called to perform.
The teaching methods and tools through which the student acquires the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are those traditional to university teaching delivered through annual courses organized according to current regulations, and through the dissemination of teaching programs and recommended textbooks for exam preparation, but also the provision of an internship experience. Verification methods for achieving expected outcomes, also from the perspective of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, consist of an exam for each individual course, the preparation of a final report at the end of the internship experience, and a pass/fail test regarding foreign language knowledge. The decision on exam modalities (written or oral) is left to the course instructor, who annually, in the exam program, also indicates the modalities for conducting the final exam, which aims to verify the achievement of the set objectives, including the ability to apply knowledge and understanding. Passing the relevant exam entails the acquisition by the student of the CFU numbers required for the individual course and the awarding of a grade out of thirty attesting to the quality level achieved by the individual student.
III - Judgment autonomy The Master's graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance possesses the ability to integrate acquired knowledge and formulate independent judgments in the business and economic field regarding issues concerning the direction and management of public and private entities and in the performance of free professions.
The Master's graduate possesses high judgment autonomy regarding the issues faced by those holding leadership and responsibility positions in private and public entities and in the performance of free professions.
The possession of judgment autonomy is achieved through the preparation and passing of the various exams that make up the Master's degree course, which also includes the internship activity and a language exam. A Master's thesis is also required, in which the student must demonstrate reflection ability, with also original elements on a specific topic.
IV - Communication skills The Master's graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance possesses communication skills to convey information, ideas, problems, and solutions to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors in the business and business economics field concerning issues typical of the direction and management of public and private entities, as well as in the performance of free professions. The Master's graduate possesses communication skills to effectively carry out tasks related to leadership and management positions in private and public entities to develop appropriate solutions.
The possession of communication skills is achieved through the preparation and passing of the various exams that make up the Master's degree course, which also includes the internship activity and a language exam. A Master's thesis is also required, in which the student must demonstrate reflection ability, with also original elements on a specific topic.
V - Learning ability The Master's graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance possesses learning abilities that enable continued autonomous or self-directed study within the field of business and economic studies.
The possession of learning and self-learning ability is achieved through the preparation and passing of the various exams that make up the Master's degree course, which also includes the internship activity and a language exam. A Master's thesis is also required, in which the student must demonstrate reflection ability, with also original elements on a specific topic.

The Master's graduate in Administration, Economics and Finance performs responsible functions within the company or consultancy or free-professional activities, due to specific competencies regarding the functions of business administration and control. ENGLISH Specific Educational Objectives.
Graduates in Master's Degree courses of class LM17, specifically LMAST4MC, must:
possess in-depth and flexible training, attentive to the latest developments in scientific research and technology in the field of atmospheric physics;
have a solid cultural preparation in various fields of classical physics and geophysics in their theoretical, experimental, and applied aspects, as well as a strong mastery of the scientific method of investigation;
have a high level of scientific and operational preparation in disciplines characterizing the class regarding atmospheric physics;
have in-depth knowledge of measurement instruments and data analysis techniques;
have in-depth knowledge of mathematical and computer tools supporting atmospheric modeling;
be able to operate with broad autonomy, also assuming responsibility for projects and structures, in the field of research and innovation in atmospheric physics;
be able to use acquired specific knowledge for the utilization and design of sophisticated measurement instruments and for the modeling of complex systems in various fields of atmospheric sciences;
be able to fluently use at least one European Union language in written and oral form, with reference to disciplinary and technical lexicons.
In view of the acquired skills, graduates of the class can carry out professional activities with responsibility in all fields requiring mastery of the scientific method, specific technical-scientific skills, and the ability to model complex phenomena. In particular, among the activities graduates will perform, the following are indicated: promotion and development of scientific and technological innovation, participation, also at a managerial level, in activities of public and private research institutions, as well as management and design of technologies in occupational areas with high scientific, technological, and cultural content, related to physical disciplines in the fields of environment, cultural heritage, and public administration; high-level dissemination of scientific culture, with particular reference to theoretical, experimental, and applied aspects of the latest developments in atmospheric research.
In relation to the specific objectives of the LMAST4MC course, the course:
includes activities aimed at acquiring in-depth knowledge of atmospheric physics, the dynamics and thermodynamics of the Earth system, meteorology and climate, numerical calculation techniques applied to atmospheric modeling, meteorological radar, satellite observations, and advanced experimental techniques;
provides sufficient laboratory activities, particularly dedicated to the operational knowledge of the most recent and sophisticated experimental methods, measurement, and analysis applied to the atmosphere and data processing from ground and satellite, as well as knowledge of numerical calculation techniques for atmospheric modeling;
Specifically, the student's training path in LMAST4MC is distributed over two years (four semesters). In the first two semesters, students will acquire basic and advanced knowledge of atmospheric physics, meteorology, climate, atmospheric dynamics, climate modeling, and atmospheric composition from experimental, theoretical, and numerical perspectives. In the remaining two semesters, students will acquire knowledge of fluid mechanics from a hydraulic perspective, along with electromagnetism associated with meteorological radar, satellite observations, and the experimental/observational aspects of the atmosphere. Elective courses will allow students to finalize and complete their specific training in the various fields explored over the two years and to deepen specific themes. For example, themes such as hydrological modeling, snow and glacier physics, physical oceanography, urban climatology, etc., can be explored, as well as investigation techniques such as machine learning.
The Master's Degree Course LMAST4MC includes a training internship to be carried out within the university or at public or private companies with appropriate agreements, as an integral part of the training path.
Finally, a final exam is required, involving the preparation of a supervised thesis.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The LMAST4MC training path allows consolidating knowledge of Physics directly related to atmospheric physics topics (with particular attention to geophysical dynamic systems physics, geophysical fluid mechanics, and classical electrodynamics) and the related numerical investigation methodologies applied to atmospheric modeling and observation technologies. At the end of the LMAST4MC training path, students will have solid theoretical-modeling and experimental knowledge of the atmosphere's structure and processes determining short- and long-term weather conditions, i.e., meteorological forecasting and climate, as well as air quality.
In particular, the core of the training activities contributing to achieving specific learning outcomes are those of the Physics degree class (LM-17), extended according to DM 987/2017 to some engineering fields (hydraulics and electromagnetic fields), specifically:
- experimental-applied field;
- theoretical-modeling numerical field
- geophysical field
Master's graduates LMAST4MC: i) must know and understand the fundamental elements of atmospheric physics and technology at experimental, applied, and numerical modeling levels; ii) demonstrate achievement of these objectives through attendance of characteristic courses of the specializations and passing the related exams; iii) may acquire knowledge in hydraulics, physical oceanography, hydro-meteorological modeling, advanced electromagnetism, and other areas through attendance of related and complementary courses and passing the related exams.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The LMAST4MC graduate will have the ability to apply their skills to:
- model various components of the atmospheric system;
- interpret and model basic processes related to dynamics, thermodynamics, chemistry, and radiative transfer in the atmosphere;
- use measurement instruments for climatic and meteorological quantities;
- develop and apply measurement instruments and methods related to dynamic, thermodynamic, radiative, and chemical processes occurring in the atmosphere;
- process data from electromagnetic satellite sensors;
- use advanced numerical methods for data analysis and meteorological and climatic modeling;
- verify and validate meteorological and climatic models;
- forecast weather and chemical composition based on measurements and predictive models;
- develop meteorological forecasting models and techniques for their transfer to society;
- integrate long-term climate forecasts with societal needs.
Knowledge and skills are achieved and verified in characteristic courses providing students with knowledge of atmospheric physics, meteorology, atmospheric dynamics, fluid mechanics, electromagnetism, meteorological radar, satellite Earth observation, and statistical mechanics. Additionally, the laboratory course completes the LMAST4MC graduate's training.
Three groups of elective courses of type C are also available to LMAST4MC Master's students to further complete their specific preparation.
LMAST4MC Master's graduates will also be able to:
- professionally apply acquired knowledge in basic and applied research and other high-technology work areas requiring modeling, analysis of complex systems, interpretation of experimental or phenomenological data in the field of atmospheric sciences. These abilities will be developed primarily in laboratory, modeling courses, and during thesis preparation.
- work in groups with a high degree of coordination and autonomy, as learned during group work in the laboratory and during the thesis-related internship.
- develop the learning abilities necessary for potential continuation of studies in doctoral schools or second-level master's programs.
These results will be achieved through the path proposed in LMAST4MC with characteristic training credits, seminars, and internships. Additionally, they will be verified through course exams and the final exam.
III - Judgment Autonomy Master's graduates must be able to collect and interpret experimental data, evaluate experimental results in light of applicable theories or models, recognize the presence of unexpected phenomena not reducible to prior hypotheses, and modify hypotheses and models to adapt to observed phenomena. They will also be able to model observed physical processes to correctly reproduce the dynamic and thermodynamic structure of the atmosphere. Specifically, in the LMAST4MC training path, these abilities will be developed primarily in laboratory and Earth observation courses (from ground and satellite) for the first part, while in theoretical and atmospheric modeling courses for the second part. Additionally, during the thesis work, students can further specialize their acquired knowledge. They will demonstrate achievement of these objectives through passing exams and during the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills Master's graduates must be able to clearly and unambiguously communicate the conclusions of their research to both specialists and non-specialists. Additionally, they must be able to defend their conclusions in debate. These abilities will be acquired in seminar-style lectures and in writing laboratory reports, during oral exam presentations, and will be demonstrated in the writing and presentation of the thesis during the final exam.
V - Learning Ability Master's graduates must have developed the learning abilities necessary for potential continuation of studies in doctoral schools or second-level master's programs. They must be able to independently and continuously update their knowledge in their field through consultation of scientific publications. These abilities will be acquired in writing the thesis and demonstrated during the final exam.
Job Context Function.
Job Context Function:
METEOROLOGIST Role: Researcher or Technologist
- monitoring weather conditions, analysis, and forecasting;
- analysis and interpretation of synoptic charts;
- processing, analysis, and interpretation of remotely sensed meteorological data (from ground and satellite);
- research on atmospheric dynamics, interaction between dynamic and thermodynamic processes at various spatial scales;
- research on modeling of atmospheric microphysics and convective processes CLIMATE PHYSICIST Role: Researcher or Technologist
- management and development of climate databases, development of local-scale climate scenarios;
- research on regional and local-scale climate modeling;
- assessment of climate change impacts on ecosystems and human activities;
- processing, analysis, and interpretation of meteorological and remotely sensed data (from ground and satellite);
- development of algorithms and methodologies for processing spatial-temporal distributed atmospheric data;
- research on climate dynamics, feedback mechanisms at various spatial-temporal scales;
- climate-scale atmospheric chemistry modeling and geo-engineering techniques.
ATMOSPHERIC PHYSICIST Role: Researcher or Technologist
- processing, analysis, and interpretation of meteorological and remotely sensed data (from ground and satellite);
- development of algorithms and methodologies for probing atmospheric processes;
- research on atmospheric dynamics, interaction between radiation, gases, clouds, and aerosols;
- monitoring and modeling of gaseous pollutant dispersion in the atmosphere;
- management and development of atmospheric databases.

ITALIAN Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in CULTURAL HERITAGE Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's Degree course in Cultural Heritage aims to provide a deep awareness of artistic, theoretical, and practical themes. The overall structure of the educational path involves studying the main historical-artistic areas and themes in order to (a) provide the student with a sufficiently rich and structured overview, and especially (b) equip them with the appropriate tools to expand their competencies in response to stimuli and demands from the context in which they will operate. Special attention will be given to foundational preparation for the thesis through meetings with guest scholars and artists, didactic experiments, seminars, and joint research, with particular emphasis on the thesis, considered as a test of the student's independent work and the first personal stepping stone for their subsequent professional activity. Regarding additional professional competencies, internships, workshops, and training periods in high-quality work environments (museums, newspapers, archives and libraries, associations, and cultural institutions) will be organized.
The course is structured to allow students to consolidate their knowledge in historical-artistic disciplines through a flexible and meaningful path. Further enrichment will come from Methodological Disciplines, with particular attention to restoration, also in light of the current context, and from disciplines in the Economics and Management of Cultural Heritage field for knowledge of legislation and valorization strategies. Additionally, through a wide range of related disciplines, students will better define their path. In the first year, students will deepen their knowledge of a foreign language through a sufficient number of CFU, reserved for this purpose, while other CFU will be available for IT and telecommunication skills, training and orientation internships, other knowledge useful for entering the job market, or internships and traineeships at companies or public or private entities. The education will continue with the further field of Archaeological and Architectural Disciplines and will be completed by student-selected exams and the final thesis.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The Master's Degree in class LM-89 is structured to provide a good knowledge of art history, ensure secure competence in using sources and issues related to the protection and conservation of artistic heritage, and develop a good historical-artistic methodology.
Knowledge and understanding are acquired through the didactic activities provided by the course, internship activities, and laboratories. Verification of knowledge and understanding is conducted through exams, presentation of bibliographic and iconographic research, and didactic activity simulations. Archaeological disciplines also include laboratory activities for verification. The internship is evaluated by the hosting organization, and the final exam is conducted.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The Master's Degree in class LM-89 emphasizes the acquisition by students of the ability to critically and constructively address problems, situations, and contexts with full autonomy of judgment, which is one of its most distinctive features.
Verification of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding occurs simultaneously with the verification of knowledge and understanding, i.e., through exams, presentation of bibliographic and iconographic research, and didactic activity simulations.
Verification of the ability to apply linguistic skills at B2 level in at least one foreign language is conducted through the certification of CFU in the activity "Additional Language Knowledge."
III - Autonomy of Judgment The Master's Degree in Cultural Heritage aims to foster the development of autonomy of judgment and critical and evaluative skills in the context of various historical-artistic issues and cultural heritage, along with the knowledge necessary to deepen developments in the field of historical-artistic disciplines and cultural heritage, particularly regarding the protection of heritage. Students will be required to formulate independent analyses and evaluations on topics and problems presented by professors in lectures and seminars, encouraging them to develop independent judgment through the collection of personal documents, data, and information related to the content of the courses.
Students' critical spirit will be tested by comparing them with differentiated didactic materials, such as artistic and architectural artifacts, texts, performing arts works, historical documents, and image-based narratives (photographic, filmic, graphic, etc.).
The ability to evaluate the topics covered in courses will also be stimulated through the presentation of short reports (written or oral) during lectures.
Particular attention will be paid to students' correct and critical use of primary and secondary sources, both in individual meetings with students and during exams, as well as in the discussion of the thesis.
IV - Communication Skills The Master's graduate in Cultural Heritage will possess the ability to clearly communicate themes and problems related to history, theory, and technical principles of their field of expertise, integrating them appropriately into the understanding of different historical contexts. They will also fully master the necessary IT and telecommunication skills to manage and disseminate, in a critical and complex manner, documents and profiles of artistic phenomena within their field. Naturally, they will have a good knowledge of at least one foreign language, in addition to Italian. To enhance foreign language skills, up to 12 CFU are reserved for "Additional Language Knowledge" under "Other Training Activities."
They will be able to argue effectively in both written and oral form, using different linguistic registers depending on the context and interlocutor, communicating their judgments and historical perspectives to both specialists and non-specialists with awareness of potential ambiguities inherent in communication forms. They will also have the ability to combine critical vision with understanding of the technical issues underlying artistic creation.
Public and seminar meetings will be encouraged to provide students with opportunities to express their convictions with precise terminology and conceptual clarity. The development of communication skills on even specialized topics will be achieved and verified through various didactic tools: writing reports on seminar activities and study topics, oral presentations and discussions during lectures, individual meetings with professors during office hours, writing and presenting the final thesis under a professor's guidance, and public oral presentation, possibly using multimedia tools (PowerPoint presentations).
V - Learning Ability The Master's graduate in Cultural Heritage will be able to apply learned knowledge in cultural, communicative, and editorial activities. They will also be able to collaborate in designing research programs and organizing cultural events.
The graduate will develop the ability to learn and organize work, enabling them to continue studying independently and responsibly and to orient themselves in the division of intellectual work.
These abilities, acquired through exam preparation during the study course, writing of essays within individual exams, and thesis preparation, are then verified during the taking and passing of individual exams, the writing and presentation of essays within individual courses, and the preparation and discussion of the thesis.
Professional Role in Work Context.
Professional Role in Work Context:
1. Official in the cultural heritage sector in public administration roles (Museums, Superintendencies, Local Authorities), directing Art Galleries, Publishing, and other non-teaching professional opportunities.
2. With additional training in compliance with current laws Teaching in secondary schools.
3. To reach higher levels of responsibility: graduates may access Master's programs, Doctoral Schools, and Specialization Schools.
Associated Professional Competencies.
Associated Professional Competencies:
1. In-depth knowledge of methodologies regarding specific themes and their application for the elaboration of historical-artistic studies and related exhibition skills in lectures, seminars, and conferences.
2. Advanced competencies in both historical and methodological fields for research and critical exegesis in various areas and chronological sectors related to the development of arts from the Middle Ages to the contemporary era; knowledge of specific issues related to the history and conservation of a particular artistic sector.
3. Comprehensive knowledge in various areas and chronological sectors related to the development of arts from the Middle Ages to the contemporary era, tools, and methodologies of teaching.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
The expected employment opportunities and professional activities will be in sectors where graduates will perform tasks and responsibilities of significant responsibility, such as:
- State, municipal, provincial, and regional Superintendencies, museum bodies, cultural foundations;
- Organizations, cooperatives, and private companies in the publishing, public relations, media, and multimedia communication sectors;
- Consultancies and collaborations for the conception and realization of exhibitions and permanent and temporary displays, research activities, and studies in the antique and art market sector.
The degree obtained in the two-year program will allow access, according to legal procedures, to second-level Master's programs, Doctoral Schools, and Specialization Schools. Graduates with sufficient credits in appropriate subject groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary school teaching training paths. Graduates at the end of the course will have developed specific learning abilities to continue independent study and research.

ITALIAN Degree Awarded.
Degree in Therapy of Neuro and Psychomotricity of the Evolving Age (Qualifying for the Health Profession of Neuro and Psychomotricity Therapist of the Evolving Age)
Specific Training Objectives.
Within the health profession of the neuro and psychomotricity therapist of the evolving age, graduates are healthcare professionals entitled to the attributions provided by the Ministry of Health Decree of January 17, 1997, No. 56 and subsequent modifications and integrations, or they carry out prevention, therapy, and rehabilitation interventions for child neuropsychiatric diseases in the areas of neuro-psicomotricity, neuropsychology, and developmental psychopathology, in collaboration with the multidisciplinary team of child neuropsychiatry and in collaboration with other disciplines in the pediatric field. Graduates in neuro and psychomotricity of the evolving age, in reference to medical diagnoses and prescriptions, within their specific competencies:
- Adapt therapeutic interventions to the unique characteristics of patients in the evolving age with multifaceted clinical conditions that change over time in relation to emerging functions;
- Identify and develop, within the multidisciplinary team, the prevention, therapy, and rehabilitation program aimed at overcoming the health needs of a child with developmental disability;
- Implement therapeutic and rehabilitative interventions for perceptual-motor disorders, neurocognitive disorders, and symbolization and interaction disorders in children from birth;
- Implement procedures for the inclusion of individuals with neuro-psicomotor and cognitive disabilities and handicaps;
- Collaborate within the multidisciplinary team with school operators for the implementation of prevention, functional diagnosis, and dynamic functional profile of the individualized educational plan;
- Carry out therapeutic activities for neuro-psicomotor, psychomotor, and neuropsychological disabilities in the evolving age using specific techniques for age groups and individual developmental stages;
- Implement evaluation procedures of the interrelation between affective, cognitive, and motor functions for each specific neurological, neuropsychological, and psychopathological disorder of the evolving age;
- Identify the need and implement the diagnostic and therapeutic balance between somatic representation and bodily experience, and between general functional potential and objectual relationship;
- Develop and implement the therapeutic program that uses neuromotor schemes and projects as mental acts and as cognitive and metacognitive tools;
- Also use body diagnosis as an integration of mental functions and interpersonal relationships;
- Verify the adoption of prostheses and aids in relation to neuropsychological compensations and psychopathological risks;
- Participate in functional rehabilitation for all acute and chronic pathologies of childhood;
- Document the correspondences of the implemented rehabilitation methodology according to functional recovery objectives and the specific characteristics of pathologies that change in relation to development;
- Carry out study, teaching, and specific applied research and professional consulting activities in healthcare services and places requiring their professional competence;
- Contribute to the training of support staff and directly participate in updating related to their professional profile;
- Carry out their professional activities in healthcare structures, public or private, in dependency or as self-employed professionals.
Training Objectives Year I:
- Knowledge of essential morphological characteristics and functional mechanisms of systems, organs, and apparatus in humans and their interactions. Study of sensory organs, Central and Peripheral Nervous System, skeletal, muscular, cardiovascular, digestive, respiratory, and genital apparatus. Knowledge of histological characteristics of bone, striated muscle, and nervous tissue.
- Knowledge of the individual's inner world in terms of thought, emotions, motivations, cognitive processes, and relational dynamics. Knowledge of main disease causes. Fundamental physiopathological mechanisms of major apparatuses and systems.
- Understand the historical evolution of development models and the processes that characterize them, appropriating the methodology for studying the child and their development. Understand how early experiences influence the development of the child's brain architecture. Understand physical development of the child and adolescent. Understand mental development and the stages that characterize emerging competencies in the areas: motor-praxic, communicative-linguistic, cognitive, affective-relational.
- Know English terms related to the scientific-health field, understand and express basic knowledge in English. Introduction to the technique of comprehending a text in language for assistance and scientific purposes through reading and general and specific comprehension phases.
- Know the basics of epidemiological, descriptive, analytical, experimental studies, association measures and risk estimation, screening tests, national and regional guidelines, quality indicators. Acquire the basic methodology of medical-scientific informatization and know how to use the most common search engines, access databases, and find and interpret the best available evidence in the literature.
Training Objectives Year II:
- Know the clinical symptoms, functional alterations, and pathogenetic mechanisms of major diseases of the Central and Peripheral Nervous System, both congenital and acquired, including those resolved through neurosurgery.
- Know evaluation protocols and appropriate methodology to develop targeted and individualized rehabilitation intervention programs considering clinical picture variability and environmental and emotional conditions of the child and adolescent.
- Know the tools and specific methods to achieve the objectives outlined in the rehabilitation program.
- Be able to recognize and evaluate the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions in the context of neurological pathologies of children and adolescents.
- Know the clinical symptoms, functional alterations, and pathogenetic mechanisms of major locomotor apparatus developmental alterations.
- Know evaluation protocols and appropriate methodology to develop targeted intervention programs.
- Be able to recognize and evaluate the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions in the context of pediatric orthopedic pathologies.
- Know the clinical symptoms, functional alterations, and pathogenetic mechanisms of communicative-linguistic developmental alterations, particularly those due to anatomical-functional alterations of the oropharyngeal and auditory apparatus.
- Know instrumental methods for evaluating these alterations.
- Know the clinical symptoms, functional alterations, and pathogenetic mechanisms of cognitive disabilities and neurolinguistic pathologies in the evolving age.
- Know evaluation protocols and appropriate methodology to develop targeted and individualized rehabilitation intervention programs considering clinical picture variability and environmental and emotional conditions of the child and adolescent.
- Be able to recognize and evaluate the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions in the context of cognitive and neurolinguistic disorders of children and adolescents.
- Know regulatory sources.
- Know the health profession and professional act.
- Have knowledge of the Italian healthcare protection system, AASSLL, evolution of professions in the rehabilitation area, and concepts of quality.
- Learn to collect epidemiological data for maintaining health and preventing disease. Safety procedures in the healthcare context.
Training Objectives Year III:
- Know the basics of emergency medicine and first aid: acute patient, respiratory support, assisted ventilation, neurological function, and resuscitation.
- Be able to use protocols to evaluate patients in critical areas. Be able to use specific tools and methods to achieve the objectives outlined in the rehabilitation intervention plan.
- Appropriately use terminology.
- Know the main psychiatric conditions that may associate with developmental disabilities; be able to identify rehabilitation interventions with parallel interventions carried out by other members of the multidisciplinary team.
- Achieve mastery of relational and behavioral skills to activate verbal and non-verbal communication with the child.
- Be able to prepare a therapeutic setting that promotes welcome and facilitates interaction with the child and adolescent.
- Be aware of their professional role in group work in collaboration with other professionals composing the rehabilitation team.
- Be able to use body dynamics as an integration of mental functions and interpersonal relationships.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Ability At the end of the training path, graduates in Therapy of Neuro and Psychomotricity of the Evolving Age will have acquired a broad and extensive range of knowledge in basic sciences, characteristic disciplines, and communication and professional management fields.
In particular, they must achieve solid cultural and scientific foundations in:
- Preliminary, basic, biomedical, and psychological sciences for understanding biological phenomena, organ and apparatus functioning mechanisms, motor and psychomotor development, physiological phenomena, also in correlation with psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of disability;
- Sciences of Neuro and Psychomotricity Therapy, necessary to identify preventive and rehabilitative needs of the patient for implementing prevention, functional diagnosis, and dynamic-functional profile of the individualized educational plan; to carry out therapeutic activities for neuro-psicomotor, psychomotor, and neuropsychological disabilities in the evolving age using specific techniques for age groups and individual developmental stages; implement evaluation procedures of the interrelation between affective, cognitive, and motor functions for each neurological, neuropsychological, and psychopathological disorder of the evolving age; identify the need and implement the diagnostic and therapeutic balance between somatic representation and bodily experience, and between general functional potential and objectual relationship; develop and implement the therapeutic program that uses neuromotor schemes and projects as mental acts and as cognitive and metacognitive tools; also use body diagnosis as an integration of mental functions and interpersonal relationships; verify the adoption of prostheses and aids in relation to neuropsychological compensations and psychopathological risks; participate in functional rehabilitation for all acute and chronic pathologies of childhood; document the correspondences of the implemented rehabilitation methodology according to functional recovery objectives and the specific characteristics of pathologies that change in relation to development;
- Interdisciplinary and medical-surgical sciences for understanding physio-pathological elements applicable to different clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters; as well as knowing the critical elements for the appearance of symptoms indicating acute "life-threatening" pathology and performing first aid maneuvers (BLS);
- Sciences of Prevention and Healthcare Services to achieve the ability to analyze health problems of individuals and/or communities and the responses of healthcare and social services to the main needs of citizens;
- Statistical sciences, quantitative methods, and scientific update to develop knowledge of statistical tools useful for planning the research process, some analytical methods to choose and use in professional practice, using the best available scientific evidence in the literature in the field of Physiotherapy Sciences; as well as the ability to evaluate epidemiological data in the rehabilitation context;
- Health Management Sciences aimed at organizing rehabilitation activities through defining priorities, appropriateness, and using available resources, both by delegating tasks to collaborators and working in teams, ensuring continuity and quality of care;
- Computer knowledge allowing consultation of clinical and scientific databases, database management, and interaction with the network, particularly regarding e-learning opportunities. Knowledge of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian, within their specific field of competence and for exchanging general information and understanding international scientific literature.
- Teaching Tools: classroom activities, practical lessons, laboratory exercises, and internships.
The assessment of such knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through the following verification methods: Oral and written exams, simulated practical tests, assisted person practical tests, written reports, folder compilations.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Graduates at the end of the training path will be able to construct a rehabilitation setting aligned with therapeutic intervention, adopting problem-solving methodology (clinical reasoning) and implementing correlated procedures in diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation of child neuropsychiatric pathologies in the areas of neuro-psicomotricity, neuropsychology, and developmental psychopathology.
The application of knowledge will be developed considering fundamental aspects such as interpersonal and inter-professional relationships, organizational management of aspects directly related to the type of work performed.
This ability will be fully achieved through attendance at the Professional Internship and didactic laboratory activities, both quantitatively and qualitatively, through professional laboratory activities, systematic assessment of acquired professional skills via a logbook certifying presence and a validated assessment grid (GOVNPM) measuring attitudes, behaviors, and skills compiled by the Tutor and Coordinator at the end of each internship experience; the overall knowledge and skills will be assessed through an exam held at the end of each academic year (which, at the end of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd year, results in a 30-point exam evaluation). The entire set of activities is programmed by the Didactic Coordination Council and planned, monitored, and verified by the Coordinator of theoretical/practical activities and internships, who promotes meetings with tutors, students themselves, proposes training activities, facilitates students in developing self-training, accessing bibliographic sources, etc.
Teaching Tools: classroom activities, didactic laboratories, practical lessons in laboratories or equipped rooms, internships, reading and interpretation of international literature, interactive teaching with e-learning tools and methodology.
The assessment of such knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through the following verification methods: Theoretical/practical exams, written reports on technical aspects (compilation of Functional Diagnosis and Rehabilitation Project and Project Verifications in the Clinical Folder), oral and written presentation of projects, practical tests.
III - Judgment Autonomy At the end of the study path, the graduate will be able to know and apply, autonomously, the appropriate rehabilitative therapeutic intervention using clinical reasoning as a guiding tool for decision-making within the possible options composing the various phases of the rehabilitation process. This autonomy will be realized through the ability to effectively respond to individual and/or collective health needs as a single operator or in a multidisciplinary team, opting for the best therapeutic strategies, identifying appropriate approaches and tools, performing data collection (including social context analysis), neuropsychomotor diagnosis/evaluation, defining prognosis and therapeutic objectives (short, medium, and long term), developing the therapeutic program, selecting and applying appropriate neuromotor methodologies and techniques for the clinical case (including intensity, time, type of therapeutic approach) according to the best possible and available scientific evidence, following international guidelines and Evidence-Based practice; in ethical terms, it will manifest through respect for reference regulations, professional, legal, health, and ethical standards.
The judgment autonomy of the graduate in Therapy of Neuro and Psychomotricity of the Evolving Age will be fully realized through the habitual and judicious use of communication, knowledge, technical skills, clinical reasoning (diagnostic and evaluative process), emotions, values, and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual or community.
Teaching Tools: classroom activities, didactic laboratories, practical lessons in laboratories or equipped rooms, Internship, reading and interpretation of international literature.
Verification Methods: written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, clinical case discussions, definition of Rehabilitation Plan/Program and compilation of the clinical folder for their area of competence.
IV - Communication Skills At the end of the study path, the graduate must be able to best manage communication as the ability to establish a meaningful therapeutic relationship with the child and their family and to establish an effective relationship within the multidisciplinary team; they must also be able to use communication tools in the healthcare context, demonstrating the ability to compile the clinical folder as per their competence, draft a therapeutic report, design a neuromotor intervention, and communicate it verbally and in writing. They must be able to communicate appropriately in international scientific contexts to convey ideas, problems, and related solutions.
Teaching Tools: classroom and laboratory activities, Internship.
Verification Methods: written and oral reports on communication aspects of the rehabilitation setting; briefings with tutors and coordinators; oral and written presentation of projects; Internship.
V - Learning Ability The graduate in Therapy of Neuro and Psychomotricity of the Evolving Age will be able to conduct a self-assessment of their educational level to maintain their knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice and to plan self-training paths to enhance their competencies, with particular reference to Evidence-Based Practice in rehabilitation and physiotherapy.
Over the three years, they will acquire learning abilities and competencies enabling, at the end of the path, the continuation of studies with high autonomy.
This ability will be developed and verified through exam preparation, attendance and evaluation of the internship (where theory and practice are combined), critical use of scientific literature and bibliography for final exam preparation.
Teaching Tools: classroom activities, seminars, simulation laboratories (also in e-learning), internship.
The assessment of learning abilities will be carried out through the following verification methods: Theoretical-practical exams, written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, clinical case discussions, definition of Rehabilitation Plan/Program and compilation of the clinical folder for their area of competence; research and production of teaching materials.
Work Context Function.
Work Context Function:
Graduates are healthcare professionals entitled to the attributions provided by the Ministry of Health Decree of January 17, 1997, No. 56 and subsequent modifications and integrations; or they carry out prevention, therapy, and rehabilitation interventions for child neuropsychiatric diseases in the areas of neuro-psicomotricity, neuropsychology, and developmental psychopathology, in collaboration with the multidisciplinary team of child neuropsychiatry and in collaboration with other disciplines in the pediatric field. Graduates in neuro and psychomotricity of the evolving age, in reference to medical diagnoses and prescriptions, within their specific competencies, adapt therapeutic interventions to the unique characteristics of patients in the evolving age with multifaceted clinical conditions that change over time in relation to emerging functions; identify and develop, within the multidisciplinary team, the prevention, therapy, and rehabilitation program aimed at overcoming the health needs of a child with developmental disability; implement therapeutic and rehabilitative interventions for perceptual-motor disorders, neurocognitive disorders, and symbolization and interaction disorders in children from birth; implement procedures for the inclusion of individuals with neuro-psicomotor and cognitive disabilities and handicaps; collaborate within the multidisciplinary team with school operators for the implementation of prevention, functional diagnosis, and dynamic functional profile of the individualized educational plan; carry out therapeutic activities for neuro-psicomotor, psychomotor, and neuropsychological disabilities in the evolving age using specific techniques for age groups and individual developmental stages; implement evaluation procedures of the interrelation between affective, cognitive, and motor functions for each specific neurological, neuropsychological, and psychopathological disorder of the evolving age; identify the need and implement the diagnostic and therapeutic balance between somatic representation and bodily experience, and between general functional potential and objectual relationship; develop and implement the therapeutic program that uses neuromotor schemes and projects as mental acts and as cognitive and metacognitive tools; also use body diagnosis as an integration of mental functions and interpersonal relationships; verify the adoption of prostheses and aids in relation to neuropsychological compensations and psychopathological risks; participate in functional rehabilitation for all acute and chronic pathologies of childhood; document the correspondences of the implemented rehabilitation methodology according to functional recovery objectives and the specific characteristics of pathologies that change in relation to development; carry out study, teaching, and specific applied research and professional consulting activities in healthcare services and places requiring their professional competence; contribute to the training of support staff and directly participate in updating related to their professional profile; carry out their professional activities in healthcare structures, public or private, in dependency or as self-employed professionals.
Function-Associated Competencies.
Function-Associated Competencies:
The Neuro and Psychomotricity Therapist of the Evolving Age is placed within the National Health Service (SSN) and Regional framework in dependency or as a self-employed professional. Additionally, this figure finds opportunities in accredited private structures, clinics, and rehabilitation centers, as well as in state educational structures or local authorities.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Opportunities:
The Neuro and Psychomotricity Therapist of the Evolving Age is placed within the National Health Service (SSN) and Regional framework in dependency or as a self-employed professional. Additionally, this figure finds opportunities in accredited private structures, clinics, and rehabilitation centers, as well as in state educational structures or local authorities.
