Roles President MARIAGRAZIA PERILLI Program, Texts, and Objectives Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN Degree Awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques (enabling the Sanitary Profession of Biomedical Laboratory Technician)
Specific Educational Objectives.
The educational objectives of the Biomedical Laboratory Techniques study program are achieved through a training path based on the acquisition of basic and characteristic knowledge and skills of the sector, with reference to the training of the biomedical laboratory technician figure, in the following areas:
-biomedical sciences, such as, for example, biochemistry, applied biology, histology, human anatomy, etc.;
-first aid sciences, such as, for example, pharmacology and anesthesiology;
-preparatory sciences, such as, for example, applied physics, computer science, and medical statistics;
-biomedical laboratory sciences and techniques, such as, for example, clinical biochemistry and clinical molecular biology, medical genetics, clinical pathology, etc.;
-medical-surgical and interdisciplinary clinical sciences, such as, for example, pathological anatomy, medical oncology, etc.;
-prevention sciences for health services, such as, for example, hygiene, medical imaging diagnostics, etc.;
-health management sciences, such as, for example, business economics;
-interdisciplinary sciences, such as, for example, information processing systems;
-human and psychopedagogical sciences, such as, for example, psychology.
TRAINING PATH The degree program is conducted over 3 years, organized into semesters, with the acquisition of 180 CFU. The training path aims to provide knowledge/skills in the disciplinary areas mentioned above, which are also fundamental as prerequisites for undertaking internship experiences, directly aimed at acquiring competencies in the reference field. Optional training activities (AFO) are also provided for student choice, as well as other training activities divided into further activities (e.g., laboratory, computer, seminar-based) and acquisition of English language knowledge at least at B1 level.
The training activities are primarily organized into integrated courses, aimed at providing a unified and, at the same time, multidisciplinary approach to achieving the objectives. Teaching methods include various types of activities (e.g., lectures, seminars/conferences, discussion groups, internship).
Internship activities are aimed at enabling students to acquire specific competencies as defined by the professional profile. The credits reserved for internships should be understood as the overall effort required for students to achieve the professional competencies of the "core curriculum." Practical and clinical internship training must be carried out under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors and coordinated, with a three-year mandate, by the Director of Professional Training Activities (DADP) belonging to the specific professional profile, holding a Specialist or Master's Degree in the respective class. The Director of Professional Training Activities is responsible for planning and organizing the internship: in collaboration with the Tutors of Technical-Practical Activities, they develop the annual internship training project and submit it for approval to the CAD. At the end of each academic year, a certification evaluation of the completed internship is conducted.
Upon completion of the training path, the student will be able to:
a) verify the biological material to be analyzed, in accordance with the request, and manage its preparation for subsequent phases;
b) plan and implement the analytical phase using appropriate methods and technologies, in compliance with recommendations and quality requirements;
c) evaluate and document the reliability of analysis results, referring to the laboratory quality systems and considering the health and care status of patients;
d) manage and implement methods and technologies in relation to the diagnostic process;
e) manage workplace safety, collaborating in risk assessment and improving prevention and protection measures;
f) independently conduct database and search engine investigations related to different laboratory technologies, to implement clinical and biomedical research applications;
g) respect ethical and deontological principles in various processes and activities;
h) manage their own educational and professional growth in relation to technological, scientific, and social progress.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the Bachelor's Degree, students will be able to demonstrate knowledge and the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- biomedical and medical-surgical, in relation to the structural and functional principles of biological macromolecules, cells, tissues, and organs of the human body, and their organization, to interpret the main mechanisms altering organ and system functions, fundamental pathogenic processes, and interventions to safeguard health;
- biomedical laboratory sciences, in relation to laboratory organization, maintenance of high quality standards, understanding of the correct application of methodologies, even advanced, used for diagnostic or research purposes in different processes and applicable to biomedical laboratories (e.g., analytical processes and chemical-clinical, microbiological, pathological anatomy, clinical biochemistry, clinical pathology, and hematology analyses, including pharmacotoxicological, biotechnological, immunohematological, molecular biology, immunometric, genetic analyses, with in vitro cultures and anatomo-cytopathology and sector rooms);
- computer, information processing, statistical, and applied physics sciences for understanding the use and consultation of databases, data processing, even in epidemiological fields, and the physical principles applied to medicine;
- health management for understanding the need to act according to regulations in a complex organizational system such as the healthcare system;
- human and psychopedagogical sciences for understanding working relationships, areas of integration and interdependence with other operators, and professional autonomy in the healthcare context, also in relation to service users.
The training path includes supervised internship activities in healthcare facilities contracted with the University or university/research laboratories.
Optional training activities are also provided, as well as other activities chosen by the student in accordance with the educational objectives of the study program, and knowledge of the English language at least at B1 level.
Teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures; - guided reading and application; - demonstrations, diagrams, and graphic materials; - cognitive map construction; - case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; - exercises and simulations; - internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, step-by-step case tests, project work, reports; - classroom discussions; - evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and professional practice reports).
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding At the end of the course, graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques must be able to:
- manage biological samples in terms of appropriateness and the entire analytical process;
- correctly set up and conduct analytical methods in relation to various types of analyses;
- maintain high quality and safety standards in laboratory organization and analytical procedures;
- discuss obtained results, propose solutions for problem-solving and methodology optimization, document used procedures with appropriate scientific language;
- possess knowledge of first aid techniques in case of emergency.
Teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures; - guided reading and application; - demonstrations, diagrams, and graphic materials; - cognitive map construction; - case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; - exercises and simulations; - internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral exams, step-by-step case tests, project work, reports; - classroom discussions; - evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and professional practice reports).
III - Judgment Autonomy The Biomedical Laboratory Technician graduate must demonstrate judgment autonomy through the following skills:
- demonstrate ability to account for their professional practice in accordance with the professional profile;
- use critical thinking skills to provide effective technical-diagnostic services;
- assume responsibility for their actions in relation to work activity goals and priorities;
- demonstrate ability to consider other operators in the exercise of their actions;
- apply ethical principles in their professional behavior.
Teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop expected outcomes: - Case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; - Internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility; - Debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences. Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes: - Written and oral exams, step-by-step case tests; - Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports on professional practice).
IV - Communication Skills Graduates in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques must develop the following communication skills:
- ability to listen and communicate appropriately with users and different healthcare professionals using various communication forms: written, verbal, non-verbal;
- ability to establish effective relationships with other healthcare professionals;
- demonstrate ability to transmit and manage information to users within their work context;
- demonstrate ability to use information and computer technologies in their work context;
- establish professional and collaborative relationships with other healthcare professionals, aware of the specificities of different professional roles.
Teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop expected outcomes: - Videos and critical analysis, simulations, narratives, and testimonials; - Case and relational situation discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions; - Internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team. Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes: - Observation of film or written frames, dialogues with structured grids; - Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets, and clinical reports).
V - Learning Ability The Biomedical Laboratory Technician graduate must develop the following self-learning abilities:
- demonstrate ability in self-assessment of their competencies and identify their development and learning needs;
- demonstrate proficiency in planning, organizing, and developing their actions;
- demonstrate ability for collaborative learning and sharing knowledge within work teams;
- develop independent study skills;
- demonstrate ability to seek necessary information to solve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, critically selecting secondary sources (guidelines, systematic reviews) and primary sources (research studies).
Teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop expected outcomes: - Problem-Based Learning (PBL); - Use of cognitive maps; - Use of self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment; - Research methodology workshops for printed and online literature; - Guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English. Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes: - Project work, reports on specific research mandates; - Tutor supervision of the internship path; - Active participation in work and debriefing sessions; - Adherence to deadlines and quality in the presentation of deliverables.
Work Function.
Work Function:
The Biomedical Laboratory Technician, holding the university degree enabling the profession, is the healthcare professional who can perform laboratory analysis and research activities related to various types of analyses (e.g., biomedical and biotechnological, in the field of clinical biochemistry and clinical molecular biology, microbiology, virology, parasitology, pharmacology, immunology, clinical pathology, hematology, cytology, histopathology, and pathological anatomy).
Upon completion of the course, the Biomedical Laboratory Techniques graduate independently performs technical roles in collaboration with qualified personnel responsible for different responsibilities, and must be able to:
a) manage sampling and verification of biological material to be analyzed in accordance with the request;
b) plan and implement the analytical phase using appropriate methods and technologies, in compliance with laboratory quality recommendations and requirements;
c) critically evaluate and document the reliability of test and analysis results in relation to the laboratory quality system;
d) manage and implement methods and technologies supporting biomedical research laboratories;
e) manage workplace safety and collaborate in risk assessment, improvement, and optimization of prevention and protection measures;
f) independently conduct database and search engine investigations to acquire new knowledge related to different laboratory technologies and apply them to improve analytical methods and biomedical research;
g) respect ethical and deontological principles in collaborative interdisciplinary relationships and with other healthcare professionals;
h) manage their own educational and professional growth in line with technological, scientific, and social progress.
Competencies Associated with the Function.
Competencies Associated with the Function:
The Biomedical Laboratory Technician must have acquired knowledge, skills, and abilities of a disciplinary and transversal nature:
- basic competencies, referring to preparatory sciences (e.g., applied physics, computer science, medical statistics), biomedical sciences (e.g., biochemistry, anatomy, histology, physiology, immunology, general pathology), and first aid (e.g., anesthesiology, pharmacology); characteristic competencies, referring to medical-surgical sciences, biomedical laboratory sciences and techniques (e.g., clinical biochemistry and clinical molecular biology, medical genetics, clinical pathology and microbiology, pathological anatomy, biomedical laboratory sciences), prevention and health services (e.g., medical imaging diagnostics, hygiene), interdisciplinary (e.g., information processing systems) and clinical interdisciplinary (e.g., oncology, rheumatology, blood and skin diseases), human and psychopedagogical (e.g., general psychology), and health management (e.g., labor law and business economics);
- competencies in the use of methodologies and technologies used in different areas of the biomedical laboratory, also in relation to privacy protection, computer science, and data processing, for consulting clinical-healthcare/scientific databases and archiving reports;
- competencies in the functioning, organization, and management of laboratory equipment, also in relation to health and safety regulations in the workplace and those governing the organization of the Healthcare System;
- organizational competencies, establishing priorities with efficient time management;
- relational competencies, aimed at facilitating interaction with colleagues and medical and administrative staff;
- competencies for developing self-learning processes and continuous updating.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
Biomedical Laboratory Techniques graduates perform their activities in public or private laboratory structures, in dependent or freelance status, also contributing to the training of support staff and operating within the update of their reference profile.
The main employment opportunities are identifiable in:
- various specialized areas of hospital and non-hospital laboratories belonging to the National Health Service
- similar private structures and Scientific Research and Care Institutes (IRCCS)
- public and private analysis and quality control laboratories;
- research laboratories.

Roles President ALESSANDRA SPLENDIANI Course content, textbooks and objectives Official languages of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in Techniques of Medical Radiology, Imaging and Radiation Therapy (Eligible for the Health Profession of Medical Radiology Technician)
Specific educational objectives.
Graduates in the Course of Study in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy must have acquired knowledge, skills and attitudes to practice the profession of Medical Radiology Health Technician, as described in the specific professional profile.
The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy is eligible to perform, independently or in collaboration with other health professionals, on medical prescription, all interventions requiring the use of ionizing and non-ionizing radiation, thermal energy, ultrasound and magnetic resonance, as well as interventions for physical and dosimetric protection.
They must possess indispensable training in the field of protection from ionizing and non-ionizing radiation.
These competencies must be immediately applicable in the workplace.
To achieve these goals, the graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy must be able to:
use methodologies and tools for quality control, evaluation and review of equipment and technical procedures;
implement regulations regarding safety and protection from ionizing, non-ionizing radiation and biological risk, and use personal protection equipment;
establish professional and empathetic communication with patients and colleagues;
ensure patient comfort, safety and privacy during diagnostic-interventional investigations and radiation therapy treatments;
act competently and responsibly towards patients, the work team, institutions and civil society, adopting professional behaviors in line with ethical and deontological principles;
guarantee necessary patient assistance during the execution of radiological procedures;
welcome and manage patient preparation for diagnostic investigations or radiation therapy treatment, obtaining informed consent where applicable;
be able to use first aid techniques in case of emergency;
collaborate with other health professions, colleagues and all staff to ensure optimal service functioning and contribute to problem-solving;
use information systems present in the Health Service for data collection, analysis and information management;
seek the best scientific evidence to deepen areas of uncertainty or improvement in their professional practice;
be prepared for continuous updating and training activities, ensuring the maintenance of the highest possible professional level;
contribute to the training and updating of health personnel in their areas of competence;
contribute to research in the health field;
know English language for the acquisition, exchange of instructions and information in scientific and professional fields.
In particular, the graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy must be able to:
Radiology –
perform independently, on medical prescription, radiological examinations of the skeletal system, chest, abdomen and breast, as well as computerized bone mineral density examinations, CT and MRI without contrast, in compliance with national and international protocols and guidelines;
collaborate with the health team in performing radiological procedures in emergency-urgent situations in emergency department, operating room, bedside, CT, MRI and angiography;
collaborate directly with the radiologist in all remaining diagnostic and interventional investigations using ionizing, non-ionizing radiation, thermal energy and ultrasound;
manage the acquisition, processing, archiving and transmission of radiological examinations using HIS, RIS, PACS systems;
Radiation Therapy –
collaborate with the radiation therapist and health physicist in planning and executing radiation therapy treatment, including all complementary radiological investigations and dosimetric operations;
prepare and use auxiliary shielding, centering and immobilization devices for the patient;
prepare and position the patient for radiation therapy treatment and monitor correct centering;
implement quality assurance and control procedures for radiation therapy equipment;
perform dosimetric control of radiation therapy equipment;
collaborate with the radiation therapist and health physicist in planning and executing brachytherapy, IMRT, stereotactic radiosurgery, tomotherapy, TBI and IORT;
manage the technical part of the radiation therapy chart;
acquire specific competencies in the evaluation, management and control of oncological patients, also in collaboration with other health professionals.
Nuclear Medicine –
receive radioactive sources, managing their loading, unloading, movement, storage and disposal of radioactive waste, and perform related recordings;
perform necessary operations for the production of isotopes via Cyclotron and preparation of radioactive doses to be administered to patients and manipulated in vitro, and perform all other operations concerning the hot lab work;
implement quality assurance and control procedures for Nuclear Medicine equipment and environmental and personal contamination control;
collaborate with the nuclear physician in performing diagnostic investigations and radiometabolic procedures;
collaborate with the nuclear physician in in vitro studies and examinations using equipment to detect radio-nuclides in samples;
perform all static and dynamic scintigraphy, SPECT, PET and MOC examinations and any other examination using hybrid technologies;
perform decontamination of contaminated objects or environments and implement all operations related to radioprotection according to current regulations;
manage acquisition, processing and archiving procedures for diagnostic examinations;
collaborate with the nuclear physician in in vivo/vitro studies and examinations concerning the research, development and use of new generation radiopharmaceuticals;
Health Physics know in depth national and international regulations regarding protection from ionizing and non-ionizing radiation and the institutions and bodies dedicated to them;
apply principles and procedures of radioprotection and safety in MRI;
collaborate with the qualified expert in physical surveillance for protection against ionizing radiation;
use equipment dedicated to measuring ionizing radiation (ionization chambers, Geiger-Muller counters and dosimeters) and quantitative and qualitative analysis of radioactive isotopes (dose calibrators, sodium iodide and germanium detectors and multi-channel analyzers);
perform dosimetry and environmental and personal contamination measurements both external and internal.
perform gamma spectrometry on food and non-food samples;
use tools for quality control and evaluation on RX, MRI and ultrasound equipment and on display, processing and reporting monitors for radiological examinations;
express technical opinion during acquisition, commissioning and installation of new equipment, as well as after any repairs;
collaborate with the health physicist in acceptance, status and functional testing of equipment;
collaborate with the health physicist in periodic verification of LDR;
control the calibration and calibration of equipment dedicated to quality control;
collaborate with the health physicist in dosimetric operations on radiation therapy equipment;
perform the setup of radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery treatment plans;
perform quality control on radiopharmaceuticals;
contribute to the training of health personnel in radioprotection and to physical research in the health field;
TRAINING PATH
1st year Focused on providing a good knowledge of essential theoretical disciplines derived from basic sciences, in the perspective of their subsequent professional application. The fundamentals of disciplines characterizing the profession of Medical Radiology Health Technician and concepts of radioprotection and safety will also be learned, as requirements for undertaking the first internship experience aimed at orienting the student to the professional fields of reference and acquiring basic competencies.
2nd year Aimed at deepening specific sectors, procedures and techniques of Imaging Diagnostics such as CR and DR equipment, the mammography field, ultrasound, computed tomography, angiography and magnetic resonance, as well as basic techniques in nuclear medicine and radiation therapy and oncology.
Additionally, relational and communication skills will be acquired.
Multiple internship experiences are planned in contexts where the student can apply the knowledge, methodologies and techniques learned.
3rd year Specialized deepening in radiology, with particular reference to Interventional Radiology, Neuroradiology, Nuclear Medicine and Radiation Therapy.
Learning also focuses on acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice, health legislation and service organization, as well as legal, bioethical and deontological principles inspiring the profession.
The importance of internship experiences increases, where the student can experiment with a gradual assumption of autonomy and responsibility under the supervision of mentors. This logic is also reflected in the credit allocation for internship experiences, which gradually increases from the 1st to the 3rd year.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy demonstrates knowledge and understanding in the field of:
- PRELIMINARY SCIENCES that facilitate learning the constructive concepts and usage methods of equipment used in the profession of Medical Radiology Health Technician;
- BIOMEDICAL SCIENCES for understanding human anatomy and physiological and pathological processes related to health and disease;
- PREVENTIVE HYGIENE SCIENCES for understanding health determinants, hazards and risk factors, prevention strategies, collective and individual protection systems, and interventions aimed at safeguarding health and safety of workers and users;
- DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC TECHNICAL SCIENCES to ensure the use of appropriate methods and technologies, guaranteeing necessary radioprotection and safety measures;
- PSYCHOSOCIAL, ETHICAL, LEGAL AND ORGANIZATIONAL SCIENCES for understanding the complexity of the National Health System organization and the importance and usefulness of acting in accordance with regulations and guidelines. They also aim to foster understanding of professional autonomy, work relationships, and areas of integration and interdependence with other health professionals;
- INFORMATICS AND LANGUAGE DISCIPLINES to know and understand English and the processes of computerized management of clinical-radiological information and images.
Teaching tools, methodologies and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Lectures;
- Guided reading and application;
- Videos, image demonstrations, diagrams and graphic materials;
- Seminars;
- Individual study;
- Case discussions.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy applies knowledge, skills and understanding in the field of radiological sciences to:
-demonstrate a professional approach to work, possessing adequate skills, as well as abilities to support arguments to solve potential problems and interdisciplinary themes related to their field of study;
-develop reasoning in diagnostic and therapeutic techniques, ensuring the use of appropriate methods and technologies, guaranteeing necessary radioprotection and safety measures;
-integrate knowledge and skills by collaborating to maintain high quality standards in various contexts of Imaging Diagnostics, Radiation Therapy, Nuclear Medicine and Health Physics.
Teaching tools, methodologies and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Lectures;
- Demonstrations, diagrams and graphic materials;
- Case discussions with presentations in plenary sessions;
- Exercises and simulations;
- Internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Written and oral exams, staged case tests, project work, reports;
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets and professional practice reports).
III - Judgment autonomy The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy has the ability to:
-collect and interpret data and situations characterizing their professional activity to develop independent thinking and judgment, including reflection on relevant professional, social, scientific or ethical issues;
-use critical thinking skills to deliver effective technical-diagnostic and therapeutic performances;
-assume responsibility for their actions in relation to the goals and priorities of their work activity;
-identify criticalities in organizational contexts or diagnostic/therapeutic techniques, proposing solutions applying the best evidence while respecting deontological regulations.
Teaching tools, methodologies and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Case discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- Internship with supervised experiences in different contexts and with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility;
- Debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Written and oral exams, staged case tests;
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through structured evaluation sheets and clinical reports on professional practice).
IV - Communication skills The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy:
- communicates effectively and understandably, ideas, information, problems and solutions to the public and specialist interlocutors, justifying their actions and decisions;
- demonstrates listening and understanding abilities with users, colleagues, doctors and other professionals;
- communicates with users respecting cultural or ethnic differences;
- adapts language, using English when necessary, and verifies understanding of provided information;
- uses various specific information and computer technologies in their work context.
Teaching tools, methodologies and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives and testimonies;
- Case and relational situation discussions in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- Group and individual computer lab exercises on specific applications;
- Internship with supervised experiences in different contexts with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Observation of film or written frames, dialogues with structured grids;
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation sheets and clinical reports).
V - Learning ability The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy has developed abilities, strategies, learning methods and practical skills necessary to continue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
In particular:
- demonstrates self-assessment abilities of their own competencies and outlines their development and update needs;
- demonstrates ability for independent study;
- demonstrates autonomy in seeking necessary information to solve professional practice problems or uncertainties, selecting critically the literature;
- promotes their knowledge in academic and professional contexts.
Teaching tools, methodologies and training activities to develop expected outcomes:
- Problem-Based Learning (PBL);
- Use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower the student in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- Research methodology laboratories for printed and online literature;
- Guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes
- Project work, reports on specific research mandates;
- Tutor supervision on internship path;
- Active participation in work and debriefing sessions.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiation Therapy is eligible to perform, independently or in collaboration with other health professionals, on medical prescription, all interventions requiring the use of ionizing and non-ionizing radiation, thermal energy, ultrasound and magnetic resonance, as well as interventions for physical and dosimetric protection.
The graduate performs their activity in:
- imaging, radiation therapy, nuclear medicine and health physics departments and services operating in hospital and non-hospital structures of the National Health System and in similar private structures and Scientific Research and Care Institutes;
- production industries and sales agencies operating in the imaging and radiation therapy sector;
- university and non-university research centers in the biomedical sector;
- universities and national health service training offices, dealing with specific training in diagnostic medical techniques;
- free profession.

Program, textbooks, and objectives Official languages of teaching and assessment
ITALIAN
Specific educational objectives.
The professional-oriented bachelor's degree course in 'Techniques of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety' has been structured in accordance with the provisions of DM 446/2020 of August 12, 2020, and the recent DM 682/2023. It is designed as a specialized study path for training highly qualified technicians in Civil Protection and, more generally, in territorial management.

In general, compared to the declaration of the professional degree class 'Technical professions for construction and territory' (L-P01) to which the Study Course belongs, graduates in 'Techniques of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety' have:

- A preparation in basic disciplines aimed at acquiring an adequate theoretical-practical understanding of the methodologies and technologies typical of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety;
- Adequate knowledge of aspects related to technical and economic feasibility, cost estimation, and the production and realization process of works (including temporary ones) necessary for managing Civil Protection and Territorial Safety emergencies;
- Adequate knowledge of the methodological-operational aspects of engineering sciences, both in general and in depth regarding those related to Civil Protection and territorial management in the context of natural disaster effects;
- The ability to understand the impact of engineering solutions in the social and physical-environmental context within emergency management and territorial safety;
- Relational and decision-making skills;
- The ability to communicate effectively, in written and oral form, in Italian and at least one other language of the European Union;
- Basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of knowledge;
- Appropriate knowledge to carry out professional activities in various fields, including contributing to activities such as design, production, management and organization, technical-commercial structure assistance, risk analysis, safety management in prevention and emergency phases, both in self-employment and in manufacturing or service companies and public administrations, particularly within emergency management and territorial safety;
- A consolidated set of essential operational knowledge to work independently in the field of emergency management and territorial safety (e.g., without claiming completeness: topographic and cartographic surveying, georeferenced restitution of surveys, use of digital methodologies supporting emergency planning, management and updating of databases, site safety, particularly in relation to emergency management and territorial safety, design, work supervision, and vigilance of structural, distributional, and plant aspects related to temporary constructions for emergency management).

More specifically, graduates in 'Techniques of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety', without claiming completeness:

- Are able to characterize potential natural disasters;
- Can assess the magnitude of structures and services and quantify the number of people exposed to damage following natural disasters;
- Can define the necessary operational organization to reduce the effects of natural disasters (with particular attention to human life protection);
- Can define responsibilities at various command and control levels;
- Are able to define risk scenarios, with evaluation of vulnerability, exposure, and territorial hazard;
- Are able to collaborate in the design and implementation of interventions aimed at minimizing environmental and territorial risks and ensuring the protection of life;
- Are able to develop and manage territorial information systems, monitoring networks, and metric surveys of the territory;
- Are able to survey areas and structures.

The teaching organization is a direct consequence of the educational objective and the type of Course. It consists of a two-year period during which, through conventional methods, the courses are characterized by a strong professional orientation. Specific laboratory activities (predominantly practical exercises) are used as a teaching method throughout the entire training path. The training cycle concludes with a third year dedicated to internships at companies, public bodies, or private entities.

The training path is divided into four different learning areas:
- Basic area;
- Engineering area;
- Risk assessment and territorial safety area;
- Practical application area.

More specifically, the training path consists of six semesters. The first semester is dedicated to acquiring the tools of basic sciences (chemistry, physics, mathematics, and computer science). The second and third semesters are dedicated to acquiring basic, methodological, and technological preparation related to the disciplines characterizing the field of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety emergency management. The fourth semester is dedicated to applied disciplines typical of emergency management and territorial safety, such as natural risk assessment, emergency management, economic evaluation of emergency structures, and legislative aspects. The final year (fifth and sixth semesters) concludes the training path with three internships (at companies, private entities, and public bodies, including Civil Protection structures) focused on acquiring field competencies related to natural risk and emergency management. One of the internships is specifically oriented towards self-employment activities as specified in DM 682/2023. The first four semesters are characterized by laboratory activities (of strictly operational nature) during which, individually or in groups, students apply the necessary competencies in the field of emergency management and territorial safety. Laboratory activities include field or site work.

In other words, and in summary, the training path includes:
- Adequate knowledge of mathematical tools and other basic sciences to practically interpret and describe Civil Protection and Territorial Safety problems;
- Basic methodological and technological preparation accompanied by a solid culture in some of the characterizing disciplines, such as drawing, structural mechanics, soil mechanics, applied hydraulics, and structural safety, aimed at understanding the fields of construction, infrastructure, and territory, with particular attention to emergency management and territorial safety;
- Technical-practical preparation in the fields of topographic surveying, hydraulic constructions, structures, risk assessment and management, site safety, urban planning, hydrogeology and applied geology, and administrative law.

Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Upon completion of the degree, the graduate will have acquired the disciplinary knowledge forming the core foundation of the study course. In particular, at the end of the training process, the graduate will have:

- Adequate knowledge of mathematical tools and other basic sciences useful for understanding Civil Protection and territorial management issues;
- Basic methodological and technological preparation accompanied by a solid culture in civil and environmental engineering, related to drawing, structural mechanics, soil mechanics, applied hydraulics, and structural safety;
- Technical-practical preparation in the fields of topographic surveying, hydraulic constructions, structures, risk assessment and management, site safety, urban planning, hydrogeology and applied geology.

Additionally, the general approach of the Study Course, typical of a 'Professional-oriented Study Course', aims to provide students with the opportunity to develop awareness based on the balance between methodological rigor, inherent to scientific disciplines, and the practical and applied aspects that should characterize a professional-oriented Study Course. Consequently, the teaching approach involves theoretical training accompanied by examples, applications, laboratory activities (predominantly practical exercises), individual work, and assessments that encourage active participation, propositional attitude, autonomous processing ability, and communication of work results.

In accordance with the fundamental principles of the professional-oriented degree's training path, knowledge and understanding are acquired through lectures and laboratory activities (as required by regulations) in the form of practical exercises, during which students are also encouraged to interact in groups. Laboratory activities are also part of the verification process.

Verification of knowledge and understanding acquisition is carried out through:
- Written and/or oral exams.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Upon completion of the degree, the graduate will have acquired the disciplinary competencies enabling them to perform the functions of the professional profile they will occupy, involving them in the field of Civil Protection and territorial management. In particular, in accordance with the characteristics of the professional profile and the already mentioned employment opportunities, the graduate in 'Techniques of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety' will, among other things:

- Be able to frame Civil Protection and territorial management issues from a theoretical perspective;
- Be able to assess the risk level associated with natural disasters;
- Know and understand from a technical-practical perspective the effects of natural disasters;
- Be able to manage emergencies;
- Be able to design emergency plans;
- Know the regulatory framework governing verification and design activities for medium-complexity civil works;
- Have skills in technical drawing;
- Know the computer tools supporting design;
- Know the computer tools supporting territorial analysis.

In accordance with the fundamental principles of the professional-oriented degree's training path, the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is acquired through laboratory activities (predominantly practical exercises) characterizing the courses of the training path. This is complemented by the entire final year of the Study Course, which will consist almost exclusively (apart from the thesis writing) of a curricular internship at structures operating in the field of Civil Protection and Territorial Safety, during which students are also encouraged to interact in groups. Laboratory activities are also part of the verification process.

Verification of the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is carried out through:
- Evaluation of practical exercises conducted during the attendance of individual courses;
- Written and/or oral exams;
- Evaluation of internship reports;
- Thesis evaluation.

III - Independent judgment During the training process, students will acquire independent judgment: the ability to collect and interpret data necessary for the practical application of acquired knowledge and, therefore, for the development of competencies. In particular, students will have:

- The ability to conduct bibliographic research and use databases and other information sources;
- The ability to understand analytical techniques (including territorial), aware of their applicability and limitations;
- The ability to critically interpret the results of analyses (including territorial);
- The ability to choose and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods;
- The ability to combine theory and practice to solve problems in the field of Civil Protection and territorial management;
- Awareness of the non-technical implications of engineering practice.

The methodological training and necessary information to enable students to acquire all the above-mentioned abilities will be distributed in a coordinated and progressive manner within all courses and teaching activities of the study course.

Verification of the achievement of educational objectives for each student will be conducted in an integrated manner within all profit assessments provided during the study course.

IV - Communication skills Upon completion of the training process, the graduate will be able to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences. During the training process, students will acquire:

- The ability to work effectively both individually and as part of a group;
- The ability to communicate effectively with the engineering community and, in general, with society, both in national and international contexts;
- Knowledge of the safety and legal aspects and responsibilities of engineering practice, and the impact of solutions in the social and environmental context;
- Understanding of project management and commercial practices, such as risk management;
- Understanding of the importance of dissemination in the field of Civil Protection and territorial management.

These abilities will be developed through regular training activities and various discussion and comparison moments in group work and during various meetings with representatives of the business world (conferences, guided visits, etc.), as well as during the curricular internship period.

Verification of communication skills is carried out through written and/or oral exams, as well as other training activities, particularly through the final exam.

V - Learning ability The successfully completed training path will enable graduates to develop the learning abilities necessary to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy. Indeed, students are offered various tools to develop sufficient learning ability to pursue further studies (noting that enrollment in a master's degree does not constitute a natural outcome of the Study Course). The training path also involves students in part of it through individual work, offering the opportunity to verify and improve their learning ability. Other useful tools for achieving this ability include the production of reports requiring students to measure and understand new information not necessarily provided by the instructor, and internships and/or training periods.

Work context function.
Work context function:
The professional profile of graduates is characterized by the following functions in a work context:
- Design of data acquisition, management, and processing for environmental and territorial surveys;
- Collaboration in the design and implementation of interventions aimed at minimizing environmental and territorial risks and ensuring the protection of life;
- Collaboration in the design of civil works;
- Collaboration in the design of building systems;
- Surveying of areas and structures;
- Collaboration in control activities during the execution of civil works;
- Collaboration in assisted design and territory management, including defense against natural disasters;
- Development and management of territorial information systems, monitoring networks, and metric surveys of the territory;
Collaborating with other professional figures, such as:
- Civil Engineers;
- Environmental Engineers;
- Planners;
- Public safety specialists;
- Forest Corps agents;
- Firefighters.

Competencies associated with the function.
Competencies associated with the function:
In accordance with the above, the competencies provided by the Study Course can be summarized as follows, as the graduate:
- Is able to assess the risk level associated with natural disasters;
- Knows and understands from a technical-practical perspective the effects of natural disasters;
- Is able to manage emergencies;
- Is able to design emergency plans;
- Knows the regulatory framework governing verification and design activities for medium-complexity civil works;
- Has skills in technical drawing;
- Knows the computer tools supporting design;
- Knows the computer tools supporting territorial analysis.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The possible professional opportunities for graduates, within the context of collaboration with Public Authorities or Public or Private Companies, as well as in the field of self-employment, can be listed as follows:
- Public emergency planning offices;
- Professional offices operating in emergency planning;
- Construction and maintenance companies for works, plants, and civil infrastructure;
- Professional offices and companies designing works, plants, and civil infrastructure;
- Companies, bodies, consortia, and agencies managing and controlling systems of works and services;
- Companies, public and private bodies, professional offices dealing with the design, planning, implementation, and management of works and systems for environmental and territorial control and defense;
- Companies, laboratories, public and private bodies, professional offices dealing with measurements and surveys for controlling and protecting the territory;
- Companies, bodies, consortia, and agencies managing and controlling systems of works and services; service companies for feasibility studies of urban and territorial impact of infrastructure;
- Authorities and agencies for environmental and territorial planning and control;
- National and regional technical and cartographic services.

Regarding the possibility of enrollment in professional registers, it is emphasized that the degree is Qualifying and allows enrollment in the Register of Geometers and Licensed Geometers (DM 682/2023).

Continuation of studies in master's degrees is not a natural outcome for graduates of this course.

ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Degree in PREVENTION TECHNIQUES IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND WORKPLACES (licensed for the health profession of Environmental and Workplace Prevention Technician)
Specific educational objectives.
The educational objectives of the Degree Course are directed at enabling the graduate to acquire a preparation that allows them to:
- Acquire the necessary knowledge to understand biological phenomena, the main mechanisms of organ and system functioning in correlation with the social and environmental dimensions of health.
- Understand the fundamentals of pathophysiology applicable to different clinical situations, in relation to environmental quality parameters that may represent health risk conditions.
- Know the environmental and work factors that can influence human health status.
- Adequately know the quality processes regarding food production, transformation, marketing, and issues related to food health surveillance.
- Know the radioprotection standards set by European Union directives (d.l.vo 26 May 2000, n. 187);
- Plan, manage, and evaluate surveillance and inspection activities in living and working environments;
- Be able to conduct assessments and investigations for occupational accidents and diseases;
- Be able to collaborate with judicial administration in investigations on environmental property crimes, hygiene and safety conditions in living and working environments, and food;
- Act both individually and in collaboration with other health and social operators, utilizing support staff when necessary;
- Directly contribute to updating one's professional profile and research;
- Develop the ability to work in a team and integrate with other health professions;
- Know the general bioethical, deontological, legal, and medical-legal principles of the profession;
- Use at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian, within the specific area of competence and for general information exchange.
The specific objectives of the course provide the necessary competencies for entering professional activity at the end of the three-year program. For this purpose, the educational path must include knowledge in the basic prerequisite disciplines. The aspect of environmental risk factors will be developed in hygiene, epidemiology, and occupational medicine courses; and health impacts will be the subject of medical disciplines: internal medicine, respiratory diseases, and skin diseases. Prevention methods, especially focused on the environment, will be studied in hygiene, occupational medicine, radioprotection, environmental technical physics, and environmental health engineering. Special attention will be given to food, in terms of composition, transformation methods, and hygienic-sanitary surveillance. The educational path also includes knowledge of treatment plants for liquid and solid waste and water purification and potabilization, whose sampling techniques for plant control will be the subject of internship activities. The graduate must know the moral, ethical, and legal responsibilities connected to the profession of prevention technician.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The graduate in Prevention Techniques in the Environment and Workplaces, during the three-year educational period, must acquire knowledge of basic disciplines, general chemistry, organic chemistry, and physics. Must acquire the necessary knowledge to understand biological phenomena, the main mechanisms of organ and system functioning. Must know the determinants and main risk factors for human health, with particular attention to chemical and physical environmental factors or occupational exposure. Must know epidemiology, etiology, the natural history of infectious and chronic diseases, toxicology. Must know the most frequent diseases resulting from exposure to risk factors. Must be able to apply environmental prevention standards, with particular reference to food safety, safety of water for human use, waste disposal, air pollution, and workplace safety, also acquiring elements of environmental legislation.
Such knowledge will be acquired through attendance at basic, characteristic, and related training activities, organized into integrated courses to ensure a unified and interdisciplinary view of educational objectives, which can be supplemented by guided technical visits. The verification of achieving the expected learning outcomes occurs through written and/or oral exams.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The graduate in Prevention Techniques in the Environment and Workplaces must be able to apply the knowledge acquired during studies, must have understanding capabilities and skills to solve problems, even on new topics; in particular, must be able to manage surveillance and inspection activities in workplaces, be able to exercise surveillance and control activities on the quality of food and beverages for consumption; be able to monitor and control the compliance of structures and environments related to their activities and the safety conditions of facilities; be able to contest and notify, also in collaboration with judicial authorities, non-compliance with safety in the workplace. Such competencies will be acquired through professional internship activities, during "internship" periods in public structures and with exercises conducted with technical area teachers.
III - Judgment autonomy The graduate in Prevention Techniques in the Environment and Workplaces will be able to independently collect and interpret data collected in the quality control of food and beverages for human use, in the control of cooling and heating systems (domestic and industrial), in the control of water potabilization plants, and liquid and solid waste disposal. Must be able to collect and interpret "outdoor" and "indoor" pollution data using dedicated equipment. Must know how to collect and interpret data from radiation emissions, respecting radioprotection standards. The graduate must be able to identify the essential elements characterizing the profession of Prevention Technician, including moral, ethical, and legal responsibilities. Must acquire professional values including reliability, honesty, and integrity. Such competencies will be acquired through professional internship activities carried out at public structures and front-line teaching activities of disciplines related to these aspects.
IV - Communication skills The graduate in Prevention Techniques in the Environment and Workplaces must be able to describe, in clear and rigorous terms, general topics within the scope of activities and professional relationships, also with the help of multimedia systems. Must be able to interact with other figures involved in their professional activities. Communication skills will be developed throughout the educational path through seminars, reports on internship activities, activities related to the preparation of the final exam. The verification of achieving these skills will occur through the final exam, where ability, correctness, rigor of presentation, and the capacity for multimedia project presentation will be evaluated.
V - Learning ability The graduate in Prevention Techniques in the Environment and Workplaces must be able to undertake future studies or enhance their professional training; must be skilled in bibliographic research, database consultation, and online research; be able to apply new knowledge and methodologies; be able to work towards goals; be able to adapt to different work environments. The verification of learning ability will be continuous, and in particular, the ability to meet deadlines for submitting reports and the self-learning ability developed during the three-year period will be assessed.
Function in the workplace context.
Function in the workplace context:
The profession of Prevention Technician is characterized by competence in the evaluation and monitoring of living and working environments:
1) as provided by health and human activity protection regulations,
2) regarding safety and safeguarding the qualities inherent to each area,
3) regarding technological and hygienic aspects of food and beverages.
The consequent preventive intervention or control and sanctioning capabilities derive from the specific area of action and the role performed.
Competencies associated with the function.
Competencies associated with the function:
The professional competencies guaranteed at the end of the three-year educational program, with specific reference to employment opportunities, of our graduate include:
1) the ability to analyze and evaluate different environmental sectors: atmospheric air, air in confined environments, water for human consumption, wastewater, mineral and spring water, food from primary production to consumption, soil (characteristics and protection) with reference to the safety and protection of the general population, users, and consumers;
2) the ability to analyze and evaluate different production areas with reference to the safety and protection of workers' health;
3) the ability to intervene corresponding to the role (consultant, controller, UPG) both in concert with the responsible parties of the specific area, in collaboration with health managers, and finally in collaboration with the Judicial Authority.
The professional competencies related to occupational areas derive from the knowledge acquired in courses and the experiences gained within guided internships in public and private structures covering the broad scope of reference professional activities of the Prevention Technician.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
Employment opportunities for such professional figures include – in the public sector – the Health Service and in particular the Prevention Departments, which have historically relied on technical staff for part of the surveillance and inspection activities.
Within Prevention Departments (regardless of regional organizational variations), Prevention Technicians can use their competencies in public hygiene (housing quality, sports facilities, etc.), in the Food Hygiene and Nutrition Service, often in collaboration with the veterinary service for surveillance of animal-origin food, in the Occupational Medicine Service; in the public sector, regional environmental protection agencies use technical staff with the competencies of the profession in question for water protection, air quality monitoring, and surveillance of the correct treatment of solid and liquid waste, etc.
Also in the private sector, the workers' health protection regulations provide for multiple activity areas for Prevention Technicians, both among the mandatory figures of Legislative Decree 81/08 and in relation to the need to activate monitoring or training for workers, etc. The food industry can constitute an employment area for Prevention Technicians in relation to competencies in food hygiene and self-control. Companies involved in waste management, environmental management for local authorities, use the competencies of Prevention Technicians.

Program, Texts, and Objectives Official teaching and assessment languages. ITALIAN
Degree Awarded. Bachelor's Degree in PSYCHIATRIC REHABILITATION TECHNIQUE (qualifying for the health profession of Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technician)
Specific Educational Objectives. The graduate, upon completion of the training path, is able to:
- identify physical, psychological, and social needs and assess the need for assistance of people of different ages, cultures, and health statuses in various social contexts;
- assess social discomfort and psychiatric disability related to mental disorders, as well as identify the subject's potential and detect family and socio-environmental context resources and constraints;
- identify psychiatric rehabilitation care goals and formulate specific intervention programs aimed at recovery and development of the subject in treatment;
- implement interventions of varying complexity involving the teaching of social skills directed at the subject's rehabilitation/ability;
- implement rehabilitation interventions aimed at adherence to the care plan, interpersonal relationships of varying complexity, work activities where possible, and housing autonomy;
- work with families and the subject's social context to facilitate their reintegration into the community; establish and maintain helping relationships with the assisted person and their family;
- use evaluation and quality review tools for assistance, collaborating in the evaluation of outcomes of the rehabilitation program for individual subjects in relation to predefined goals and the social context;
- apply research results in rehabilitation to improve intervention quality;
- operate in the primary prevention context on the territory to promote network relationships, facilitate acceptance and management of at-risk situations and manifest pathologies;
- contribute to the training of support staff and directly participate in updating related to the professional profile;
- recognize and respect one's own and others' roles and competencies to collaborate with colleagues from one's own and other multidisciplinary teams.

Training Path
- 1 year – aimed at providing students with biomedical knowledge, the fundamentals of the professional discipline as prerequisites for undertaking the first internship experience for orientation in the psychiatric professional field and acquisition of basic professional competencies;
- 2 year – aimed at deepening clinical knowledge and rehabilitation professional competencies in the psychiatric field. At least internship experiences in Psychiatry Operational Units, structured in different contexts where students can follow the patient's path from initial reception to discharge and deepen knowledge acquired in clinical, therapeutic, and rehabilitation fields, as well as in organizational fields;
- 3 year – aimed at deepening specialist knowledge, but also acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice and the ability to work in a group; students can gradually assume responsibilities under expert supervision. Acquisition of scientific research methodology skills to support thesis development.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding The graduates in Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technique must demonstrate knowledge and understanding in the following areas:
- biomedical sciences for understanding physiological and pathological processes related to health and illness states of people at different life stages;
- neurobiological sciences underlying psychological processes through experimental evidence on humans related to normal and pathological subjects;
- basic knowledge on the general mechanisms of cultural processes, as a historical and cultural interpretative key for concepts of normality, health, illness, disability, handicap, and the historical evolution of assistance, care, and rehabilitation;
- psychosocial sciences for understanding normal and pathological relational dynamics and the defense or adaptation reactions of people to psychological and social discomfort;
- fundamental elements on psychological functions, main psychopathological phenomena, and psychiatric semiotics; knowledge of normal and pathological child development, general knowledge on aging phenomena and main pathologies characteristic of the elderly, with particular reference to the rehabilitation dimension;
- psychiatric foundations of rehabilitation within the context of clinical and social psychiatry: concepts of mental health and illness, classification of mental disorders, clinical aspects of major diseases, organization of psychiatric services, characteristics of the therapeutic relationship with particular regard to the rehabilitative perspective;
- fundamental knowledge of psychology and psychotherapy relevant to psychiatric rehabilitation, with specific references to major psychological thought currents and psychotherapeutic schools; different approaches to individual, group, and family therapy; main elements of psychodiagnosis and their relevance in psychiatric, clinical, and rehabilitative fields;
- organization of Psychiatric Operational Units, identifying: institutional purposes, scope of intervention, roles and competencies of professional figures present, connections and interactions with other public and private services;
- ethical, legal, and sociological sciences for understanding the complexity of the healthcare system, the importance and utility of acting in accordance with regulations and guidelines, as well as respecting ethical values and dilemmas encountered in daily practice; aimed at promoting understanding of professional autonomy, areas of integration and interdependence with other members of the psychiatric team and the service network;
- information sciences and languages with particular emphasis on English for understanding scientific literature, both printed and online.

Teaching Methods and Activities, Didactic Tools to Develop Expected Outcomes:
- formal lectures to introduce the topic
- guided reading and application to case studies
- videos, images, diagrams, and materials, graphs
- conducting simulations
- case discussions
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes
- written and oral exams
- staged case tests
- project work
- reports

II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding The graduate in Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technique demonstrates the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the exercise of their profession, particularly:
- integrates knowledge, skills, and attitudes to deliver effective, evidence-based rehabilitation interventions;
- uses a body of theoretical knowledge derived from psychiatry, psychological and social sciences, and other disciplines to recognize disabilities related to mental disorders in people receiving care at various ages and life stages;
- uses (and when possible integrates) different theoretical models in rehabilitation practice to facilitate the growth, development, and adaptation of individuals with mental disorders toward the best possible quality of life;
- is responsible for their own actions in providing and evaluating therapeutic rehabilitation interventions in accordance with professional quality standards, considering legal guidelines and ethical responsibilities as well as the rights of the assisted person;
- interprets and applies psychiatric research results to rehabilitation practice and links research processes to the theoretical development of psychiatric rehabilitation discipline;
- participates with the team in the realization of the therapeutic rehabilitation project and actively engages in problem identification, priority selection, identification of rehabilitation goals, selection and implementation of interventions in relation to professional competencies, identification of criteria and systems for evaluating achieved results;
- participates with the multidisciplinary team in evaluating the results achieved in the therapeutic rehabilitation process;
- facilitates the development of a safe environment for the assisted person in various care contexts, ensuring constant attention and vigilance.

Teaching Methods and Activities, Didactic Tools to Develop Expected Outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic
- guided reading and application to case studies
- videos, images, diagrams, and materials, graphs
- conducting simulations
- case discussions
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes
- written and oral exams
- staged case tests
- project work
- reports

III - Independent Judgment The graduate in Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technique demonstrates independent judgment in the exercise of their professional activity, particularly:
- recognizes the therapeutic value of relationships with the family of the assisted person and participates in their realization in harmony with team-shared guidelines;
- participates in care and rehabilitation decision-making and acts in accordance with legal, ethical, and deontological dimensions regulating healthcare organization and professional responsibility;
- contributes to organizing global rehabilitation care through the appropriate use of available resources, ensuring unity, continuity, and quality of interventions;
- analyzes and solves problems within their competence, considering their complexity, and handles unexpected situations with appropriate solutions.

Teaching Methods and Activities, Didactic Tools to Develop Expected Outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic
- problem-based learning (PBL)
- videos, images, diagrams, and materials, graphs
- conducting simulations
- case discussions
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes
- written and oral exams
- staged case tests
- reports

IV - Communication Skills The graduate in Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technique demonstrates communication skills in interpersonal relationships, particularly:
- establishes and maintains effective relationships with the assisted person, their family, and others interested in that user, adopting attitudes that facilitate contact with the person (respecting interpersonal distance, attention to physical contact, movements, tone of voice);
- demonstrates effective communication skills with users of different cultures and lifestyles, recognizes the characteristics of a trusting relationship and applies them in the professional relationship, not in a friendly relationship;
- implements mental health education interventions for individuals or groups and therapeutic education interventions aimed at self-management of the disorder, treatment, and rehabilitation;
- works with families and the subject's social context to facilitate their reintegration into the community through helping relationships with the assisted person and their family;
- aware of the therapeutic value of relationships with the family of the assisted person, participates in their realization in harmony with team-shared guidelines;
- evaluates the possibility of providing assistance to families in modifying any incorrect or distorted representations regarding the patient or situation and activates to facilitate their involvement in the therapeutic rehabilitation process, reducing physical, psychological, or relational barriers;
- actively participates in service meetings and activities, contributing knowledge and experience.

Teaching Methods and Activities, Didactic Tools to Develop Expected Outcomes:
- lectures to introduce the topic
- video films
- role-playing simulations
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes
- written and oral exams
- staged case tests
- reports

V - Learning Ability The Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technician does not exhaust their learning in the three-year training period but draws on daily operational activities to reflect on their experience and enhance their competence. To refine this ability, during the training path, the student:
- develops skills to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activity as a source of new learning;
- develops the ability to pose questions related to the exercise of their activity, formulating relevant questions at the right time, place, and to the right interlocutors;
- demonstrates the ability to continuously seek opportunities for self-learning;
- takes responsibility for their professional development and responds to the continuous evolution of knowledge in psychopathological and therapeutic rehabilitation fields;
- demonstrates autonomous study skills and uses effective and relevant evidence-based research methods.

Teaching Methods and Activities, Didactic Tools to Develop Expected Outcomes:
- problem-based learning (PBL);
- use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower students in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- research methodology workshops for online and printed bibliographic research.
Assessment Tools to Verify Achievement of Expected Outcomes:
- written and oral exams;
- project work;
- reports.

Work Context Function.
Work Context Function:
The Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technician works individually or in a team with the specific function of case-manager with specialized competencies in assessing the social functioning of individuals with mental disorders and their resource group. Additionally, they carry out integrated psychosocial interventions aimed at recovering social skills with individuals with mental disorders and members of the resource group based on their life goals.

Competencies Associated with the Function.
Competencies Associated with the Function:
The Psychiatric Rehabilitation Technician performs their professional activity aimed at rehabilitation and social reintegration of individuals in care, in public or private healthcare facilities and services:
- Mental Health Centers
- Day Centers
- Residential Rehabilitation Communities
