Roles Study plan approval responsible LINA MARIA CALANDRA Chair LINA MARIA CALANDRA Program, textbooks, and objectives Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Specific educational objectives.
The Bachelor's degree in Sciences of Education and Training (SEF) aims to provide graduates with solid knowledge and skills in the main areas of pedagogical, methodological-didactic, psychological, social, historical-anthropological-geographical, and legal sciences, enabling them to analyze complex educational phenomena and problems and to design, implement, and evaluate educational interventions, in order to provide educational support and care to children, young people, and adults throughout life. To respond to the growing educational demand, the Course provides training aimed at preparing a versatile professional figure capable of meeting the educational needs expressed by social reality and operating within services for childhood, individuals, and communities.
In this sense, the graduate will be able to
- master the main epistemological-disciplinary foundations of basic disciplines;
- master principles, languages, and tools of basic disciplines and pedagogical and methodological-didactic disciplines;
- integrate and combine knowledge and skills related to different disciplinary fields (pedagogical, sociological, psychological, etc.) to read and interpret educational problems, phenomena, facts, and events in their various dimensions, synchronic and diachronic, including intercultural, inclusion, and gender aspects;
- be able to combine different disciplinary skills and content (sociological, psychological, etc.) from an interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral perspective to build appropriate educational projects corresponding to the needs of the target groups (children, adolescents, adults, and elderly);
- master methods, techniques, and tools for managing educational activities, processes, and interventions, with particular attention to the age group 0-6 years and pre-adolescence;
- combine theoretical knowledge with methodological and technical skills to analyze realities and needs and to design, implement, manage, and evaluate qualitatively appreciable educational projects and interventions, also making use of new technologies;
- master specific methodologies, tools, and techniques in relation to the target groups of the educational intervention;
- be able to identify appropriate techniques and tools depending on the context to develop relevant educational strategies for children, adolescents, adults, and elderly, as well as for individuals, groups, or communities;
- master communication and relational skills to interact appropriately with targets of different ages (children, young people, adults, and elderly) and to manage individual and group relationships effectively, also in reference to intercultural processes, social inclusion, and disability;
- be able to manage communication, interact, and operate in contexts with high cultural and variability;
- master organizational skills to manage projects and interventions directed at childhood, pre-adolescence, and adulthood;
- be able to identify educational needs to respond appropriately to emerging societal needs;
- be able to decode and interpret complex events, facts, and phenomena, even within recent societal transformations, to understand their characteristics and activate partnership forms and collaborative networks to promote quality educational interventions;
- combine transversal knowledge, methods, and techniques of work and research to elaborate and manage educational interventions in educational services;
- use appropriate methods and techniques of educational research and analysis tools to understand educational needs, with particular reference to inclusion issues, intercultural questions, gender dynamics, and emergent problems;
- be able to collaborate in professional, multiprofessional, and inter-institutional teams;
- be able to combine theoretical knowledge with experiential knowledge acquired through external internships carried out at public and private entities and third-sector organizations;
- master appropriate tools for data analysis, communication, and information management;
- master observational, recording, and analysis tools for critical reflection on projects and interventions activated.
- master, in written and oral form, a foreign language of the European Union, in addition to Italian.
Therefore, during the first year, the student will acquire all the necessary theoretical knowledge and skills to define a theoretical, technical, and methodological framework necessary for the profession of Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator and Educator in services for childhood. During the second and third years, disciplinary fields will offer more specific skills accompanied by professionalizing laboratories, with particular attention to the age group 0-6 years, to better understand the various professional opportunities in the different contexts where this figure operates, proposing targeted intervention proposals.
The Course is structured in cultural/disciplinary axes that are articulated into learning areas.
1 - Pedagogical and methodological-didactic area: disciplinary and methodological knowledge aimed at understanding and interpreting complex educational phenomena, facts, and processes, as well as intercepting new needs to activate interventions directed at children, adolescents, adults, and elderly, as well as individuals, groups, or communities, calibrated on contexts and promoting educational and formative well-being, also with the intent of enabling the graduate to operate in professional teams or multidisciplinary teams implementing forms of cross-sectoral and inter-institutional co-design. These are knowledge and skills related to pedagogical disciplines, educational design, and evaluation, useful for better managing methodological-didactic interventions, the relationship, and educational communication, to ensure care and development of learning and potential of individuals and groups, programming, implementing, managing, and evaluating educational interventions, also in reference to social inclusion processes, gender issues, intercultural issues, and disability.
2 - Psychological and social disciplines area: knowledge and skills related to developmental processes at all ages of the individual, with particular attention to childhood, psychological functioning, relationships between individuals and groups, and methods of study and intervention techniques that, in different operational models (individual, relational, group), characterize clinical psychology applications in different contexts (people, groups, systems) for solving their problems, to be applied in the different contexts where the graduate operates. Such knowledge and skills help to read, interpret, and intercept problems and forms of discomfort to be addressed in an integrated way with other professional functions, within the limits of their educational, mediation, intervention, orientation, promotion, and support functions for educational and psycho-physical well-being. Moreover, it includes adequate knowledge and skills related to basic disciplines, methods, and educational techniques useful for programming and implementing individual and social educational projects related to the treatment of social discomfort situations for individuals, families, groups, and communities, also in the perspective of social inclusion. It refers to sociological disciplines encompassing theoretical and methodological aspects, as well as issues related to the implementation of interventions for specific target groups.
3 - Historical-anthropological area: in-depth knowledge and skills related to the ability to interact with cultures, including gender cultures and immigrant populations, from the perspective of multicultural and multi-ethnic social relationships, as well as those connected to the territoriality of phenomena in both diachronic and synchronic senses, to implement appropriate educational interventions.
4 - Economic-legal and technological-informatic area: knowledge and skills related to communication, documentation, and information management, particularly regarding citizenship rights and accompanying individuals in difficulty; legal knowledge and skills aimed at supporting advocacy and protection functions of subjects, guiding them in the space of fundamental rights, framing professional functions within norms and deontology; information technology and scientific knowledge useful for supporting the analysis of real situations through data processing.
5 - Linguistic and expressive area: knowledge and skills related to languages and verbal and non-verbal languages realized through the contribution of multiple disciplines: related to music education, art and image, body and movement, as well as knowledge and skills related to the effective use, in written and oral form, of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian, also in reference to terminology related to the professional context, accompanied by a good acquisition of specialist and sector languages. All these disciplines contribute to defining a common expressive area related to the need for the Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator to adopt methodological and communicative tools in the exercise of their function.
6 - Scientific area: knowledge and skills related to sciences concerning the knowledge of the world and environment: physical and geographical.
The scientific area, therefore, concerns a wide variety of subjects, so job opportunities will be the most diverse.
Fundamentally, it is divided into:
7 - Transversal area of application and transfer of skills: the ability to apply knowledge and skills in situational contexts is linked to training experiences aimed at strengthening the acquisition process through qualifying internships (training project) at public and private entities and third-sector organizations, as well as through other activities (laboratories, workshops, co-designed seminars with welcoming structures, etc.) useful for increasing the transfer of precise skills, also in reference to a better understanding of the employability of skills and occupational prospects. These are professional skills to be acquired on the field, through significant internship experiences in all operational contexts within which the graduate can perform their functions, with particular reference to educational services, structures for childhood and adolescence, and all contexts (public, private, and non-profit) where educational projects are implemented (nurseries, family houses, etc.).
Consistent with the indicated axes, the Course, alongside basic, characteristic, and related disciplines, provides:
– one or more professionalizing laboratories aimed at simulating and transferring practical applications of what is learned in curricular courses;
– mandatory internship activities:
a. indirect, which, carried out under the guidance of the university tutor at the Department's structures or other sites, aims to prepare, reflect, and discuss the main observation and documentation methods to be activated in the phases of direct internship, and in supervision phase, in the drafting of the final internship report;
b. direct, which, carried out at the University of L'Aquila's conventioned structures, under the guidance of a Supervising Tutor, aims to apply knowledge and skills learned through courses and laboratories and to experience guided learning in the reality of educational and territorial services (local authorities, communities, private social organizations, etc.), allowing students to appropriately use observational techniques and documentation tools, which are part of professional action.
The offered training balances a strong territorial rooting (marked by forms of distress opened by the post-earthquake and economic crisis) and an openness to an international perspective, especially in a European key. In this sense, the training path prioritizes the characteristic disciplines provided in Class L-19 that most help develop a versatile Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator figure, capable of acting and collaborating with structures operating at local, national, and international levels, and to carry out systematic inter-institutional collaboration in internship and laboratory activities, as well as in other integrated training activities, aimed at qualifying the training as a whole (transversal skills such as soft skills). The integration between different teaching activities (courses, laboratories, internships) and between pedagogical, psychological, sociological, historical-anthropological, geographical, and legal approaches is pursued through an intense transversal and in-depth laboratory and seminar activity (especially with the aid of local professionals), aimed at linking courses to the concrete needs of the labor market and different professional realities. To this is added an intense seminar activity related to international exchanges.
The interdisciplinary character of the Bachelor's degree, in reference to the courses, laboratories, and internship activities provided in the curriculum, is in line with the knowledge, skills, and competencies outlined in the Dublin Descriptors.
Basic knowledge of a foreign language will also help the graduate to move within a reality also characterized by linguistic and cultural diversity. Regarding the ability to interact and communicate with different cultures, the Course pays particular attention to the acquisition of relational and social skills with the intent of enabling the graduate to operate in multicultural and multi-ethnic contexts. The achievement of such educational objectives implies a teaching organization aimed at combining and integrating the different disciplines dealing with educational situations and problems, accompanied by an intense activity of critical reflection on practice. The internship, in particular, will ensure the student acquisition of methodologies, techniques, and tools proper to the profession of Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator, reflective tools on the ethical-professional dimension, and different forms of educational emergency related to the rapid changes in society in recent years. The Course, therefore, provides a professional internship path, which is essential for acquiring the skills and abilities that characterize the profession of Socio-Pedagogical Educator and allow for the appropriate employability of the degree and its successful insertion into the labor market.
At the end of the training path, the student must also have acquired the ability to integrate the above-mentioned knowledge and skills to be able to face the complexity of their functions and the contexts in which they are carried out. In this sense, the Course aims to mature the ability to read and analyze educational needs and training requirements emerging to implement forms of planning and management of educational interventions directed at children, adolescents, adults, and elderly, within educational, socio-educational, community, territorial, and integrated services, in public, private, and third-sector contexts.
The flexibility of the path allows the student to choose and orient their training towards a professional activity mainly linked to structures and services for early childhood (nurseries) or directed towards the social and community field, heading towards employment opportunities ranging from educational and socio-educational services to territorial and socio-health services, dealing with minors, adolescents, detained subjects, immigrant families, people with disabilities, etc., as well as cultural, recreational, and sports (museums, youth gathering centers, etc.) and environmental education (parks, eco-museums, environmental agencies, etc.).
The offered training also presupposes a strong territorial rooting (marked by forms of distress opened by the post-earthquake and economic crisis) and an openness to preparation oriented to the ability to operate in diversified and emergent contexts, as shown by the inclusion of specific disciplines (e.g., Emergency Pedagogy). The approach assumed in courses, laboratories, and seminar activities is, however, that of relationships and exchanges with local, national, and international stakeholders that take into account social requests from the labor market. The integration between different perspectives is pursued, among other things, with an intense seminar activity, internal and transversal to the courses, some of which are held by sector professionals due to existing conventions.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The graduate, at the end of the training path, must demonstrate a solid mastery of knowledge and skills of understanding of the main processes, techniques, and tools with which to program, activate, and qualify intervention in different contexts and operational areas. Starting from the acquisition of knowledge and skills in pedagogical, psychological, social, legal, historical-geographical-anthropological areas and their interrelation, the graduate will be able to understand disciplinary principles and indispensable conceptual nuclei necessary for the analysis and understanding of problems related to different educational contexts, with the intent of identifying specific solutions needed to prevent and solve educational situations, even complex, related to children, adolescents, adults, and elderly, as well as individuals, groups, and communities. In this sense, they will be able to conduct needs analysis and implement intervention-centered projects for precise target groups of educational action. They will also be able to understand the functions of management, organization, and programming of educational, territorial, and community services, paying particular attention to the realities of Abruzzo and neighboring areas, also in reference to emergent characteristics.
In particular, the graduate must be able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding in depth of:
- the main pedagogical, psychological, sociological, historical-anthropological, geographical, and legal aspects related to study and intervention fields, also in reference to transpositions and laboratory applications, possibly supported by information and multimedia technologies, and different methodologies, techniques, and strategies to support educational processes;
- the different psychological, pedagogical, and social aspects concerning childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and old age, from the perspective of lifelong education;
- the historical evolution and operational realities of the main types of educational service present in the local, regional, national, and international context;
- the nuclei and fundamental principles related to professionalizing curricular disciplines, which allow operation in a scientifically grounded manner within educational and territorial services;
- emerging needs and relevant educational dynamics developing within complex realities and societies, also in reference to multi and intercultural dynamics;
- the methods of managing educational services;
- the pedagogical, formative, psychological, deontological, legal, and organizational dimensions related to the nature of educational interventions, the ways to respond to the needs of the target groups, and the tools to face and solve problems;
- the observational, recording, and educational intervention techniques and tools to be used in different contexts and situations of expressed educational need by individuals and communities in relation to children, adolescents, adults, and elderly;
- the methods and tools of the sciences of education and technological and multimedia models useful for designing and evaluating learning environments and systems and promoting educational initiatives.
Such knowledge and understanding skills will be realized by referring to the most advanced theoretical references and methodological apparatuses and will be directed at forming a professional who can understand the multiple variables interacting in educational phenomena, even the most complex, identifying causes and origins of existing problems and on which the Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator must intervene with appropriate solutions or corrections.
Knowledge and understanding skills are acquired through participation in frontal lessons, directly, and personal study, as well as through the training activities provided in the curriculum, particularly those related to basic and characteristic sectors, paying specific attention to pedagogical, psychological, and social disciplines. The verification of learning outcomes is mainly carried out through oral and written exams in predominantly structured and semi-structured form at the discretion of the examiner.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The graduate, at the end of the university path, will be able to apply knowledge and understanding regarding what has been understood and interpreted, demonstrating the ability to use specific approaches, methods, and professional tools to carry out educational profession and to realize targeted planning, accompanied by intervention actions aimed at care and educational support, in the direction of promoting the well-being of children, adolescents, adults, and elderly, as well as individuals, groups, and communities, also in reference to subjects with special needs or at risk of marginalization. In this sense, the graduate will be able to:
- use tools for analyzing problems, changes, and educational dynamics related to the planning of care and educational support interventions;
- use principles, methods, techniques, and tools of educational research to realize appropriate forms of planning;
- establish and build positive relationships with subjects of different ages and with individuals and groups, targets of educational action;
- apply methods, tools, and techniques of observation, evaluation, and documentation of phenomena, facts, events, and educational processes;
- realize integrated and multi-perspective interventions;
- realize educational projects in continuity and progression with other agencies and educational and cultural institutions of the territory;
- design support and care pathways according to one or more educational models, also with the aid of information and multimedia technologies;
- promote, realize, and implement pathways of support and protection of citizenship rights of subjects in difficulty and social marginalization (unaccompanied minors, etc.);
- carry out activities aimed at promoting educational well-being, targeting even complex educational issues.
- use and transfer what has been learned through disciplinary knowledge in direct internships at public and private structures and third-sector organizations, local, national, and international, as well as at organizations, communities, and educational and territorial services;
- operate in professional and inter-professional work groups;
- use techniques for managing dynamics of professional and inter-professional groups and for developing the ability to work in groups with all figures present within educational services.
The application of the above-mentioned knowledge and understanding skills occurs through lessons and activities of transposition and use of critical reflection on texts and case studies proposed, active methodologies, simulation activities, inquiry method learning, role play, programming methods, but also through the adoption of heuristic and creative strategies, traceable, in particular, to the area of training, psycho-pedagogical, sociological, and legal, as well as to courses connected to specific professional skills of the trained figure, which place the student at the center of the teaching process. The internship also contributes to developing the required application skills and is accompanied by the drafting of a training project, realized under the guidance of a University Tutor (internal) and supervised, in the external training site, by a Business Tutor (Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator, who performs the Supervising role throughout the path). At the end of each internship cycle carried out within services or other structures, the student must draft a complete and exhaustive report on the activities carried out, using precise parameters in the elaboration.
The common teaching approach for all courses provides that theoretical training is constantly accompanied by examples, applications, and forms of planning that stimulate active participation, autonomous elaboration ability, and communication of the results of the work carried out.
Verification of the achievement of results occurs through written reports in which the student applies observation, planning, evaluation, and documentation tools. The assessment of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding will mainly include forms of evaluation that provide production tests, written and oral, at the discretion of the examiner.
The thesis will constitute a moment of application of acquired learning, in an interdisciplinary perspective, during which the graduate can produce a well-structured, logical, and rigorous elaboration.
III - Judgment autonomy At the end of the training path, the graduate will be able to demonstrate the ability to collect, interpret data, and identify criteria useful for formulating autonomous judgments and reflections on the educational, social, and deontological dimensions involved in the development processes of children, adolescents, adults, and elderly, as well as individuals, groups, and communities, in the management of educational interventions.
In particular, the graduate:
- is able to evaluate educational situations, identifying factors and problems, often multiple, focusing attention on central issues and correctly identifying objectives and pertinence of the intervention in relation to the context, correctly applying professional ethical-deontological principles;
- knows how to reflect on the construction of training paths, also of an integrated type, from the perspective of educational continuity with the family and other educational institutions, valuing cultural, gender individualities, and considering possible disabilities of the subjects;
- knows how to evaluate the functionality of models and tools used in educational services to be able to systematically verify one's own work and document it adequately;
- knows how to evaluate the functionality of models for childhood and adolescence services to monitor the adequacy of the proposed model in relation to requests and cultural and social changes, as well as to counteract phenomena of marginalization and deviance.
Judgment autonomy is developed in particular within basic and characteristic courses that deepen the history and theoretical and epistemological foundations of different disciplines and differentiated application methodologies, as well as through participation in laboratories or seminars inspired by critical reflection on different professional models and approaches that accompany the development of critical skills. In reference to project and co-project choices, in-course tests must be provided that allow students to critically evaluate a choice between different alternative hypotheses, addressing typical educational issues related to the phases of intervention planning and implementation up to its evaluation. Such tests are carried out through the use of simulations, case studies, etc., which must induce choices and decisions based on work material, appropriate documentation, and selected specialized literature.
Judgment autonomy, supported by reflection and critical thinking, is developed transversally by all disciplines, using both devices in use in frontal teaching and those related to collateral activities (seminars, workshops, and laboratories), focusing on dimensions such as participation, collaboration, reflection on, in, and for action centered also on the analysis of critical incidents (CIT technique), co-design of written elaborations, programming and procedural plans, and oral reports, as well as on confrontation with the supervisor for the preparation of the final exam. The final exam, working progress, and reports on internship activities carried out allow verifying the achievement by the student of autonomous professional skills based on critical thinking, awareness, and critical reflection and related, at different levels, to the different dimensions of curricular knowledge. In this sense, an important role in the formation and verification of judgment autonomy is played by the preparation and presentation of production tests and the dissertation and discussion of the final elaboration.
IV - Communication skills The graduate, at the end of the university path, will be able to demonstrate the ability to communicate, effectively, information, ideas, problems, with different interlocutors, also making use of one or more foreign languages. The Course, through the acquisition of specific disciplinary skills, allows the use of sector and specialist languages related to the semantic fields of disciplines that are part of the curriculum. During the three years, the intersection between such languages allows the achievement of precise communication skills that place graduates in a position to interact with the different targets of the educational proposal and with the different categories of users of services, to engage in fruitful confrontation with institutional interlocutors and with the different professional figures with whom they work in teams or networks, in order to be able to make appropriate decisions regarding the types of intervention to activate in various contexts and areas of competence. Graduates in the Course will develop a methodological, technical, and operational language, which enables them to communicate effectively with the targets to which they refer at each moment, matching the intervention to their characteristics. In this sense, they will be able to grasp the key aspects of a problem and make it communicatively understandable when interfacing with professional figures and interlocutors of different fields.
In particular, they will be able to:
- draft and verify written documents, reports, and relations;
- analyze and prepare tools and documentation;
- communicate and work effectively in groups, also in laboratory activities;
- draft and present the results of an action, intervention, and educational project;
- independently conduct bibliographic research, using information sources and databases;
- communicate orally and present summary reports.
The graduate, in this sense:
- possesses, in written and oral form, basic knowledge of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian;
- possesses adequate skills and tools for communication and information management, also in relation to the age and social, psychological, linguistic conditions of their interlocutors;
- uses conventional languages and/or new communication technologies to document experienced processes and present them to public and private service interlocutors;
- possesses the ability to operate in different organizational and community contexts, also in the intercultural perspective of managing misunderstandings and conflicts;
- possesses the ability to operate in relation to individuals, groups, and communities, collecting necessary information, anticipating and managing conflicts of interests or values, pursuing educational goals, and creating relationship networks capable of producing educational well-being.
The acquisition of the above-mentioned communication skills is provided in different ways within the training activities: preparation of written reports in Italian and foreign language, oral presentation of the same, drafting and discussion of the final exam, multimedia documentation of internship and laboratory activities, field relationship and communication experiences through internships. The verification of such skills occurs through the analysis of the types of performance indicated.
Some courses and laboratories, providing group activities under the supervision of the teacher, will provide useful stimuli for discussion and in-depth exploration of themes and problems, which will help expand the professional vocabulary and acquisition of technical specialist languages.
Internship activities will constitute useful tools for developing communication skills, strongly encouraged by meeting and confronting with professionals operating on the field, favoring the personal and professional growth of the student. Moreover, the promotion of seminars, interventions, and testimonies of experts and professionals in the field of educational sciences, operating in entities and organizations at local, national, and international levels, connected to basic and characteristic disciplines, will contribute to refining the student's specialist and technical communication tools. Such activities will be strengthened by basic knowledge of a foreign language that will also help the graduate to move within culturally and linguistically diversified realities.
The acquisition of communication and relational skills occurs through different types of training activities (frontal, seminar, and laboratory) that imply active student participation and provide for the drafting of reports, diaries, and written documents, as well as their oral presentation and discussion with the teacher or other students. Such acquisition is guaranteed transversally by different disciplines, which work on the communicative plane, intersecting with each other. The verification of communication skills occurs through the assessment of the student's ability to understand, present, and argue within the different teaching activities, as well as in the drafting, presentation, and discussion of the final thesis. The final exam will offer an opportunity for deepening and verifying the abilities of analysis, elaboration, and transfer of knowledge, content, and themes related to the work carried out by the student, taking place before a commission. Oriented to combining multiple disciplinary sectors, it will constitute a learning ground during which the graduate can carry out multidisciplinary research. The Bachelor's degree provides for the preparation of a final elaboration and an oral interview in which the student has the opportunity to verify their communication abilities on the studied topic.
V - Learning ability The graduate, at the end of the university path, will have developed critical awareness regarding the importance of promoting intentionally and consciously directed educational processes towards precise target categories of action, concerning children, adolescents, adults, or elderly, as well as elaborating accurate planning directed at individuals, groups, or communities, building a virtuous interaction and effective communication between individuals, groups, organizations, and professional and inter-professional teams.
In this sense, the graduate will have developed the learning ability necessary to update on methods, tools, and techniques oriented to the characterization, planning, implementation, and monitoring of educational interventions, and to promote actions aimed at care, support, and educational well-being of individuals, groups, and communities. Moreover, they will be able to manage the programming, management, and execution of educational projects and interventions concerning the field of Sciences of Education and Training, making use of the collaboration of other professionals and forms of co-design realized by multiprofessional teams, in which previous experience can be reinterpreted and reinvested. Therefore, for the type of professional training, the graduate will be able to undertake, with a high degree of autonomy, higher-level studies where they can apply, with methodological rigor, previous acquisitions, which form the basis of all disciplines of the three-year path, to deepen them and acquire new ones. Graduates of the Course must develop learning abilities at different levels that range from individual study, which involves the adoption of precise personal strategies, to the preparation of projects, reports, and activities carried out in view of the preparation of the final elaboration (thesis). These abilities are built within the different types of activities provided within the curriculum (courses, laboratories, and internships) that also make use of supplementary or integrated teaching activities (thematic seminars and workshops), also of a transversal nature (such as those dedicated to soft skills), which imply active student participation. Such activities, individual and group, guarantee the student constant updating and appropriate revision of skills, with the help of higher-order skills.
In particular, the graduate possesses abilities that enable them to:
- analyze educational problems, employing various disciplines and relevant approaches and reflecting on previous experience to solve new problems;
- reflexively define what has been learned previously, identifying further learning needs in relation to the problems to be addressed;
- independently use training and information sources regarding educational intervention areas, relating them to the various disciplines involved;
- autonomously identify different training opportunities;
- apply developed learning methods and tools to update and deepen studied content, also in professional contexts, and to undertake subsequent studies, directing their interests towards the desired direction.
Learning abilities are acquired in the overall study path and verified in its individual articulations with particular regard to promoting study and research skills through the use of appropriate tools, also leveraging new information and communication technologies, such as forms of reflection on professional practice through the adoption of video recording techniques.
Learning abilities are assessed through forms of intermediate verification during training activities, requiring the presentation of elaborations, re-elaborations, research, deepening, etc., to be carried out individually or in groups, through continuous, in-course, and tutoring orientation. The verification of the achievement of learning abilities will also be the subject of specific exam tests, as well as during the discussion of the final exam. To facilitate the achievement of these objectives, the Course may organize specific meetings on topics of particular interest, on experiential, methodological, and technical aspects, in collaboration with the world of work and more directly related to the employability of the degree in the labor market. Verification also occurs on the plane of the execution of individual projects, through self-assessment and self-perception tools that enable students to verify their learning ability during different moments of the training path. Such abilities are indispensable for facing potential 'crises' of the path and for best undertaking subsequent study steps, placing the student in a favorable position to continue undertaking further studies with a high degree of professionalism to insert into highly qualified and qualifying professional contexts.
Professional function in work context.
Professional function in work context:
The Bachelor's degree in Sciences of Education and Training of the University of L'Aquila prepares for the profession of Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educator and, according to what is provided by Law 205/2017 paragraph 594-601 and by Decree Law 65 of April 2017 regarding Law 107/2015, and of Educator in services for childhood, due to class and curricular constraints, as provided by DM 378 of May 9, 2018.
The graduate will carry out the following tasks:
- design, implement, manage, and evaluate educational interventions, ensuring appropriate learning conditions and significant experiences for the targets of the educational proposal (children, young people, and adults, as well as individuals, groups, and communities);
- evaluate the outcomes of the interventions carried out;
- document processes, educational practices, and results;
- analyze and interpret educational phenomena, facts, and events, to be able to satisfy the needs of the targets of the proposal;
- design appropriate learning environments and coherent with individual and group needs;
- structure educational interventions based on the characteristics of the target of the educational action and on their learning needs;
- analyze educational phenomena, even complex, and make appropriate decisions in reference to cultural, institutional, organizational, contextual implications, etc.
- design and implement educational interventions directed at individuals with special educational needs, resorting to personalization and individualization strategies, as well as compensatory and dispensative tools;
- carry out interventions aimed at promoting re-education, inclusion, and integration processes of subjects at risk of social marginalization and to care for specific insertion and reinsertion paths, also leveraging forms of co-design and network work;
- activate prevention and health education activities to modify risk behaviors;
- prepare social participation pathways through the elaboration of specific educational paths;
- use cooperative and collaborative abilities to work and design in teams;
- use thinking and critical reflection to carry out professional tasks with commitment and responsibility.
In compliance with Article 1 of Legislative Decree No. 65 of 2017, the educator in early childhood educational services, in a collegial perspective and in collaboration with families, prepares educational environments and designs, organizes, and implements activities aimed at stimulating, in girls and boys from zero to three years of age, the acquisition of relational skills, autonomy processes, creativity, in appropriate learning contexts for affective, playful, and cognitive development, guaranteeing "equal opportunities for education, instruction, care, relationship, and play, overcoming inequalities and barriers of territorial, economic, ethnic, and cultural nature."
The educator carries out the main tasks:
- design and implement educational proposals by preparing appropriate environments and learning experiences through playful, expressive, and creative activities;
- program learning paths;
- evaluate the quality of educational proposals and their outcomes on the targets, the children, and their families;
- evaluate the organizational quality of educational activities and their outcomes on the context and relationships with interested subjects.
Professional skills associated with the function.
Professional skills associated with the function:
The Bachelor's degree aims to provide the following knowledge and professional skills:
a. methodological-didactic and planning skills;
b. communication-relational skills;
c. organizational-management skills;
d. evaluation and information management and documentation skills;
e. media skills;
f. critical-reflexive skills.
In particular, for the graduate working in early childhood services:
- be able to observe children and girls in nursery and early childhood services, regarding cognitive, social, and psychomotor processes among peers and relational processes with adult reference figures, professional figures, etc.;
- be able to design educational, support, and compensatory paths;
- be able to conduct and manage educational interventions directed at children and girls in early childhood present in nursery and early childhood services;
- be able to elaborate intervention strategies, individualization, personalization, directed at subjects with special needs to promote inclusion and integration processes in reference to gender, cultural belonging, etc.;
- be able to realize verification processes of processes and activities, as well as the quality of educational practices affecting children in nursery and early childhood services;
- be able to document processes and educational practices;
- know how to create educational alliances between services, agencies, families, parent actors, and professional figures;
- be able to activate continuity paths between nursery, family, and other early childhood services;
- be able to work in teams to implement programming, management, implementation, and evaluation processes of activities.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The Course provides graduates who will become Professional Socio-Pedagogical Educators (based on what is provided by Law 205/2017 paragraph 594-601 – integrated by paragraph 517 of the Budget Law 145/19) and Educators in services for childhood (Decree Law 65/2017). The graduate will carry out their activity as a Socio-Pedagogical Educator in services for childhood, in communities and social services, in territorial educational structures linked to Third Sector activities, in cultural services, within public administrations and private organizations. Professional figures operate in services and socio-educational and socio-assistive presidiums, towards people of all ages, prioritarily in the following areas: educational and training, school, socio-assistive, limitedly to socio-educative aspects, parenthood, and family, cultural, judicial, environmental, sports and motor, integration, and international cooperation.
In particular, the professional figure will exercise the function of:
- educator in early childhood services, carrying out their activity in nurseries, micro-nurseries, early childhood centers, play spaces, family nurseries, corporate nurseries, and other types of services, in socio-educational and integrated services for early childhood;
- social educator and in social services and for families;
- educator in socio-assistive structures;
- socio-educational and assistive educator;
- educator for social integration of adults;
- socio-community educator in Adult Education Centers;
- educator who provides information, orientation, and placement services (job agencies, educational institutions, etc.);
- educator who provides internal training and updating services within companies, institutions, and externalized services;
- educator who provides services related to training and orientation internships, insertion, and reinsertion;
- educator in tutoring paths (school, corporate, etc.);
- educator in socio-educational services and territorial networks for assistance services;
- socio-educational educator in free professional practice.
