ITALIAN Specific educational objectives.
The graduate must possess solid knowledge and skills in the main areas of social sciences, pedagogical, juridical-economic, psychological, medical, historical-geographical-anthropological sciences, enabling them to analyze complex social phenomena, design and implement, with awareness and responsibility, integrated social interventions, and evaluate them to understand their outcomes and prepare possible corrective actions in relation to the recipients of the actions (individuals, groups, communities).
The bachelor's degree aims to provide students with skills, cultural and scientific content, methods, tools and techniques necessary to achieve adequate preparation in the professional area of social service.
The graduate must be able to:
- Master the languages and tools of basic disciplines (sociological, juridical, etc.);
- Be able to combine basic skills and disciplinary content (sociological, anthropological, psychological, etc.) from an interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral perspective to build appropriate intervention projects corresponding to the needs of the recipients of the actions (individuals, groups, communities);
- Master methodologies and techniques of social service in relation to the recipients of the social intervention;
- Decode and interpret complex events, facts and phenomena, even within more recent societal transformations, to understand their characteristics and activate collaboration networks to promote increasingly effective individual and social intervention projects;
- Use appropriate methods and techniques of social research and analysis tools to understand social changes, with particular reference to issues of individual, group and community distress, also starting from the examination of gender dynamics, emergency issues, intercultural questions and inclusion-related issues;
- Identify new social needs to respond appropriately to emerging societal needs;
- Design, plan, manage, implement and evaluate integrated interventions across different operational fields;
- Detect through the use of appropriate techniques and tools the conditions and situations of social distress to develop adequate treatment strategies for individuals, families, groups and communities;
- Manage integrated interventions related to forms of social protection;
- Activate actions and forms of prevention of social distress, promoting the well-being of individuals, families, groups and communities;
- Develop appropriate social emergency intervention and support actions for accessing resources and services;
- Operate within multiprofessional and inter-institutional teams;
- Manage communication, interact and operate in contexts with high cultural and variability, including gender, immigrant and multicultural contexts;
- Be able to combine theoretical knowledge with experiential knowledge acquired through external internships carried out at public national or international administrations, non-governmental organizations and third sector organizations, social enterprises where professional social service is present;
- Communicate effectively and manage information appropriately, especially regarding citizenship rights and accompanying individuals in difficulty;
- Communicate effectively, in written and oral form, in at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian.
At the end of the training path, the student must also have acquired the ability to integrate the above-mentioned knowledge and skills to support the confrontation with the complexity of their own functions and the contexts in which they are carried out. In this sense, the degree course aims to foster the ability to read and analyze social, educational and intervention needs, as well as to provide resources for managing appropriate interventions directed at individuals, groups, public and private organizations, profit and non-profit organizations, and for managing integrated and networked services, in institutional, territorial and community contexts.
The study plan includes basic, characterizing and related courses aimed at developing a solid cultural foundation and necessary technical-operational knowledge for the profession, supported by professionalizing courses and laboratories related to the field of social sciences, taking into account different dimensions (theoretical, experiential, contextual, relational, etc.).
The bachelor's degree is structured in a single curriculum, articulated into courses, professionalizing laboratories and direct and indirect internship activities, accompanied by integrative activities such as seminars, workshops, etc., and other coordination and curricular linking initiatives aimed at strategically integrating the different training activities.
The study plan includes the following scientific-disciplinary sectors: SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/17, SECS-S/05, M-PSI/01, M-PSI/02, M-PSI/04, M-PSI/05, MED/42, INF/01, M-STO/06, M-GGR/01, M-DEA/01, M-PED/01, M-PED/02, M-PED/03, M-PED/04. For the thesis, 6 CFU are provided.
The course is structured in cultural/disciplinary axes that are articulated into learning areas.
1 - Sociological and social service area: adequate knowledge and skills related to basic disciplines, methods and techniques of social service and social research useful for programming and implementing integrated interventions across various operational fields, as well as for building individual and social intervention projects related to the treatment of social distress situations of individuals as well as families, groups and communities, also in the perspective of social inclusion. These are knowledge and skills related to sociological and social service disciplines, including theoretical and methodological aspects, as well as issues related to the implementation of social policies for specific recipients.
2 - Medical-psychopedagogical area: disciplinary and methodological knowledge to understand and interpret complex phenomena and situations to activate preventive actions for various forms of social distress, promotional actions for the well-being of individuals, families, groups and communities, as well as for social emergency intervention and support in accessing resources and services, also with the intent of enabling the graduate to operate in multidisciplinary teams. These are knowledge and skills related to:
- Pedagogical disciplines, useful for better managing relationships, caring for moments of individual and group potential development, designing interventions and evaluating their outcomes, also in relation to processes of social and intercultural inclusion and issues related to disability;
- Psychological disciplines useful for mastering fundamental aspects of psychological functioning, relationships between individuals and groups, and intercepting forms of distress to be treated in an integrated manner with other professional functions;
- Social medicine disciplines aimed, within the limits of their functions, at promoting and supporting physical and mental health.
3 - Historical-anthropological-geographical area: in-depth knowledge and skills related to the ability to interact with cultures, including gender and immigrant populations, from the perspective of multicultural and multiethnic social relationships, as well as those connected to the territoriality of phenomena in both diachronic and synchronic senses.
4 - Economic-juridical, statistical-demographic and technological-informatic area: knowledge and skills related to communication and information management, particularly regarding citizenship rights and accompanying individuals in difficulty; knowledge and skills in the legal field (regional, national and European regulations), aimed at supporting advocacy and protection functions for subjects, guiding them in the space of fundamental rights, framing professional functions within the norm and deontology; statistical, computer, scientific knowledge useful for supporting the analysis of real situations through data processing.
5 - Linguistic and foreign languages area: knowledge related to the effective use, in written and oral form, of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian, also in reference to professional context terminology, accompanied by a good acquisition of specialist and sector languages.
6 - Transversal area of application and transfer of skills: the ability to apply knowledge and skills in situational contexts is linked to training experiences aimed at strengthening the acquisition process through qualifying internships (training project) at public national or international administrations, non-governmental organizations and third sector organizations, social enterprises where professional social service is present, as well as through other activities (laboratories, workshops, co-designed seminars with welcoming structures, etc.) useful for increasing the transfer of specific skills, also in the context of a better understanding of the employability of skills and occupational prospects. These are professional skills to be acquired on the field, through significant internship experiences in all operational contexts within which the graduate can carry out their functions, with particular reference to social services and extracurricular services, structures for children and adolescents, and all contexts (public, private and non-profit) where projects related to prevention and recovery of distress are implemented (ASL, family houses, etc.).
Consistent with the indicated axes, the degree course provides alongside basic, characterizing and related disciplines:
– one or more professionalizing laboratories aimed at simulating and transferring practical applications of what is learned in curricular courses;
– mandatory internship activities:
a. indirect, which, carried out under the guidance of the university tutor at the Department's structures or other sites, aims to prepare, reflect and discuss the main observation and documentation methods to be activated in the phases of direct internship, and in supervision phase, during the drafting of the final internship report;
b. direct, which, carried out at the University of L'Aquila's cooperating structures, under the guidance of a Supervising Social Assistant, aims to apply knowledge and skills learned through courses and laboratories and to experience guided learning in the reality of territorial services (local authorities, health agencies, private social organizations, etc.), allowing students to appropriately use observation techniques and documentation tools that are part of professional action.
The offered training balances a strong territorial grounding (marked by forms of distress following the post-earthquake and economic crisis) and an openness to an international perspective, especially in a European context. In this sense, the training path prioritizes the characterizing disciplines provided in Class L-39 that most help develop a versatile Social Assistant figure, capable of acting and collaborating with structures operating at local, national and international levels, and to carry out systematic collaboration with the Order of Social Assistants of the Abruzzo Region in internship and laboratory activities, as well as in other integrative training activities, aimed at qualifying the training as a whole (transversal skills such as soft skills). The integration between different types of teaching activities (courses, laboratories, internships) and between sociological, psycho-pedagogical and juridical approaches is pursued through intense transversal and in-depth laboratory and seminar activities (especially with the aid of local professionals and the Order of Social Assistants), aimed at linking courses to the concrete needs of the labor market and different professional realities. To this is added an intense seminar activity related to international exchanges.
The interdisciplinary nature of the bachelor's degree, in reference to the courses, laboratories and internship activities provided in the curriculum, is in line with the knowledge, skills and competencies outlined in the Dublin Descriptors.
Basic knowledge of a foreign language will also help the graduate to move within a reality also characterized by linguistic and cultural diversity. Regarding the ability to interact and communicate with different cultures, the course pays particular attention to the acquisition of relational and social skills with the intent of enabling the graduate to operate in multicultural and multiethnic contexts. The achievement of such educational objectives implies a teaching organization aimed at combining and integrating the different disciplines dealing with problematic situations and social distress, accompanied by intense critical reflection on practice. The internship, in particular, will ensure the student acquisition of methodologies, techniques and tools of the social assistant profession, reflective tools on the ethical-professional dimension and different forms of social emergency related to rapid changes in recent years. The study course indeed includes a path that includes 17 CFU "for internships and traineeships at companies, public or private bodies, professional orders" and 1 CFU of "Additional training activities (art. 10, paragraph 5, letter d) – Training and orientation internships", for a total of 450 hours of activities. In both cases, activities will be carried out under the supervision of Social Assistants regularly registered with the professional order.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The graduate, at the end of the training path, must demonstrate solid mastery of knowledge and skills for understanding the main processes, techniques and tools with which to program, activate and qualify the intervention of the Social Assistant in different contexts and operational fields. Starting from the acquisition of knowledge and skills in psychological, pedagogical, social, medical, juridical-economic, statistical-demographic, historical-geographical-anthropological areas and their interrelation, the graduate will be able to understand the indispensable conceptual nuclei and reinterpret them for the analysis and understanding of problems related to the social field in different contexts and with the intent of identifying specific solutions necessary to prevent and resolve problematic situations and distress of individuals, groups and communities within complex and organized systems. In this sense, they will be able to conduct social resource analysis and promote and implement integrated interventions. They will also be able to understand the functions of management, organization and programming of social services, paying particular attention to the social issues of the Abruzzo region and neighboring areas.
In particular, the graduate must be able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding in depth of:
- The main pedagogical, psychological, sociological, juridical aspects related to study and intervention fields, also in reference to laboratory transpositions and applications, possibly supported by information and multimedia technologies, and techniques for group management and strategies for supporting inclusive processes mediated by social intervention;
- The different medical-psychological, pedagogical and social aspects concerning childhood, adolescence and adulthood;
- The operational reality and historical evolution of the main types of educational service present in the local, regional, national and international context;
- The nuclei of professionalizing curricular disciplines that enable operation in the perspective of social service, recovery and inclusion;
- The relevant dynamics of complex societies and their social welfare systems, also in reference to multi and intercultural dynamics;
- The methods of managing primary and secondary social networks and advanced methods regarding social, psychological, educational, deontological, juridical and organizational dimensions concerning social problems and ways to face them;
- Techniques and tools for prevention, detection and treatment of situations of risk and social distress expressed by individuals, families and communities;
- Methods and tools of social sciences and technological and multimedia models useful for evaluating systems and promoting social initiatives.
Such knowledge and skills will be achieved by looking at the most advanced theoretical references and methodological frameworks and will be directed at forming a professional who can understand the multiple variables interacting in social phenomena, even the most complex, identifying causes and origins of existing problems and intervening with appropriate solutions or corrections.
The knowledge and understanding skills listed above are acquired through participation in course lectures, in direct form, and personal study as part of the training activities activated, particularly within basic and characterizing sectors, paying specific attention to disciplines of socio-anthropological, pedagogical, juridical and psychological areas. Verification of the achievement of learning outcomes occurs mainly through oral and written exams, predominantly structured and semi-structured.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The graduate, at the end of the university path, will be able to apply knowledge and understanding regarding what has been understood and interpreted, demonstrating the ability to employ specific professional approaches to social work, activate preventive actions for social distress, promotional actions for the well-being of individuals, families, groups and communities, also in reference to support actions and services for children, young people and adults. In this sense, the graduate will be able to:
- Employ principles, methods, techniques and tools of social research;
- Operate in work groups and multi-professional teams;
- Use and transfer what has been learned through disciplinary knowledge in direct internship activities at structures, bodies and local, national and international public administrations, as well as at non-governmental organizations and third sector organizations where social service is present;
- Establish and build relationships with people and groups from an interconnected perspective, operating in a systemic perspective;
- Apply methods, tools and techniques of observation and documentation within social processes;
- Employ techniques for managing dynamics of professional and inter-professional groups and for developing the ability to work in groups with all operators present in the service;
- Use tools for analyzing problems, social changes and dynamics concerning families to design support interventions for parenting;
- Realize integrated and multi-perspective interventions;
- Realize social projects in continuity and progression with territorial agencies and the family;
- Design support and care pathways in relation to one or more social models, also with the aid of information and multimedia technologies;
- Carry out activities aimed at promoting social well-being, targeting complex social problems;
- Promote and support pathways for the promotion and protection of citizenship rights of subjects in situations of difficulty and social marginality.
The application of the knowledge and understanding skills listed above occurs through lectures and activities of critical reflection on proposed texts, active methodologies and simulation and case study activities, inquiry method learning, role play, and through the adoption of heuristic and creative strategies, particularly related to the sociological, psycho-pedagogical and juridical areas, as well as courses connected to the specific professional skills of the trained figure, which place the student at the center of the teaching process. The internship also contributes to developing the required application skills and is accompanied by the drafting of a training project carried out under the guidance of a University Tutor (internal) and, in the external training site, by an Enterprise Tutor (Supervising Social Assistant). At the end of each internship cycle carried out within services, the student must draft a complete and exhaustive report on the activities carried out.
The common teaching approach for all courses provides that theoretical training is constantly accompanied by examples, applications and forms of design that stimulate active participation, autonomous elaboration ability, and communication of the results of the work carried out.
Verification of the achievement of results occurs through written reports in which the student applies observation, design and documentation tools. Assessment of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding will mainly involve forms of evaluation that include written and oral production tests at the discretion of the examiner.
The thesis will constitute a moment of application of learning, from an interdisciplinary perspective, during which the graduate can produce a well-structured, logical and rigorous elaboration.
III - Judgment autonomy At the end of the training path, the graduate will be able to detect and interpret information, sources and data related to their professional field and identify criteria for formulating autonomous judgments and reflections on the social, ethical, deontological and practical dimensions involved both in the development processes of individuals, groups and communities, and in the management of social interventions.
Specifically, the graduate will be able to:
- Evaluate cases to be resolved in the field of social problems by identifying problematic factors, often multiple, and focusing on the key issues they relate to, correctly and clearly identifying the objectives of the intervention;
- Critically reflect on the appropriateness of using models and techniques of social service intervention, applying professional deontology correctly in accordance with the New Code of Ethics of the Social Assistant, approved on February 21, 2020 and effective from June 1, 2020, which introduces among new duties also that of contributing to the protection of the environment;
- Evaluate the quality of integrated social pathways, from the perspective of continuity between different institutions (family, consultoriums, etc.) and the valorization of cultural, social and gender individualities, considering possible difficulties of subjects, even on the disability level;
- Choose communication models and service evaluation tools to be able to systematically evaluate and document one's own work;
- Evaluate the usefulness of applying specific social service intervention models in relation to the clientele (childhood, adolescence and adults), to monitor their adequacy to requests and cultural and social changes;
- Choose the most appropriate action plans, tools and means to counteract phenomena of distress and marginality.
The courses proposed in the study plan will contribute, also through individual and group activities, to developing the ability to reflect on relevant data and central social, scientific and ethical themes useful for cultivating responsibility, which implies, in the exercise of the profession, judgment and choice autonomy.
Among the purposes of such courses, the ability to work in groups, the ability to select relevant information, the collaborative elaboration of reports, strategies and projects, the justification of choices, the dialectical approach, the awareness of the implications of interventions also social and the actions taken to solve a problem, constitute the central character of the training. Graduates will also be able to promote and become protagonists of approaches and contributions based on interactions, using information critically to design, execute, interpret, characterize and evaluate interventions, contributing to reaching solutions to specific problems through various training activities, such as guided group discussions, personal elaborations and collective meetings, accompanied by seminars and testimonies from the professional world, which will offer the opportunity to develop decision-making abilities and judgment autonomy, essential for cultivating professional ethics.
The curriculum path of the degree course indeed allows the graduate to acquire knowledge and skills, also of a higher order, that enable them to express value judgments regarding approaches and theoretical and methodological choices concerning the quality of interventions to be carried out within Social Service, making use of different disciplinary tools, as well as developing in students judgment autonomy, primarily based on the ability to observe, analyze, interpret and evaluate social problems, leveraging the tools and methods of social research in use and distinguishing factual interpretations, observed in comparison with reality, from subjective interpretations.
Judgment autonomy is developed particularly within basic and characterizing courses, which deal with the theoretical and epistemological foundations of different disciplines and differentiated application methodologies, and through participation in laboratories or seminars inspired by different professional visions that accompany the development of critical skills. In reference to project choices and co-planning, in-course tests must be provided that allow students to critically evaluate a choice between different alternative hypotheses, addressing typical issues related to the programming phase of the intervention and its implementation up to its evaluation. Such tests must be carried out through the use of simulations, case studies, etc., which must induce choices and decisions based on work material, appropriate documentation and selected specialized literature.
Judgment autonomy, supported by reflection and critical thinking, is developed transversally by all disciplines, using both devices in use in frontal teaching and those related to collateral activities (seminars, workshops and laboratories), focusing on dimensions such as participation, collaboration, reflection on, in and for action centered also on the analysis of critical incidents (CIT technique), co-design of written reports, programming and procedural plans and oral reports, as well as on confrontation with the supervising teacher for the preparation of the final exam. The final exam and the reports on the internship activities carried out allow verifying the achievement by the student of autonomous professional skills based on critical thinking, awareness and critical reflection and related, at different levels, to the dimensions of curricular knowledge. In this sense, an important role in the formation and verification of judgment autonomy is played by the work of preparation and presentation of production tests and the final dissertation and discussion of the elaboration.
IV - Communication skills The course, through the acquisition of specific disciplinary skills, allows the use of sector and specialist languages related to the semantic fields of disciplines that are part of the curriculum. During the three-year period, the intersection between such languages enables the achievement of precise communication skills that place graduates in a position to interact and engage profitably with different institutional interlocutors and with different professional figures with whom they work in networks, as well as with different categories of service users in order to be able to make appropriate decisions regarding different types of intervention in various fields of competence. Graduates in the degree course will develop a methodological, technical and operational language that enables them to communicate effectively also with the recipients to whom they refer. In this sense, they will be able to grasp the key aspects of a problem and render it communicatively understandable when interfacing with interlocutors from different sectors.
In particular, they will be able to:
- Draft and verify social files and technical reports;
- Analyze and prepare reports and documentation;
- Communicate and work effectively in groups, also in laboratory activities;
- Draft and present the results of an intervention and a project;
- Conduct bibliographic research autonomously, using information sources and databases;
- Identify and interpret regulations.
Some courses and laboratories, involving group activities under the supervision of the teacher, will provide useful stimuli for discussion and in-depth exploration of themes and problems, which will help expand the professional vocabulary and acquisition of technical specialist languages.
Internship activities will constitute useful tools for developing communication skills, strongly encouraged by meeting and confronting with professionals operating on the field, favoring the personal and professional growth of the student. Furthermore, the promotion of seminars, interventions and testimonies of experts and professionals in the field of Social Service Sciences operating in bodies and organizations at local, national and international levels, connected to basic and characterizing disciplines, will contribute to refining the student's specialist and technical communication tools. Such activities will be strengthened by basic knowledge of a foreign language that will also help the graduate to move within culturally and linguistically diverse realities.
The acquisition of communication and relational skills occurs through various types of training activities (frontal, seminar and laboratory teaching) that involve active student participation and require the drafting of reports, diaries and written documents, as well as their oral presentation and discussion with the teacher or other students. This acquisition is guaranteed transversally by different disciplines, which work on the communicative plane, intersecting with each other. Verification of communication skills occurs through the assessment of the student's ability to understand, present and argue within the different teaching activities, as well as in the drafting, presentation and discussion of the final thesis. The final exam will offer an opportunity for deepening and verifying the abilities of analysis, elaboration and transfer of knowledge, content and themes related to the work carried out by the student, taking place before a commission. Oriented to combining multiple disciplinary sectors, it will constitute a learning ground during which the graduate can carry out multidisciplinary research. The bachelor's degree provides for the preparation of a final elaboration and an oral interview in which the student has the opportunity to verify their communication abilities on the studied topic.
V - Learning ability The graduate at the end of the path will have developed the necessary learning ability to update on methods, tools and techniques oriented to the characterization, planning, implementation and monitoring of social interventions, and to promote actions aimed at the well-being of individuals, groups and communities. Moreover, they will be able to manage the programming, management and execution of social projects falling within the field of Social Service Sciences, making use of the collaboration of other professionals and forms of co-planning realized by multi-professional teams, in which previous experience can be reinterpreted and reinvested. Therefore, the graduate will be able to undertake, with a high degree of autonomy, higher-level studies where they can apply, with methodological rigor, previous acquisitions, which form the basis of all disciplines of the three-year path, to deepen them and acquire new ones. Graduates of the Study Course must develop learning abilities at different levels that range from individual study, which involves the adoption of precise personal strategies, to the preparation of projects, reports and activities carried out in view of the preparation of the final elaboration (thesis). These abilities are built within the different types of activities provided within the curriculum (courses, laboratories and internships) that also make use of supplementary or integrative teaching activities (thematic seminars and workshops), also of a transversal nature (such as those dedicated to soft skills), which involve active student participation. Such individual and group activities guarantee the student constant updating and appropriate revision of competencies.
Learning abilities are assessed through forms of intermediate verification during training activities, requiring the presentation of elaborations, re-elaborations, research, deepening, etc., to be carried out both individually and in groups, through continuous, in-course and tutoring orientation. Verification of the achievement of learning abilities will also be the subject of specific exam tests, as well as during the discussion of the final exam. To facilitate the achievement of these goals, the degree course may organize specific meetings on topics of particular interest, on experiential, methodological and technical aspects, in collaboration with the world of work and more directly related to the employability of the degree in the labor market. Verification also occurs on the plane of the execution of individual projects, through self-assessment and self-perception tools that enable students to verify their learning ability during different moments of the training path. Such abilities are indispensable for facing potential "crises" in the path and for undertaking the next steps of study and deepening most effectively, placing the student in a favorable position to continue undertaking subsequent studies with a high degree of professionalism to enter highly qualified and qualifying professional contexts.
Work context function.
Work context function:
The bachelor's degree in Social Service Sciences is aimed at training graduates who will carry out the profession of Social Assistant. The Social Assistant operates within services for people, families, groups, communities to contribute to their development, supporting them in using their own resources and society, identifying areas of need, preventing situations of distress and promoting initiatives aimed at building inclusive and solidary communities. In light of the specificity of the identified need situations, they elaborate appropriate interventions aimed at prevention, support and recovery of the affected subjects (individuals, families, groups and communities), as well as the protection of minors, the elderly, the disabled, immigrants, etc., making their knowledge and abilities available for issues concerning mental health, disability, drug addiction, poverty, exclusion and social marginality, and adopting appropriate methods, techniques and tools of social service that take into account the specific contexts in which this figure operates. This figure performs tasks of different nature ranging from socio-assistential to organizational and is capable of analyzing complex social situations, phenomena and problems, proposing appropriate solutions and coordinating the territorial inter-institutional and interdisciplinary network, including socio-health services. Specifically:
- Identifies situations of marginalization based on reports from teachers, doctors, law enforcement;
- Takes charge of people, families and/or social groups in distress situations starting from the analysis of their needs;
- Identifies methodologies and tools suitable for the individual case and available on the territory;
- Contacts competent territorial services and coordinates activities carried out by competent structures;
- Reports to the competent judicial authorities cases requiring intervention (abandonment, abuse, etc.) and collaborates with them for foster care, adoption of minors, etc.;
- Carries out social case management;
- Develops intervention paths with people in need, also using multidisciplinary and multiprofessional teams and forms of participatory planning;
- Collaborates with the judicial authority to establish alternatives to prison sentences;
- Performs consultations at courts and social secretariat functions;
- Analyzes social needs and resources present on the territory;
- Decodes social demand;
- Identifies the resources necessary to activate assistance paths in response to social demand and problems, as they are detected;
- Activates and integrates services and resources in network;
- Periodically verifies the project, plan and assistance path until the achievement of the identified goals.
The Social Assistant carries out their activity in the public and private sector with tasks that may vary (from organizational to coordination), with particular attention to employment in Ministries, hospitals, ASL, private clinics, family houses, prisons, reception centers, Juvenile Courts, drug centers, as well as in research activities (thus Universities and research bodies), services for children and adolescents, and public, private or third sector structures (cooperatives, associations, family houses, etc.) dealing with training, family support, inclusion, social reintegration, distress and marginality. Typical work areas for this professional figure are healthcare and hospital enterprises, Municipalities and their Consortia, the External Penitentiary Execution Office and the Social Service Office for Minors of the Ministry of Justice, as well as all Bodies, including those related to the non-profit sector (e.g., social cooperatives) in the management of Health and Social Care Residences, Day Centers, Family Houses, etc.
Competencies associated with the function.
Competencies associated with the function:
The Social Assistant must be able to operate with a certain degree of autonomy in decision-making and judgment, as well as to be able to manage, plan and coordinate professional interventions aimed at favoring the recovery and reintegration paths of subjects in society, also making use of the support of other professional figures (socio-health operators, psychologists, educators, doctors, etc.); they must also possess communication, relational and methodological skills that enable them to master techniques and tools for collecting and processing specific data for the elaboration and evaluation of interventions. For the performance of the Social Assistant function, the following are required:
- Reflective and critical thinking skills to read, interpret facts, events and phenomena and intervene in complex social contexts;
- Ability for self-learning and continuous updating;
- Transversal communication-relational, organizational-management, planning and programming skills, in reference to the degree of autonomy and responsibility assigned;
- Relational and collaborative skills that allow working in teams with other professional figures with autonomy of judgment;
- Skills in managing clientele and the ability to promote synergies between different functional areas;
- Organizational skills to activate network work with the main interested interlocutors (colleagues, other professionals, etc.);
- Communication skills, also in relation to foreign language (B1 level), considering the multicultural context in which different socio-assistential interventions are carried out.
Professional status conferred by the title.
Employment opportunities:
The bachelor's degree in Social Service Sciences represents the indispensable requirement to access the State Exam for the qualification to practice the profession of Social Assistant (D.P.R. L. June 5, 2001, n. 328), which allows registration in the Register of Social Assistants - Section B - established at the Order. The Social Assistant can carry out activities at:
- Public bodies (Ministries and local bodies, such as Regions, Municipalities, Provinces, within Health (ASL, Hospitals, Consultoriums, etc.), Justice (Prefectures, Courts, etc.), etc.);
- Third sector bodies (cooperatives, associations, volunteer associations, NGOs, profit and non-profit social enterprises), in Italy and abroad;
- Private sector: rehabilitation centers for minors with justice issues, residential structures, family houses, houses of refuge for abused women, reception centers for refugees and asylum seekers.
After registration with the Order, the Social Assistant can also work as a self-employed professional.
Employment opportunities are, however, continuously evolving, in relation to the emergence of new situations of distress and citizen needs, as well as the increasing social complexity, and the manifestation of new areas of poverty and exclusion. The training path of the degree course aims to enable immediate insertion of graduates into the different areas of the labor market related to social service in the socio-health field: public and private structures, third sector organizations, as well as the possibility of carrying out research and training activities at public and private bodies, but also of socio-health integration. Social Assistant roles are indeed provided in Local Authorities, territorial bodies of the SSN (ASL, hospital enterprises), Ministries, at various subjects active in the third sector (voluntary organizations, associations, non-profit bodies and NGOs, etc.).

ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Degree in BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES Specific educational objectives.
The Biological Sciences degree course aims to prepare graduates with solid foundational knowledge in the main fields of biology, who possess a good mastery of methodologies related to the respective scientific research areas, and have adequate preparation to assimilate scientific and technological progress and to correctly know and handle living organisms. In detail, graduates will acquire skills in basic non-biological fields such as mathematics, physics, and chemistry, as well as fundamental linguistic abilities to continue their studies and acquire specific skills in the fields of botany, zoology, cytology, histology, comparative anatomy, ecology, biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics, general physiology, microbiology, plant physiology, and hygiene. Additionally, they will acquire laboratory skills due to the curricular changes introduced, which will include 20 CFU of curricular exercises in the study cycle. Through an internship at a university or externally contracted laboratory, students will gain knowledge of the complex world of work in the biological sector, verify the relationship between university preparation and professional activities, and not only within the specific production context but also in organizational and managerial aspects.
The qualifying educational objectives of the study course refer to the principles of European harmonization, which encourage the alignment of graduates' competencies with the specific requirements identified by the Dublin Descriptors system according to the national Tuning table (CBUI College) for class L-13.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The graduate must acquire the fundamentals in mathematical, physical, and chemical disciplines, with particular reference to the basic principles of inorganic and organic chemistry. They must achieve a solid biological culture regarding the knowledge of microorganisms and animal and plant organisms, considering all possible aspects: morphological, cellular, functional, biochemical, molecular, related to reproduction and inheritance, environmental, and evolutionary. The graduate must know the main methodological and instrumental procedures for biological research. Laboratory practical activities are aimed at developing the ability to conduct experiments. These objectives are dedicated to basic and characterizing courses for over one hundred credits; the level of learning achieved will be verified through in-course assessments and individual written and/or oral final exams.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The graduate must be able to apply acquired knowledge in the field of Biology, identifying the most appropriate methodologies for solving problems, operating both independently and in a group. They must know the techniques for biodiversity analysis, biochemical, biomolecular, microbiological, and cytological methodologies; the principles of toxicological and biomedical analyses. They must also be able to collect, interpret, and process scientific data within the limits of their knowledge. These skills will be developed primarily through courses with an experimental and laboratory approach and will be verified by assessing the ability to solve problems and write scientific reports.
III - Judgment autonomy Graduates must acquire conscious judgment autonomy, particularly regarding the evaluation and interpretation of laboratory experimental data. The acquisition of such skills will mainly occur through classroom and laboratory exercises and during activities carried out for the credits assigned to internship and thesis activities.
The verification of the achievement of this capability will be carried out through the preparation of concise reports (oral or written) aimed at evaluating the ability to interpret, reprocess, and present experimental results.
IV - Communication skills The graduate must acquire the ability to present a topic concisely and clearly, illustrate the purpose and results of a scientific work, and present experimental data in graphical form. These skills are primarily acquired during laboratory and practical exercises, which also promote group work and interpersonal relationships, and during the preparation and presentation of the final exam. Communication skills are also verified in all oral exam assessments.
V - Learning ability Graduates must have acquired the ability to study scientific topics; the ability to integrate and connect knowledge learned in different disciplines; the ability to evaluate their potential applications in appropriate contexts. They must also be able to choose textbooks and suitable study materials, including any didactic support for further study, even in English.
Learning abilities will be developed in all courses that involve consulting databases and information available on the web and/or consulting bibliographic material, particularly during the preparation of written and oral reports, but especially during the internship and thesis period. Expected outcomes will be verified during the preparation of the final report and through the final exam.
Work context function.
Work context function:
The main functions that a Biological Sciences graduate must be able to perform in the workplace, applying the acquired knowledge and procedural competencies, are listed below:
- Instrumental analysis connected to biological investigations;
- Technical analysis in biotechnology, biomolecular, and biomedical fields, also aimed at research activities;
- Technical and control analysis in environmental and water, air, soil, and food hygiene;
- Analysis in chemical-physical, biochemical, microbiological, toxicological, pharmacological, and genetic fields;
- Analysis aimed at quality control of products and processes;
- Evaluation of biotic impact on the conservation of cultural assets;
- Scientific training and dissemination;
- Creation and management of biological databases.
Function-associated competencies.
Function-associated competencies:
For the performance of the functions of a junior biologist, the specific knowledge, skills, and abilities that the biologist will acquire during the three-year course are required, including:
- Adequate basic knowledge of the various fields of Biology
- Multidisciplinary methodological and technological knowledge for biological investigation
- Solid technical and analytical skills in biological and instrumental analysis
- Knowledge of at least one foreign language within the specific field of competence
- Appropriate competencies and tools for communication and information management
- Ability to operate in the workplace both in groups and independently, with insertion capabilities in work environments
- Basic knowledge tools for continuous updating of one's own knowledge.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Career opportunities:
A biologist holding a three-year degree naturally finds employment opportunities in the following structures or entities:
- Universities and public and private research centers
- Public and private bio-health, agri-food, environmental, biotechnological, food, research, and pharmaceutical industry laboratories
- Communication, dissemination, and scientific information studios
- Institutions responsible for the protection of cultural assets, parks, museums, botanical gardens, biological or biochemical monitoring and environmental impact assessment bodies
- Multidisciplinary professional studios engaged in environmental impact assessment, project development for conservation and restoration of the environment and biodiversity, and biological safety
- Structures involved in scientific publishing in the biological-naturalistic field and translations in the biological field
The occupational fields, their corresponding educational objectives, and the consequent structure of the Bachelor's Degree Course have been harmonized nationally within the coordination of the CBUI, through periodic meetings attended by representatives of the Order of Biologists, Biologists' unions, representatives of Entities, and the national productive world.

ITALIAN
Degree awarded.
Degree in Obstetrics (enabling the health profession of Midwife)
Specific educational objectives.
The Second Degree Course in Obstetrics aims to train the professional figure of Midwife (Code: 3.2.1.) prepared to assist women throughout the physiological course of their life cycle, together with the protagonists of the reproductive process. This is enabled by passing the graduation exam and registration with the relevant professional register.
The cultural profile of the professional figure requires specific preparation in communication methodology for the purpose of:
- promoting a woman-centered approach;
- transmitting scientific evidence to the protagonists of the reproductive process in simple and understandable terms;
- continuously accompanying the woman in her biological-sexual journey, personalizing her care.
The direct care profile of the professional figure must meet the needs of the areas where she carries out her activities (public area: hospital, university, territory - private area: clinics and private practice) without favoring any of these.
This profile presupposes:
- clinical skills (consultation; diagnosis; prognosis; direct assistance to spontaneous processes not open to pathology of pregnancy, labor, birth, and postpartum with the execution of procedures consolidated by the art of midwifery and updated by scientific evidence);
- organizational skills (planning; programming; epidemiological surveys);
- exercise of responsibility (awareness; controls; limits; collaboration);
- teaching skills (public health information and education for areas of competence; mentoring for colleagues; personal updating).
The teaching profile of the Midwife must provide that training, normally, is carried out by personnel of the same professional profile.
Every performance conceived by the professional profile of the Midwife arises as an autonomous act with full responsibility. This autonomy ceases for all events deviating from physiology and requiring the involvement of the physician.
In any case, the Midwife maintains a continuous and efficient collaboration with the physician in the patient's best interest.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Regarding knowledge and understanding, at the end of each year, the student must have acquired:
1) for the first year:
- the terminology and method of Biological Sciences and possession of basic knowledge on the functioning of biological life, with particular attention to the transmission of hereditary characteristics;
- knowledge on embryological evolution, the microscopic and macroscopic structure of human organs and tissues, with particular emphasis on the female and male genital apparatus;
- preparatory information for the internship with experiential methods;
- knowledge on the areas of competence of the Midwife where basic obstetric care is applied in the maternal-infant area;
- knowledge of the historical development of the profession, through the evolution of obstetric thought;
- knowledge of the rights and duties of the professional and the evolution of their role, particularly for the obstetric profession;
- knowledge/understanding of individual and team work organization;
- knowledge of drugs and their fate in the organism;
- understanding of the role, characteristics, and responsibility of the obstetric professional figure;
2) for the second year:
- knowledge on natural morphological and functional modifications of the organism and the needs induced by the pregnancy context;
- knowledge on the morphological and sensory development of the embryo and fetus;
- ability to understand the psychology of the woman, her culture, and the best socio-environmental conditions for pregnancy;
- knowledge and ability to apply maneuvers for normal childbirth;
- scientific knowledge related to assistive procedures;
- further refinement of one's ability to understand the role and responsibilities of the Midwife in care during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum;
3) for the third year:
- knowledge related to the pathological newborn, with the specific needs that their care entails;
- knowledge on the legal aspect of the obstetric profession, with particular regard to responsibility and legal obligations;
- ability to understand the competencies of the Midwife and the consequent autonomy and responsibility;
- knowledge and awareness of the ethical and deontological issues related to the profession of Midwife;
- knowledge of international and national regulations for training and professional activity of Midwife, also in relation to placement within the National and Regional Health Systems;
- ability to understand the role and responsibilities of the Midwife in care during pathological pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, and events in the biological sphere with pathological characteristics.
The methodologies and training activities, together with the teaching tools to develop these expected outcomes, will use:
- lectures;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams and materials, graphs;
- guided reading and application;
- seminars;
- individual study.
The assessment tools to verify the achievement of these expected outcomes will use:
- written and oral exams;
- clinical case analysis.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Regarding the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, at the end of each year, the student must have acquired:
1) for the first year:
- knowledge of the physical and chemical bases and understanding of metabolic pathways in order to interpret physiological and pathological mechanisms of the human body, during pregnancy and childbirth;
- knowledge and applied understanding in the field of radioprotection;
- basic knowledge of pathogens, their aggressiveness, and the defense mechanisms predisposed by the organism against them, to understand their practical-clinical reflections;
- knowledge on the normal functioning of various organs and systems, to contribute to maintaining the integrity of the organism;
- knowledge of the causes and phenomena leading to the alteration of the physiological state of the organism, on the mechanisms of disease onset and the defense tools of our organism, to understand how to identify disease signs and symptoms and learn assistive maneuvers to prevent and treat them;
- understanding of general concepts on vital functions and the needs of the person and ability to perform obstetric assistive services in these areas;
- ability to plan/perform care plans;
2) for the second year:
- basic knowledge that allows understanding the morphology, functionality, psychology, and cultural and social context of women during puberty and the subsequent fertile period for a comprehensive and coherent care approach;
- basic knowledge on the modifications of female physiology during menopause and aging to interpret genital morphology, functionality of target organs of sex hormones, as well as the psychology of women in this life stage and establish a comprehensive and coherent care approach;
- knowledge related to a global, personalized, and continuous obstetric care model that considers the specific needs of pregnant women and their families, to understand the importance of the woman's centrality, her emotional process, and the uniqueness of the event in a relational context that activates maternal competencies, leading the woman to be the protagonist of the birth journey;
- anatomical, functional, and semiological knowledge that allows knowing, recognizing, and maintaining the physiological evolution of labor and birth as a bio-psychosocial and emotional event in the life of the woman, newborn, couple, and family;
- knowledge and understanding to apply methods for monitoring fetal and maternal well-being;
- ability to use technological resources correctly and appropriately;
- applied knowledge for neonatal care and promotion of breastfeeding;
- knowledge and ability to apply different approaches to childbirth care, respecting the wishes and/or physical and emotional needs of the woman in labor;
- understanding of morphological and physiological modifications and needs induced on the organism by the postpartum and lactation, for psychological and/or bodily relationships woman/child, woman/partner, woman/family, woman/social environment, and the psychosocial mechanisms related to assuming parental commitment within the couple;
- understanding and ability to use statistical procedures necessary to collect, organize, and analyze data from professional reality, in order to appropriately use scientific literature and set correct evaluations of one's clinical experiences within research programs.
3) for the third year:
- basic knowledge that allows correct use of semiology to produce a diagnosis of pregnancy pathology and, if necessary, offer an appropriate care approach for emergencies/urgencies;
- ability to discern the pharmacological and pharmacotherapeutic action on the organism in various diseases of interest;
- knowledge of the causes and phenomena determining alterations in the physiological evolution of childbirth and postpartum, so that, with judgment autonomy, one can recognize the signs and symptoms of such alterations;
- basic knowledge that allows correct use of semiology to produce a diagnosis of pathological labor or dystocic birth or at risk of maternal-neonatal pathology or pathological postpartum;
- applied knowledge and understanding to offer an appropriate care approach for emergencies/urgencies;
- basic knowledge to recognize and illustrate to interested parties the main oncological, involutive, or epidemic gynecological pathologies, stimulating, in at-risk cases, appropriate precautionary measures or the execution of suitable diagnostic screenings;
- basic knowledge to disseminate the principles of preventive gynecology and to promote, organize, and carry out the main early diagnostic screenings;
- technical and organizational tools to responsibly carry out dissemination and culturalization programs in the field of social medicine;
- basic knowledge to recognize the main gynecological pathologies, describe their risks, and produce an appropriate care approach for emergencies/urgencies;
- applied ability in organizational models specific to the area of competence of the Midwife in the maternal-infant area, as well as methods and tools related to internal and external communication within the reference organizational structure;
- knowledge and possession of tools that allow managing work organization, together with colleagues and collaborators, with balance and efficiency;
- clinical, technical, and relational skills required in clinical situations where one exercises their professionalism.
The methodologies and training activities, together with the teaching tools to develop these expected outcomes, will use:
- lectures, role-playing;
- exercises, simulations;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams and materials, graphs;
- discussion of cases in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship in various contexts with supervised experiences and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility.
The assessment tools to verify the achievement of these expected outcomes will use:
- written and oral exams, clinical case analysis, obstetric record compilations and drafting of care plans, drafting of reports;
- evaluation feedback during the internship.
III - Autonomy of judgment Regarding autonomy of judgment, at the end of each year, the student must have acquired:
1) for the first year:
- ability to understand and judgment autonomy to determine the aggregation of various disciplines in order to systematically pursue preparation and continuous growth on both personal and professional levels;
- judgment autonomy that provides for constant adaptation of knowledge moments characterizing training to subsequent theoretical levels of clinical exercises;
- judgment autonomy on work organizational skills through training experiences requiring the implementation of concrete professional behaviors;
- ability to measure one's skills to adapt acquired scientific concepts to precise application requirements in delivering obstetric care;
- judgment autonomy consistent with acquired knowledge in analyzing the needs of the person;
- clinical judgment autonomy, consistent with acquired knowledge in identifying the principles of basic obstetric care applicable in the fields of prevention, care, and rehabilitation;
2) for the second year:
- ability to apply knowledge, understand, and exercise one's judgment autonomy to evaluate one's abilities and adapt acquired scientific concepts to precise application requirements to deliver obstetric care that does not overlook events in the biological-sexual sphere of the woman, with particular attention to physiological pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum;
- judgment autonomy to evaluate if the pregnancy process proceeds normally, knowing how to apply necessary procedures in situations deviating from normality;
- judgment autonomy to understand the needs of the woman in labor/couple as well as the boundary between physiology and pathology and to know which assistive acts to apply when needed;
- judgment autonomy to evaluate the well-being of mother and newborn and any alteration thereof;
- judgment autonomy consistent with acquired knowledge in analyzing the needs of pregnant, laboring, and postpartum women;
- clinical judgment autonomy consistent with acquired knowledge in health education interventions within the community;
3) for the third year:
- judgment autonomy consistent with acquired knowledge in delivering one's care in every situation provided for by the professional profile of the Midwife;
- organizational and judgment autonomy, consistent with acquired knowledge, in health organization interventions and programming of care plans in the maternal-infant area.
The methodologies and training activities, together with the teaching tools to develop these expected outcomes, will use:
- clinical case discussion in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship in various contexts with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility with tutor-supervised experiences;
- debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences.
The assessment tools to verify the achievement of these expected outcomes will use:
- written and oral exams, case analysis;
- evaluation feedback during the internship (through structured evaluation sheets and clinical reports on professional practice).
IV - Communication skills Regarding communication skills, at the end of each year, the student must have acquired:
1) for the first year:
- tools for direct or indirect analysis of the individual, their needs, peculiarities, and socio-cultural context;
- theoretical-practical knowledge of personalized obstetric care respecting the values of the woman, couple, and family;
- communication skills for concrete use in obstetric care practice;
- basic knowledge for good communication using computer tools;
- ability to understand, locate, select, record, and express information effectively and efficiently, using the English language;
- communication skills with the person being assisted, with relatives, and with healthcare team professionals.
2) for the second year:
- communication skills capable of adapting to any type of woman in her particular clinical situation, with particular attention to support during labor;
- communication skills supporting the mother/newborn relationship, woman/partner, woman/family, woman/social environment;
- ability to refine communication through computer tools;
- ability to identify communication methods appropriate to the clinical situation, with women, with relatives, and with healthcare team professionals.
3) for the third year:
- the ability to manage communication in events of particular emergency/urgency, both with the woman/couple and with healthcare professionals with whom they collaborate in the team;
- knowledge and possession of tools that allow establishing a trusting relationship and building a therapeutic alliance with the woman, recognizing one's and others' psychosocial conditioning;
- ability to identify communication methods appropriate to people and clinical/organizational situations faced.
The methodologies and training activities, together with the teaching tools to develop these expected outcomes, will use:
- lectures; role-playing;
- videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives, testimonies;
- discussion of cases and paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with tutor-supervised experiences in various contexts with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.
The assessment tools to verify the achievement of these expected outcomes will use:
- observation of films or written materials, dialogues with structured grids;
- evaluation feedback during the internship (through structured evaluation sheets and clinical reports).
V - Learning ability Regarding the ability to learn, at the end of each year, the student must have acquired:
1) for the first year:
- ability to learn and apply the principles underlying assistive, diagnostic, and therapeutic procedures;
- ability to record and organize information effectively and efficiently, using the main writing, calculation, database, and multimedia presentation programs currently available;
2) for the second year:
- ability to locate, select, and record information effectively and efficiently;
- knowledge and possession of tools that allow maintaining and controlling, in one's work path, an adequate level of theoretical preparation and practical activity, developing the scientific ability to select epidemiologically valid and applicable information;
3) for the third year:
- knowledge and possession of tools that allow producing and controlling, in one's work path, a constant flow of quality, acquiring consistency with one's assumptions and developing responsibility through the setup and review of critical points of the programs set;
- ability to apply acquired knowledge, understanding, and judgment autonomy to evaluate one's abilities and use scientific concepts in obstetric care practice for pathological events in the biological-sexual sphere of the woman, with particular attention to pathological pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum.
The teaching tools, methodologies, and training activities to develop these expected outcomes will use:
- cognitive maps;
- contracts and self-learning plans to empower the student in planning their internship path and self-assessment;
- workshops on bibliographic research methodology, both paper and online;
- guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
The assessment tools to verify the achievement of these expected outcomes will use:
- presentation of reports on specific research mandates;
- tutorial supervision on the internship path;
- active participation in work sessions and debriefing;
- punctuality and quality in the presentation of assignments.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
The professionalism acquired with the Obstetrics Degree opens to all assistive employment opportunities of the profile (code 3.2.1.5) present in the territory and in hospital settings – both public and private – as well as to the free professional activity that includes the autonomous conduct of physiological home birth.
The degree also allows for further studies, with selective access to Level I Masters, Master's Degree, and from there to Level II Masters, Research Doctorate, to reach the role of Researcher, with an opening towards an academic career.
Entering into the specifics of the performances, where decisional autonomy of the Midwife exists, it is necessary to remember that these can be modified, both in an expansive and restrictive manner, by the constant updating of knowledge on the meaning, correlations, and consequences of the prescribed assistive acts in the areas of intervention.
The groups of autonomous performances, provided for in the workplace, are currently the following.
- Physiological pregnancy care - all acts that allow care for pregnant women: health information and education, data collection, obstetric examination, prescription of exams, execution of some of them, diagnostic synthesis, registration of events and resolutions.
- Conducting birth accompaniment courses, prioritizing those paths that promote the bond with the fetus, self-knowledge, and its maturation as a parental figure.
- Physiological labor and birth care, valuing the woman's centrality and her emotional process in birth, and respecting the phases and timing of its natural evolution in labor. This involves welcoming, direct assistance to labor and normal birth with repair of first and second-degree lacerations, identifying situations at risk of pathological evolution for the mother, fetus, and newborn, and recording events and care.
- Healthy newborn care with particular attention to the immediate postnatal phases and promotion of the communicational and nutritional bond between mother and child.
- Normal postpartum care in a desirable continuous care with the woman, the Midwife enhances the mother-child bond by supporting breastfeeding and providing information on events related to the child's needs and the restoration of normal relationships involving the husband and family.
- Postpartum course conduct contributing to strengthening maternal competence, fostering security in her relationship with the child, and inducing early rehabilitation of the perineal and abdominal muscle tone of the postpartum woman.
- Health education activities directing one's commitment, in both individual and organized situations, to prevention, early diagnosis, and rehabilitation for tumors and chronic degenerative or involutive diseases of the female genital sphere.
- Health organization activities participating in maternal and neonatal care programs.
In any other area where autonomous intervention of the Midwife is not provided, the principle holds that her assistive collaboration is enhanced by the values recognized by the cultural profile.
