ITALIAN Degree Awarded.
Nursing Degree (entitled to the health profession of Nurse)
Specific Educational Objectives.
Graduates of the Course must achieve the following specific educational objectives:
a. Promotion and maintenance of health
- manage preventive and assistive interventions directed at the assisted individuals, their families, and the community;
- design and implement, collaborating with other professionals, information and educational interventions for the control of risk factors for individuals and groups;
- educate individuals to healthy lifestyles and to modify risk behaviors.
b. Organization and continuity of care
- define priorities of interventions based on care needs, organizational requirements, and optimal use of available resources;
- design and manage, collaborating with others, nursing care for a group of patients (including night shifts);
- distinguish care needs from nursing care needs, differentiating the contribution of support staff from that of nurses;
- assign and supervise care activities for support staff;
- manage paper and computerized information systems supporting care;
- document nursing care provided in accordance with legal and ethical principles;
- ensure patients and significant persons receive information about their health status;
- prepare conditions for the discharge of the assisted person in collaboration with team members;
- ensure continuity of care between different shifts and services;
- use professional integration tools (meetings, team sessions, case discussions);
- work integratively within the team respecting areas of competence;
- establish professional relationships and collaborate with other healthcare professionals, aware of the specificities of different roles and their integration with nursing care;
- assume leadership roles for support staff and/or students;
- communicate nursing assessments and decisions effectively to team members using verbal, non-verbal, and written methods.
c. Safety and risk control in care contexts
- ensure a physical and psychosocial environment effective for patient safety;
- use practices for protection against physical, chemical, and biological risks in the workplace;
- adopt manual handling precautions;
- adopt infection prevention strategies (standard precautions) in hospital and community settings.
d. Helping relationship and adaptation/Mental Health
- activate and manage a helping relationship with the user, their family, and significant persons;
- identify and manage, collaborating with other professionals, frequent and high-risk behavioral alterations such as mental confusion, disorientation, agitation;
- support, collaborating with the team, the patient and their family during the terminal phase of illness and grief;
- contribute, collaborating with other professionals, to managing psychological distress, particularly during stabilization phases.
e. Clinical Nursing for Patients with Priority Health Issues (Maternal-Infant/Adults/Elderly)
- manage nursing care for patients (pediatric, adult, elderly) with issues related to priority health conditions such as acute and chronic respiratory, cardiovascular, metabolic, rheumatic, acute and chronic renal, gastrointestinal, hepatic, neurological, oncological, infectious, orthopedic-traumatic, obstetric-gynecological, and hematological problems;
- assess and manage nursing care for patients with chronic conditions and disabilities;
- manage perioperative nursing care;
- activate and support residual capacities of the person to promote adaptation to limitations and alterations caused by illness and modification of lifestyle;
- identify nursing care needs and related reactions to illness, treatments, institutionalization, changes in daily activities, and quality of life;
- monitor the clinical and psychosocial status of patients, identifying early signs of deterioration;
- activate necessary nursing interventions for acute and/or critical situations;
- identify and prevent triggers for exacerbation in chronic patients.
f. Application and management of diagnostic and therapeutic pathways
- ensure safe administration of therapy and monitor its effectiveness;
- activate decision-making processes based on patient conditions, vital parameters, reports, and laboratory data;
- manage, collaborating with other professionals, diagnostic pathways, ensuring appropriate patient preparation and follow-up;
- integrate nursing care into multidisciplinary care plans.
g. Patient Education and Community Intervention Methods
- activate informal care networks to support the user and family in long-term care projects;
- develop educational projects with the person and family to develop self-care skills;
- support patient learning in self-management of problems/therapies/devices;
- educate caregivers in managing the needs of the assisted person;
- manage patient discharge.
h. Clinical Method
- assess nursing care needs using assessment methods and tools;
- use the nursing care process in patient care;
- revise nursing care planning based on patient problem evolution;
- predict future nursing care needs;
- evaluate the results of provided care and adjust nursing care planning based on observed evolution.
i. Evidence-Based Practice
- search literature for evidence-based practice starting from clinical practice questions;
- critically analyze the literature;
- apply the best evidence in practice, adapting to user values, beliefs, preferences, available resources, and clinical judgment.
j. Self-Learning
- assess personal learning needs through discussion with mentor/tutor;
- design a self-learning plan for professional training activities;
- request feedback from supervisors in clinical learning contexts;
- develop a plan for elective courses and professional activities;
- prepare a personal portfolio.
k. Techniques
- perform nursing techniques defined by the Degree Course standards.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding Graduates in Nursing must know and understand:
- biomedical sciences for understanding physiological and pathological processes related to health and illness across the lifespan, including end-of-life;
- psychosocial and humanistic sciences for understanding normal and pathological relational dynamics and defensive or adaptive reactions to psychological, social, and physical distress;
- learning and change theories for understanding educational processes for citizens or patients;
- general and clinical nursing sciences for understanding nursing intervention fields, clinical methods, intervention techniques, and available evidence guiding decision-making;
- ethical, legal, and sociological sciences for understanding the complexity of the healthcare system, the importance of acting in compliance with regulations and guidelines, and respect for values and ethical dilemmas; these also aim to foster understanding of professional autonomy, areas of integration and interdependence with other team members;
- hygiene and preventive sciences for understanding health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions promoting safety for healthcare workers and users;
- computer and language disciplines, with particular emphasis on English, for understanding scientific literature in both print and online formats.
For the training activities in question, reference is made, in particular, to basic, characteristic, and related activities. Results will be verified through written and/or oral exams. Learning verification and achievement of predefined knowledge and understanding levels may also occur through in-course assessment methods, which will be considered during the final exam. For activities related to computer and language disciplines, verification methods will be practical, based on the use of software adopted by the University.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding Nursing graduates must demonstrate the following abilities to apply knowledge and understanding:
- integrate knowledge, skills, and attitudes to provide safe, effective, evidence-based nursing care;
- use a body of theoretical knowledge derived from Nursing, behavioral and social sciences, and other disciplines to recognize needs of assisted individuals across ages and life stages;
- integrate theoretical and practical nursing knowledge with biological, psychological, socio-cultural, and humanistic sciences to understand individuals of all ages, groups, and communities;
- use theoretical models and role models to facilitate growth, development, and adaptation in promoting, maintaining, and recovering health;
- interpret and apply research results to nursing practice and link research processes to the theoretical development of nursing;
- provide safe, evidence-based nursing care;
- conduct a comprehensive and systematic assessment of individual care needs;
- use assessment techniques to accurately collect data on major health issues of assisted individuals;
- accurately analyze and interpret collected data;
- plan nursing care delivery in collaboration with users and the interdisciplinary care team, including palliative care and pain therapy;
- evaluate care progress in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team;
- facilitate the development of a safe environment for the patient by ensuring constant nursing vigilance.
For training activities related to the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, reference is made in particular to some characteristic "professionalizing" activities, "professionalizing" laboratory activities, and internship activities. For activities related to "characteristic" training areas, results will be verified through written and/or oral exams. For laboratory and internship activities, learning verification and achievement of predefined knowledge and understanding levels will occur through practical and in-course assessment methods, culminating in a final exam that considers activities performed during the semester/year and in-course "partial" evaluations.
The final exam constitutes an important individual learning opportunity to complete the course. It consists of a) a practical test in which the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-professional knowledge specific to the professional profile; b) preparation and defense of a thesis.
III - Judgment Autonomy Nursing graduates must demonstrate judgment autonomy through the following abilities:
- make care decisions;
- prioritize care for groups of patients;
- decide interventions to assign to support staff;
- provide personalized nursing care based on similarities and differences of assisted persons regarding values, ethnicity, and socio-cultural practices;
- decide appropriate care interventions considering legal, political, geographical, economic, ethical, and social influences;
- critically evaluate outcomes of care decisions based on patient outcomes and care standards;
- assume responsibility and accountability for professional practice in accordance with the profile, code of ethics, and ethical and legal standards;
- make decisions through a scientific problem-solving approach for patient issues;
- analyze organizational problems and propose solutions;
- decide in situations characterized by diverse positions (conflicts or dilemmas).
IV - Communication Skills Nursing graduates must develop the following communication skills:
- use appropriate communication skills (verbal, non-verbal, and written) with users of all ages, their families, and other healthcare professionals;
- use appropriate communication methods in multidisciplinary teams;
- use teaching and learning principles for specific information or educational interventions for individual users, families, groups, and other professionals (support staff, nursing students, nurses);
- support and encourage users toward health choices, reinforcing coping skills, self-esteem, and available resources;
- manage conflicts arising from different positions;
- facilitate coordination of care to achieve agreed health care outcomes;
- collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
V - Learning Ability Nursing graduates must develop the following learning abilities:
- develop independent study skills;
- demonstrate the ability to cultivate doubts and tolerate uncertainties arising from study and practical activities;
- develop the ability to pose questions relevant to time, place, and interlocutors regarding professional practice;
- demonstrate the ability to continuously seek self-learning opportunities;
- demonstrate the ability to self-assess competencies and outline personal development and learning needs;
- demonstrate collaborative learning and knowledge sharing within work teams;
- demonstrate the ability and autonomy to seek necessary information to resolve professional practice problems or uncertainties, critically selecting literature evidence.
Function in Work Context.
Function in Work Context:
Pursuant to Ministerial Decree No. 739/94, the main functions of the nurse are:
- disease prevention;
- care for sick and disabled individuals of all ages;
- health education.
Competencies associated with the function.
Regarding competencies, pursuant to Ministerial Decree No. 739/94, the nurse:
- participates in identifying health needs of individuals and the community;
- identifies nursing care needs of individuals and the community and formulates related objectives;
- plans, manages, and evaluates nursing care interventions;
- ensures correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions;
- acts individually or in collaboration with other healthcare and social operators;
- for the performance of functions, utilizes, where necessary, the work of support staff.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
The graduate nurse is entitled, upon registration with the professional register, to practice the nursing profession in healthcare facilities, public or private, hospital and territorial, including home care, in an employee or self-employed capacity.

ITALIAN
Degree Awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in DENTAL HYGIENE (Qualifying for the Sanitary Profession of Dental Hygienist)
Specific Educational Objectives.
Graduates of the Course must achieve the following specific educational objectives:
Within the sanitary profession of Dental Hygienist, graduates are the healthcare professionals to whom the responsibilities defined by the Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of Health of March 15, 1999, No. 137 and subsequent amendments and integrations apply, or they perform, upon the indication of Dentists and Medical Surgeons authorized to practice Dentistry, tasks related to the prevention of oral and dental diseases. Graduates in Dental Hygiene perform activities of dental health education and participate in primary prevention projects within the public health system; collaborate in compiling the dental and stomatological clinical record and are responsible for collecting technical-statistical data; perform the removal of tartar and root planing, as well as the topical application of various preventive means; provide instruction on various oral hygiene methods and the use of diagnostic tools suitable for detecting bacterial plaque and dental stains, motivating the need for periodic clinical checks; indicate the norms of rational nutrition for the protection of dental health; carry out their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in a dependent or self-employed capacity, upon the indication of Dentists and Medical Surgeons authorized to practice Dentistry.
Graduates in Dental Hygiene are equipped with adequate preparation in basic disciplines, enabling them to best understand the most relevant elements underlying pathological processes that develop in childhood, adulthood, and old age, which form the focus of their clinical intervention. They must also be able to use at least one language of the European Union, in addition to Italian, within their specific field of competence and for the exchange of general information. The educational structures identify, through the appropriate selection of disciplinary areas of the characteristic training activities, with particular attention to professionalizing scientific-disciplinary sectors, the specific training paths for the aforementioned sanitary profession.
The achievement of professional competencies is carried out through theoretical and practical training that also includes the acquisition of behavioral competencies and is obtained within the specific work context of the profile, thereby guaranteeing, at the end of the training path, full mastery of all necessary competencies and their immediate applicability in the work environment. Particular emphasis, as an integral and qualifying part of professional training, is placed on practical training and clinical internship, carried out under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors specifically assigned and a clinical internship coordinator.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and Understanding
Graduates in Dental Hygiene must acquire post-secondary level knowledge in the field of basic biomedical disciplines and clinical disciplines, manual skills, and operational techniques, functional to the exercise of the Dental Hygienist profession.
In particular, the Dental Hygiene graduate must:
- Possess knowledge of the fundamentals of human morphology, physiology, and pathology, integrating the study of physiopathological and pathological aspects with clinical methodology and therapeutic procedures defined by the professional profile;
- Know the main disease patterns and therapeutic procedures, medical and surgical, complementary to the Dental Hygienist profession, as well as basic knowledge of care and assistance according to psycho-pedagogical principles, sociology, and health ethics;
- Understand the effects of pharmacological therapy for systemic diseases on oral health and the potential implications for therapeutic procedures defined by the professional profile;
- Know the demographic aspects, prevention, and treatment of oral and dental diseases in childhood, adulthood, and old age, including in medically compromised patients or those with physical or psychological disabilities, with specific focus on preventive and therapeutic procedures relevant to the clinical activities of the Dental Hygienist (caries, periodontal disease/oral health education, compilation of clinical records and collection of clinical-epidemiological indices, tartar removal, root planing, application of various preventive means, oral hygiene instruction, patient motivation, dietary counseling, and anti-tobacco counseling).
The aforementioned knowledge is acquired through basic and characteristic activities. The teaching methodology includes lectures, laboratories, exercises, and clinical internships. Verification methods include oral interviews, written essays (requiring logical rigor), and, where required, practical tests on simulators and patients.
Graduates must also be able to use the specific language of Dental Hygiene Sciences.
Graduates must achieve knowledge and understanding in a post-secondary field of study and be at a level that, characterized by the use of advanced textbooks, also includes knowledge of some cutting-edge topics in their field of study.
For the training activities in question, reference is made in particular to basic, characteristic, and related activities. The results will be verified through written and/or oral exams. The assessment of learning and the achievement of the specified knowledge and understanding levels may also occur through interim evaluation methods during the training path, which will be duly considered during the final exam. For activities related to computer science and language disciplines, verification methods will be based on practical approaches, also using software adopted by the University.
II - Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding
Graduates in Dental Hygiene must be able to independently organize the knowledge and operational techniques acquired for the exercise of the Dental Hygienist profession. To this end, graduates must be able to use the acquired knowledge by leveraging both the understanding gained from individual study and the professionalizing knowledge derived from internship activities.
In particular, graduates must:
- Be able to recognize, at the level of the oral cavity, clinical signs of local and systemic diseases as well as typical morphological-functional aspects of oral and stomatological health;
- Be able to recognize vital signs and perform first aid maneuvers in the work environment;
- Be able to perform the full range of operational procedures specific to the professional profile, upon the indication of the dentist and within the context of the patient's overall treatment without producing additional risks for the patient;
- Be able to interact with other parties in planning interventions aimed at preventing oral diseases in the community, based on knowledge of the principles and practice of community dentistry;
- Be able to control cross-infection in the exercise of the profession;
- Know and apply anti-tobacco counseling techniques (brief intervention), techniques for motivating patients to home oral hygiene, regular professional check-ups, and rational nutrition for the protection of oral health;
- Be able to interact with other members of the dental team (dentist, dental office assistant, administrative staff, orthognathic or oral surgery specialist).
The teaching tools aimed at achieving the ability to apply knowledge within characteristic activities include, in addition to the overall teaching activities directed at the student (lectures, self-learning, etc.), pre-clinical activities at individual workstations and clinical internships with patients. Other fundamental tools will be the use of information technology, consultation and/or construction and updating of databases, bibliographic research, use of textbooks, and preparation of the thesis for the final exam.
The evaluation of these abilities will occur through exams (depending on the type of teaching activity administered), periodic practical evaluations within internship activities, as well as through the final exam of the internship, aimed at verifying the acquisition of manual and technical-operative skills in various clinical activities specific to the professional profile, and through the final exam itself.
Graduates must be capable of applying their knowledge and understanding to demonstrate a professional approach to their work and must possess adequate competencies to design and support arguments and solve problems in their field of study.
For training activities related to the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, particular reference is made to certain "professionalizing" characteristic activities, "professionalizing" laboratory activities, and internship activities. For activities related to the "characteristic" training areas, the results will be verified through written and/or oral exams. For laboratory and internship activities, the assessment of learning and the achievement of the specified knowledge and understanding levels will occur through practical and interim evaluation methods during the training path, culminating in a final exam that takes into account the activities carried out during the semester/year and the interim "partial" evaluations.
The final exam constitutes an important individual training opportunity to complete the path. It consists of a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate the acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile; b) preparation and defense of a thesis.
III - Judgment Autonomy
Graduates must have the capacity to collect and interpret data (normally within their field of study) deemed useful for determining independent judgments, including reflection on social, scientific, or ethical issues related to them.
The Dental Hygiene graduate:
- Must be able to independently manage non-surgical periodontal treatment and caries prevention, always upon the indication of the dentist or other persons authorized to practice dentistry.
- Must be able to evaluate the effectiveness of the treatment plan, the interventions carried out, and the results achieved.
- Must be able to recognize their own limitations in patient care and recognize the need to refer the patient to other competencies for dental-rehabilitative or medical therapies.
Graduates' judgment autonomy will be expressed through the recognition and ability to autonomously evaluate critical issues related to the patient's condition, in relation to oral hygiene and prevention of dental diseases, and in developing practical and/or experimental prevention schemes and choosing methodologies, strategies, and, if necessary, equipment, optimal for achieving the expected results, also through the critical review of information obtained through bibliographic and/or computer research.
The maturation of such capacities will occur and be verified during internships, where encounters with people, professionalities, structures, and different methodologies will facilitate the development of independent critical thinking. Equal relevance will be given to active participation in lectures, preparation for exams, and the final exam, further moments of maturation and verification.
Knowledge of the relevant regulations, professional, legal, health, and their consequent application will be aimed at achieving specific professional competencies, i.e., the ability to master and manage with autonomy and/or in a team, tools, technologies, and procedures.
The acquisition of a behavior consistent with the ethical foundations will be one of the objectives that completes the training path.
Judgment autonomy will be verified through evaluations by assigned tutors, through internship exams, and through the verification related to the final exam.
IV - Communication Skills
The graduate must establish and maintain a relationship with the user, starting from prevention, taking into account the various levels of complexity related. This constitutes the foundation of professional practice, which must be centered on the individual, respecting differences and taking into account their influence on dietary habits related to oral health, lifestyle, and individual habits.
The Dental Hygiene graduate:
- Will interview patients for needs assessment;
- Will carry out their activities in accordance with the principles of patient-centered professional practice;
- Will build a relationship/partnership as the foundation of oral hygiene intervention;
- Will employ a variety of personalized strategies based on the patient's needs;
- Will develop educational programs and educational materials to meet the learning needs of individuals and groups.
Graduates must be particularly skilled in interpersonal communication, including oral and written communication with professionals and service users, in group work, and within interdisciplinary teams with health and social professionals.
To achieve this, the Dental Hygiene graduate must:
- Select appropriate communication methods;
- Identify and address communication barriers (problems in reading or writing, misunderstanding, cultural issues, fear, etc.);
- Adapt communication style to meet the needs and learning abilities of individuals and/or groups;
- Employ effective verbal communication skills;
- Write clearly, concisely, and professionally, technically and grammatically accurately;
- Build educational materials that consider the comprehension capacity of the target group and/or individuals;
- Facilitate two-way communication;
- Employ active listening techniques;
- Interpret and respond to non-verbal communication;
- Apply principles of collaboration and negotiation in group work;
- Incorporate the knowledge, experiences, and skills of other team members during their activities;
- Collaborate with other team members to define goals;
- Adapt personal approach to team members and situations involving the team;
- Work with other team members to identify and resolve conflicts;
- Contribute to decisions made within the team;
- Take responsibility for completing assigned tasks.
Communication skills will be acquired through the teachings of human sciences, psychopedagogy, and sociology to ensure the learning of necessary behavioral and relational competencies to navigate a complex work environment. Additionally, the internship involves close contact between the student and patients under the supervision of tutors, whose task will be to modulate the approach methodology from the initial phase to the completion of professional training.
Communication skills will be evaluated by tutors during related teaching activities, during the internship, and through evaluations of teaching activities, up to the final exam.
Graduates must be able to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
V - Learning Ability
Graduates in Dental Hygiene must possess the ability to update their theoretical knowledge through consultation and analysis of scientific publications in the field of Dental Hygiene Sciences, also through the use of online databases.
Graduates must achieve sufficient knowledge and methodological skills to continue their study and cultural growth independently (specialist degree, university postgraduate courses, university master's degrees).
Graduates must be able to correctly interpret the legislation concerning the exercise of the Dental Hygienist profession in the European Union country where they practice and carry out professional activities in compliance with the medical-legal and ethical regulations in force in the country where they practice.
The learning ability is assessed through continuous verification methods during training activities, integrating knowledge acquired during specific activities with those obtained through personal study, evaluating the critical contribution demonstrated during seminar activities and clinical internships, as well as through the verification of the ability to self-learn developed during the final exam activity (thesis).
Graduates must have developed the learning abilities necessary to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Work Context Function.
Work Context Function:
The Dental Hygienist (D.H.), being the professional figure primarily dedicated to the prevention of oral cavity pathologies, in addition to performing preventive actions on the genesis of certain pathologies such as caries, periodontal disease, malocclusion, neoplasms, etc., possesses specific competencies:
- Motivation for general health and particularly oral health
- Individual home oral hygiene techniques, with particular reference to tools, means, and methodologies used
- Psychological approach to the dental patient in its various aspects: child, adolescent, adult, elderly, patient with orthodontic and prosthetic appliances, during pregnancy, oncological
- Removal of hard and soft deposits, supra- and sub-gingival, with manual and mechanical instruments
- Topical application of sealants, varnishes, foams, and desensitizers
- Fluoride prophylaxis methods
- Vital tooth whitening and taking impressions for mask construction
- Collaboration in compiling the clinical record
- Compilation of the periodontal record and measurement of periodontal disease parameters and indices
- Prevention and epidemiological projects, also on the territory
- Intra- and extra-oral photographic documentation
- Polishing of restorations
- Periodic clinical check-ups
Associated Competencies with the Function.
Associated Competencies with the Function:
The training of graduates in Dental Hygiene is integrated with periodic meetings with leading companies in the prevention sector to learn about the results of specific research and the goals pursued before introducing a product to the market; such information will help the future professional to orient themselves in the market to make the best choices regarding equipment and tools useful for their activity.
Particular attention is dedicated to acquiring skills useful for specific medical research in the sector (PUBMED) to constantly access the most recent acquisitions in the specific field of action.
The Course of Study, through targeted instruction and attendance at specialized departments (Maxillofacial Surgery, Internal Medicine, Family Clinics, etc.), allows the student to acquire competencies in managing dental patients with special needs, affected by important underlying pathologies (cardiac, hematological, diabetic, oncological, radio and chemotherapy-treated patients, etc.).
These patients, in fact, present concurrent oral pathologies, which, following the medications taken for the underlying condition, can evoke particular discomforts in terms of functional limitations (phonation, swallowing, chewing, taste, etc.) and algic symptoms, compromising quality of life.
Following specific (theoretical-practical) instruction on such patient types, the trained Dental Hygienist is able to work within public healthcare facilities, particularly hospitals, where patients with treatable conditions are routinely admitted.
Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Employment Prospects:
Currently, it is a profession still too concentrated in the private sector, requiring great attention from public health authorities.
For the Dental Hygienist, rapid access to public structures is hoped for, where certainly there is the possibility to successfully place one's professional skills, ensuring, at low costs, the maintenance and improvement of oral health through the prevention of oral cavity pathologies, similar to those that manifest in all other body districts.
In this way, the patient could benefit from public assistance for oral pathologies, which are still too expensive for society in terms of individual costs, for treatments, rehabilitations, medications, work days, etc.

Physiotherapy Degree (eligible for the health profession of Physiotherapist)
Specific educational objectives.
The main objective of the Physiotherapy Degree Course is to train the professional figure of the Physiotherapist (Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of Health, September 14, 1994, No. 741 and subsequent amendments), who is able to:
1) Formulate the physiotherapeutic diagnosis and prognosis:
- Collect data related to anamnesis, functions, activities, participation, and personal and environmental factors;
- Perform assessment of different functional systems using validated tools, measurements, guidelines, according to the principles of Evidence-Based Practice (EBP);
- Critically analyze and interpret relevant data to identify a physiotherapeutic functional diagnosis and prognostic hypotheses, considering recovery indices;
- Identify the level of disability in relation to the ICF (impairment, disability, social participation);
- Define possible alternative interpretations of the data;
- Explicitly state the clinical reasoning used in relation to the physiotherapeutic functional diagnosis;
- Compare data emerging from the assessment with potential bibliographic deepening in the interest of patient health protection.
2) Define and plan the physiotherapeutic intervention:
- Involve the patient by requesting active participation and informing them of the sequence of the physiotherapeutic path;
- Define physiotherapeutic problems and the related objectives to be achieved progressively during treatment;
- Identify possible preventive, educational, therapeutic, and palliative interventions;
- Choose resources usable within the rehabilitation path;
- Justify planning choices based on theoretical knowledge, constructed from assessment data, and based on the best available evidence and patient preferences;
- Propose the physiotherapeutic plan to the team for defining the rehabilitation project goals for the patient;
- Participate in planning educational-informational interventions and suggest activities for managing the person and self-care for patients and families.
3) Manage one's work within the Service:
- Plan one's work considering service objectives and priorities in line with organizational needs and optimal use of available resources;
- Evaluate in the planning of physiotherapeutic treatment the duration and frequency of the intervention in relation to potential side effects of medications that may influence physiotherapeutic treatment;
- Plan each rehabilitation session according to the priority of interventions, in relation to the problems and needs of each individual patient.
4) Perform the physiotherapeutic treatment:
- Pursue physiotherapeutic goals according to the path established in the intervention planning;
- Choose physiotherapeutic proposals in relation to the presence of possible comorbidities;
- Prepare the setting to implement the physiotherapeutic intervention;
- Implement preventive interventions;
- Propose activities consistent with the planned program to the assisted person, ensuring patient safety and compliance with current regulations;
- Propose and suggest creative alternative solutions in relation to the results achieved by the patient;
- Use aids/orthoses to facilitate functional abilities;
- Maintain a growing and continuous collaborative process in the care of the patient and/or family and/or caregiver.
5) Verify and evaluate the results obtained:
- Critically analyze the treatment plan and rehabilitation proposals in a constructive manner;
- Verify interim results of the physiotherapeutic proposal in collaboration with other professionals;
- Evaluate the achievement of goals and measure the outcomes of the physiotherapeutic intervention using validated methodologies and tools;
- Evaluate the entire physiotherapeutic process in relation to the effectiveness and efficiency of the results obtained.
6) Adopt professional attitudes in accordance with the code of ethics:
- Ensure confidentiality of information related to the person;
- Respect the individuality, ideas, and expectations of the patient;
- Operate with methodological rigor, applying continuous scientific acquisitions to the field of competence;
- Demonstrate awareness of one's own limitations regarding professional attitude, abilities, and competencies through critical self-assessment.
7) Establish an effective relationship with the assisted person, family, and team:
- Establish effective communication within the helping relationship through understanding non-verbal communication, body expressiveness, and adopting behavior consistent with the person's characteristics;
- Explain to the person how physiotherapeutic proposals may influence and/or modify functional activity;
- Share the physiotherapeutic project with the person and family.
8) Manage clinical and professional risk in the workplace:
- Ensure a physical and psychosocial environment suitable for patient safety;
- Identify and analyze clinical risk;
- Prevent and control major events that are sources of clinical risk;
- Use protective practices for the professional from physical, chemical, and biological risks in the workplace;
- Adopt precautions for the professional regarding manual handling of loads.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The Physiotherapy graduate possesses a wide range of knowledge in both basic sciences and core disciplines, as well as in communication and professional management.
In particular, the Physiotherapy graduate:
- Possesses solid cultural and scientific foundations in the fields of "Preliminary Sciences" and "Biomedical Sciences";
- Is able to understand physical and biological phenomena, human anatomy, mechanisms of operation of organs and systems, with particular attention to neurophysiology, motor and psychomotor development;
- Possesses a wide range of knowledge in the field of "Physiotherapy Sciences" necessary to identify preventive and rehabilitative needs of the subject through clinical data assessment in motor, psychomotor, cognitive, and functional fields, considering the severity and significance of symptoms;
- Is able to understand the underlying components of pathological processes on which rehabilitation and/or therapeutic intervention focuses, in pediatric, adult, or geriatric age; develop the best therapeutic, technical, and methodological approaches for resolving health problems of the person; acquire the scientific basis of functional alterations and general and specific rehabilitation methodology in various specialized fields (neurological, orthopedic, cardiovascular-pulmonary, maternal-infant area); design and verify the physiotherapeutic intervention using objective assessment and effective therapeutic methods and all appropriate tools for case resolution (instrumental therapies, manual therapies, psychomotor and occupational therapies, proposing the possible use of orthoses, prostheses, and aids) also in relation to medical indications and prescriptions;
- Possesses a wide range of knowledge in the field of "Human and Psychopedagogical Sciences";
- Is able to understand normal and pathological relational dynamics and defense or adaptation reactions of people in situations of psychophysical discomfort, also in correlation with psychological, social, and environmental dimensions related to processes determining priority health issues and disabilities, in acute phases, chronicity, in relation to different life stages and their impact on lifestyle and personal autonomy; improving understanding of educational processes directed at citizens;
- Possesses knowledge in the field of "Interdisciplinary and Surgical Medical Sciences";
- Is able to understand pathophysiological elements applicable to different clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters;
- Possesses knowledge in the field of "Health Services Sciences";
- Is able to understand and analyze health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions aimed at promoting safety for healthcare workers and users;
- Possesses knowledge in the field of "Management, Ethical, and Legal Sciences" aimed at organizing rehabilitation activities through the definition of priorities, appropriateness, and use of available resources, also working in teams, ensuring continuity and quality of care;
- Is able to understand the importance and utility of acting in accordance with regulations and guidelines, respecting values and ethical dilemmas encountered in daily practice, with the aim of promoting understanding of professional autonomy, areas of integration, and interdependence with other members of the care team;
- Possesses knowledge in the field of "Informatics and Linguistic Sciences" aimed at managing information necessary for the development of professional knowledge. Is able to use at least one European Union language besides Italian, namely English at an intermediate level, within the specific field of competence and for exchanging general information and understanding international scientific literature.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The Physiotherapy graduate is able to:
- Use the body of theoretical knowledge and skills derived from physiotherapy sciences to recognize the needs of assisted individuals across various ages and developmental stages in different life phases;
- Integrate theoretical and practical knowledge with biological, psychological, socio-cultural, and humanistic sciences useful for understanding individuals of all ages, groups, and communities;
- Use theoretical models in the care process to facilitate growth, development, and adaptation in promoting, maintaining, and recovering citizens' health;
- Correlate procedures enabling the implementation of effective and safe interventions based on evidence in rehabilitation areas of motor function, cortical functions, and visceral functions following pathogenic events of various congenital or acquired etiology;
- Apply the physiotherapeutic process within the rehabilitation setting, both in simulated form and with the patient, adopting problem-solving methodology and clinical reasoning;
- Apply and develop knowledge considering fundamental aspects such as interaction with the real-life context of people, interpersonal and inter-professional relationships, and organizational management of aspects directly related to the type of work performed;
- Implement, also in interdisciplinary teams, health promotion strategies for individuals or communities, evaluating progress;
- Be responsible for providing and evaluating treatment in line with professional quality standards in relation to ethical, bioethical, legal standards, and the rights of the assisted person;
- Interpret and apply research results to clinical practice and link research processes to the theoretical development of physiotherapy discipline;
- Deliver direct physiotherapeutic treatment safely to individuals and groups of patients through evidence-based practice, using the physiotherapeutic process to assess and diagnose health status, plan goals, implement, and evaluate care provided, considering the physical, psychological, and socio-cultural dimensions of the person;
- Manage a variety of activities required to deliver physiotherapy/rehabilitation interventions to patients in the wide variety of care contexts: hospital, territorial, residential, outpatient, home care;
- Formulate training programs after conducting self-assessment, taking responsibility for one's own training, reflecting on professional practice with the aim of learning.

III - Independent judgment The Physiotherapy graduate possesses the tools of clinical reasoning in physiotherapy and is able to:
- Independently apply the physiotherapeutic process using clinical reasoning as a decision criterion within possible options composing the various phases of the process, with a critical thinking approach to deliver personalized treatment according to national, international, and evidence-based guidelines;
- Carry out professional activity by effectively responding to individual and/or collective health needs, both as a single operator and within a team;
- Evaluate the effectiveness of one's own work, identifying criticalities and participating in their solution;
- Integrate knowledge on cultural diversity, values, and rights of the individual and community within ethical frameworks, respecting relevant regulations, professional, legal, health, and ethical guidelines;
- Fully realize through habitual and judicious use of communication, emotions, values, a creative attitude oriented towards research and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual and the community.

IV - Communication skills The Physiotherapy graduate possesses the tools of communication in the healthcare context and is able to:
- Use communication tools in the healthcare context, demonstrating the ability to complete clinical documentation and prepare a therapeutic report;
- Communicate verbally and in writing clearly, concisely, and professionally, technically and grammatically accurately, also knowing how to translate technical language into understandable terms for patients and the team;
- Use meaningful therapeutic communication and relationship skills, including non-verbal communication, with people of all ages and their families, and establish effective relationships with other healthcare professionals;
- Listen, inform, dialogue effectively with patients and families, communicate, argue, and justify one's actions and decisions with colleagues and different professional figures;
- Adapt communication according to context and respect cultural, ethnic, and value differences of the assisted persons;
- Communicate appropriately in scientific contexts to convey ideas, problems, and related solutions.

V - Learning ability The Physiotherapy graduate possesses the tools to plan self-education and is able to:
- Develop competent and independent problem-solving abilities, demonstrating the capacity to continuously seek self-learning opportunities;
- Take responsibility for one's professional development and respond to continuous changes in knowledge and health and social needs;
- Use self-assessment of one's educational level to maintain one's knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice;
- Design self-education paths to enhance one's competencies, with particular reference to Evidence-Based Practice in physiotherapy/rehabilitation.

ITALIAN Awarded degree.
Bachelor's Degree in PHYSICS Specific educational objectives.
The Bachelor's Degree in Physics provides a solid foundational preparation in Physical Sciences and skills useful both for continuing studies with a second-level degree and for direct entry into the workforce. The specific competencies imparted aim to provide the ability to model a natural phenomenon, formulate an interpretative model, and use scientific instrumentation and computer tools consciously. The cultural background provided is broad and includes, besides basic knowledge in classical and modern physics, the necessary foundations of mathematics and chemistry.
In particular, the proposed training activities aim to achieve the following specific learning outcomes:
a) Basic Logical-Mathematical Area: knowledge of mathematical analysis and geometry for acquiring basic methods of logical-deductive reasoning and mathematical tools, indispensable for operating in scientific fields b) Basic Classical and Experimental Physics Area: includes the fundamentals of classical physics, the experimental method, and the development of the ability to model a physical phenomenon in mathematical terms, as well as the critical sense necessary to evaluate the reliability of a measurement and a particular experimental/numerical methodology. The objective of these courses is to enable students to correctly use the principles of classical physics, instrumentation, and the computer to manage numerical data, produce graphs, interpret measurements, and deduce information and relationships between relevant physical quantities of a particular phenomenon.
c) Basic Chemistry Area: includes the basics of general chemistry, terminology, and nomenclature, useful both for entering the workplace and for continuing to higher studies.
d) Theoretical Physics, Models, and Advanced Mathematical Methods Area: includes the theoretical foundations and advanced mathematical formalism necessary to address problems in modern physics related to the atomic and sub-atomic structure of matter. The goal is to enable students to skillfully use this formalism to solve complex problems in macro and micro physics, which are of specific interest in both professional and advanced scientific research contexts.
e) Microphysics and Matter Structure Area: includes the theoretical foundations and principles underlying the experimental methods of physics of matter constituents; students will be able to use formalisms and concepts that form the basis of complex instrumentation operation in both professional and scientific research contexts.
f) Affine-Integrative Area: includes competencies and techniques in analog and digital electronics useful for entering the workforce and experimental research; it also includes concepts and competencies related to fluid physics and its dynamics, which form the basis of applications in both matter physics and geophysical-atmospheric contexts.
The first two years of the course focus on the activities described in points a)-c), while the final year is dedicated to the activities described in points d)-f).
Given the complexity and breadth of the basic topics necessary for the formation of both the professional figure of a physicist and the background required to continue higher studies, the proposed path features a single curriculum integrated with knowledge useful for entering the workforce and with in-depth studies that form the indispensable basis for continuing in more specialized studies. The training path is structured in:
i) Theoretical courses integrated with written exercises that provide the logical-deductive basis of mathematical reasoning and the scientific method, as well as the necessary mathematical formalism to address problems in both classical and quantum physics;
ii) Experimental laboratory courses that prepare students to confront various measurement methods and instruments, from simpler to more complex, with data analysis and processing, and to familiarize students with group work;
iii) Courses dedicated to or involving the critical use of the computer, the use and development of computational algorithms to simulate and/or solve simple and complex physical problems.
In all proposed activities, students are encouraged to use and improve their knowledge of the English language both in consulting texts/bibliography and in writing or presenting brief reports/relatives.
Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Graduates in Physics must acquire in-depth knowledge of advanced mathematical tools and concepts of classical and modern physics, as well as their application for modeling a physical phenomenon and classical and modern physics.
In particular, they must acquire in-depth knowledge and the ability to understand literature and specific texts in the following fields:
- Basic mathematics (mathematical analysis in one and multiple variables, linear algebra, methods for solving differential equations, complex analysis, functional analysis, probability theory) and be able to understand specific texts using their formalism
- Classical Physics (Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Optics) and related experimental aspects of measuring physical quantities, as well as the ability to understand advanced texts using their concepts and formalism
- Basic Chemistry and related scientific-technological aspects
- Modern Physics (Quantum Mechanics, Statistical Mechanics) and the necessary mathematical formalism
- Matter constituents (basic knowledge of atomic physics, condensed matter physics, nuclear and subnuclear physics)
- Fluid mechanics and its implications in condensed matter physics and geophysics Learning methods:
- Dedicated courses (basic and characteristic)
- Experimental and computational laboratory courses Over 120 CFU are dedicated to these activities Assessment methods: Individual exams with written and oral final exams for frontal courses; practical and oral exams for laboratory courses. In both course types, intermediate assessments are conducted.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding At the end of the training path, the Physics graduate will have acquired the ability to apply knowledge and understanding to operate professionally in various technical-scientific fields.
In particular, the graduate will have acquired the following skills:
- Ability for inductive and deductive reasoning.
- Ability to model a natural phenomenon in terms of scalar and vector physical quantities, to formulate a problem using appropriate relationships between physical quantities (algebraic, integral, or differential), and to solve it using analytical and/or numerical methods.
- Ability to set up and calibrate simple experimental configurations, and to use scientific instrumentation for thermo-mechanical, electromagnetic, and optical measurements, being able to critically discern and interpret the results.
- Ability to critically interpret experimental/numerical data, manage measurement systems, and analyze large sets of data using scientific methodology. Learning methods:
Theoretical courses in subjects with axiomatic treatments; extensive practice of numerical exercises and experimental and computational laboratory activities.
Assessment methods: All written assessments require applying knowledge to problems not previously addressed; practical laboratory assessments (experimental and/or computational) require formulating an appropriate measurement/computational device project aimed at determining the relevant quantities for the specific problem.
III - Judgment autonomy Physics graduates must have acquired the ability to:
- Reason critically
- Identify the most appropriate methods for analyzing and solving physical problems and for designing systems
- Understand the limits of their own knowledge and independently undertake appropriate investigations at their level of knowledge and understanding, resorting to bibliographic research, experimental design and conduct, interpretation of experimental data, and numerical simulation on the computer. They may also request consultation of databases and regulations.
In summary, graduates will have achieved:
- Critical reasoning ability.
- Ability to identify the most appropriate methods for analyzing and interpreting (using graphical and analytical methods) experimental data, theoretical predictions, or model forecasts, providing answers (certain or probabilistic) to previously posed questions.
- Ability to provide suggestions/solutions for optimizing a process through formalization and solution of the problem.
- Ability to understand the limits of their own knowledge and find appropriate methods to enhance them. Learning methods: These abilities result from theoretical courses and over 40 CFU of laboratory courses, where students are progressively guided to make the most conscious and appropriate choices for each specific problem, while being discouraged from applying recipes without understanding their meaning.
Assessment methods: Written and oral exams where students are stimulated to independently seek the best path for solving a given problem. Practical laboratory assessments requiring the design of measurement/numerical methods for solving specific problems.
IV - Communication skills At the end of the training path, graduates must acquire:
- The ability to orally present a scientific topic
- The ability to write a scientific report illustrating motivations and results,
- The ability to prepare and present a scientific topic using graphical and tabular representations, for both specialist and general audiences
- The ability to use methods to communicate effectively with the scientific community by presenting appropriate arguments to support their theses
- The ability to work effectively individually and as a team member
- The ability to integrate and organize activities within collaborative projects
- The ability to appropriately use, beyond Italian, the English language in both technical-scientific contexts and for general information exchange. Learning methods: Theoretical and laboratory training activities carried out through group work, writing of laboratory reports; training activities focused on learning the English language, preparation of written and oral presentation of the final thesis (also in English).
Assessment methods: Evaluation of presentation ability during oral exams and class seminars; presentation of the thesis.
V - Learning ability Graduates must:
- Have acquired the ability to study new scientific topics, even in different contexts, to effectively integrate acquired notions and skills.
- Be able to construct logical-deductive reasoning and modify standard ones to support scientific arguments/theses.
- Be able to understand the limits of their own knowledge and have skills in identifying textbooks, relevant bibliography, and useful materials for in-depth study.
- Have the ability to read and learn in English. Learning methods: Learning ability is continuously monitored through achievement assessments and exams focusing on acquired notions, especially through self-study. To this end, students are guided from the first year in improving their study methods by teachers and tutors.
English language is taught in dedicated courses and acquired through the progressive use of the foreign language in studying Physics via the use of textbooks and bibliography in English.
Assessment methods:
- Evaluation of study method through written, oral, and practical laboratory exams
- Evaluation of learning of topics proposed for self-study.
Professional function in the workplace.
Professional function in the workplace:
The three-year Physics graduate performs activities involving the use of methodologies, systems, and processes in the following fields:
a) Industrial and laboratory technological applications for electronic measurement instrumentation and control systems for data and image acquisition and analysis;
b) Modeling, analysis, and related computer-physics implications using software for measurement instrumentation, computer network management, and physical measurements for applied purposes;
c) Scientific support for industrial and healthcare activities concerning the environment, meteorology, climatology, materials technology, civil protection, soil protection, energy saving, and cultural heritage;
d) Operation and management of complex equipment in industries, public bodies, and hospital companies;
e) Control of acoustic pollution;
f) Use and control of medical equipment;
g) Dissemination of scientific culture.
Associated professional competencies.
Associated professional competencies:
The three-year Physics graduate acquires knowledge and skills to study and formulate a mathematical model of a physical phenomenon. Their knowledge enables them to perform technical-scientific support activities in industrial contexts, in research laboratories of public or private bodies in the fields of electronics materials and innovation in general, environment, healthcare, energy, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), cultural heritage conservation, education, and scientific culture dissemination.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Career opportunities:
The three-year Physics graduate is required by public and private research bodies, by bodies and industries operating in the fields of technological innovation, environment, civil protection, electronics, innovative materials, healthcare/medical technologies and equipment, software, ICT, cultural heritage conservation, banking/insurance services, and all companies requiring basic knowledge in physics and mathematics and problem-solving abilities.
The three-year Physics degree allows continuation of studies through enrollment in a Master's Degree in Physics and/or Level I Master's programs.
