ITALIAN Degree awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in BIOTECHNOLOGIES Specific educational objectives.
The Biotechnology Bachelor's Degree has a three-year duration, is offered in Italian, meets the requirements of the Class of Degrees in Biotechnology (L-2), and aims to train graduates with a cultural/scientific profile and conceptual/methodological knowledge/skills, suitable for roles in technical-operational professional activities in research, service and production processes typical of applied biotechnology sectors at various levels in the medical-pharmaceutical field.
The study path is structured to ensure both the acquisition of cultural experience and prerequisite skills for the professional role of a biotechnologist with a first-level degree; and a basic and multidisciplinary training that enables the acquisition of requirements for access to more advanced study cycles in the field of "Life Sciences" (e.g., Master's degrees with a biotechnology/biological focus, first-level Master's degrees in biology and biotechnology).
In accordance with the profile of the graduating student, the educational objectives are defined within a single path articulated across cultural and methodological aspects of various disciplinary areas of the Class of Degrees in Biotechnology (L-2): the study course, in addition to offering a solid preparation in Basic Activities and in-depth on Common Biotechnology Disciplines and Disciplines for Regulation, Economy and Bioethics, will be characterized by the acquisition of knowledge and tools for experimental and applied operation in Biotechnology Disciplines with specific purposes in the biological field and in the medical/therapeutic field.
The study path is completed with knowledge and skills acquired through related and integrative training activities, which contribute to the characterization of the study course, developing specific technical-methodological aspects of certain scientific fields, even not characteristic of the L-2 degree class, which, consistently with the educational objectives, will contribute to the acquisition of more application-oriented experimental and practical tools for the technical-operational role that characterizes the professional fields in which the graduate can operate.
In particular, in the first part of the study path, the graduate acquires:
-A basic scientific education in mathematical, physical, computer, statistical and chemical disciplines that allow the acquisition of both theoretical skills/applications regarding calculus fundamentals, physics principles, basic statistics, and prerequisite computer skills for a scientific approach to the study of biological phenomena; as well as theoretical skills/applications in chemical disciplines that enable the use of chemical principles to interpret system structure and transformation, and the acquisition of theoretical and practical skills for the analysis and design of chemical processes;
-A basic education in biological disciplines within Life Sciences, enabling the use of models (from the simplest to the most complex) for an integrated study of the cell and living organisms, focusing on biochemical mechanisms underlying cellular functions, functions of informational macromolecules, and morpho-functional aspects underlying biological phenomena: the student acquires a basic culture and a set of technical-methodological tools and skills fundamental for a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach to the study and design/intervention of actions/activities on biological systems in their structural and functional complexity (simple and complex molecules, cellular organelles, cells, tissues, organs and organisms/microorganisms);
-An education in disciplines for regulation, economy and bioethics that, on one hand, allows the acquisition of knowledge and practical skills contributing to the scientific method and research within the respect and application of ethical regulations, and on the other hand focuses on ethical, social, legal, economic criteria fundamental in the choice and evaluation of the appropriateness and validation of choices/actions related to technological-scientific evolution with socio-economic implications;
-An education in common biotechnology disciplines focusing on physiological aspects of biological systems and the principles and application potentialities, as well as limitations, of genetic-molecular methodologies, cell and/or tissue culture selection, and the use of model organisms, DNA recombinant technology management and genetic engineering principles and application potentialities, and the principles and application potentialities of biotherapeutics/bioactive molecules. This training will provide the graduate with the basic tools for the use of concepts and practical tools for the production of goods and services and in general for the development of biotechnological approaches not only with mastery of procedures, but also with the ability to critically use protocols and in general the use of biological materials/systems.
In the second part of the study path, specific sectors in SSD more oriented towards applied biotechnology training with biological and medical-therapeutic purposes will be deepened, with knowledge and ability to apply more specific knowledge for "Red Biotechnology" relevant in support sectors for diagnostic-therapeutic activities at various application levels in research, production and service sectors in diagnostic and therapeutic/pharmaceutical fields. The student will acquire interdisciplinary knowledge in the biomedical field supported by a scientific and technical-applicative culture in the biological field to ensure professional biotechnological operation that also interfaces with an organic and multidimensional view of the human body in its functioning, under physiological and pathological conditions, and in its most complex regulatory levels.
The English language exam (at least B1 level) will complete the training, providing communication skills and mastery of the language predominantly used in the international scientific field.
Particular attention will be paid to the continuous innovations characterizing the biotechnology sector, which is continuously and rapidly developing, and practical-experimental activities (classroom exercises or practical laboratory activities provided in many of the training activities of the study path) will complement the training not only by acquiring "familiarity" with the applied experimental method, but also by contributing to the development of the ability to apply knowledge to innovative scientific themes.
The completion of training internships, in Italy or abroad, at research institutions, universities, laboratories, companies and/or public administrations, also within the framework of international agreements, will complete the educational objectives of the study course.
The study path provides flexibility in study plans for at least 12 CFU, offering the possibility to choose courses within the framework of university training activities, within a panel of proposals offered by the CDS of the Biotechnology area specifically included in the training offer and/or within the framework of seminar-type courses on biotechnology/pharmacological/biomedical topics, periodically proposed (also in English) by university teachers or external experts in the Department/University.
Adequate skills and tools for communication, information management, and the ability to work in teams with good operational and decisional autonomy will be acquired during the study path through lectures, laboratory exercises, consultation of teaching materials, understanding and critical analysis of scientific literature, classroom discussions on course topics, intermediate and final assessments, and preparation of the thesis.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The study path of the three-year Bachelor's Degree in Biotechnology includes training activities that will allow the graduate to acquire knowledge and understanding:
-of mathematical and statistical methods, as well as the general principles and concepts of physics and computer skills necessary for a scientific approach to the study of phenomena
-of general principles in chemistry to relate the chemical properties of elements and their inorganic compounds, the structure and properties of the main classes of organic molecules to the main types of reactions occurring in biological processes of interest
-of the structural and functional properties of "biomolecules" and the regulatory mechanisms operating in biological systems at molecular, cellular and organismal levels under physiological and pathological conditions
-of the substructure, structure and functions of animal and plant cells and tissues
-of the substructure, structure and biological properties and biotechnological applications of microorganisms
-of regulations and ethical and bioethical issues and the economic and bioethical impact that biotechnological solutions can have in the social context
-of the cultural foundations and methodologies such as genetic engineering and DNA recombinant technologies, cell and tissue cultures, model and transgenic organisms, basic omics technologies, use of databases
-of the main biomolecular, biochemical and bio-clinical techniques used in biomedical and biotechnology laboratories and experimental methodologies for the study of cellular processes
-of the fundamental principles of human pharmacology and toxicology, biotechnological drugs, and the main classes of clinically important drugs and biotherapeutics
-of the genetic mechanisms underlying biological processes
-of the mechanisms underlying the immune response and pathological processes and the biological and biochemical parameters associated with physiopathological states
-of cellular physiology and the functions of human organs and systems, the mechanisms controlling processes determining the maintenance of homeostasis
-of the general organization and structure of the human body and the main morpho-functional relationships of the human organism The learning methods used to ensure knowledge acquisition will be:
-Lectures, classroom discussions and teaching materials (textbooks, scientific articles, materials provided by the teacher)
-Laboratory exercises, provided in some teaching units or training activities
-Seminar-type courses (with final assessment), chosen by the student.
-Thesis preparation Knowledge acquisition will be verified through the following assessment methods:
-Final exam (written or oral) individual
-Intermediate tests provided in some teaching units/activities for ongoing assessment of learning outcomes.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Ability to apply knowledge and understanding:
The study path of the three-year Bachelor's Degree in Biotechnology consists of training activities that will allow the graduate to:
-apply mathematical, physical, statistical and computer methods for the analysis and processing of information and experimental data related to biological systems and phenomena
-apply basic analytical methodologies and procedures specific to chemical disciplines
-apply innovative biotechnological strategies in the fields of cellular and molecular biotechnology, biomedical and diagnostic biotechnology
-apply innovative biotechnological methodologies for the identification, characterization, study, design and production of molecules and biological systems
-apply fundamental knowledge of biological phenomena at molecular, cellular and organismal levels under physiological and pathological conditions to understand molecular, informational and integrative logic
-apply conventional laboratory medicine techniques for the analysis of "determinants" of physiopathological conditions
-apply knowledge of regulations and ethical issues to understand the economic and bioethical impact that biotechnological solutions can have in the social context
-apply fundamental knowledge for the use in biotechnology of methodologies such as genetic engineering and DNA recombinant technologies, cell and tissue cultures, model and transgenic organisms, use of databases
-work in groups and operate autonomously
-communicate the results of conducted activities, in written and oral form in national and international contexts
-know one's own ethical responsibilities
-stay updated on developments in sciences and technologies.
The learning methods used to ensure the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding will be:
-Lectures on biotechnological methodologies
-Laboratory exercises in classroom and laboratory, provided in some teaching units or training activities
-Training internship and orientation
-Thesis preparation.
The assessment of applied abilities will be verified through the following assessment methods:
-Tests involving the solution of technical-scientific problems through written and/or oral tests, laboratory experiences, processing and discussion of reports on experiments conducted
-Final exam involving a presentation and discussion contributing to the evaluation of critical ability, originality and autonomy of the graduate.
III - Judgment autonomy The study course aims to train graduates, through the study path, who, autonomously, have:
-the ability to collect and interpret data, based on their basic mathematical, statistical and computer preparation as well as specific biotechnology preparation;
-the ability to produce autonomous judgments and reflections of a bioethical, economic and legislative nature related to the applications and use of products and procedures developed through biotechnology;
-critical abilities in the application, interpretation and methodological correctness of experimental data and in the planning of experimental activities;
-the ability to evaluate computational and experimental methodologies that allow the optimal resolution of a biological problem.
-interpret biotechnology literature The theoretical (lectures, teaching materials, seminar-type courses) and practical (exercises, laboratories) activities of the CDS, internship activities and thesis preparation represent the tools that contribute to the development of a critical, scientific and autonomous sense in the student.
The verification methods for achieving judgment autonomy will be assessed by teachers during the exams, during which the ability to respond to written, multiple-choice and/or open-ended questions, the ability to argue orally the acquisition, processing and correct interpretation of experimental data, theories, scientific laws, and during the thesis preparation will emerge.
IV - Communication skills Biotechnology graduates must be able to:
-communicate information both orally and in written/graphic form, present problems and solutions to both specific interlocutors in the biotechnology and applied biological sciences field and to non-specialists, demonstrating communication and public dissemination skills also in English;
-use computer tools for the organization, management and communication of technical-scientific information;
-use scientific terminology and common usage for each discipline, also in English.
Frontal teaching and practical experience, learning tools, group work during the internship and preparation of the final thesis contribute to the development of communication skills.
The acquisition of communication skills will be verified:
-by the ability to interact with course peers during frontal teaching activities and practical laboratory experience using appropriate language;
-through mastery of scientific and technical language demonstrated during verification tests and discussion of the thesis.
V - Learning ability The Biotechnology study course ensures that the student acquires adequate mastery of general methods and content to manage the complexity and variability of biotechnology and market scenarios for eventual entry into professional activities at the end of the three-year path or to pursue subsequent master's studies.
During the course, the student acquires adequate cultural preparation for the biotechnologist profession through regular attendance at lectures, seminars, laboratory exercises, and possible overseas experiences. The student is encouraged to continuously deepen their skills, also through constant reference to developments at both theoretical and technological levels of different disciplines, to pursue subsequent studies (master's, master's degrees) with a high degree of autonomy. Moreover, tools are provided that allow the understanding and use of databases, bibliographic material, and other information for continuous knowledge updating and easier entry into the job market.
Through traditional and innovative teaching tools (e.g., use of multimedia platforms), all courses and teaching activities provided in the study course's training offer contribute to achieving learning abilities.
The verification methods for achieving these abilities are applied throughout the student's study path and consist of controlling the ability to solve specific problems related to the more general topics covered in the courses. The individual work carried out by the student under the supervision of the supervisor but in an autonomous manner for the thesis preparation will further allow the evaluation of the achievement of the ability to learn and update knowledge.
Professional role in the workplace.
Professional role in the workplace:
The Biotechnologist is a professional figure who has acquired in the study path the conceptual/methodological knowledge and skills necessary to carry out, within the framework of current Italian/EU regulations and in industrial/social, service and research contexts, activities of analysis and production or development of scientific and technological innovation in "Life Sciences." The professional profile of the Biotechnologist is characterized by operating technical, analytical and verification interventions on biotechnological processes requiring the use of biological systems and/or parts of them, supporting scientific/services activities in companies/laboratories, applied research activities in biological/biotechnology fields, and production activities in the "Industry."
The Biotechnologist:
-performs with scientific method and critical ability protocols for analysis and/or preparation of biotechnological material in which DNA recombinant, genomics, biochemistry, microbiology, molecular, cellular and computational methodologies are applied;
-increases scientific knowledge and operates, in technical roles, in the development of innovative procedures in research and production contexts;
-possesses the theoretical and experimental foundations, basic molecular and cellular knowledge, main competencies on regulatory and ethical issues, conceptual and methodological tools to perform application protocols, operate and fulfill technical/technical-experimental functions in industrial/social, goods and service contexts and in research in biotechnology fields;
-analyzes and uses biological information present in databases through bioinformatics programs;
-contributes, within the respect of current regulations, to procedures for transferring products and processes from the research phase to actual industrial application;
-carries out activities of promotion of products obtained from research/production activities involving the use of biotechnological processes or methodologies;
-designs and follows scientific communication and dissemination activities.
Competencies associated with the role.
Competencies associated with the role:
For the performance of the above-described functions, the Biotechnology graduate has acquired during their study path:
-basic knowledge in mathematical, physical, biological, chemical disciplines for the maturation of the scientific method as a fundamental tool in every applied/technological process used in various fields of biotechnology;
-knowledge and ability to apply technical-analytical procedures in chemical, biochemical, microbiological and pharmaceutical fields;
-basic preparation on analytical-instrumental procedures connected to biological investigations supported also by knowledge of fundamental notions of genetics, molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry;
-ability to apply experimental methodologies and use specific and innovative instrumentation for the analysis and manipulation of genes, proteins, cells, etc.;
-competencies also in ethical/deontological aspects in applying common biotechnology experimental procedures;
-basic knowledge of biological systems, interpreted from a molecular and cellular perspective, as well as of pathophysiological processes on which to operate from a biotechnological perspective with various purposes;
-knowledge of the potentialities and characteristics of instrumentation and laboratory methodologies;
-skills in bioinformatics methodologies for managing and analyzing large amounts of data and, within the respect of current regulations, accessing databases and using their information in research and diagnostic fields;
-knowledge and tools to support activities of presentation/promotion of biotechnological products;
-knowledge of bioethics and processes and regulation, not only regulatory, but also economic, for transferring products from the research phase, to the patenting phase, to the production phase, and to understand the impact of biotechnological solutions in the social context;
-ability both for self-learning and continuous updating, as well as predisposition to teamwork/group work
-ability to express oneself orally and in writing (also in English) to communicate results, information and ideas;
-ability for analysis, critical sense and problem solving (collect information, evaluate possible strategies and elaborate solutions)
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
Graduates of the class carry out technical-applicative support activities in scientific contexts at:
-laboratories/research institutions (public and private) and companies developing biotechnology products and services and/or applying biological technologies in the medical, chemical-pharmaceutical and biomedical fields, etc.;
-in public and private laboratories and institutions dealing with clinical/biological and microbiological analysis, quality control of biological origin products, assisted reproduction procedures;
-Studies, entities and/or consulting companies involved in processes for patent and intellectual property registration;
-Communication and scientific dissemination agencies.
Graduates can also:
-Access second-level university studies (Master's degrees both in Biological and Biotechnology focus) and first-level university Master's degrees.
-On the basis of current regulations, enroll in Section B of the Order of Biologists (Junior Biologist).
-Access, according to current regulations, the profession of Patent Consultant

ITALIAN Awarded degree.
Bachelor's degree in Economics and Business Administration Specific educational objectives.
The Economics and Business Administration degree course aims to prepare students for consultancy activities benefiting companies and organizations in tax, pension, organizational, managerial, and financial fields.
In particular, the degree course prepares students for the profession of certified accountant section B of the Register of Chartered Accountants, as well as for managerial and responsible roles within public and private entities with specific duties related to the entity's financial management.
The educational path consists of courses belonging to economic, business economics, statistical-mathematical, and legal fields, aimed at providing students with fundamental knowledge in business and economic areas, along with basic knowledge in statistical-mathematical and legal fields.
In particular, graduates in Economics and Business Administration must acquire solid foundational knowledge of economic-business, economic, and legal principles governing company operations; additionally, they must develop the ability to interpret the company system in its various components (functions, processes, etc.).
The educational path includes foundational courses such as Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Business Economics, General Mathematics, and Private Law and Public Law Institutions.
In characteristic activities, courses are provided in business area (Accounting, Financial Statements, Business Economics and Management, Corporate Finance, Business Organization), economic area (Economic Policy and Finance), statistical-mathematical area (Statistics and Financial Mathematics), and legal area (Commercial Law and Labor Law).
In complementary training activities, courses belonging to business, economic, and legal areas are provided, specifically Financial Intermediaries Economics, Economic History, and Tax Law.
Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The Economics and Business Administration graduate, due to the educational path followed, acquires, through the use of advanced textbooks (typical of a university course), economic-business, economic, statistical-mathematical, and legal knowledge that ensures knowledge and understanding of issues and questions related to business phenomena (in their multiple dimensions: accounting, management, organizational, etc.) and related multiple issues, including some cutting-edge topics related to current business phenomena.
The methods through which the expected outcomes are achieved are traditional university teaching methods delivered through annual courses organized according to current regulations, along with the dissemination of course programs and recommended textbooks for exam preparation. Verification of achieving the expected outcomes consists of an exam for each individual course. The decision on exam modalities (written or oral) is left to the course instructor, who annually indicates in the exam program the modalities for the final exam, which aims to verify the achievement of the set objectives with the assignment of the CFU numbers required for each course and the awarding of a grade out of thirty attesting to the quality level achieved by the individual student. Knowledge and understanding are acquired through preparation and passing the various exams that make up the study course, which also includes an internship activity and an English language exam. Additionally, a thesis must be written in which the student must demonstrate the ability to organize and systematize acquired information. II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding The Economics and Business Administration graduate (thanks to the study path completed) has the ability to apply knowledge and understanding regarding problems, even complex ones, related to phenomena connected to business life, both from an organizational and operational perspective. The Economics and Business Administration graduate is therefore capable of addressing and solving, in the workplace, concrete issues, as well as theoretical problems through structured and developed arguments by the graduate. The areas in which the Economics and Business Administration graduate can apply knowledge and understanding are typical of economic-business phenomena, from both the organizational structure and operational activity perspective, as well as regarding basic legal issues. The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is achieved through preparation and passing the various exams that make up the study course, which also includes an internship activity and an English language exam. Additionally, a thesis must be written in which the student must demonstrate the ability to organize and systematize acquired information. III - Judgment autonomy The Economics and Business Administration graduate has the ability to collect and interpret business and economic-business data in order to independently form judgments regarding issues connected to business, legal-business, and economic-business problems. The Economics and Business Administration graduate has the ability to collect and interpret economic-business data in order to independently form judgments regarding theoretical and practical issues related to the actions of companies and public and private entities, and the efficiency of private and public administration. Judgment autonomy is verified through preparation and passing the various exams that make up the study course, which also includes an internship activity and an English language exam. Additionally, a thesis must be written in which the student must demonstrate the ability to organize and systematize acquired information. IV - Communication skills The Economics and Business Administration graduate has the ability to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialists and non-specialists in business and economic-business contexts regarding issues connected to typical company problems and public entities, particularly concerning issues related to business economics, business financial statements within a broader economic and legal knowledge framework. Communication skills are acquired through preparation and passing the various exams that make up the study course, which also includes an internship activity and an English language exam. Additionally, a thesis must be written in which the student must demonstrate the ability to organize and systematize acquired information. The Economics and Business Administration graduate has the ability to communicate concepts, data, projects, problematic issues, and solutions to specialists and non-specialists in business contexts regarding operational and theoretical aspects of the company. V - Learning ability The Economics and Business Administration graduate possesses learning abilities necessary to undertake and continue subsequent studies with a high degree of autonomy, both within the strictly business studies area, with a focus on typical business professions, and within economic and economic-business studies, as well as with a focus on specialization studies in public administration management, third sector entities, and public and private entities. Learning abilities are acquired through preparation and passing the various exams that make up the study course, which also includes an internship activity and an English language exam. Additionally, a thesis must be written in which the student must demonstrate the ability to organize, systematize, and systematically present acquired information regarding a specific topic or issue. Professional role in work context.
Professional role in work context:
The professional figure of the Economics and Business Administration graduate primarily performs the following functions: economic-business-management consultancy for private companies, processing of business-management issues, processing of economic-business issues, processing of legal-business issues, management coordination function, support and solution functions regarding accounting, economic-business, economic-management, and legal issues. The competencies associated with these functions are typical economic-business, economic-management, and legal-business competencies.
Competencies associated with the role.
Competencies associated with the role:
The expected professional opportunities (in addition to those listed under the ISTAT codes below and described) are those typical of professional activities, consultancy, and public or private employment in economic-business, economic-management, accounting, and legal-business contexts.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
1) Labor consultant;
2) Auditor;
3) Secretarial management;
4) Accounting and administration;
5) Public official.

ITALIAN Awarded degree.
Bachelor's Degree in PHILOSOPHY AND THEORY OF COMMUNICATION PROCESSES Specific educational objectives.
The study program aims to train graduates with philosophical knowledge and argumentative skills; and who, based on such knowledge and skills, are able to analyze and interpret social, political, and economic phenomena with a multidisciplinary approach. Upon completion of the program, students will be able to clearly communicate the contents of the history of philosophy; formulate and communicate arguments supporting their theses accurately; analyze and evaluate the arguments of their interlocutors; read complex texts, also in at least one language other than Italian, and synthesize them accurately and effectively; use bibliographic tools.
To this end, the study program first aims to ensure that students know:
1) the logical-analytical tools of philosophy used to evaluate and produce arguments;
2) the history of Western philosophy, in its fundamental lines, from ancient Greece to the present, also in its relationship with the history of science.
For this purpose, the study program offers numerous courses on philosophical and historical-philosophical topics. These courses are largely mandatory, to establish a core of basic knowledge that characterizes all graduates of the study program. An additional course on the history of science is also available.
The study program also aims to provide knowledge in other disciplines related to philosophy. Therefore, the study program offers students the possibility to choose some courses on literary, artistic, anthropological, sociological, psychological, geographical, and pedagogical topics. Additionally, there are courses and other training activities, partly mandatory, related to foreign languages and computer-related training activities.
Graduates who, at the end of their overall study path, including a master's degree, have sufficient credits in appropriate sets of sectors may, in accordance with current legislation, participate in the admission tests for teacher training paths in secondary school. For this purpose, the study program includes courses on historical topics in sufficient number to facilitate future access to the teaching competition class A/19 Philosophy and History.
The training path is thus concretized in the first year of the course through courses on the history of philosophy, laying the foundation for historical-philosophical training; through at least one philosophical course specifically related to logic, providing argumentative tools useful in subsequent years of the study program; through a course on the history of science; and through elective courses in other disciplines related to philosophy, allowing immediate connection between philosophy and other disciplines. In the second year, the content of fundamental philosophical disciplines is deepened, both in theoretical and historical-philosophical areas; a course on knowledge of at least one foreign language is followed; and the investigation of disciplines related to philosophy and useful for understanding the contemporary world continues. In the third year, attention is directed towards more advanced areas of philosophy, and history courses are also addressed. Additionally, at the third year, student-selected activities are provided, offering space for personal customization of the path according to the cultural interests and training needs of each student. Throughout the three years, other training activities are also available that: ensure knowledge of English at least at B1 level of the Common European Framework; offer the possibility to acquire computer skills and skills related to the world of work; and bring the student into contact with some research initiatives. A final exam is required to complete the training path, consisting of the preparation of a short thesis and its discussion before a committee.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The study program provides a solid knowledge of current debates in various areas of philosophical research and the history of philosophy from antiquity to the present. To this end, the study program includes numerous philosophical courses, which also serve to understand various aspects of contemporary society. This understanding also occurs through courses on non-philosophical topics. Historical-philosophical courses also enable students to understand philosophical texts in their context, while the history of science course contextualizes the evolution of scientific thought.
Upon successful completion of the study path, the student:
- masters the basic aspects of philosophy, the history of philosophy, and the history of science;
- possesses linguistic knowledge enabling them to understand philosophical texts in at least one European language other than Italian and to communicate their arguments in at least one European language other than Italian;
- navigates various disciplines related to philosophy and understands their importance for philosophy;
- understands and contextualizes some fundamental themes of various areas of humanistic culture, in historical-cultural, linguistic, literary, and artistic contexts.
Regarding linguistic knowledge, the student acquires good written and oral proficiency in at least one European Union language other than Italian and applies it outside the philosophical context.
Additionally, the presence of numerous research activities organized by the study program's faculty among other credit-bearing activities offers students the opportunity to understand what philosophy as a research activity entails and to observe closely how a cultural event is organized.
The above-mentioned knowledge and understanding are primarily acquired through basic, characteristic, and related courses, which, distributed differently according to the annuality of the course, on one hand aim to broaden the spectrum of knowledge from an interdisciplinary perspective; on the other hand, they allow appreciation of the methodological specifics of various study areas.
Courses are delivered through frontal and interactive lectures, also using multimedia tools, and in the case of the history of science course, through direct experiences with historical scientific instruments. During lectures, institutional and methodological topics are presented, and aspects and problems related to research in various disciplinary fields are also introduced.
In addition to courses, knowledge and understanding are also acquired through:
- seminar activities and internships, diversified according to the disciplinary field, complementing frontal lectures;
- teaching modules for achieving at least B1 level in English;
- autonomous choices by the student to acquire or recognize credits in other training activities (selecting from additional courses, internships, additional linguistic knowledge, computer and telecommunication skills, seminars, conferences, etc.);
- preparation of the thesis work in view of the final exam, with consultation and analysis of the relevant bibliography.
Verification of knowledge acquisition and understanding depends on the type of activity:
- courses provide various examination methods (written, oral, or through student-prepared works of various types), integrated, depending on the course, with intermediate assessments, group work, etc.;
- other training activities are accredited based on suitability assessments (such as B1 English certification and computer certification);
- the final exam requires the preparation of a thesis to be discussed before a committee that issues a final judgment based on the student's academic record, the thesis, and the discussion itself.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding Upon successfully completing the study program:
- is able to organize, classify, and analyze historical-philosophical texts and documents;
- effectively contextualizes texts, documents, but also themes and issues concerning philosophy and other humanistic disciplines related to philosophy;
- prepares descriptive and argumentative texts and oral interventions on topics, particularly in the philosophical field;
- has the tools to undertake some initial research experiences;
- applies classification, elaboration, contextualization, and analysis skills in the workplace within editorial and documentary services, cultural services, and communication in general.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is acquired through courses, seminar activities, and internship activities.
Verification of the acquisition of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding occurs mainly in credit exams, but also in activities that provide suitability or credit recognition without a grade.
In evaluation, both ongoing and final, for philosophical courses, instructors pay particular attention to mastery of philosophical terminology and the ability to apply it autonomously, both orally and in written texts.

III - Judgment autonomy By studying various aspects of philosophy and the history of philosophy, the student autonomously develops preferences for certain topics over others, and is constantly invited by instructors to express and justify such preferences. This process of acquiring motivated preferences is also manifested in the choice of topic for the written work of the final exam.
Within all courses, the student is encouraged to ask questions and raise objections, progressively acquiring the ability for autonomous evaluation of considered arguments. Instructors often provide suggestions for independent reading, additional to those indicated in the course syllabi, and give indications for independent research of further literature.

IV - Communication skills The student acquires the ability to communicate philosophical ideas and arguments and to effectively illustrate the history of philosophy, also in relation to the history of scientific thought. The ability to communicate ideas and arguments is developed in relation to numerous areas of philosophy and also in relation to the disciplines connected to philosophy present in the training offer. The variety of such topics ensures that, at the end of their study path, they can communicate ideas and arguments on new topics (with which they have no prior familiarity) and not only philosophical ones.
Acquisition of basic knowledge in at least one language other than Italian enables the student to manifest such communication skills in that language or languages.
These communication skills will be developed through seminars, reading groups, preparation of reports on assigned topics, and verified through ongoing exercises and oral and written exams.

V - Learning ability Teaching activities emphasize selective and comparative skills for the acquisition of a learning method: within complex philosophical texts to be read within various courses, the student must select truly important information and focus on argumentative connections. At the end of the path, the student will have acquired skills enabling rapid learning of new themes and identifying their essential nodes.
Learning abilities will be verified through ongoing exercises and oral and written exams.

Professional function.
Professional function:
Graduates of the study program, who become specialists in public relations, image, and related professions, will perform one or more of the following functions in the workplace:
- handle public relations, ensuring the argumentative and expressive quality of communication in written and oral form;
- compose and edit complex and articulated texts, both in traditional format and in multimedia formats;
- contribute independently and critically to the making of complex decisions with ethical implications;
- organize cultural events with interdisciplinary aspects;
- facilitate communication between different cultural fields.

Associated competencies.
Associated competencies:
Graduates of the study program, to perform the functions associated with this profile, must possess the following competencies:
- be able to set up, plan, and manage relationships between the organization they work for and its stakeholders (internal or external to the organization);
- be able to build, maintain, and develop more or less complex relationship networks;
- have the ability to organize effective and targeted communication in line with predefined organizational goals;
- manage relationships with media and press;
- be able to analyze various possible decisions from an ethical perspective, seeking to maximize utility or adhere to general ethical principles adopted, thus contributing to the solution of complex problems;
- formulate independent judgments on various issues raised by contemporary culture, adopting a broad and multidisciplinary perspective;
- have adequate proficiency in at least one European Union language other than Italian.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
Employment opportunities:
- public relations officer;
- editor/writer at publishing houses and traditional and multimedia news outlets;
- press officer;
- cultural events organizer;
- consultant on ethical or strategic issues;
- spokesperson in public administrations.
